Each pipeline starts with RGB JPEG files and delivers synchronized CUDA float16 batches of 256 images. The benchmark contains 1314 measurements across 73 recipes. On the 34 recipes shared by all eight paths, DALI delivered a median of 19.7 batches/s and AlbumentationsX (AX) delivered 17.1. DALI was fastest on 34 of those recipes. Median peak process GPU memory was 1,872 MiB for DALI and 404 MiB for AX.

authors.name: Vladimir Iglovikov

papers.title: Navi-Agent: Unlocalized Monocular Navigation Agent
papers.summary: Vision-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments (VLN-CE) requires an embodied agent to execute long-horizon instructions in unknown environments. Existing zero-shot VLN-CE systems typically maintain spatial states through geometric localization or coordinate-based representations. Recent geometry-constrained navigation removes depth and globally consistent coordinates, but maintaining persistent spatial awareness for place confirmation, progress verification, and recovery remains challenging. We present Navi-Agent, a zero-shot VLN-CE agent that constructs a coordinate-free spatial state from visual observations and executed motion histories. Navi-Agent organizes this state as a navigation topology, where nodes represent visual places and edges represent motion transitions. This representation enables observation-based approximate self-localization, task progress verification, and visual revisitation-based recovery. Navi-Agent performs closed-loop navigation by decomposing instructions into sub-goals, executing local visual navigation, and verifying visited places through the constructed spatial state. Experiments on zero-shot VLN-CE benchmark and real-world robot platforms show that Navi-Agent achieves state-of-the-art performance among geometry-constrained methods while remaining competitive with approaches relying on geometric localization.

authors.name: Wenyuan Xie, Mengyang Hong, Yongzhong Wang, Yanbiao Ji, Yijin Zhou, Shaokai Wu, Shalayiding Sirejiding, Huayi Zhou, Yi-Chao Chen, Ma Ling, Yue Ding, Hongtao Lu

papers.title: WorldOracle: Benchmarking Action-Conditioned World Models against Real-World Executions
papers.summary: We introduce WorldOracle, a benchmark specifically designed to evaluate action-conditioned world models (ACWMs) against paired real-world executions. Given the same initial observation and low-level action sequence, WorldOracle asks whether a predicted rollout reproduces what happens in the real world, including physical consequences and task-state transitions. We evaluate models along four complementary dimensions: physical state correctness, interaction spatial alignment, key interaction area fidelity, and multi-view action coherence. To support this evaluation, we curate real-world training and evaluation suites that cover different interaction dynamics and embodiments. The evaluation suite contains long, multi-segment episodes with both successful and failed executions, enabling evaluation across varied action outcomes and behavior distributions. Experiments on seven representative ACWMs reveal distinct model strengths and failure modes. WorldOracle provides a systematic foundation for measuring and advancing action-conditioned world modeling for manipulation. We release the datasets, evaluation code, and leaderboard: https://worldoracle-benchmark.github.io/.

authors.name: Haoyi Duan, Liliang Chen, Nan Wang, Yang Zhang, Yuhang Lu, Xiaotong Chen, Wei-Cheng Tseng, Shenyuan Gao, Zhaoshuo Li, Jingyi Jin, Pooya Jannaty, Dhruv Shah, Yuke Zhu, Ming-Yu Liu, Maoqing Yao, Guanghui Ren

papers.title: TetraCoder: Adaptive Tetrahedral Encoding for Neural Fields
papers.summary: Implicit and explicit representations of geometry are central in computer graphics applications and come with their pros and cons. With surface sampling being faster on explicit representations and spatial queries being faster on implicit representations, finding efficient conversions between them is a highly desirable property. We present TetraCoder, a single resolution hash-free adaptive tetrahedral encoding that links an explicit tetrahedral spatial encoder with an underlying implicit signed distance field (SDF). The resulting hybrid implicit-explicit space is continuous piecewise affine (CPWA) by design, allowing to obtain an exact correspondence between the implicit SDF and the explicit analytic mesh. TetraCoder's design comes with additional perks, in particular: (a) it scales better than multi-resolution encoding methods due to its single resolution optimizable grid, (b) unlike hash-based methods, it is not affected by collisions, (c) it enables fast tetrahedral ray-tracing, geometry and appearance editing, directly through its adaptive tetrahedral scaffold. We demonstrate the versatility of TetraCoder by showing an improvement over state-of-the-art methods on multiple tasks: 2D/3D fitting from images and point clouds, 3D novel view synthesis, 3D reconstruction, and geometry/appearance editing.

authors.name: Daniele Della Pietra, Antonella Rech, Nicola Conci, Nicola Garau

papers.title: Powering the Space Elevator
papers.summary: Powering the Space Elevator is a report on the work of an International Space Elevator Consortium study group tasked with determining the technology options for delivering power to the climbers on the space elevator at any altitude above Earth. The book covers options such as laser power beaming, microwave beaming, a solar-powered climber, and delivering power through the electrical conductivity of the tether. This report starts with the reference conceptual design of a climber from the 2023 study report, "The Climber/Tether Interface of the Space Elevator," and adds features to the climber that allow it to ascend or descend the elevator tether. The strengths and limitations of current technologies are identified, along with areas for future research.

authors.name: Larry Bartoszek, A. J. Burke, Shreyansh Chauhan, Avery Davis, Hassan El Chab, Blaise Gassend, John Knapman, Martin Lades, George Neil, Adrian Nixon, Dennis Wright

papers.title: All edges lead to Rome: analyzing Late Antiquity regime shifts using coin hoard data
papers.summary: Complex network analysis and other statistical techniques can be fruitfully applied to historical data to understand dynamics that brought the territory under study to a certain state. In this paper we use the FLAME database to understand when a drastic change of trade regime occurred in the Italian peninsula by looking at mint-hoard links that are evidence of a physical connection between them. By using changepoint analysis to pinpoint precise dates in the time series of these links, and then historical as well as network data to establish the sequence of network collapse, we find that the demise of the Western Roman Empire started at the beginning of the 5th century AD, yielding a more precise sequence of how and when it reached Italia.

authors.name: Juan J. Merelo-Guerv\'os

papers.title: Application-Oriented Evaluation of CPU/GPU Quantum Simulators: From Foundational Circuits to Quantum Chemistry
papers.summary: Quantum computing simulators underpin the development and prototyping of quantum algorithms, yet the practical choice between competing software stacks and their CPU and GPU backends is rarely guided by application-oriented evidence. We present a systematic, quantum hardware-agnostic evaluation of two widely used stacks, CUDA-Q and Qiskit, selected as the simulators closest to production execution paths, across CPU and GPU backends, and across single- and double-precision arithmetic. The evaluation spans foundational utility circuits (GHZ-state preparation and QFT/QFT$^\dagger$ mirror circuits) through applied quantum chemistry (Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) energy estimation with standard UCCSD and a depth-reduced LCNot-UCCSD ansatz, and direct sampling on hydrogen chains up to 32 qubits). The results yield concrete selection guidance: GPU-accelerated double precision delivers consistent speedups, typically $2\times$ to $10\times$ for tractable application workloads and substantially larger at the widest circuits up to $100\times$ or more, and governs the maximum simulable system size under fixed compute memory, while CPU statevector backends and Qiskit Aer remain competitive, and at times preferable, at low qubit counts and wide but shallow circuits. We demonstrate the practical payoff of this guidance by extending an in-house developed QSCI(LCNot-UCCSD)-RBM electronic-structure workflow, previously constrained to a 16-qubit active space on a CPU, to a 32-qubit (10 electrons, 16 orbitals) active space with GPU acceleration, completing a 20-point potential-energy-surface scan of N$_{2}$ in the cc-pVDZ basis. This end-to-end evaluation establishes that the principled simulator selection translates directly into expanded scientific reach and faster algorithmic prototyping.

authors.name: Anurag K. S. V., Ashish Kumar Patra, Afra Navas, Ruchika Bhat, Sai Shankar P., Rahul Maitra, Manas Mukherjee, Jaiganesh G

papers.title: An improved statistical treatment for radioassay-based background projection incorporating part-to-part variation
papers.summary: For low background experiments, prediction of the background from radioactivity in detector components is of critical importance. Radioassays are often conducted on small samples or individual parts, which may be subject to differences in production or handling resulting in a part-to-part variation. This part-to-part variation can have an impact on the total activity and is not presently captured by the averaging methods used to evaluate radioassays. We propose a new method for the averaging of radioassays to incorporate this part-to-part variation into predictions of the total activity of parts. We also consider how to add component activities based on assays for component groups that are simulated as a single entity.

authors.name: Louis Varriano, Jason Detwiler

papers.title: Terahertz and infrared links in controlled non-Kolmogorov turbulence
papers.summary: Hybrid terahertz/infrared (THz/IR) links are usually modeled with Kolmogorov turbulence, but whether the turbulence spectral type matters equally for both bands has not been investigated. We transmit co-propagating 625 GHz and 1550 nm links through laboratory-controlled turbulence while a Mach-Zehnder interferometer and thermistors independently measure its spectral exponent and structure parameter on the shared path. Inlet-air temperature, not airflow speed, drives the exponent from Kolmogorov-like to non-Kolmogorov. At comparable structure parameters, this change reverses which model better reproduces the IR attenuation at the nominal inner scale, whereas the THz attenuation is insensitive to it. With type-matched models, predicted and measured bit-error-rate trends agree within 0.14 (IR) and 0.06 (THz) decades. IR predictions therefore require the spectral shape and inner scale, not turbulence strength alone.

authors.name: Hanchen Liu, He Ni, Xiaoxiang Li, Jiabiao Zhao, Yuheng Song, Lingfeng Tian, Yi Luo, Jianjun Ma

papers.title: Some Considerations on Measuring and Comparing Things
papers.summary: Measurements and relationships between measurements are basic aspects underlying science and technology. In the present text, we present and discuss some of the approaches for measuring, normalizing, and comparing entities represented in terms of a set of measurements. Three main categories of measured values (constant, direct, or inverse) are proposed, underlaid by the relationship between data variation or intervals of interest and magnitude of the quantifications. For example, in certain cases the variation of measurements can be expected to be proportional to the relative magnitude (e.g.~when the magnitudes extend over long ranges). The considered approaches to comparing measurements include the Euclidean distance, three types of proximity based on the latter, as well as the Jaccard and coincidence indices. The presentation is complemented by graphical illustrations.

authors.name: Luciano da F. Costa, Gonzalo Travieso, Alexandre Benatti

papers.title: On Quantised Magnetic Monopoles in the Nonlocal Electromagnetic Field
papers.summary: We consider Maxwell electrodynamics in the presence of both electric and magnetic charges when the fields are made nonlocal by the prescription of the Moffat-Thompson nonlocal quantum field theory. The symmetry between the electric and magnetic equations is preserved, while a point magnetic charge is a finite distribution and its field energy becomes finite. When Dirac's quantisation condition $eg=2\pi n$ is imposed, the magnetic self-energy is found to be much greater than the corresponding electric one. We conclude that magnetic monopoles may be permitted by the theory and yet require a very large energy for their production, thus making their abundance and detection a difficult feat.

authors.name: E. J. Thompson, Arvin Kouroshnia, J. W. Moffat

papers.title: Dissipative many-body theory of electron-phonon-photon systems
papers.summary: Optical cavities offer opportunities to control quantum materials, but radiative leakage and vibrational relaxation call for microscopic theories that treat interactions and dissipation on equal footing. We develop a Keldysh-Lindblad nonequilibrium Green's function framework for interacting electrons coupled to quantized photon and phonon fields. The formulation accommodates boson-number-nonconserving Hamiltonians and dissipative channels that combine electronic transitions with bosonic processes. We derive the mixed electron-boson diagrammatic expansion and the corresponding Kadanoff-Baym equations, retaining environmental noise, initial correlations, and interaction-induced memory. The equal-time equations govern the electronic density matrix and the bosonic covariance. As an illustration, we construct jump operators that preserve a semiconductor with filled valence bands and an empty photon field. Within a mean-field treatment, this state remains stationary although its two-time propagators exhibit dissipative broadening. The framework opens new avenues for studying correlated dynamics in lossy cavities and vibrational environments.

authors.name: Zhenlin Zhang, Enrico Perfetto, Gianluca Stefanucci

papers.title: Real-time dynamics with bead-Fourier path integrals. III. Atomistic condensed-phase simulations
papers.summary: Accurately accounting for nuclear quantum effects (NQEs), including zero-point energy and nuclear tunneling, is essential for a reliable prediction of the structural, thermodynamic, and dynamical properties of chemical systems, particularly those involving light atoms. However, incorporating NQEs could render simulations of large-scale chemical systems computationally prohibitive, particularly when combined with expensive electronic-structure calculations. One potential avenue for reducing cost is to use bead-Fourier path integrals (BF-PIs). In Paper I, we introduced the BF centroid molecular dynamics (BF-CMD) method, in which BF-PIs were used to compute an effective potential for CMD, and in Paper II, we introduced BF ring polymer MD (BF-RPMD), taking the BF-PI and using it for approximate real-time dynamics. Both papers featured a series of model systems and were able to reduce the number of beads needed to converge dynamical properties by a factor of 2 to 4, depending on the system. In this work, we report the first implementation and application of the BF-PI framework to atomistic simulations using liquid bulk water and hexagonal ice as test cases. As in our previous papers, we find that adding just a single Fourier component to the path yields a 4- and 8-fold reduction in the number of beads while achieving results that agree with reference PI simulations for liquid water and ice, respectively. We also demonstrate that we can reduce simulation costs by up to 5.5x compared to standard PIs by reducing the number of force calculations and normal-mode transformations.

authors.name: Nathan London, Mohammad R. Momeni

papers.title: A Beginner's Guide to Physical Networks
papers.summary: Network theory studies entities (nodes) and the relationships between them (edges). While these entities and their relationships may be abstract in general, this tutorial focuses on the special case of physical networks: spatially embedded networks that carry physical quantities such as electric charge, fluid volume, or momentum. The underlying structure is described mathematically by a graph (Section I), with the incidence matrix playing a central role in the analysis. Viewing a graph as a special case of a cell complex reveals the topological structure of the incidence matrix and its relation to familiar operators from calculus (Section II). Because these networks are physical, flows are conserved at each node and often derive from the gradient of a potential. Models that satisfy these principles behave analogously to circuits; accordingly, we first review circuit theory (Section III), then examine related fluid flow (Section IV) and mechanical (Section V) networks. Briefly, the topics of random walkers (Section VI) and nonlinear networks (Section VII) will be discussed, followed by concluding remarks (Section VIII). Analytical examples and Python implementations, in lieu of pseudocode, are included throughout. Exercises are included as footnotes. This tutorial is based on a short course taught at the Boulder School for Condensed Matter in 2019 and a course taught at the University of Pennsylvania in Spring 2024. It should be a useful resource for students, teachers, and researchers applying graph theory to physical networks. Knowledge of linear algebra is assumed, but no prior knowledge of graph theory or physics is necessary.

authors.name: Aaron Winn, Eleni Katifori

papers.title: A multi-fidelity dataset of two-dimensional steady laminar channel flow around obstacles
papers.summary: Surrogates that correct inexpensive flow simulations need the same flows solved at several fidelities and an estimate of the numerical error of the reference solutions. This dataset contains 4,500 two-dimensional, steady, laminar channel flows past a single obstacle. Each is solved in five numerical configurations: second-order convection on meshes with cell sizes of 2, 1, 0.5 and 0.25 mm, and first-order convection on the 1 mm mesh. A seeded generator draws the obstacles from five shape families in three size classes. All 22,500 OpenFOAM runs were iterated to initial residuals of $10^{-6}$, and each run's residuals, iterations and provenance are recorded. Every run provides the velocity and pressure on a regular grid with geometry channels, and the pressure and wall shear along the obstacle. Its 20 flow attributes, computed on the simulation mesh, include drag and lift split into pressure and friction parts. The four second-order levels give an estimate of the discretisation uncertainty of 19 attributes of every case. Fixed splits include three out-of-distribution test sets.

authors.name: Alper Saydam, Bar{\i}\c{s} Akg\"un

papers.title: Amortized conditional inference under changing parameter information in small-angle X-ray scattering
papers.summary: Many scientific measurements do not uniquely determine the physical system that produced them. Different parameter configurations may explain the same observations, and additional measurements or physical assumptions can change which explanations remain plausible. We develop an amortized conditional inference method to examine these alternatives as the available information changes. Using masked flow matching, the method approximates joint conditional posteriors when different parameters are supplied exactly or with uncertainty. This allows repeated analysis of the same measurement without retraining, while reusing its encoded representation. We can also examine the consequences of assumed parameter distributions and separately assess whether supplied information is compatible with the observation-only posterior. We validate the learned conditionals against analytic posteriors and compare posterior accuracy and inference cost in a simulated scattering benchmark, where the compressed architecture performs better than joint attention on both measures. We apply the method to small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) of cellulose fibrils in paper, examining structural ambiguities in simulated measurements and the effects of physical assumptions on experimental measurements of a paper during hydration. At high humidity, the inferred effective fibril size distribution broadens. Assuming that this distribution remains unchanged instead shifts the posterior towards increased interfibrillar separation, although both interpretations reproduce the measured curves similarly. The compatibility analysis identifies conserved parameter values that are difficult to reconcile with the wettest measurements.

authors.name: Maria B{\aa}nkestad, Sandra Barman, Erik Kaunisto, Eskil Andreasson, Smita Chakraborty, Shun Yu, Jerk R\"onnols, Sepideh Pashami

papers.title: A Clifford algebra approach to bosonic strings with fermionic boundaries
papers.summary: The Brauer-Weyl (1935) theorem states that the algebra of tensor products of spinors is isomorphic to the Clifford (geometric) algebra, in any number of spacetime dimensions. The algebraic relation between fermions and bosons seen in the standard model agrees with the Brauer-Weyl theorem, but not with supersymmetry. It is commonly argued that string theory requires supersymmetry, on the grounds that nonsupersymmetric bosonic string theory (1) does not admit fermions, and (2) has an unstable tachyonic ground state. This paper rebuts those standard objections, pointing out that bosonic string theory admits ferm\-ions lying on a D-brane boundary of open strings, and that the open-string tachyon has all the properties of a Higgs field. The original 1970s formulation of bosonic string theory, re-envisaged as a theory of all the forces, not just the strong force, fits the standard model beautifully.

authors.name: Andrew J S Hamilton, Tyler McMaken

papers.title: Relativistic and quantum fluid dynamics: nonlinear momentum evolution
papers.summary: We present an alternative framework for nonlinear momentum evolution in fluid dynamics, in which relativistic effects are proposed as an underlying mechanism for nonlinear behavior, even in the low-velocity regime. By interpreting the second-order velocity diffusion equation from a quantum-mechanical perspective, we establish a connection between higher-order viscous transport and the reduced Planck constant, identifying the second-order viscosity coefficient with \(\hbar\). Furthermore, we show that the coupling of second-order velocity diffusion and nonlinear momentum evolution leads to a Dirac-type equation for quantum fluids. These findings reveal a potential connection among relativistic effects, higher-order fluid transport, and quantum wave dynamics.

authors.name: Fei Wang

papers.title: Stronger-to-weaker gravity in generalized Brans-Dicke cosmology and implications for the Hubble and $S_8$ tensions
papers.summary: We investigate the cosmological implications of a Brans--Dicke-type scalar-tensor theory with non-minimal coupling $A(\phi)=1+c_1\phi+c_2\phi^2$ and power-law potentials $V(\phi)\propto\phi^{2n}$ ($n=2,3,4$), in which the dynamics of the scalar field yields a time-varying effective gravitational strength $G_{\rm eff}$. The theory is restricted to ghost-free solutions that also satisfy the dominant energy condition, sub-Planckian field ranges, as well as solar-system and big-bang nucleosynthesis bounds, keeping the scalar sector in a well-controlled and motivated regime. When confronting the model with Planck CMB, DESI DR2 BAO and Pantheon+ supernova data with the SH0ES calibration, the preferred scalar field dynamics lowers the sound horizon and raises the Hubble constant to $H_0=71.09\pm0.66\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ for $n=3$, which also shows a moderate Bayesian preference over $\Lambda$CDM ($\ln B=4.55\pm0.44$) under the adopted priors. We show that, within this framework, the early stronger-gravity and late weaker-gravity phases compete for the same coefficients, forcing the latter to have amplitudes bounded by $1-G_{\rm eff}/G \lesssim 10^{-4}$. The data also prefer only brief weaker-gravity excursions after recombination for $n=2$ and $n=3$, lasting less than $0.1$ e-folds, but $n=4$ shows late-time transitions at $z\lesssim 3$ persisting for up to $\sim 1.9$ e-folds. In all cases the weaker-gravity regime is far too shallow to suppress the growth of structure: the $S_8$ parameter is in fact higher than in $\Lambda$CDM and the preferred cosmologies are of the early-modified-gravity type.

authors.name: Lucas P. C. Le\~ao, Gl\'auber C. Dorsch, Sergio E. Jor\'as, Gonzalo J. Olmo

papers.title: A No-Go Theorem for Type-3 New General Relativity on $\Lambda$CDM Background
papers.summary: We investigate whether Type-3 New General Relativity can alleviate the cosmic growth tension. On a $\Lambda$CDM background, we derive the scalar perturbation equations and find the effective gravitational coupling to exceed Newton's constant throughout the parameter range compatible with ghost-free and background-hierarchy conditions. By confronting the theoretical model with growth-rate measurements from major galaxy redshift surveys, including WiggleZ, SDSS-IV eBOSS, BOSS, and VIPERS, we obtain constraints on the effective coupling that are consistent with the $\Lambda$CDM value. Consequently, the conditions for stability and tension reduction are mutually exclusive.

authors.name: Shivam Kumar Mishra, B. Mishra

papers.title: Revisiting the Capacitance of a Hollow Metal Cylinder
papers.summary: We complete the analysis of the capacitance of a hollow metal cylinder by deriving series representations for different aspect ratios and a practical formula that approximates the capacitance of the tube for any aspect ratio with an error below 1%.

authors.name: Antonio Iadicicco, Luigi Verolino

papers.title: The magnetic field of a homogeneously magnetized circular piece
papers.summary: The magnetic field of a homogeneously magnetized circular piece, i.e. the part of a finite cylinder that is cut off by two planes parallel to the coordinate axes, is determined. The field is expressed as the product between the demagnetization tensor describing the geometrical part of the problem and the magnetization. All nine components of the tensor are expressed in closed form in terms of elementary functions and incomplete elliptic integrals of the first, second and third kind. The complementary geometrical piece, bounded by the same arc from the outside, is obtained from the same expressions. The solution, implemented in the open source magnetic framework MagTense, is verified against direct numerical integration and against a finite element calculation of the magnetic field, showing excellent agreement.

authors.name: Kaspar K. Nielsen, Rasmus Bj{\o}rk

papers.title: The magnetic field of a homogeneously magnetized cone
papers.summary: The magnetic field of a homogeneously magnetized right circular cone is determined. The field is expressed as the product between the demagnetization tensor describing the geometrical part of the problem and the magnetization. Additionally, its magnetic scalar potential is expressed as the product between a demagnetization vector and the magnetization. All nine components of the tensor and three components of the vector are expressed in terms of elliptic integrals of the first, second and third kind, and a single scalar function of the field point. This function is given as a one-dimensional integral and as a series, and it reduces to the known logarithm on the axis of the cone. The demagnetization tensor and vector for the truncated cone and the annular cone are given by simple superposition. The magnetometric demagnetization tensor is also derived in closed form. The tensors are verified against direct numerical integration of the surface charges and with a finite element model, showing excellent agreement.

authors.name: Rasmus Bj\o{}rk

papers.title: What explainable deep learning reveals about wall-bounded turbulence: insights from conditional surprisal
papers.summary: Explainable deep learning (XDL) has identified regions of wall turbulence important for prediction that are only partly captured by classical coherent-structure criteria. We examine turbulent channel flow at friction Reynolds numbers $Re_\tau\simeq125$ and $550$ by comparing SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) with conditional surprisal, which quantifies how unexpected an observed velocity transition is given its initial state. Although SHAP selection favours energetic fluid and largely overlaps classical masks, selected fluid outside these masks is less energetic but exhibits higher surprisal. Near the wall, at comparable fluctuation energy and wall distance, high-surprisal voxels outside classical masks are approximately 11 and 5 times more likely to be selected by SHAP than low-surprisal voxels, respectively. Within classical masks, the factor is about 1.3. SHAP-selected structures containing paired high- and low-speed regions exhibit surprisal maxima near their internal $u=0$ interfaces, where transverse velocity fluctuations remain nonzero. These interfaces contain vortical and SHAP-only regions, with the latter accounting for more than half of their reconstructed area. In part of the buffer layer, the SHAP-only portions have higher mean surprisal than the vortical portions. However, comparison with generic $u=0$ surfaces indicates that much of the raw interfacial surprisal excess is associated with surrounding fluctuation energy; after energy matching, the equally weighted surface comparison is statistically compatible with unity on the retained common support. Together, these results show how state-conditioned velocity transitions complement instantaneous structure-identification criteria in characterizing SHAP-selected flow.

authors.name: Bel\'en Reverte-Badillo, Andr\'es Cremades, Ricardo Vinuesa, Sergio Hoyas

papers.title: Exposing and overcoming the polarizability pathology of the Fermi-Omont pseudopotential
papers.summary: Any realistic electron-atom or ion-atom potential energy function contains a long-range contribution from the atomic polarizability which gives a $1/r^4$ long-range tail. This modifies the well-known Wigner threshold law for orbital momenta $L>0$, causing these $L\neq 0$ scattering phase shifts to vary linearly in energy instead of as $k^{2L+1}$. The $L>0$ Fermi-Omont zero-range pseudopotentials are erroneously divergent at zero energy due to this modification, a divergence deriving from very long-range physics that should not be incorporated into a Dirac delta function. Here, we investigate some alternative scenario for repairing this pathological behavior to obtain smooth and accurate potential energy curves calculated using the Fermi-Omont pseudopotential concept, with some systematic benchmarking tests for comparison.

authors.name: S. Efe G\"urleyen, Matthew T. Eiles, Chris H. Greene

papers.title: Graph Neural Network based non-local models: Toward application to RANS turbulence modeling
papers.summary: Most machine-learning closures for the Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) equations are local, predicting the closure quantities at each point solely from local flow features, despite the non-local nature of turbulent interactions. We propose a non-local closure framework based on Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) that exploits the mesh connectivity. Each finite-volume cell becomes a graph node, and cells sharing a face are connected by an edge. Through message passing, each layer aggregates information from neighboring nodes, so that after $k$ layers the prediction at a cell depends on its $k$-hop neighborhood, which naturally accounts for non-local effects. To make training feasible when each simulation yields a single large graph, we also introduce a breadth-first-search $k$-hop subgraph sampling strategy, which acts as data augmentation and cuts the cost per processed graph during training. We compare GCNs with feed-forward networks (FNNs) of equal size on two periodic-hills benchmarks: a laminar advection-diffusion transport problem that mimics the non-local character of RANS closures, and the turbulent eddy-viscosity prediction of the Closure Challenge dataset at $Re = 5600$. In the laminar case, FNNs are accurate only within the training regime and with sufficiently informative inputs, whereas GCNs generalize better to unseen geometries, including out-of-distribution flows, and partly compensate for missing input features. In the turbulent proof-of-concept case, the graph-based models achieve modest but consistent improvements compared to FNNs, supporting GCNs as a promising route to non-local RANS closures.

authors.name: Salvatore Civiello, Davide Oberto, Antonia Larese, Gianluigi Rozza

papers.title: An Analytic Two-Dimensional Benchmark for Integrated Autocorrelation Times in Branching Monte Carlo Part I: Transport Spectra and Branching Theory
papers.summary: Predicting correlations between source generations can support uncertainty estimation and variance reduction in Monte Carlo transport. We derive a two-dimensional benchmark for planar isotropic exponential flights in a reflecting square. An image construction gives the exact collision and absorption spectra. Critical branching preserves the mean transport operator but changes mode covariances through the offspring second moment. These covariances give tally autocorrelations and integrated autocorrelation times, with a large-population, finite-window approximation for normalized source tallies. Direct Monte Carlo measurements test the predictions for absorption/rebirth and two-offspring fission. The benchmark provides a reference for assessing reduced correlation models, for correcting reported tally uncertainties, and for checking the tallies of a production code for correlation bias.

authors.name: Jilang Miao, Guillaume L. Giudicelli, William Reed Kendrick

papers.title: An Analytic Two-Dimensional Benchmark for Integrated Autocorrelation Times in Branching Monte Carlo Part II: Operator Estimation from Functional Expansion Tallies
papers.summary: Functional expansion tallies can represent transport operators for Monte Carlo correlation prediction without first constructing a fine cell transition matrix. We tally Galerkin operators directly from birth-to-absorption histories, retaining the sampled departure measure through an empirical mass matrix. Operator moments and an estimated offspring second moment give branching autocorrelations and integrated autocorrelation times without an eigendecomposition. The analytic benchmark from Part I supplies continuum and noise-free finite-model references. At the compared sizes, cosine and Legendre models have smaller IACT errors and require less operator storage than the cell model, and the branching reweighting reduces their representation error by a further factor near five while leaving the cell error unchanged. The measured runtime benefit is basis dependent. Profiling separates shared transport from the additional costs of operator assembly and prediction.

authors.name: Jilang Miao, Guillaume L. Giudicelli, William Reed Kendrick

papers.title: On the numerical representation of atmospheric Lamb waves in dynamical cores
papers.summary: Atmospheric Lamb waves are horizontally propagating acoustic waves that are supported by hydrostatic and nonhydrostatic compressible equation sets. They are classically defined in an isothermal atmosphere and generate no vertical velocity. In a dynamical core, the numerical representation of the Lamb wave is sensitive to modelling choices, such as the upper boundary condition and spatial discretisation. To evaluate the numerical Lamb wave in dynamical cores, we present a new idealised test case that contains a localised pressure perturbation to primarily excite the Lamb wave mode, in a nonrotating, isothermal atmosphere at rest. Lamb waves are identified through their phase speed and the vertical structure of their zonal velocity in three dynamical cores: Spectral Element (SE), Finite-Volume Cubed-Sphere (FV3), and Model for Prediction Across Scales (MPAS), which are available in the Community Atmosphere Model (CAM). Consistent with vertical structure equation theory, the pressure-based coordinate models with an isobaric lid (SE, FV3) generate reduced Lamb wave speeds with low model tops; we show speed reductions of around 25% for a 10 km model top and an isothermal initial temperature of 275 K. For a rigid lid upper boundary condition, such as for the height coordinate MPAS model, the Lamb wave speed is virtually independent of the model top height. Wave amplitudes differ substantially among the tested configurations, with SE producing the largest amplitudes. MPAS' time-adjusted acoustic filter strongly attenuates and broadens the Lamb wave signal, whilst the amplitude and propagation speed are sensitive to the dynamics time step in FV3. Zonal wavenumber-frequency spectra reveal how well the numerical dispersion relations of Lamb and gravity waves follow the theoretical relations, and show element-order-dependent behaviour in SE consistent with linear dispersion theory.

authors.name: Timothy C. Andrews, Nicholas C. Forcone, Nicholas H. Androski, Owen K. Hughes, Christiane Jablonowski

papers.title: Working with writing experts to enhance a physics curriculum
papers.summary: A common observation of physics faculty and professionals hiring physics graduates is that undergraduate students have deficient physics-specific writing skills, in particular difficulties with writing genres such as abstracts, reports, articles, proposals, and posters. Students are not often exposed to such authentic writing experiences as part of their curriculum, and faculty may not feel qualified to teach writing. Scholarship focused on writing transfer, defined as the ability to apply the writing skills and knowledge learned in one context in a new writing context, suggests that students need support with transfer-focused writing skills such as genre and audience awareness and that these are skills in which students can be trained. For physics students, physics faculty are best placed to do this as successful participants in their disciplines. We present an interdisciplinary effort, by faculty of physics and writing studies, of developing a writing in physics curriculum using a scaffolded approach including three courses in the second through fourth year of an undergraduate physics program. This approach uses threshold concepts from writing studies, such as genre, audience, and purpose. Students are given the methodological tools to approach writing, and the instruction includes structured peer feedback that is connected to the instructor's feedback and grading. This effort led to improvements in the written and oral communication skills of students in a broad range of genres and for various audiences, evidenced, for instance, by an increase in successful fellowship applications. The course materials developed for this effort are publicly available to the community.

authors.name: Alexander J. van der Horst, Rachel C. Riedner, Gary D. White, Carol L. Hayes, Axel W. Schmidt, Evangeline J. Downie, William J. Briscoe

papers.title: Multi-echo AxCaliberSMT: Mapping effective axon radius from restricted diffusion and radius-dependent intra-axonal T2
papers.summary: Diffusion-based axon radius r mapping preferentially detects larger axons since restricted-diffusion contrast scales with r^4, limiting sensitivity to thin axons dominating human white matter (WM). Surface relaxation provides complementary sensitivity through an intra-axonal R2 proportional to 1/r. We combined these mechanisms to broaden the dynamic range of radius estimations. Multi-echo AxCaliberSMT (ME-AxCaliberSMT) models spherical-mean diffusion-relaxation signals using cylinder-restricted diffusion and histologically calibrated surface relaxation. Simulations compared its accuracy and robustness with AxCaliberSMT and a diffusion-filtered R2 model, which infer radius solely from restricted diffusion and intra-axonal R2, respectively. Five healthy adults were scanned on Connectome 2.0 (C2; 500 mT/m), and four also on Cima.X (200 mT/m), using multiple b-values at two diffusion times, each paired with a different echo time. Diffusion and relaxation contrasts were comparable at a protocol-dependent transition radius (C2: 1.42 um; Cima.X: 1.85 um). Below this threshold, relaxation dominated, yielding effective r estimates approximately / in most WM. At SNR 40, ME-AxCaliberSMT achieved normalised bias $\pm$6%, whereas AxCaliberSMT overestimated small radii. ME-AxCaliberSMT was less sensitive to tested calibration errors than the R2 model. In vivo, ME-AxCaliberSMT bundle radii on C2 were 0.30-0.51 um (AxCaliberSMT: 1.03-1.38 um) and followed the histological pattern along the corpus callosum. ME-AxCaliberSMT estimates correlated between scanners (mean Pearson correlation 0.73), unlike AxCaliberSMT (-0.23), although Cima.X values were systematically higher. Combining diffusion and relaxation extends axon radius mapping from large to small axons. Translation to a commercial high-gradient scanner reproduced bundle-wise patterns, although absolute estimates remained protocol-dependent.

authors.name: Kwok-Shing Chan, Yohan Jun, Aneri Bhatt, Berkin Bilgic, Susie Y. Huang, Hong-Hsi Lee

papers.title: SPLAT: An Event-Specific System Response Model for Continuous-Domain List-Mode TOF PET
papers.summary: Modern position-sensitive PET detectors provide continuous estimates of photon interaction position and event-specific timing, energy, and depth-of-interaction (DOI) information. We introduce Spatial Probability Localization and Transformation (SPLAT), a continuous-domain, event-specific projection model for time-of-flight (TOF) list-mode PET. Each coincidence is represented by a three-dimensional spatial response kernel incorporated into consistent forward and adjoint operators without detector-coordinate binning. While supporting general response distributions, we develop an anisotropic Gaussian implementation whose center is determined by measured interaction positions and TOF difference, and whose full covariance follows from propagating measurement uncertainties through event geometry. The model accounts for DOI, photon non-collinearity, and energy-dependent, correlated, and depth-dependent detector responses. Using GATE Monte Carlo simulations with known annihilation positions, we compare continuous and virtually segmented representations of identical accepted coincidences. Event-localization diagnostics and point-source and brain-phantom reconstructions assess model accuracy and image formation. The Gaussian formulation also yields information-equivalent count gain, an approximate measure of relative spatial information accounting for localization uncertainty and detection efficiency. Results support the value of event-specific modeling, particularly measured DOI, while an optimized GPU implementation demonstrates computational feasibility. SPLAT provides a flexible framework for incorporating detailed detector measurements directly into PET reconstruction.

authors.name: Ronglong Fang, Andrzej Krol, Yuesheng Xu, Eric S. Harmon, Michael O. Thompson, Wei Zheng, C. Ross Schmidtlein

papers.title: Adiabatic Electronic Momentum and the Continuity Equation with Nonlocal Effective Core Potentials in an Electronic Phase-Space Hamiltonian
papers.summary: Adiabatic electronic momentum and current density provide fundamental information about electronic motion induced by nuclear motion under the Born-Oppenheimer separation. In practical electronic structure calculations, core electrons in heavy atoms are commonly replaced by effective core potentials (ECPs), whose nonlocal components introduce additional contributions to electronic momentum and the continuity equation. Here, using a phase-space electronic Hamiltonian approach, we investigate these nonlocal components on adiabatic electronic momentum and the continuity equation in small molecules with moving nuclei. We demonstrate that this approach efficiently describes adiabatic electronic momentum and the divergence of electronic current density when the nonlocal contributions to the corresponding electronic operators are properly accounted for. We find that the nonlocal correction to electronic momentum is important when the ECP-centered atoms move but is small otherwise, reflecting the spatial locality of the electronic response and ECP. We further examine the implications of moving ECPs, which account for the motion of nonlocal pseudopotentials with the nuclei to restore Galilean covariance, for adiabatic electronic transport. We show that, for nondegenerate systems with time-reversal symmetry, moving ECPs do not modify the coordinate space adiabatic evolution of time-reversal even observables through second order in nuclear velocity, although they can alter the electronic momentum operator and its feedback on nuclear dynamics.

authors.name: Bismark Ninson, Zhen Tao

papers.title: Reflective Spin Wave Filtering Limiters with Bandpass to Bandstop Bifurcation
papers.summary: Spin wave (SW) filters using thin-film yttrium iron garnet are an attractive technology for reconfigurable and software defined radio (SDR) systems in which parameters such as channel frequency or transmit power are adjusted in real time to efficiently utilize constrained spectrum resources. Operating in congested electromagnetic environments leave communication systems vulnerable to damage or disruption from strong interference and jamming. Therefore, frequency tunable filters and power limiters are needed to support SDR operation on the physical layer. Here, we report a frequency tunable bandpass filtering limiter which reflects excess above threshold power using a network of nonlinear SW resonators in a ladder filter topology. The reported devices show insertion losses as low as 3.29 dB, isolation above 14.22 dB, center frequency tuning over more than two octaves from 4.75 GHz to 21.08 GHz, fast transient response of 14.01 ns, and low transient spike leakage. A physics-informed nonlinear SW model is discussed and a method to simulate and design networks of nonlinear resonators is introduced.

authors.name: Connor Devitt, Sunil A. Bhave

papers.title: Community Odour Reports as a Forecastable Sensor of Fugitive Emissions
papers.summary: Ambient air quality monitors (AAQMs) measure exposure to emissions from waste facilities at few points; for most residents the only record is their own odour reports, used by regulators as evidence of impact but not typically as measurements of exposure. Calibrated public reports are accepted measurements in seismology, but whether community odour reports can serve as a sensor of exposure, and be forecast, is untested against independent monitors. Here we show they can, at a UK landfill, with SENTINEL, which combines the public weather forecast, run through a dispersion model, with the reports already received and no instrument at the site. Judged against the independent monitors, monthly report frequency was correlated with hydrogen sulphide (r = 0.92) and daily reports remained associated with it beyond weather; they fell fourteenfold after a change at the source while modelled transport did not; and, with no gas data as input, gave exposure in both monitored postcodes within a factor of three of that measured. SENTINEL forecast daily report counts with skill 0.64 one day and 0.50 four days ahead, exceeding damped persistence four days ahead; the one-day gain over persistence was unresolved. Community odour reports can act as a relative sensor complementing sparse monitoring; a monitor is needed for absolute scale.

authors.name: Timothy C. Pearce, David J. T. Smith, Alec Dobney, Alessia Freddo

papers.title: Universal Statistics of Random Waves in Multi-Port non-Hermitian Scattering Systems
papers.summary: We study the statistical properties of wave transport of a fixed multi-port non-Hermitian scattering system through wavefront shaping to explore all possible coherent illumination conditions. This is a departure from traditional approaches utilizing cavity shaping to create an ensemble of systems with different detailed scattering arrangements that lead to uncorrelated field configurations. Using microwave measurements in the low channel-number limit, we empirically demonstrate universal statistics in the probability density functions (PDF) of reflectivity, transmissivity, and absorptivity, Fisher information and the difference between forward propagating and time reversed transmissivity. Because the PDFs depend only on the number of input channels and the eigenvalues of Hermitian operators, we demonstrate how cavity shaping can be used to manipulate these eigenvalues, even creating Diabolic Point degeneracies, giving us direct control over the shapes and bounds of transport phenomena PDFs. We further investigate the PDFs when the excitations are finite bandwidth pulses as opposed to monochromatic waves, and determine the behavior in the limits of two channels and many channels. Our results establish a new paradigm in statistical investigations and cavity shaping applications by focusing on outcomes arising from all possible excitations, rather than creating conditions for one specific wavefront that optimally achieves a desired purpose.

authors.name: Nadav Shaibe, Jared Erb, Steven M. Anlage

papers.title: Tunable Multi-Frequency-Band Generator and Detector of AC Signals Based on a Spin Hall Device with Two Antiferromagnetic Layers
papers.summary: Antiferromagnetic (AFM) spin Hall oscillators offer an electrical route to compact terahertz sources, while AFM spin Hall diodes can be used as a promising detectors of terahertz signals, however, their attainable frequency and the redout efficiency are constrained by the dynamics of a single AFM layer. We theoretically and numerically investigate a spin Hall multilayer junction Pt/AFM/Pt/AFM/Pt comprising two canted AFM layers, driven by independent drive DC currents flowing in the outer platinum (Pt) layers. Using a model based on the coupled Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert-Slonczewski equations for four AFM sublattices and a phase-dependent two-interface spin Hall magnetoresistance model, we show that the device manifests itself as a DC current-driven oscillating spin Hall magnetoresistance. When an additional DC (AC) signal current is applied to the junction, the device generates an output AC (DC) voltage. Our model predicts current-driven, locked, co- and counter-rotational states of the net magnetization at Neel-vector frequencies in the top and bottom AFM layers, respectively. These states result in a multi-frequency response of the spin Hall magnetoresistance at the sum and difference frequencies. The counter-rotation regime additionally activates the phase-sensitive mixing contribution, producing a fourth harmonic. In contrast, the co-rotation regime provides a difference-frequency channel on the order of 100 GHz, although mutual locking prevents this output from being tuned continuously toward zero. Our estimations show that the device matched to an external load can generate output AC power of 1.2 nW at the second harmonic and 0.8 pW at the fourth harmonic, and can produce a DC voltage of about 1 mV for a 6 mA input signal current.

authors.name: Oleh Shtanko, Volodymyr Prokopenko, Oleksandr Prokopenko

papers.title: Spacer-Engineered Spectral Selectivity in Metal-Carbon Solar-Thermal Absorbers
papers.summary: Spectrally selective solar-thermal absorbers must capture sunlight while limiting emission at operating temperatures where the Planck spectrum overlaps the solar band. We connect this trade-off to a controlled optical mechanism in a metal-carbon metasurface. A radiative-limit calculation using AM1.5D illumination identifies how cutoff wavelength, infrared absorptivity and concentration together constrain equilibrium temperature, while the metasurface calculations reveal the additional role of a sharp spectral transition. We then separate the dielectric gap from the absorbing carbon layer in a gold--carbon architecture. Frequency-domain fields and material-resolved dissipation show that the spacer controls the overlap of a gap-localised mode with carbon, extending the high-absorptivity band and sharpening its infrared roll-off. A thickness sweep demonstrates that the spectrum with the strongest visible absorption need not give the highest radiative-limit equilibrium temperature. Polar-angle- and polarisation-resolved calculations demonstrate the angular robustness of the proposed plasmonic metasurface and assess the extent to which normal-incidence spectra approximate hemispherical emission. The calculated high-temperature values are benchmarks for the fixed-geometry, fixed-optical-constant model, not operating temperature predictions for the gold structure. The study establishes spacer-controlled loss partitioning as a route to shaping solar-thermal spectra and distinguishes optical selectivity from materials durability and useful heat output.

authors.name: X. Romain, A. P. Vafa, M. Florescu

papers.title: AI climate trajectories shaped by growth, power choices and decarbonization
papers.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a major source of electricity demand, yet its operational greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions remain difficult to resolve geographically. We develop a facility-level global inventory of AI-oriented data centers and extend it to 2030 using documented expansion plans and grid-policy scenarios. Under Current Policies, emissions increase from 20.4 MtCO$_2$e in 2024 to 68.7 MtCO$_2$e in 2030, with parameter-side Monte Carlo 5th--95th percentile ranges of 19.3--21.0 and 60.8--73.9 MtCO$_2$e, respectively. Only six geographies, representing less than 3% of projected capacity, avoid rising emissions. Grid decarbonization consistent with net zero by 2050 lowers projected 2030 emissions to 48.3 MtCO$_2$e, but fossil-based behind-the-meter generation erodes this benefit. Under that scenario, the U.S. behind-the-meter emissions penalty exceeds the combined AI-data-center emissions outside the United States. These findings support coordinated capacity planning, faster access to low-carbon electricity and limits on routine fossil-based behind-the-meter supply.

authors.name: Xiaoyu Xie, John Bistline, Ming Xu, Sangwon Suh

papers.title: How to Agree Without Agreeing
papers.summary: Consensus lets institutions decide without a central authority, but a record of agreement reveals neither its basis nor its credibility. We model support, standing aside and veto as responses to a proposal. A proposal can pass without active support, and the member least willing to allow passage limits what can be adopted, however many members oppose the proposal. Letting proposers moderate their demands can ease agreement while undermining the prescribed punishment. Proposal restrictions or deviation costs can preserve that threat. Across the initialisations tested, learning agents agree frequently even though many reconstructed rules allow profitable departures. In our sample of Antarctic Treaty working papers, 80% of proposals revising existing arrangements were adopted at submission, against 38% of new proposals. Consensus can keep producing agreement on what already exists while new protection waits.

authors.name: Casper van Elteren, Maria Kleshnina

papers.title: Scaling of the Radial Motion and Size of Filamentary Structures in the Scrape-Off Layer Inferred from 100 kHz Visible Imaging on 294 MAST Discharges
papers.summary: Filaments are important carriers of cross-field transport in the scrape-off layer of a tokamak. Analytic models predict that their radial velocity varies with their size. We measured the radial velocity and size of a large population of filaments on MAST, using data recorded from a 100 kHz, 48 x 256 pixel camera in the outboard midplane in the FAIR-MAST archive. Computer vision techniques were used to automate the identification of filaments and tracking of their trajectories, which yielded 86,042 filament tracks over 294 discharges in 4 campaigns. The archive does not contain spatial calibration, so we have obtained a pixel scale by regression of the plasma limb column in the image on the EFIT outboard LCFS radius, with bootstrap intervals. The scale is 2.7-5.2 millimetres per pixel. We find a median velocity of 424 m/s, and median radial width of 3.6 cm. The dependence of velocity on size is mild, with a log-log slope of +0.05 (95% interval +0.03 to +0.07) when the effects of exposure blurring are corrected for. This is because filaments are not in either velocity regime; they span the range $\hat{a}$ = 0.13-1.97 in two-region units, which straddles the maximum velocity predicted by the two-region model, but the normalized velocity $\hat{v}$ is much smaller than the scale of the model, at $\hat{v} \approx 0.06$.

authors.name: Jessie Dong, Ryan Wu

papers.title: Bringing coherent closer to compute: coherent-lite multidimensional on-chip interconnect beyond 100 terabits per second
papers.summary: The continued scaling of artificial intelligence (AI) demands optical interconnects that deliver higher bandwidth density within stringent electrical-bandwidth and energy budgets. Coherent optics offers a route beyond the per-lane bandwidth constraints of intensity-modulation direct-detection links, yet its receiver complexity and power overhead have largely confined its use to longer reaches. Here we bring coherent optics closer to compute by demonstrating a coherent-lite multidimensional on-chip interconnect that combines wavelength- and mode-division multiplexing with self-homodyne detection. The architecture co-transmits the local oscillator (LO) and parallel data channels within a single silicon waveguide, using polarization-division routing to preserve LO purity and support high-order modulation. Based on this principle, we develop an inverse-designed dual-polarization mode multiplexer that provides over 37 dB inter-polarization isolation across the C band in an $8 \times 6~\mu$m$^2$ footprint, enabling millimetre-scale on-chip multimode routing. Without power-intensive digital carrier recovery, the architecture delivers a single-wavelength line rate of 2 Tb s$^{-1}$ and scales to an aggregate line rate of 103.96 Tb s$^{-1}$ across four modes and 100 wavelengths, using formats up to 64-ary quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM). These results extend on-chip coherent interconnects into the hundred-terabit-per-second regime, offering a scalable route to bandwidth-dense optical connectivity for next-generation computing systems.

authors.name: Yongzhu Hu, Aolong Sun, Huayuan Qin, An Yan, Jialin He, Yuqin Yuan, Junhao Zhao, Chao Shen, Ziwei Li, Peng Sun, Hui Chen, Chao Li, Xu Zhang, Bowei Dong, Zhixue He, Nan Chi, Shaohua Yu, Junwen Zhang

papers.title: Femtosecond Free-Space Time-Frequency Transfer at km/s Relative Motion with Doppler Compensation
papers.summary: A global optical clock network holds great promise for a wide range of applications, including international metrology--particularly the redefinition of the ``second''--as well as navigation, geoscience, and fundamental physics. Satellite-based high-precision time-frequency dissemination is essential for realizing such a network. Despite remarkable progress in ground-based free-space simulations over high-loss channels, the Doppler effect arising from satellite motion has remained an unsolved barrier. Here we demonstrate femtosecond two-way time-frequency transfer over a 113-km free-space link under simulated Doppler shifts of up to 1.55 km/s. To overcome the Doppler barrier, we first reproduce satellite-like Doppler shifts of up to 1.55 km/s on the ground by locking a frequency comb to a broadly tunable laser. We then correct the resulting disturbances with two complementary techniques: a dual-channel sampling architecture that compensates for optical dispersion and radio frequency (RF) nonlinearity while eliminating Nyquist dead zones, and an iterative interferogram reconstruction algorithm that removes Doppler-induced distortion. After correction, residual systematic errors are within $\pm10$ fs over the full 1.55 km/s range. Using simulated medium earth orbit (MEO) and geosynchronous orbit (GSO) satellite trajectories, we achieve fractional frequency instability of $3.9\times10^{-19}$ at 4,600 s and $3.6\times10^{-19}$ at 23,600 s, respectively. This extends the operational velocity range by nearly two orders of magnitude beyond previous free-space demonstrations, removing the last major technical barrier to a global femtosecond-precision satellite-based time-frequency link.

authors.name: Jian-Yu Guan, Qi Shen, Lei Hou, Jin-Jian Han, Shen Zhang, Feng-Heng Che, Yi-Cheng Zhang, Shi Chen, Yao-Dong Hu, Zhi-Kang Qian, Yong Wang, Min Li, Shao-Mao Wang, Dan-Yang Zhu, Fa-Xi Chen, Li-Bo Li, Esamdin Ali, Ji-Gang Ren, Juan Yin, Rong Shu, Cheng-Zhi Peng, Hai-Feng Jiang, Qiang Zhang, Jian-Wei Pan

papers.title: Fourier Crosstalk and Leakage Correction for Binary-Encoded Fourier Single-Pixel Imaging
papers.summary: Digital micromirror devices enable high-speed Fourier single-pixel imaging (Fourier-SPI), but their binary modulation introduces quantization errors that degrade the reconstructed image quality. In particular, each binarized Fourier probe contains non-target Fourier components, thereby distorting the corresponding Fourier-domain measurement. This Letter presents a Fourier domain correction framework that characterizes these errors using the Fourier-domain response matrix of the decoded binary Fourier patterns. Accordingly, a response-matrix-based Fourier-SPI measurement model is established by partitioning the matrix into components associated with the sampled and unsampled frequencies, thereby decomposing the quantization error into sampled-frequency crosstalk and unsampled-frequency leakage. This model established a generalized correction framework, termed Fourier Crosstalk and Leakage Correction (FCLC), alongside two simplified methods: Fourier Sampled-Frequency Crosstalk Correction (FSCC) and Fourier DC Crosstalk Correction (FDCC). FSCC is implemented via an inversion-free Richardson-type iteration, whereas FDCC admits a closed-form solution. Numerical simulations and experiments across multiple binary encoding strategies reveal that the proposed framework improves reconstruction fidelity without modifying the binary patterns or acquisition process.

authors.name: Chongwu Shao, Yue Cao, Wei Zhang, Xiao-Peng Jin, Yinran Shen, Shijian Li, Xu-Ri Yao

papers.title: Predicting local electric field in Al$_x$Ga$_{1-x}$N p-i-n photodiodes using exciton Franz-Keldysh photocurrent spectroscopy
papers.summary: In AlGaN p-i-n photodiodes, reverse bias redshifts and broadens the sub-bandgap photocurrent responsivity through the eXciton Franz-Keldysh (XFK) effect, and this spectral line shape encodes the local electric field inside the device. Fitting the photocurrent spectra of two such photodiodes, with 5% and 40% Al, to an XFK absorption model at each bias yields the local voltage, $V_l$, a single parameter that sets the line shape and uniquely determines the electric-field profile inside the device. In both devices, $V_l$ varies linearly with the applied bias ($R^2 = 0.994$ and $0.998$) but changes far more slowly than the bias itself, revealing a strong local reduction of the electric field that points to non-uniform electrostatics. The slopes show that only 12.4% of the applied bias in the 5% Al device, and 45.8% in the 40% Al device, drops across the junction at the probed location. Extrapolated to zero bias, $V_l$ gives built-in voltages of 3.39 and 4.29 V, within 0.02 V of the 3.41 and 4.28 V obtained from technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulation, which validates the extracted local voltages at equilibrium. These results extend sub-bandgap photocurrent spectroscopy to AlGaN devices as an optical probe of local electrostatics, relevant to ultraviolet photodetectors and high-voltage electronics.

authors.name: Himel Kundu Utsha, Manjur Muntasir, Md. Mohsinur Rahman Adnan

papers.title: Numerical Integration Instabilities in Likelihood Fits: Mechanisms and Remedies
papers.summary: Numerical instabilities in the normalization of probability density functions can produce artificially lower negative log-likelihood (NLL) values than the true minimum of a likelihood fit, even when the resulting fit provides a poorer description of the data. Motivated by anomalously low NLL values found in non-converged fits associated with a recent CMS search for fully charmed tetraquark candidates, we use a pseudo-dataset generated from a likelihood model based on that analysis to investigate how numerical integration can yield unreliable normalization results, how these errors affect likelihood minimization, and how they can be addressed. We find that, even at fixed integration tolerance, the stopping decision of a numerical integrator can change with the fit parameters, introducing discontinuities in the normalization integrals that propagate to the likelihood surface. Such discontinuities can trap the minimizer at a numerical step and yield an artificially lower NLL. Tightening the integration tolerance mitigates these numerical discontinuities, while adaptive integration methods, such as Gauss--Kronrod quadrature, can also improve the numerical stability. A more severe failure occurs when the integration grid cannot adequately resolve a sharply localized contribution. In this case, the integrator may satisfy its estimated-error criterion despite substantially underestimating the normalization, allowing the minimizer to enter a region with an artificially low NLL. Tightening integration tolerances or using alternative adaptive integration methods does not necessarily resolve sharply localized contributions. We demonstrate that a suitable variable transformation can improve their numerical resolution, yielding more accurate normalization integrals and restoring fit convergence.

authors.name: Manqi Zhu, Gerry Bauer, Kai Yi, Xining Wang

papers.title: Parity nonconservation in hyperfine transitions of hydrogen-like muonic atoms
papers.summary: We investigate parity nonconservation (PNC) in the $2s_{1/2}(F=0)\leftrightarrow 2s_{1/2}(F=1)$ hyperfine transition of hydrogenlike muonic $^{13}\mathrm{C}^{5+}$ and $^{15}\mathrm{N}^{6+}$. Finite-nuclear-size effects and the Uehling potential are incorporated directly into the Dirac equation, whereas the leading kinematic-recoil and Fermi--Breit hyperfine corrections to the energy levels are treated to first order in perturbation theory. The spin-independent PNC amplitude is evaluated using hyperfine-resolved energy denominators and is proportional to the weak charge $Q_W$. The spin-dependent amplitude is proportional to $\kappa=\kappa_a+\kappa_Z$, where $\kappa_a$ and $\kappa_Z$ denote the nuclear-anapole and direct neutral-current couplings, respectively. For absorption we obtain the PNC degree $\mathcal P_{\rm abs}(^{13}\mathrm{C})=-5.9\times10^{-8}Q_W +1.3\times10^{-5}\kappa$ and $\mathcal P_{\rm abs}(^{15}\mathrm{N})=-8.8\times10^{-9}Q_W -8.1\times10^{-6}\kappa$. Nuclear-structure calculations indicate that $^{13}\mathrm{C}$ has enhanced relative sensitivity to direct $Z^0$-boson exchange, whereas the spin-dependent interaction in $^{15}\mathrm{N}$ is expected to be dominated by the nuclear-anapole contribution. In an idealized cavity-polarimetry model, a column density of order $10^{15}~\mathrm{cm^{-2}}$ is required; however, the production of metastable hydrogenlike muonic ions remains the principal experimental challenge.

authors.name: D. V. Chubukov, M. I. Kuznetsov, I. A. Aleksandrov, A. V. Malyshev

papers.title: An implicit high-order flux reconstruction method with logarithmic variables for hypersonic flows in thermochemical nonequilibrium
papers.summary: Simulating hypersonic flows in thermochemical nonequilibrium requires solving the Navier-Stokes equations for reacting, possibly ionised mixtures. Compact high-order computations of viscous two-temperature air flows on unstructured grids have not gone beyond P = 2. We present an implicit Flux Reconstruction (FR) method for such flows, built on three ingredients. First, the solver stores and updates the logarithms of the partial densities and temperatures, making every state admissible without a positivity limiter and, for ionised mixtures, imposing charge neutrality consistently with the implicit update. Second, shocks are captured by subcell order blending, extended to steady implicit computations on curved Gauss-Legendre meshes, with second-order subcell blending in subsonic regions and an automatic freeze of the blending near convergence. Third, a pseudo-transient Newton method with a physicality-limited update and automatic CFL control reaches steady state from the free stream with the same settings at every order. The design order is verified up to sixth order on a manufactured solution for five-species air with finite-rate chemistry and vibrational relaxation. Steady viscous solutions up to sixth order are obtained for five- and eleven-species air on the High Enthalpy shock tunnel G\"ottingen (HEG) cylinder and for eleven-species air on the RAM-C II vehicle. To our knowledge, this work gives the first design-order verification of a high-order method with finite-rate air chemistry and vibrational relaxation, and the first high-order finite-element-type computations of viscous eleven-species, two-temperature air. On the HEG cylinder, the stagnation-point heat flux is within 2% of finite-volume references and within 6% of the measurements, with a comparable number of degrees of freedom to second-order finite-volume computations but on meshes with 20 to 40 times fewer elements.

authors.name: Rayan Dhib, Vatsalya Sharma, Vincent F. Giangaspero, Firas Ben Ameur, Jos\'e Miguel Luzia Murteira, Stefaan Poedts, Andrea Lani

papers.title: Food co-purchasing networks encode geographic disparities in cardiometabolic health
papers.summary: Unhealthy diets are a major driver of cardiometabolic disease, yet the geospatial structure of dietary behavior and its links to population health remain poorly understood. While large-scale retail transaction data offer a unique view of population dietary behavior, conventional approaches reduce purchases to isolated items, not accounting for how foods are actually combined. Here, we analyze 51 million grocery receipts across 95 Danish municipalities using a statistically validated bipartite network framework to isolate co-purchases that product popularity alone cannot explain. We find that, although municipalities buy largely the same products, their co-purchasing networks reorganize along a continuous urban-to-peripheral gradient in how those products are combined. The network backbone can be resolved into modular dietary communities whose local cohesion allows us to predict cardiometabolic prescriptions, explaining a quarter to a half of the variance left after sociodemographic adjustment, beyond what product prevalence alone accounts for. Ultra-processed foods (UPFs) show no spatial gradient in prevalence and are located at the network periphery, where they share baskets with fresh foods but rarely form the combinations that hold the network together. Taken together, our findings show that geographic dietary differences are encoded not only in what people purchase, but in how foods are systematically combined within shopping baskets, offering a scalable network approach for population nutritional epidemiology.

authors.name: Antonio Desiderio, Leonardo Rodovero, Sune Lehmann

papers.title: Hydration-induced local diffusivity heterogeneity modulates aqueous $H_2+OH$ reaction kinetics
papers.summary: At room temperature, a Kramers reaction rate calculated with homogeneous solvent friction exceeds the measured rate of the aqueous reaction $H_2 + OH -> H + H_2O$ by about an order of magnitude. We show that spatially correlated hydration-induced diffusivity fluctuations increase effective friction and suppress the predicted escape rate. Estimates based on hydration-shell properties bring the theoretical rate closer to experiment. The suppression weakens with increasing temperature, linking local solvent heterogeneity to activated aqueous reaction kinetics.

authors.name: Ming-Gen Li, Shi-Yuan Zhang, Alessio Zaccone

papers.title: Characterization of an Optical Time Projection Chamber prototype with Ar:CF$_4$ at atmospheric pressure
papers.summary: We report on the characterization of an Optical Time Projection Chamber (OTPC) developed as a prototype for neutron-induced reaction studies at Soreq Applied Research Accelerator Facility (SARAF). The prototype was operated with Ar:CF$_4$ (95:5) at 1 bar, using parallel mesh electrodes for charge multiplication and electroluminescence, and alpha particles from a $^{241}$Am source. Both induced charge and light signals were recorded. A systematic characterization was carried out to study charge multiplication and scintillation yield. We present the results of these measurements in single-gap amplification configurations, along with two-gap operation and a demonstration of synchronized optical readout.

authors.name: R. Felkai, M. Borysova, L. Moleri, J. Pienaar, D. Vartsky, A. Breskin, I. Mor, L. Weissman, S. Bressler

papers.title: A full-wave ICRH solver with full kinetic accuracy using only first order differential equations
papers.summary: Accurate full-wave computation of ion cyclotron resonance heating (ICRH) typically requires solving the computationally demanding integro-differential dielectric tensor of the hot plasma. Based on the method in [Phys. Plasmas 32, 082110 (2025)], we develop BO-FW1D, a 1D frequency domain finite difference full-wave solver which generates full kinetic, accurate and efficient simulations utilizing a fluid plasma model. To accurately convert the conductivity tensor in phase space into a first-order differential equation, we introduce a mathematically rigorous framework using pseudodifferential operator theory based on Kohn-Nirenberg ordering. Benchmarks with an all-orders 1D full-wave solver show high consistency in critical kinetic effects and electric-field distributions, while substantial computational acceleration is achieved. This work could lay the foundation for developing full-wave solvers that combine full kinetic accuracy with high computational efficiency.

authors.name: Liuheng Wu, Ziyu Wang, Huasheng Xie, Chang Liu

papers.title: Self-similarity of axisymmetric Marangoni flows on a deep viscous subphase
papers.summary: Local gradients of surface tension caused by inhomogeneous distributions of surfactant molecules are known to generate Marangoni flows, the mechanics of which have important consequences in various areas of science and engineering. In this paper, we investigate the deposition of insoluble surfactants on the surface of a deep, viscous subphase, which propagate axisymmetrically without diffusing. We study these flows from the perspective of self-similarity, i.e., seeking solutions which show universal features on appropriate length and time scales. We first present a closed form, self-similar solution of the first kind for the axisymmetric spreading of surfactants, which is globally valid at long times. We then numerically study `filling' flows of surfactant, where the surfactant distribution is locally depleted such that inward flows are generated to `fill' the surfactant-free area. These flows have the special feature of forming cusp-like structure in finite time, which have been studied extensively in the literature of self-similarity of the second kind. We show that these flows admit a countably infinite number of stable similarity solutions based on the local behavior of the initial surfactant concentration profile. We remark on a few unique features of these results in contrast to filling flows in other physical limits.

authors.name: Sacha J. -B. Escudier, Fernando Temprano-Coleto, Howard A. Stone

papers.title: Ship-as-a-buoy for Phase-resolved Reconstruction of Surface Waves
papers.summary: We develop a data assimilation framework to address the ``ship-as-a-buoy'' problem, i.e., estimation of the wave field from time series of ship motion. Unlike previous algorithms which only provide information of wave spectrum, our approach reconstructs the instantaneous phase-resolved wave field. The full framework includes two steps: the first step to generate an initial (rough) estimation of the wave field using the response-amplitude-operators (RAOs), and the second step to refine the reconstruction using an ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF) to incorporate the measured motion time series. Together with EnKF in the second step, we model the coupled wave-ship dynamics by a high-order spectral (HOS) method for waves and a Cummins equation for ship motion (although higher-fidelity ship model can be applied). We conduct extensive tests of our method for the case with one ship, and the naturally extended cases with multiple ships or with uncertain parameters in the ship motion model. For all test cases we demonstrate favorable reconstruction of the wave field, which in general further improves with the number of ships available and with uncertain parameters properly estimated. We also provide insights on the successful reconstruction in terms of ensemble correlations between the motion time series and features of the wave field.

authors.name: Yifan Du, Guangyao Wang, Yulin Pan

papers.title: A quantitative measure of predictability for surface gravity waves
papers.summary: We introduce a Bayesian inference framework to characterize the predictability of a one dimensional ocean surface wave field given surface elevation measurements from a sensor. Unlike the classical theories that only sketch the boundary of a predictable zone based on group velocity, we use the Bayesian posterior uncertainty of surface elevation to quantify the local predictability at every spatiotemporal location. Our approach first constructs a prior distribution to encode existing knowledge of the wave field such as the spectrum and propagation direction. By conditioning on the (possibly noisy) measurement data, we infer the posterior distribution of the wave field, from which a spatiotemporal uncertainty map is extracted. This map agrees well with the group-velocity-based classical predictable zone theory when the frequency spectrum has bounded support. Meanwhile, it also demonstrates predictability even for a spectrum with unbounded frequency support where the classical predictable zone degenerates. A refined analysis of posterior uncertainty using observability Gramian matrix reveals a `data-informed' part and an `un-informed' part of the wave field, with the latter being fundamentally un-predictable. Furthermore, nonlinear effects can be naturally introduced into the Bayesian framework by incorporating the nonlinear ocean surface wave equations. This is the first time that nonlinearity is rigorously treated in the predictable zone problem. We perform numerical tests using both bounded, piecewise constant spectrum and unbounded JONSWAP spectrum.
