The numerical results confirm the proposed advantages of our method for linear waves and reveal how wave steepness affects the predictability of nonlinear waves. Nonlinear modal interactions redistribute uncertainty between the inside and the outside of the predictable zone with an amount proportional to the wave steepness.

authors.name: Yifan Du, Kevin Maki, Jing Sun, Yulin Pan

papers.title: Latent Molecular Rollout Towards Causal World Models: Direction is Learnable, Amplitude Control is Readout-Dependent
papers.summary: A molecular world model should predict how structural changes alter physical properties, not merely assign labels to static molecules. We build a latent molecular rollout system on an 8B Qwen3 backbone, trained on 9,202 aqueous experimental pKa pairs from iBonD, and assess its progress toward causal control by auditing three often-conflated capabilities: predictive fidelity through the intended molecular pathway, directional learnability versus amplitude calibration of target-conditioned displacements, and transfer of latent control to decoded structures. After removing textual shortcuts, continuous latent inference achieves a test MAE of 2.087, significantly outperforming direct molecular feature readout (MAE difference -0.276, 95% CI [-0.352, -0.203], p<0.001). A target-conditioned policy reliably learns displacement directions, with a median cosine of 0.577 and 62.8% of 43 held-out pairs exceeding the 0.3 threshold. Amplitude conclusions are strictly readout-dependent. A frozen linear readout yields near-zero amplitude correlation (-0.020), while a nonlinear gradient-based readout recovers relative amplitude ordering (correlation 0.585, sign accuracy 0.744-0.767) with compressed absolute scale. At the decoded structure level, neither input-slot editing nor direct final-state injection produces meaningful changes across 80 test sources, bounding the tested control surfaces rather than indicating a universal decoder bottleneck. Generation fine-tuning shows relative improvement under internal oracle evaluation but does not surpass a simple constant baseline in single-sample settings. These results delineate the capability frontier of fixed-scale latent molecular interfaces: directional control is robustly achievable, but calibrated amplitude control and decoded structural transfer remain open challenges on the path to causal molecular world models.

authors.name: Rui Wang

papers.title: A Compact Single-Flange Low-Energy Inverse Photoemission Spectrometer with Elliptical-Mirror Photon Collection
papers.summary: Low-energy inverse photoemission spectroscopy (LEIPS) is limited by weak photon emission, so photon collection optics largely determine its sensitivity. We compare four photon-collection configurations, each addressing a limitation of its predecessor: a detector beside the sample without collection optics (no-mirror), an off-axis parabolic (OAP) mirror delivering a collimated beam to a head-on photomultiplier tube (PMT), external optics coupling the OAP output to a side-on PMT with about twice the quantum efficiency (OAP-external), and an in-vacuum elliptical mirror focusing the emitted light onto the detector (elliptical). Ray-tracing shows that the elliptical mirror delivers 91.9% of the emitted photons to the detector, compared with 63.3% for the OAP mirror and 3.06% without a mirror, while a plane mirror folding the light path by about 90$^\circ$ allows the electron gun, collection optics and detector to fit on a single 8-inch flange. For C$_{60}$ films, the elliptical configuration gives the highest lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) intensity of the four, 271 counts per second per $\mu$A of sample current, 1.74 and 3.23 times those of the OAP and OAP-external configurations and about 45 times that of the no-mirror configuration. The gain over the OAP configuration is comparable to the 1.45-fold increase predicted by ray-tracing, but the filter and detector also differed, so the geometric contribution could not be isolated. The OAP-external configuration gave only 0.54 times the OAP signal despite its higher quantum efficiency. High sensitivity therefore requires both a large collection solid angle and a short optical path kept inside the vacuum.

authors.name: Jong-Am Hong, Min-Jae Maeng, Kyu-Myung Lee, Seunggu Lee, In-Sung Park, Yongsup Park

papers.title: Simulations of turbulent heat and particle transport in stellarator plasmas
papers.summary: Achieving sustained energy production in magnetic confinement fusion reactors requires a deep understanding of turbulent transport of heat and particles. This thesis investigates turbulent transport with a particular emphasis on stellarators, using simulations with the $\delta f$ gyrokinetic code stella for the W7-X, LHD, TJ-II and NCSX stellarators, the ASDEX Upgrade (AUG) tokamak and the Cyclone Base Case (CBC). It addresses two questions: how do density gradients affect turbulent heat transport, and can turbulence help retain particles in the plasma core? In the first part, an inter-machine study shows a strong reduction of the ion heat flux in NCSX and W7-X with increasing density gradients, attributed to the stabilization of ion-temperature-gradient-driven modes without significantly destabilizing trapped-electron modes or universal instabilities. This beneficial effect is absent in tokamaks, where the heat flux increases with the density gradient, highlighting the role of magnetic geometry. The ion heat flux in stellarators does not follow the growth rate of the fastest-growing linear mode, underscoring the importance of nonlinear effects. Trapped-electron modes dominate in CBC, AUG, TJ-II, LHD and NCSX, while passing-particle-driven universal instabilities contribute significantly in W7-X. The second part addresses the long-standing discrepancy between the strongly hollow density profiles predicted by neoclassical theory in large stellarators and the flat or weakly peaked profiles measured in W7-X. Nonlinear simulations and a particle balance analysis show that turbulence provides a robust inward particle flux, driven by finite ion and electron temperature gradients, that can account for the observed profiles: the sign of the turbulent particle flux matches the sign of the discrepancy between the experimental and neoclassical fluxes across the entire plasma radius of W7-X.

authors.name: Hanne Thienpondt

papers.title: Affordable Analytic Gradients for G0W0-BSE Excited States for Multiple GW Variants via Back-Propagation
papers.summary: We derive, implement and validate analytic nuclear gradients for three variants of $GW$ self-energies---the contour-deformation (CD), the analytic continuation (AC), and the contour deformation with $W$-analytic-continuation (CD-WAC)---and for the Bethe--Salpeter equation (BSE) built on top of them. All gradients are expressed as contractions of a set of covectors connected to derivatives of primitive quantities in SCF calculations. The derivation of these covectors is a back-propagation procedure through the $GW$ and BSE equations. Central finite differences confirm the correctness of all implemented gradients. With the AC-$GW$-BSE gradient we optimize the excited-state geometries of carbon monoxide, a donor-acceptor dye labelled as DA1, and DMABN, a typical model system for twisted intramolecular charge-transfer phenomena (TICT), and have obtained results that successfully reproduce observations from experiments or high-level calculations. We also performed trajectory surface hopping (TSH) simulations of nonadiabatic molecular dynamics (NAMD) of DMABN using the SHARC NAMD package, showing the capacity of our method to simulate NAMD problems. We performed timing and memory scaling tests, demonstrating that the gradient calculations of both $GW$ and BSE scale asymptotically as $N^4$ for timing and $N^3$ for memory. All source codes used in the present work, including the REST program package and the modified SHARC NAMD package that supports REST as the quantum chemistry backend, are available on Gitee https://gitee.com/restgroup/rest and https://gitee.com/qirui-gao-2025/sharc

authors.name: Qirui Gao, Igor Ying Zhang, Xin Xu

papers.title: Extracting Damping Ratio and Shear Wave Velocity through Joint Inversion of Rayleigh Wave Attenuation and Phase Velocity Data
papers.summary: Methods for reliable in-situ estimation of small-strain damping ratio remain far less developed than those for in-situ shear wave velocity (Vs) measurements. For surface wave-based approaches, challenges with extracting damping ratios are caused by both difficulties associated with developing attenuation coefficients from recorded wavefields and complexities involved when interpreting their multimodal irregularities during inversion. This study presents a joint inversion framework for extracting shear damping ratio (Ds0) and Vs profiles from Rayleigh-wave attenuation and phase velocity data using a viscoelastic predominant-mode approach. Unlike conventional inversion, the proposed formulation identifies the mode contributing most strongly to the measured wavefield, allowing multimodal attenuation and dispersion data to be incorporated without explicit modal indexing. This approach has significant benefits for inverting attenuation data, whose modal behavior is much more irregular than phase velocity. A coupled inversion strategy is adopted to jointly estimate the Vs and Ds0 while addressing their different sensitivities to phase velocity and attenuation. The predominant-mode attenuation concept is first validated against two synthetic ground models of increasing complexity. The synthetic inversion results demonstrate the framework's ability to recover the Ds0 and Vs profiles and capture modal transitions associated with a low-velocity layer. The framework is then applied to active-source field data from Mirandola, Italy, where the fundamental mode dominates, and Bird's Landing, California, where a soft peat layer produces significant higher-modes. At both sites, the inverted Vs profiles agreed well with independent site characterization data, while the damping estimates exhibit physically plausible trends and provide site-specific information that complements empirical estimates.

authors.name: Mrinal Bhaumik, Brady Cox

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Influences of Magnetic Field Inputs on Simulating the 2017 September 10 Solar Energetic Particle Event
papers.summary: Physics-based solar energetic particle (SEP) models simulate the ambient solar wind, coronal mass ejections (CMEs), and SEPs using photospheric magnetic field maps as the inner boundary condition. In this study, we select the 2017 September 10 SEP event, which produced the first ground level enhancement observed on the surfaces of both Earth and Mars, to examine how these inputs influence the modeled results. We use the SOlar wind with FIeld lines and Energetic particles (SOFIE) model suite, driven independently by the GONG and ADAPT-GONG magnetic field maps, to simulate the solar wind, CME, and SEPs from the low corona to beyond Mars' orbit. The two maps yield different open flux regions and hence different solar wind conditions, both globally comparable to in situ observations at Earth, STA, and Mars, with the GONG-driven results performing slightly better. We find that in the ADAPT-GONG-driven run, a more energetic CME flux rope propagates into a slower, wider stream, producing broader CME expansion and a more extended shock, which reaches both planets within ~4 hours of the observed arrival, while the GONG-driven run misses both arrivals. Both simulations reproduce the observed SEP fluxes at Earth within a factor of ~3, while the ADAPT-GONG-driven results compare better with observations at Mars, which connects magnetically to the shock flank. Therefore, for this event, the relative performance of the two simulations depends on the observer and observable, with SEP fluxes shaped by CME propagation through the ambient solar wind and by magnetic connectivity to the evolving shock.

authors.name: Weihao Liu, Nishtha Sachdeva, Lulu Zhao, Igor V. Sokolov, Hongfan Chen, Christina O. Lee, Patrick A. Dunn, Alessandro Bruno, David Lario, Kathryn Whitman, Xianyu Liu, G\'abor T\'oth, Tamas I. Gombosi, Meng Jin, Robert F. Wimmer-Schweingruber, Robin Ramstad, Jasper S. Halekas, Claudio Corti, Yoshifumi Futaana, Davin E. Larson, Donald M. Hassler, Bent Ehresmann, Shannon Curry

papers.title: Is Gravity a Real Force or Merely a Geometrical Effect?
papers.summary: Whether gravitation should be regarded as a fundamental force or as a manifestation of spacetime geometry remains an interesting conceptual question in physics. In Newtonian mechanics, gravitation is described as a force acting between massive objects, whereas General Relativity describes gravitational phenomena in terms of spacetime curvature, with freely falling bodies following geodesics. With this fundamental difference, it is legitimate to ask whether gravity is a real force or not, and it is very common to receive from experts a somewhat condescending answer such as "Drop a rock on your foot and you will feel that the force is real". This paper does not attempt to determine whether gravity is fundamentally a force or a geometrical phenomenon. Rather, it questions whether commonly invoked everyday experiences provide valid grounds for deciding between these interpretations.

authors.name: Val G. Rousseau

papers.title: Formulation of Brownian chain molecular dynamics and the path-resolved quasi-density operator
papers.summary: Brownian chain molecular dynamics (BCMD) [M. Shiga, J. Comput. Chem. 43, 1864 (2022)] was introduced as a practical path-integral-based approach to approximate quantum vibrational dynamics in molecular and condensed-phase systems. Its equations of motion combine Newtonian dynamics of the centroid variables with overdamped Brownian dynamics of the non-centroid path variables. Here, we introduce a path-resolved quasi-density-operator (path-QDO) representation by extending the QDO construction underlying centroid molecular dynamics to the full discretized imaginary-time path. For two position-diagonal observables, this representation gives an exact expression for the Kubo-transformed correlation function in the fine-discretization limit, without requiring either observable to be linear. BCMD can be viewed as a phenomenological, time-homogeneous Markov approximation to the exact reduced propagation in these path variables, although its generator is not derived from the path-QDO formulation. We also formulate and validate a multiple-time-step algorithm that allows pseudo-Hamiltonian errors in the deterministic propagation to be controlled by separating the Brownian refresh interval from the inner integration time step. We test the path-QDO representation on one-dimensional models and present BCMD infrared spectra of q-TIP4P/F ice, ambient water, and hot water, comparing them with published results from other approximate quantum-dynamics methods.

authors.name: Motoyuki Shiga

papers.title: A Five-Dimensional Geometric Formulation of Geophysical Fluid Dynamics
papers.summary: We apply a geometric formulation of Newtonian dynamics to inviscid compressible geophysical flow, with gravity and the effects of rotating or moving coordinates incorporated in the metric tensor. This construction relies on the introduction of an auxiliary fifth coordinate, which allows mass and momentum transport, internal energy, and pressure work to be combined into a single mass--momentum tensor. The covariant divergence of this tensor leads to the continuity equation for mass density, the three momentum equations, and the thermodynamic equation, with the system closed by an equation of state. A time-independent metric also yields conservation of total energy. We recover familiar forms of the equations and illustrate the construction in rotating spherical and terrain-following coordinates. The thin-shell and spherical-geopotential approximations, with constant effective gravity, simplify the metric while retaining vertical gravity and the traditional Coriolis terms. Emphasis is placed on the connection between the geometric structure of the formulation and the equations commonly used in atmospheric dynamics.

authors.name: St\'ephane Gaudreault, Seth Taylor, Arad Nasiri, Sanjeev S. Seahra, Raymond J. Spiteri

papers.title: A generic route to chaos in self-excited plasma oscillations
papers.summary: We propose a generic autonomous route to chaos in self-excited plasma oscillations through nonlinear feedback from a finite-rate charging variable. Near the threshold of an oscillatory ion-acoustic instability, a multiple-scale reduction yields a Stuart-Landau amplitude equation, represented by a van der Pol-type modal surrogate and coupled to debris-charge evolution in a prototype case of plasma-debris interaction scenario. For a debris-induced ion-ion counter-streaming instability, charge-dependent forcing and frequency modulation, finite charging relaxation, phase-lagged modal response, mixed nonlinear feedback, and saturation form a closed dynamical system without an externally imposed periodic driver. Numerical bifurcation and Lyapunov analyses reveal multistability and a bounded chaotic branch reached through period doubling bifurcation and band formation. We test the proposed mechanism using a one-dimensional open-boundary \emph{hybrid} particle-in-cell-Monte Carlo collision simulation incorporating particle collection, photoemission, secondary-electron emission, and surface regulation. Weak-form sparse regression identifies finite intervals whose projected dynamics reproduce the sign structure of the reduced model, while independent $0$-$1$ chaos test, nonlinear predicatbility, surrogate-data, and Lyapunov diagnostics provide localized evidence of deterministic chaotic organization in the subsonic case. The combined results establish a proof-of-principle route by which a self-excited plasma mode can become chaotic through internally generated charging feedback.

authors.name: Bikramjit Joardar, Kalpana Bora, Asheesh Gupta, Madhurjya P. Bora

papers.title: Equivalent-circuit analysis of the transverse resonant beam coupling impedance due to ceramic-chamber RF shields in the J-PARC Main Ring spill-feedback quadrupoles
papers.summary: Ceramic vacuum chambers in fast-ramping or fast-response magnets are equipped with RF shields of conducting strips closed through lumped capacitors, which form a resonant circuit coupled to the transverse dipole moment of the beam. We evaluate the transverse beam coupling impedance due to the RF shields of the ceramic chambers in the spill-feedback quadrupole magnets of the J-PARC Main Ring. The RF shield is modelled by a magneto-quasi-static partial element equivalent circuit, and the laminated yoke of the magnet by a two-dimensional field solution with a complex permeability. The analysis shows a low-$Q$ resonant coupling impedance. The yoke lowers the resonance frequency and raises the shunt impedance per quality factor, and its effect cannot be neglected. The quality factor is determined mainly by the losses in the capacitors and in the laminations. The predicted peak impedance of the three chambers exceeds the resistive-wall impedance of the whole ring. The model can be applied to other machines and to the design of future rapid-cycling synchrotrons.

authors.name: Masahito Tomizawa

papers.title: The Akhmediev breather for the Dysthe equation and the unstable manifold of the Stokes wave
papers.summary: In this article we define and compute the breather of the Dysthe equation for deep water waves, the analogue of the Akhmediev breather of the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation (NLS). When a single pair of modes is unstable, the unstable manifold of the Stokes wave consists of the Stokes wave and the translates and time shifts of a single solution, the breather. The construction uses only gauge and translation invariance, not integrability or a Hamiltonian structure. We use the parameterisation method to find the breather as a power series whose coefficients follow recursively from linear equations. This is not an asymptotic expansion: the series is the Taylor series of the breather itself. For deep water waves we map the envelope amplification over steepness and group length and give a simple formula, based on the linear stability analysis, that summarises it to within a few per cent. Our results agree well with Euler simulations: the edge of the instability band of the Dysthe equation lies much closer to the onset of growth than that of the NLS, and, away from the onset and below breaking, the crest and height amplifications lie less than 5% below the Euler ones.

authors.name: David Andrade

papers.title: Optimisation of gas mixture for charge and light readout with Micromegas detectors
papers.summary: Optical readout of Micromegas detectors is a promising technique for neutron and charged-particle imaging, offering high spatial resolution while reducing the complexity of electronic readout. Within the framework of the development of optical-readout Micromegas detectors, different noble-gas-based mixtures have been investigated to optimize charge amplification and scintillation yield. Argon-, neon-, and helium-based mixtures with various quenchers were characterized using X-ray irradiation. The detector gain, energy resolution, and optical light intensity were measured simultaneously over a wide range of amplification fields. Unprecedented energy resolutions were achieved over a large detection area (several cm$^2$) with He/\CF and Ne/\CF (90/10) mixtures, reaching 10.5\% and 13.3\% (FWHM), respectively, with the He-based mixture delivering particularly remarkable performance. Simultaneous charge and optical measurements further reveal that high charge gain does not necessarily translate into a strong optical response: while He- and Ne-based mixtures achieve effective charge gains of the order of 10$^5$, Ar/\CF mixtures produce the strongest detected light signals. Among the investigated mixtures, the ternary Ar/\CF/Isobutane (95/3/2) mixture stands out as particularly promising, combining high effective charge gain, a comparatively strong optical response, and more stable detector operation.

authors.name: E. Fasoula F. Benedetti, A. Bonenfant, E. Casalotti, E. Chronopoulou, E. Ferrer-Ribas, A. Giganon, Y. Giomataris, B. Moreno, T. Papaevangelou, E. C. Pollacco

papers.title: Quantum Startup, Recoil Statistics and Collective Gain in Free-Electron Lasers
papers.summary: We examine the conditions under which quantum signatures can be distinguished from classical dynamics and statistical fluctuations in a free-electron laser. Starting from minimal coupling and the Bambini--Renieri frame, we derive the momentum-photon exchange Hamiltonian and its Raman-Nath ladder. An interaction-picture expansion retains detuning exactly and organizes recoil corrections through the mismatch between neighboring orders. Its validity depends on the accumulated recoil phase over the populated ladder, rather than on elementary recoil alone. Numerical checks and Gaussian entrance packets illustrate the effects of preparation and resonance averaging. We distinguish number-state exchange amplitudes from predictions for a coherent optical seed, and joint electron-field coherence from reduced radiation coherence. The Wigner representation connects finite recoil translations with classical transport and identifies the information required for bunching. A cavity channel then provides the basis for comparison with the recoil-resolved oscillator proposed by Kling and Giese, including the optical-undulator preparation, stimulated back-action and narrow resonance acceptance. Space charge, spontaneous diffusion and FEL-induced energy spread are compared with recoil and high-gain bandwidth scales. The coherent undulator pump is essential to exclude artificial zero-recoil antibunching from a number-state preparation. Startup and excess photon variance alone do not establish a quantum signature: the specified observable must remain distinguishable from a classical stochastic baseline under compatible preparation, propagation and detection conditions.

authors.name: G. Dattoli, A. Curcio, E. Di Palma

papers.title: Magnetic control of hydrodynamic spin coupling between rotors: Ferrohydrodynamic effects in the two-rotor problem
papers.summary: The hydrodynamic spin coupling between two rotors ("fluid gears") is investigated numerically for a magnetic fluid in non-uniform magnetic fields. An active cylinder drives a torque-free passive one inside a circular corral, with one rotor heated. The model combines magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) and ferrohydrodynamics (FHD), with the full Kelvin force and temperature-dependent Langevin magnetisation. For the oil-based ferrofluid EFH1 the Lorentz force is negligible, and the Kelvin force drives thermomagnetic convection from the heated rotor. Steady torque-free states are computed with Taylor-Hood finite elements, the gear ratio $\Gamma$ being an additional unknown. Without a field the results agree within 1-8% with published planar simulations up to $\mathrm{Re}\approx 50$. About 17,000 steady states cover 34 arrangements of wires, NdFeB rods and magnet cores, gaps $G=0.1$-$0.7$, $\mathrm{Re}=10$-$40$ and heating of 5-20 K. Because the coupling is weak, fields of 1-2 mT change $\Gamma$ by an amount comparable to $\Gamma$ itself. At 2 mT it is reversed, strengthened or weakened in nine cases out of ten. The outcome is set by the source position: at the experimental gap and $\mathrm{Re}=20$ a source below the corral or behind the active rotor strengthens the gear-like counter-rotation up to 2.7-fold, and a source above the corral reverses it into belt-like corotation. Several sources do not act additively, and a magnet core inside the active rotor raises $|\Gamma|$ at small gaps to seven times the largest hydrodynamic value. At fixed geometry and Reynolds number, field strength and heating act approximately through a single thermomagnetic source parameter.

authors.name: Efstratios E. Tzirtzilakis (University of the Peloponnese, Patras, Greece)

papers.title: Darcy plume oscillations at low injection velocities
papers.summary: We numerically investigate miscible buoyancy-driven Darcy plumes at low injection velocities. Below a critical injection velocity, the steady plume becomes unstable and develops periodic oscillations. Approaching the critical velocity, the oscillation amplitude vanishes while the frequency remains finite at the critical point, consistent with a supercritical Hopf bifurcation, whereas at lower injection velocities increasingly complex dynamics emerge. Unsteadiness also strongly enhances lateral mixing, increasing the mixing-layer thickness by a factor of approximately 2-3 compared with a steady plume. These findings reveal a previously unexplored dynamical regime of Darcy plumes with important consequences for subsurface transport and leakage.

authors.name: Xiaoning Di, Graham Patrick Benham

papers.title: GPROF V08: Improving Satellite Precipitation Estimates Across a Heterogeneous Constellation of Passive-Microwave Sensors
papers.summary: Precipitation estimates from the passive microwave observations (PMW) of the Global Precipitation Measurements (GPM) mission serve a wide range of scientific, societal, and economic applications. The Goddard Profiling Algorithm (GPROF) is the operational retrieval used to produce the precipitation estimates for all GPM PMW sensors. This study presents the implementation GPROF V08 -- the most recent version of GPROF and a major update aimed at improving the accuracy of precipitation estimates from the GPM constellation. GPROF V08 replaces the conventional Bayesian scheme used by earlier GPROF versions by a convolutional neural network (CNN). The first part of this two-part study described a novel ML framework for generating synthetic observations required for training CNN retrievals for all GPM sensors. This second part describes the final, operational implementation, which adds a second finetuning stage to the training.Retrievals from the new GPROF V08 algorithm for all principal GPM sensors are validated against reference precipitation estimates from various sources. Our results show that, while the magnitude of improvements vary by sensor and surface type, they are robust across sensors and metrics and can be as high as 40 \% for the linear correlation coefficient for precipitation estimates from SSMIS and ATMS over ocean compared to combined radar and radiometer retrievals from GPM. While some challenges remain -- such as an increased sensitivity to sensor degradation and the persistence of climatological biases, which remain of the same order as for GPROF V07 -- GPROF V08 constitutes a substantial advancement in spaceborne precipitation monitoring. Since the improvements are robust across all sensor of the constellation, the update is expected to improve the full record of GPM precipitation estimates and thus benefit a wide range of downstream datasets and applications.

authors.name: Simon Pfreundschuh, Paula J. Brown, Christian D. Kummerow

papers.title: Twister After Dark: Diagnosing a Damaging Nocturnal Tornado in Iloilo, Philippines (08 August 2026)
papers.summary: (Abridge) At ~1430 UTC (2230 LST) on 08 August 2026, a significant tornado struck the Mandurriao and Jaro districts of Iloilo City, Philippines. Its parent supercell developed within the southwest monsoon enhanced by Typhoon Dolphin, under weak synoptic forcing, as a nocturnal low-level jet of ~40 kt near 1.5-3 km advected warm, moist marine air onshore. ERA5 depicted MUCAPE of ~2000 J/kg, negligible inhibition, an LCL below 300 m, and nearly purely streamwise low-level vorticity, but deep-layer shear (DLS, 0-6 km bulk wind difference) below 3 m/s. Hodographs from the newly operational Iloilo S-band dual-polarization radar (S-ILO), ~5-7 km from the storm, revealed low-level shear (LLS, 0-1 km bulk wind difference) of ~16 m/s and 0-1 km storm-relative helicity of 124-211 m^2/s^2. The storm exhibited a hook echo with a weak echo hole, a $Z_{DR}$ arc and ring, an elevated 55-60 dBZ rear-flank core consistent with a descending reflectivity core, and a ~50 dBZ ring interpreted as a debris ball. A survey of 31 damage indicators documented a ~2.9 km long and up to ~340 m wide path rated IF2 on the International Fujita Scale. Processor smoothing of the radial velocity and a $\rho_{HV}$ threshold for rainfall estimation masked any tornadic vortex or debris signature, although a radial velocity simulation shows that a narrow vortex (core radius ~50-100 m) with a rotational velocity of ~35-45 m/s could have been concealed. This case shows that significant tornadoes can develop at night during the Philippine monsoon season and that operational radar quality control should be revised to retain severe-storm signatures.

authors.name: Generich H. Capuli

papers.title: Motion of a cylinder between parallel plates: complete Stokes resistance and pressure response
papers.summary: A circular cylinder moving between two parallel plates is the canonical confined problem of two-dimensional Stokes flow. Rotation and translation of the cylinder along the channel become coupled and generate a pressure difference along the channel under zero-net-flux conditions. Existing results use different methods. We develop a completed double-layer boundary integral formulation based on the channel Green function to resolve narrow gaps at arbitrary transverse positions. The channel Green kernels are derived from a Fourier-transformed biharmonic problem, permitting explicit treatment of the free-space singularity, the slowly decaying nearest-wall contribution, and the small-wavenumber limit for accurate kernel evaluation under strong confinement. The boundary integral equation is discretised by a spectrally accurate Nystr\"om scheme on a graded parametrisation, and the pressure jump follows from the zero-wavenumber limit of the streamwise momentum balance. A single linear system yields the full resistance matrix and pressure-jump coefficients for an eccentric cylinder; an additional right-hand side treats imposed net flux. For nonzero coefficients, comparisons with independent COMSOL finite-element simulations show relative differences below \(0.1\%\) for the resistance coefficients and at most \(0.0122\%\) for the pressure-response coefficients and excess hydraulic resistance. Reciprocity, symmetry constraints, and lubrication asymptotics provide additional checks on the numerical results. We track the coupling between rotation and translation and the pressure generated by the cylinder from the channel scale into the lubrication regime, and determine the pressure--flow relation, driving torque and efficiency of the rotating-cylinder pump for asymmetric clearances.

authors.name: Serhat Yesilyurt, Barbaros \c{C}etin

papers.title: Dynamics and stability of volatile thin liquid films on a heated vertical cylinder
papers.summary: Volatile thin liquid films flowing down heated vertical cylinders are central to many heat transfer applications, including evaporative condensers, cooling of electronics, and solar thermal systems. Despite their importance, the coupled dynamics of evaporation, thermocapillarity, and interfacial instabilities on cylindrical geometries remain poorly understood. In this work, a lubrication-based model is developed to capture the nonlinear evolution of a volatile thin film under gravity, surface tension, van der Waals forces, and non-conservative evaporative flux. The model incorporates hydrodynamic pressure contributions to evaporation, enabling a unified description of phase-change effects on curved substrates. A linear stability analysis of the model equation is performed with a non-constant base film thickness. The linear growth rate is first obtained for a spatially uniform film. Then, for a spatially nonuniform film, a coupled system of linearized equations is solved using the finite element method. Further, the full liquid-vapor interface is numerically simulated to demonstrate liquid evaporation. Results reveal that evaporation accelerates film thinning, condensation promotes thickening, and van der Waals forces stabilize ultra-thin films by preventing rupture. The influence of Bond number, wavenumber, and pressure-dependent flux laws on droplet formation and collision dynamics is quantified. These findings provide new mechanistic insights into phase-change driven instabilities in cylindrical thin films and have direct implications for the design of efficient thermal management systems, evaporative cooling devices, and surface-engineered heat exchangers.

authors.name: Sonam, Souradip Chattopadhyay, Naveen Tiwari

papers.title: Physics-Spawned Neural Integration of Rotating Shallow-Water Dynamics
papers.summary: Equation-derived neural integration can execute prescribed dynamics without training, while informative ensemble learning can estimate uncertain parameters and identify governing interactions without requiring differentiability. Together, these approaches motivate Physics-Spawned Informative Networks ($\Phi$SpIN), a framework for prescribed and adaptive hybrid dynamical systems. As a first step toward flood modeling applications, we present $\Phi$SpIN-SW, its prescribed-physics realization for the rotating shallow-water equations. Compatible C-grid operators on spherical Voronoi meshes define a computational graph that retains non-polynomial operations and advances the state through recurrent neural integration compiled with JAX. Analytical benchmarks characterize numerical errors, and global and coastal experiments closely reproduce reference solutions generated using the Model Prediction Across Scales (MPAS) model. At approximately 14~km global resolution, A100, H200 and B200 GPUs attain 9-, 19- and 34-fold higher timestep throughput than a 96-core MPAS-SW CPU reference under matched workloads. These results extend training-free neural integration beyond polynomial dynamics to complex geophysical simulation, establishing a computational foundation for subsequent adjoint-free ensemble estimation of physical and neural parameters and informative adaptation of operator structure.

authors.name: Kaushal Gianchandani, Luka Todorovic, Sai Ravela

papers.title: The role of turbulent jet dynamics on contrail formation from conventional and sustainable aviation fuels
papers.summary: Large-eddy simulations (LES) coupled with a discretised population balance equation (PBE) are used to quantify the effect of turbulence on the early stages of contrail formation (jet regime) for both conventional (soot-rich) and sustainable aviation fuels (SAFs). SAFs typically have low aromatic content which causes a shift in the dominant nucleation pathway. The contribution from soot (non-volatile particulate matter, nvPM) is reduced, while the contribution from volatile particulate matter (vPM) is increased. The computational domain reproduces an experimental jet configuration that replicates the thermodynamic conditions encountered in the upper troposphere. The LES-PBE simulations capture well the jet-core cooling and bracket the experimental values of ice-crystal characteristics (number concentration, mean diameter and mass density) if a range of judicious values for parameters not specified in the experiments are employed. With the aid of one-dimensional, one-way coupled PBE approach, it is shown that soot particle activation can be reliably captured using steady aerosol-jet models. On the other hand, volatile particle activation is significantly affected by large fluctuations in temperature and humidity (and thereby supersaturation). Further downstream, non-linear dynamic coupling between the gas and aerosol phases becomes increasingly important for ice-crystal growth as well. Overall, the results demonstrate that for SAFs, turbulence is an important driver of particle activation and subsequent ice crystal growth and cannot be neglected. This finding motivates more fundamental studies to assess how turbulent jet dynamics modulates contrail formation in realistic engine configurations.

authors.name: Luca Boscagli, Stelios Rigopoulos, George Papadakis

papers.title: Gas expansion in global models of nanosecond pulsed discharges: a reduced gas-dynamic model coupled to plasma kinetics
papers.summary: Global (zero-dimensional) kinetic models of nanosecond pulsed discharges describe the expansion of the heated gas channel (kernel) with simplified gas-dynamic closures. We show that these closures can lead to errors of tens of percent in the calculated gas density, temperature and species densities, especially in the first microseconds after every pulse. Here, we propose a fast, reduced gas-dynamic model of Lagrangian shells, closed by an approximate cylindrical acoustic radiation condition, with no fitted physical coefficient. The reduced model reproduces the axis density obtained by verified one- dimensional compressible computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations within 2.4% for smooth deposition profiles and axis pressures up to six times ambient, typically a thousand times faster than CFD. We couple it with our in-house global plasma-kinetics solver (SoPlasma-0D), whose energy partition after the pulse agrees well with that derived from measurements and with an independent calculation. Two microseconds after a single pulse in air, and compared with the proposed coupled model, the existing closures overestimate the axis density by up to a factor of 2.8, the atomic oxygen density by up to 2.7 and the temperature by up to 680 K. For repetitive pulses 200 or 430 ns apart, of equal energy per unit volume, no existing closure follows the coupled model at both intervals, in the gas density met by each later pulse and in the energy per molecule deposited by late pulses, which sets how strongly they dissociate and heat the gas. The proposed reduced model should therefore be used to describe the gas evolution during the expansion phase after every nanosecond pulse, and for repetitive pulses above about 100 kHz in kernels of radius up to about a millimetre.

authors.name: Konstantinos Kourtzanidis, Rention Pasolari

papers.title: Rovibrational state-specific quasi-classical trajectory calculation and master equation analysis of the CNO system in high-energy collisions
papers.summary: The CNO system governs the formation and depletion of the CN, CO and NO radiative species relevant to combustion, astrophysical and hypersonic applications. The NO($X^2\Pi$) + C($^3P$), CN($X^2\Sigma^+$) + O($^3P$) and CO($X^1\Sigma^+$) + N($^4S$, $^2D$) collisional systems are investigated using rovibrational state-specific quasi-classical trajectory calculations and master equation analysis under hypersonic thermal conditions. Inelastic processes proceed primarily through rotational excitation of low-lying states and rovibrational excitation of high-lying states. For most systems, rotational and vibrational relaxation times exhibit comparable scales and unconventional temperature dependences, invalidating the assumption of decoupled energy modes. Dissociation is governed by high-lying rovibrational states and correlates strongly with the state-specific energy deficit rather than vibrational-specific dynamics. At $T$ = 10,000 K, 72 to 93% of the depletion of the diatomic species occurs within a quasi-steady-state (QSS) regime for all systems. At lower temperatures, a large portion of the depletion occurs outside the QSS regime, indicating that the QSS assumption holds only for moderate to high temperatures. No such regime is established for exchange reactions, demonstrating that the QSS assumption is invalid for modelling them. The NO + C system proceeds predominantly towards CN + O at low temperatures and towards the CO + N channels at high temperatures, preferentially forming N($^4S$). The fraction proceeding towards the CO + N channels remains lower than in available shock-tube measurements, while the thermal exchange rate coefficients reproduce shock-tube measurements and high-fidelity calculations. Finally, consistent similarities across inelastic, exchange and dissociation processes offer promising physical foundations for reduced-order model development.

authors.name: Clement H. B. Civrais, Breno R. L. Galvao, Sung Min Jo, Marco Panesi

papers.title: Analytic Model for Transient Plateau Filling in Vibrational Distributions of Periodically Driven Plasmas
papers.summary: In periodically driven molecular plasmas, the vibrational distribution function is governed by the competition between vibration--vibration (V-V) up-pumping along the anharmonic ladder and vibration--translation (V-T) relaxation, producing the Treanor--Gordiets distribution. When vibrational energy accumulates across cycles faster than V-V exchange can populate the upper levels, the Gordiets plateau remains transiently depleted. Existing algebraic models assume a quasi-steady plateau, whereas exact transient solutions of the nonlinear V-V diffusion equation require the elapsed time since excitation and the source strength, which are unavailable in multidimensional simulations that track only local macroscopic variables. Here, elapsed time is replaced by a local vibrational energy timescale formed from the vibrational energy per molecule and its period-averaged rate of change. This reduces the diffusion equation in level space to an ordinary differential equation solved in closed form without linearization, yielding a level-dependent correction to the steady plateau governed by a single dimensionless group: the number of V-V collisions per energy timescale weighted by the plateau amplitude at the Treanor minimum. The distribution front advances as the square root of this group, and the steady distribution is recovered as the group grows large. Compared with state-to-state master-equation calculations for N$_2$ under nanosecond pulse trains spanning 300-1500 K, 0.041-1 atm, and 1-100 kHz (1440 sampled states), the model reduces the 90th-percentile error in level populations from 1.88 decades for the steady model and 1.32 decades for an adapted self-similar solution to 0.53 decades, at essentially the evaluation cost of the steady model.

authors.name: Colby Cinqmars, Bernard Parent

papers.title: Solver-consistent learned curvature for algebraic volume-of-fluid simulations of rising bubbles: symmetry-preserving networks, closed-loop data aggregation and a posteriori benchmarks
papers.summary: Curvature reconstructed from compressed volume fractions exhibits a persistent force-weighted bias in the tested algebraic volume-of-fluid formulation. In OpenFOAM interFoam, face curvature is underestimated by 11-22% for radii of 2.5-40 cells, explaining the 14-17% static Laplace-pressure deficit. This bias is consistent with approximately 2% rise-velocity underprediction in the first Hysing benchmark. We estimate curvature from 5 x 5 volume-fraction stencils using a two-hidden-layer perceptron with exact phase-exchange antisymmetry and invariance under all eight square-grid symmetries. Training uses solver-generated profiles of periodic translating bubbles, droplets, and flat films with exact analytical curvature labels. Iterative data aggregation incorporates model-solver feedback and resolves deployment instabilities found in 15 of 76 periodic cases with the initial model. Band-weighted face interpolation supplies the same capillary force to momentum prediction and pressure correction. Independent tests show static pressure-jump errors of 2-6% and reductions in time-averaged maximum capillary numbers by factors of 2.8-16. Across three grids, time-integrated rise-velocity errors decrease from 2.06-2.76% to 0.65-1.04% in the first Hysing benchmark and from 5.64-8.72% to 4.72-7.61% in the second. Tuned curvature smoothing gives smaller static pressure-jump errors, but its first-benchmark accuracy deteriorates with refinement and second-benchmark gains remain marginal. A separate interface-gated dissipative momentum closure achieves a held-out coefficient of determination of 0.47 on Favre-filtered targets but changes rise velocity by less than 0.03% of its peak. Capillary-force discretisation is therefore the more influential correction target for the tested laminar bubbles.

authors.name: Parisa Tayerani, Mahmood Mousavi

papers.title: A Gravitomagnetic Bootstrap: from Newtonian gravity to general relativity via localizing rotational and conformal symmetries
papers.summary: Newtonian gravity, in the light of the Equivalence Principle, is best understood as a localization of Galilean inertial structure --- or at least, of the part of Galilean inertial structure that defines rectilinear acceleration. I consider what kind of theory can be constructed if we also localize rotational inertia and spatial and temporal scales. The resultant theory, given weak assumptions, is unique up to a constant with the dimensions of velocity and an overall sign. For an appropriate choice of these, it coincides with the first post-Newtonian approximation to general relativity, so that this construction gives a method to bootstrap from Newtonian gravity to general relativity without explicitly presupposing special relativity.

authors.name: David Wallace

papers.title: Detection of minimum ionising particles with internal gain in the first Silicon Electron Multiplier demonstrators
papers.summary: The Silicon Electron Multiplier (SiEM) is a novel sensor concept for minimum ionising particle (MIP) detection that uses internal gain achieved through a composite electrode structure embedded within the silicon bulk. Unlike conventional gain sensors (LGADs, APDs), the SiEM achieves amplification through applied electric potentials rather than doped gain layers, potentially offering superior radiation hardness above $10^{16}\,n_{\mathrm{eq}}/\mathrm{cm}^2$. Following initial conceptual studies and simulation work, several fabrication approaches were explored, including Deep Reactive Ion Etching (DRIE) at Centro Nacional de Microelectr\'onica (CNM) and Metal Assisted Chemical Etching (MACEtch) at the Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI). This paper reports the first experimental results from functional SiEM demonstrators produced by Hamamatsu Photonics K. K. (HPK) using a single-electrode configuration with modified geometry. Electrical characterisation through I-V measurements and test beam studies with minimum ionising particles demonstrate clear evidence of charge multiplication, with gains comparable to simulation predictions.

authors.name: Federico De Benedetti, Sara Cesare, Victor Coco, Paula Collins, Raphael Dumps, Edgar Cid Lemos, Samuel Mico, Janina Nicolini, Alfonso Puicercus Gomez, Efren Rodriguez Rodriguez, Lotte Sikkema, Hironori Sonobe, Abraham Gallas Torreira, Morag Williams

papers.title: On the relation of secondary motions to large- and very-large-scale motions
papers.summary: The coexistence of secondary motions with large-scale and very-large-scale motions (LSMs/VLSMs) is investigated by direct numerical simulations of turbulent open-channel flow over streamwise-aligned Gaussian ridges, varying the ridge spacing $S$ and height $h$. First, the ridge height controls the secondary-motion strength and thereby the coexistence with VLSMs. VLSMs are suppressed for $h \geqslant 0.05\delta$, with $\delta$ the open-channel height, and re-emerge at $h = 0.025\delta$, where the mean secondary motions are comparable in strength to those over strip-type surfaces. Previously reported differences between strip- and ridge-type surfaces thus reflect secondary-motion strength rather than surface type. Second, proper orthogonal decomposition and conditional averaging reveal instantaneous secondary motions that span approximately $2\delta$, fill the channel height irrespective of $S$ and $h$, and are stronger than their mean. These are identified as LSMs spatially locked and amplified by the ridges. Over dense ridges, their alternation between neighbouring ridges yields weak, near-wall confined mean secondary motions, although VLSMs are suppressed over the full channel height. The ridge height thus sets the strength of the locked LSMs, whereas the ridge spacing sets where and for how long they persist. For weak locked LSMs, ridges spaced at their natural spanwise extent increase the VLSM energy, indicating that persistent locked LSMs concatenate into VLSMs. Third, large-scale instantaneous secondary motions persist over dense ridges in the absence of long streaks. This suggests that secondary motions are driven by intermittent cross-sectional motions rather than by long streaks, similar to the streak-less bursts in near-wall turbulence.

authors.name: Kay Sch\"afer

papers.title: Improving Tropical Cyclone Forecasts through Objective Ensemble Track-Error Reduction
papers.summary: Accurate tropical cyclone (TC) track guidance is essential for warnings, evacuation planning, and risk communication, but outlying members and distinct track scenarios can degrade raw ensemble forecasts. Statistical and machine-learning (ML) methods proposed to improve ensemble guidance are difficult to compare because previous studies often use different forecast systems, basins, periods, and verification methods. Using a common verification framework, this study compares six objective methods (four statistical trimming and two ML methods) with the full ensemble mean for 138 TCs forecast by GEFS, MOGREPS-G, and IFS during 2016-2024. Dynamic trimming (DT) is the most consistent statistical method, reducing mean total track error by 8.0%, 13.4%, and 16.1% at short, medium, and long ranges. Its largest benefits occur in high-spread cases, where it can reach 70% of the low-error bound. Short-lead-error trimming (SLET) provides useful delayed guidance after early observations become available, but its improvement decreases with lead time. Regression-mixture clustering (RC) shows potential in low-spread cases and provides the largest improvement over the control run. The gradient boosted tree (GBT) produces the largest medium-range improvement and exceeds the theoretical trimming bound, suggesting strong potential, particularly when the observed track is poorly represented by the ensemble family. However, its 12.8% short-range degradation and gains concentrated in a small subset of cases indicate overcorrection when the ensemble mean is already accurate, highlighting the need for additional constraints. These results provide a consistent basis for using objective error-reduction methods to strengthen TC track guidance for operational decision-making.

authors.name: Shuochen Wang, Mark S. Allen, Auroop R. Ganguly

papers.title: Geometry-Derived Capacitance Dyadics with Floquet Sideband Correction for Anisotropic Periodic Patch Metasurfaces
papers.summary: Homogenised sheet models describe periodic metallic patch layers using a scalar sheet capacitance, which is only valid when the effective response is isotropic. An isotropic response exists for unit cells with patch geometries that have rotational symmetry of order three or higher. Lower-symmetry unit cells with irregular or random geometries generically require a full 2 x 2 surface-capacitance dyadic. We present a framework that computes this dyadic directly from the arbitrary gap-connected patch geometry on a unit cell of a hexagonal lattice. The two-dimensional Bravais periodicity fixes the two independent macroscopic loading directions, the connectivity of the gap ensures a full-rank response for the geometries considered here, and the point-group symmetry of the patch constrains the form of the dyadic. A quasi-static boundary value problem on a single periodic cell then determines its independent entries. We use the surface-capacitance dyadic in the anisotropic surface- wave dispersion relation, which includes the leading spatially-dispersive first shell Floquet-sideband correction. For each new patch geometry, the dyadic and the first-shell correction are obtained from a single quasi-static cell problem and from the reconstructed boundary. So anisotropic surface- wave dispersion follows without a per-geometry full-wave eigenmode band sweep or sheet-tensor retrieval. We validate this geometry-to-dispersion chain against full-wave eigenmode simulations across six representative symmetry classes, showing that the correction captures band flattening near the Brillouin-zone boundary and improves agreement relative to the local dyadic model.

authors.name: Arghyadeep Pal, Federico Giusti, Stefano Maci

papers.title: Resolvent-based modeling of turbulent flow over multilayer compliant surfaces
papers.summary: Compliant coatings offer a passive approach to modifying near-wall turbulence and potentially reducing skin-friction drag, but high-fidelity exploration of the coupled parameter space is costly. We develop a two-way coupled resolvent-Galerkin framework for turbulent channel flow over finite-thickness, layered viscoelastic coatings. The fluid is modeled using the Navier-Stokes equations linearized about a turbulent mean state, while the solid is represented by a through-thickness Galerkin discretization of the elastodynamic equations. The solid response is condensed into a spectral surface-impedance operator at the fluid-solid interface. At $Re_\tau = 180$, stiff panels approach the rigid-wall response, whereas more compliant panels modify the low-rank response associated with the near-wall cycle. A Reynolds-number study shows that panels with fixed nondimensional material stiffness can produce different responses depending on whether their thickness scales with inner or outer flow length scales. The influence of viscoelastic damping is examined across low- and high-frequency regimes, where stiffness-proportional damping alters the high-frequency fractional-energy distribution, while the low-frequency distribution remains relatively insensitive to damping. For multilayer panels, the fluid-facing material determines the interfacial wave speed, while the subsurface stiffness distribution modifies the panel's effective thickness. Temporal stability analysis identifies regions of parameter space where a steady harmonic response is relevant and regions where instabilities grow. Finally, a leading-order, covariance-based drag-estimation framework relates the coupled response to changes in the mean flow and to the estimated skin-friction drag. Together, these tools provide a basis for screening coating designs and selecting candidates for high-fidelity simulations and experiments.

authors.name: Rutvij Bhagwat, Kourosh Shoele

papers.title: Solving the Discretised Shallow Water Equations on Distorted Structured Grids with Neural Physics
papers.summary: This paper presents a method for solving the shallow water equations on highly distorted structured grids using convolution-based operators following the Neural Physics approach. By mapping distorted physical grids to a uniform computational domain with Jacobian transformations, the governing advection and diffusion operators are reformulated in a structured convolutional form. This enables the use of efficient stencil-based operations and, following the Neural Physics concept, we do this through convolutional layers whose weights are determined by the chosen numerical methods rather than by training. The method introduces consistent mass-lumped formulations, conservative and non-conservative advection forms, and a diffusion operator, all expressed as convolutions. A nonlinear Petrov-Galerkin stabilisation is incorporated to control numerical oscillations on distorted meshes. Two approximations for the Laplacian operator are also proposed to accelerate pressure and diffusion solves. The framework is validated using the Carlisle 2005 flood event, demonstrating accurate predictions of water depth and velocity on distorted meshes for both linear and quadratic discretisations. The results show that distorted structured grids can retain conservation, stability and accuracy, whilst adapting the mesh statically. The convolutional formulation makes the method well suited to Neural Physics implementations and GPU acceleration, offering a scalable approach for flood modelling and large-scale geophysical simulations.

authors.name: Boyang Chen, Claire E. Heaney, Christopher C. Pain

papers.title: Electronic bridge for the $J=0$ state and effects of electrons on frequency and lifetime of the nuclear clock transition in $^{229}$Th$^{2+}$ ion
papers.summary: We investigate the electronic bridge (EB) process for excitation of the $^{229}$Th nuclear isomer in Th III ions initially prepared in the metastable electronic state with $J=0$. This state is of particular interest for developing a nuclear clock with suppressed electronic hyperfine interactions. Using a combination of configuration interaction and coupled-cluster methods, we calculate EB transition rates for several excitation schemes involving one or two laser fields. We express the rates in terms of the enhancement factor $R$, defined as the ratio of the EB transition rate to the direct nuclear M1 transition rate. Schemes that return the ion to its initial $J=0$ state have relatively small enhancement factors, $R \sim 1$. However, allowing the final electronic state to differ from the initial state produces a strong resonant enhancement: $R$ reaches $5\times10^3$. In addition, we calculate the shift in the nuclear transition frequency caused by changing the electronic state from the ground state to two excited metastable states. We also examine how the electronic state affects the nuclear transition lifetime and calculate the probabilities of electron transitions induced by nuclear decay. The EB mechanism shortens the nuclear decay lifetime by a factor of 2.6 when the electrons are initially in the ground state and by a factor of 6.85 when they are in the metastable $J=0$ state.

authors.name: V. A. Dzuba, V. V. Flambaum

papers.title: Ternary-Valued FDTD Method for Nonlinear Optics: Third-Harmonic Generation on a Multiplier-Free Solver
papers.summary: I show that a finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) solver with field variables restricted to the ternary alphabet $\{-1,0,+1\}$ can reproduce nonlinear optical physics quantitatively on both CPUs and field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs). Building on the general ternary-valued FDTD algorithm, in which each Yee cell stores an integer state that accumulates the discrete curl of neighbouring symbols without being drained, I extend the scheme to inhomogeneous and Kerr media and to Mur absorbing boundaries, without performing any multiplication operations. Dielectric contrast is implemented as a multiplexer, since the difference between ternary symbols takes only a few values, the instantaneous Kerr nonlinearity as a coefficient look-up table and the Mur boundary coefficients as canonical signed-digit shift--add chains. The scheme reproduces the third-harmonic conversion efficiency of a floating-point reference to within $1.4\%$. A symmetry of the governing physics, expressed through the even harmonics forbidden by centrosymmetric $\chi^{(3)}$, provides a reference-free self-check for both ternary and floating-point models. The complete solver fits on a small, low-cost FPGA and contains no multiplier anywhere in its datapath, placing nonlinear optical modelling within reach of embedded and autonomous platforms rather than of high-performance computers.

authors.name: Ivan S. Maksymov

papers.title: Wake-Powered Spreading of Encapsulated Drops Impacting Under Liquid
papers.summary: A drop impacting a wall in air spreads by converting its own kinetic energy into surface energy. We show that this picture fails when the wall is submerged in liquid. Millimetric perfluoropolyether drops, bare or encapsulated in an ultrathin silicone-oil shell, impacting a glass wall in water are flattened by the squeeze flow in the draining gap and shed most of their kinetic energy before impact. Nevertheless, they spread to more than twice their diameter on a water lubrication film that never ruptures, creating more surface energy than their entire kinetic and gravitational energy could supply. A two-stage energy scaling resolves this deficit. The liquid set in motion in the drop's wake supplies more than 90\% of the energy for spreading, so that the maximum spreading is governed by the Weber number of the ambient liquid rather than that of the drop. The shell acts mainly through its interfacial tension, while its biaxial-extension dissipation, negligible before impact, becomes appreciable during spreading.

authors.name: Tian-Yu Zhang, Sushanta K. Mitra

papers.title: Ionospheric bow waves during Starship Flight 14: coupling through vented propellant
papers.summary: Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) observations of Starship Flight 14 show clear bow-shaped waves in detrended total electron content (dTEC), including during motor-off coast. These observations raise a coupling problem because the spacecraft hull is small compared with the thermospheric molecular mean free path. Sustained visible release in flight video motivates the hypothesis that vented, unburned propellant supplies a much larger interaction region capable of producing a fluid response. We model gaseous methane and oxygen using the Stochastic Parallel Rarefied-gas Time-accurate Analyzer (SPARTA) for direct simulation Monte Carlo calculations at a combined release rate of 10 kg s$^{-1}$. The calculated collisional energy transfer extends over a region roughly 10 km across. We use this deposition pattern as a moving source of mass, momentum and total energy in a nonlinear neutral model coupled to a passive plasma response. The model produces a South American dTEC bow with broadly similar morphology and propagation speeds to the observations. Representative South American cuts have simulated root-mean-square (RMS) residuals of about 0.015 total electron content units (TECU), compared with observed values of 0.021--0.032 TECU; the North American response remains substantially weaker than observed. These results support collisional transfer of orbital momentum and energy by vented propellant as an explanation for the coast-phase waves. The release rate remains uncertain, and chemical contributions require further testing.

authors.name: Juha Vierinen

papers.title: Efficient scheduling of particle annihilation for long-time Wigner simulations
papers.summary: Particle annihilation (PA) plays an indispensable role in alleviating the numerical sign problem in long-time simulations with the Wigner branching random walk (WBRW) method. However, the effect of PA frequency on long-time accuracy remains poorly understood, leaving its choice largely empirical. To provide systematic guidance for PA scheduling, we establish an overall error estimate for PA through a uniform mesh, separating WBRW variance, resampling variance and squared bias. The analysis shows that, beyond merely controlling particle growth, PA replaces the exponential-in-time variance bound with a linear-in-time bound, thereby alleviating the numerical sign problem. It also reveals bias-variance trade-off induced by PA frequency: frequent PA limits variance but can increase accumulated bias. More importantly, building on the newfound error structure, we propose a variance-constrained cost optimization strategy for adaptive PA scheduling across several PA methods. An intrinsic-time reparameterization provides a common clock for variance control, PA scheduling, and branching dynamics under time-dependent potentials. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical variance behavior and bias-variance trade-off, and results of our schedule populate the low-cost regime of the empirical Pareto frontier objecting to balance accuracy and efficiency.

authors.name: Jingyang Huang, Sihong Shao, Yuxuan Zhang

papers.title: FiuMD: Heterogeneous Batching for Coarse-Grained Molecular Dynamics with Neural Network Potentials
papers.summary: FiuMD is a GPU molecular dynamics engine that advances many independent biomolecular simulations as a single batch, even when the systems differ in size, topology, force-field parameters, periodic box, timestep, or thermostat parameters. All systems are concatenated into global tensors, so the classical interaction terms and a shared TorchMD-Net neural network potential are evaluated for the whole batch at once, while each system keeps its own integration and thermostat. FiuMD started as a fork of TorchMD and reworks its system representation, force evaluation, and integration to handle such heterogeneous batches. We test it with coarse-grained C$\alpha$ models of chignolin, Trp-cage, BBL, and $\lambda$-repressor. In double precision, forces within a heterogeneous batch agree with isolated FiuMD and TorchMD evaluations to within the precision of repeated evaluations, with a maximum relative difference of $7\times10^{-16}$ across 60 systems. Over 1000 steps without a thermostat, batched trajectories deviate by at most $2.5\times10^{-11}$ Angstrom from isolated ones, even when periodic images lie within the neural network cutoff. With a different target temperature for each system of the ensemble, the mean and width of each system's kinetic temperature match the values expected from its own thermostat. We show that when individual simulations are too small to fill the GPU, batching can improve throughput several-fold over TorchMD. On a single GPU, batching four different protein systems achieves a 4.6-7.8-fold speedup per step compared with sequential TorchMD simulations. Compared with sequential homogeneous FiuMD batches, heterogeneous batching provides up to a 4-fold speedup for smaller batches while maintaining comparable performance for larger ones.

authors.name: Hugo D. Hern\'andez R. (Instituto de F\'isica del Sur, Departamento de F\'isica, Universidad Nacional del Sur), Paola B. Torres (Grupo Vinculado Bionanotecnolog\'ia y Sistemas Complejos, INFAP), Lara Negri (Instituto de F\'isica del Sur, Departamento de F\'isica, Universidad Nacional del Sur), Roc\'io L. Cecchini (Instituto de Ciencias e Ingenier\'ia de la Computaci\'on), Nicol\'as A. Garc\'ia (Instituto de F\'isica del Sur, Departamento de F\'isica, Universidad Nacional del Sur)

papers.title: Optimization Framework for Full-Skyrmionic Polarimetry
papers.summary: Optical skyrmionic beams hold considerable potential for applications in quantum information and weak-intensity detection. These applications require accurate measurements of full topological observables using imaging Stokes polarimetry, with measurement states optimized in advance to limit the effect of stochastic error sources. However, the optimization framework for general Stokes polarimetries is based on a linear reconstruction chain for Stokes vectors and cannot quantitatively evaluate the nonlinear reconstruction of topological observables. Here, we define full-skyrmionic polarimetry (FSP) and construct its optimization framework from the reconstruction chain for full topological observables. Based on existing polarization evaluating functions (PEF), we introduce topological evaluating functions (TEF) and develop a multi-stage FSP optimization methodology. Numerical results confirm that topological optimization can further improve the reconstruction of topological observables, even when the measurement states are already optimal for polarization. Increasing the redundant projection number also effectively suppresses the effects of all stochastic error sources, providing a low-cost methodology to improve the reconstruction of both polarization and topological observables. The FSP optimization framework can identify topologically optimal configurations for arbitrary FSP structures, providing a guideline for high-precision full-skyrmionic measurements at weak-intensity levels and potential skyrmion ellipsometry.

authors.name: Luo Wang, Haiyang Zhang, Zilong Zhang, Hanqiu Zhang, Changming Zhao

papers.title: Broadband Absorption Bounds for Coated PEC Spheres: Curvature, Angular Momentum, and Localized Sources
papers.summary: We investigate fundamental limits on broadband electromagnetic absorption by a material-coated perfectly electrically conducting (PEC) sphere. Exact reflection coefficients are derived for the transverse-electric (TE) and transverse-magnetic (TM) spherical modes. Their long-wavelength asymptotics, combined with causality and contour integration in the complex wavelength plane, yield sum rules relating the wavelength-integrated modal reflection to the static material parameters, coating thickness, curvature, and complex reflection zeros. For the dipolar modes ($n=1$), known passive spherical-wave sum rules establish analytically a material-dependent lower bound on the weighted logarithmic reflection integral. Extension to higher-order modes requires a nonnegativity condition on higher odd moments of the reflection zeros; we formulate this condition as a conjecture and provide extensive Monte-Carlo evidence for passive dispersive coatings. The resulting bounds establish a per-channel absorption--bandwidth tradeoff and reveal the spherical-harmonic order as a discrete transverse-wavenumber variable, recovering the familiar planar attenuation factor in the locally planar limit. Finally, we show how the modal bounds can be combined for a localized external source. For a radial electric dipole outside the sphere, the near-field excitation is decomposed into TM spherical channels, leading to a source-weighted broadband absorption bound. As the source approaches the surface, progressively higher angular momenta contribute, directly linking near-field spatial localization to the hierarchy of modal absorption constraints.

authors.name: Yoav Kriman, Amir Shlivinski, Yakir Hadad

papers.title: Polarization-Resilient Plasmonic Nanoantenna Arrays for Fiber-Coupled Terahertz Spectroscopy with Record-high Dynamic Range
papers.summary: Achieving polarization-resilient optoelectronic responses while harnessing the strong light-matter interactions enabled by plasmonic nanostructures remains a fundamental challenge in ultrafast optoelectronics. Here, we demonstrate that the polarization sensitivity of plasmonic optoelectronic devices is governed not simply by optical absorption, but by its interplay with ultrafast photocarrier transport and local electric-field distributions, establishing a design principle for achieving polarization resilience without compromising optoelectronic efficiency. Through theoretical modeling and experimental validation, we demonstrate that this interplay enables plasmonic nanoantenna arrays to maintain highly efficient terahertz generation and detection across different optical polarization states, overcoming a longstanding limitation of plasmonic optoelectronics. Exploiting this principle, we introduce a high-power fiber-coupled terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) architecture that integrates polarization-resilient plasmonic nanoantenna arrays with hollow-core antiresonant fibers. By suppressing optical dispersion and nonlinearities during high-power femtosecond pulse delivery, this architecture unlocks the superior optoelectronic properties of GaAs-based photoconductors without sacrificing the flexibility and robustness of fiber coupling. The resulting system generates a record-high 2.1 mW of terahertz radiation and achieves a 145 dB peak dynamic range over 60 seconds, representing a 300-fold improvement over state-of-the-art fiber-coupled THz-TDS systems. This breakthrough opens new opportunities for probing weak light-matter interactions, characterizing strongly attenuating materials, and realizing high-throughput hyperspectral imaging and spatially distributed terahertz sensing beyond controlled laboratory environments.

authors.name: Xinghe Jiang, Anika Tabassum, Fanqi Shen, Ali Jabbari, Mona Jarrahi

papers.title: A Paired Monte Carlo Intensity-Ratio Method for Incorporating Detector Resolution in Amplitude Analysis
papers.summary: Finite detector resolution can bias resonance parameters and fit fractions extracted from amplitude analyses. We present the paired Monte Carlo intensity-ratio method for incorporating resolution effects into amplitude analysis. The method uses ratios of reference intensities evaluated at paired truth-level and reconstructed kinematics to reweight the Monte Carlo normalization and approximately account for detector resolution. A resampling study of simulated $D^+\to K^+\pi^+\pi^-\pi^0$ decays shows that the method substantially reduces resolution-induced shifts in fitted resonance widths. Likelihood evaluation uses intensity calculations and normalization sums, avoiding a response convolution at each data event.

authors.name: Zhenxuan Li, Liping Yang, Bai-Cian Ke, Liaoyuan Dong, Minggang Zhao

papers.title: Recurrent losers: A network approach to cover-bidding patterns in public procurement
papers.summary: We develop and apply a network-based method to examine patterns consistent with cover bidding within procurement markets, using only bidder participation and winner identities. A statistical test identifies relationships in which firms win unusually often when particular competitors also bid. These relationships form a directed graph with links from recurrent losers to recurrent winners. We use maximum $k$-core to classify possible organizational forms of cover bidding and propose tender exposure -- the share of contested tenders involving a reported relationship -- as a market-level indicator of potential cover-bidding risk. Applied to 200,065 contracts procured by district engineering offices of the Philippine Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) from 2017 to 2025, covering three congressional terms, the method identifies 8,728 directed relationships across 407 of 564 markets. The $k$-core classes differ in network breadth, relationship depth, and bidder roles. In simpler networks, each recurrent loser is usually tied to a single winner, while highly interconnected networks involve multiple recurrent winners and broader groups of bidders that rarely win. Some of the deepest relationships and highest levels of tender exposure occur in intermediate networks, showing how relationships can reach much of a market without extensive interconnectedness. Offices named in official investigations more often contain highly interconnected networks than other offices. Two of the three offices referred for bid rigging are among the twelve in our ranking with the highest exposure in 2023-2025.

authors.name: Isabela Villamil, J\'anos Kert\'esz

papers.title: Scale-aware composite forcing enhances forward energy transfer in lattice Boltzmann simulations of forced homogeneous isotropic turbulence
papers.summary: In forced homogeneous isotropic turbulence (FHIT), conventional large-scale forcing sustains statistical stationarity but offers limited control over energy at intermediate scales. We propose a scale-aware composite forcing strategy for the lattice Boltzmann method, combining large-scale random forcing with feedback aligned with an intermediate-scale velocity field extracted by composite filtering. The magnitude of the cross-power spectrum between feedback and filtered velocity is concentrated in the target band, with a time-averaged fraction of 72.26%-74.56%. Feedback increases energy in both target and high-wavenumber bands, with larger relative gains at high wavenumbers. At feedback strengths $\alpha$ = 1%, 3%, 5%, and 7%, the target-band energy fraction increases by 6.29%, 11.65%, 18.99%, and 19.89% relative to the baseline. The mean forward nonlinear energy flux across K = 12 rises to 1.18, 1.54, 2.32, and 3.06 times its baseline value, with larger relative increases than across K = 4. As $\alpha$ increases from 0% to 7%, the mean Taylor-microscale Reynolds number rises from 73.94 to 97.86 and enstrophy increases by 181.98%, while longitudinal velocity-gradient skewness shifts toward zero and standardized velocity and normalized Q'-R' distributions largely retain their shapes. Mean $k_{\max}\eta$ values of 1.01 and 0.90 at 5% and 7% feedback indicate an approaching resolution limit and a risk of under-resolution, respectively. At approximately matched dissipation rates, 5% feedback gives a target-band energy fraction of 32.36%, versus 27.55% under enhanced large-scale forcing, and a post-transient forward flux across K = 12 generally 2.17-2.39 times larger. The strategy thus enables targeted control of energy distribution and nonlinear transfer, with feedback strength constrained by small-scale resolution.

authors.name: Hongxuan Zhang, Fanxi Gong, Yating Chen, Runchao Guan

papers.title: Dynamic infrared thermography and computed tomography angiography fusion for DIEP flap perforator selection: a novel measurement system
papers.summary: Accurate perforator selection is critical for successful deep inferior epigastric artery perforator (DIEP) flap breast reconstruction. While computed tomography angiography (CTA) provides high-resolution anatomical detail, it lacks functional perfusion assessment. Dynamic infrared thermography (DIRT), in contrast, captures superficial rewarming dynamics but lacks objective anatomical validation. This study presents a standardized multimodal measurement system enabling automated fusion of DIRT with CTA-derived perforator coordinates. The framework integrates controlled thermographic acquisition, real-time hotspot detection, metric spatial calibration, and global one-to-one assignment of thermal hotspots to CTA perforators within a predefined periumbilical region of interest.
