papers.title: Revisiting Stress Analysis in a Three-Dimensional Elastic Hollow Sphere under Uniaxial Compression via the Inverse Laplace Transform Expressions within an Elastodynamic Framework
papers.summary: The stress analysis of a three-dimensional elastic hollow sphere subjected to uniaxial compression is revisited, employing an elastodynamic framework. Through the application of the Laplace transform, the scalar and vector potentials of displacement are expanded, facilitating a detailed exploration of the system's mechanical behavior. The static solutions for displacement and stress distributions are derived in the long-time limit, which reveal key insights into the response of the elastic hollow sphere. Notably, on the inner surface, certain quantities exhibit a peak at the point where the angle between the compressive force and the point on the surface becomes perpendicular, indicating localized stress concentration. These findings provide a robust analytical approach for understanding and predicting the behavior of elastic hollow spheres under uniaxial loading, with implications for material science and structural engineering.

authors.name: Satoshi Takada, Shintaro Hokada

papers.title: Quantifying internal variability in large-ensemble climate data with the Wasserstein distance
papers.summary: Estimating forced and internal variability in climate data is fundamental to detecting the climate change signal and assessing uncertainty in climate projections. We propose a metric that quantifies the relative magnitude of internal variability in single-model initial-condition large ensembles (SMILEs). We measure forced and internal variability by two 1-Wasserstein distances, a form of optimal transport cost. The proposed metric is the distance for internal variability divided by the sum of the two. Computing this ratio requires only sorting the samples and differencing the resulting quantiles, with no additional parameters. The metric reflects the entire distribution shape and applies to non-Gaussian variables, because the 1-Wasserstein distance measures the difference between any two probability distributions. We validate the metric with synthetic climate data from Gaussian, uniform, and lognormal distributions. Unlike the two existing metrics, the proposed metric gives stable estimates in the presence of outliers irrespective of the distribution shape, provided that the ensemble has about 40 members or more. We then apply the proposed and existing metrics to the 2 m air temperature and total precipitation of the Community Earth System Model Large Ensemble (CESM-LE) under two different forcing scenarios. All three metrics agree in the spatial pattern of the difference between the scenarios but not in amplitude. The amplitude of the difference is largest for the proposed metric, consistent with the synthetic-data result that this metric changes most rapidly when internal variability dominates. The 1-Wasserstein distance thus provides a simple and useful tool for analyzing large-ensemble datasets.

authors.name: Yuki Yasuda, Shoichiro Kido

papers.title: Validating direct solvers for Newton's gravitational N-body problem, and the systematic comparison between IEEE floating point and Posits
papers.summary: We present a systematic comparison between arbitrary precise arithmetic and integration, IEEE-754 compliant floating point arithmetic (fp16, bfp16, fp32, double precision fp64, and quadruple precision fp128), and two implementations of Posits (type III unum) for solving Newton's chaotic N-body problem. Each implementation is benchmarked with arbitrary precise calculations to objectively evaluate their performance in precision as well as speed. We rely on hardware and compiler implementations for fp64, and software implementations for arbitrary-precision arithmetic and Posits. Half precision arithmetic (fp16, bfp16, and Posits$$) are insufficiently precise for solving Newton's equations of motion. Single precision (fp32, and Posits$$) could be used for statistical ensemble calculations, but lead to relatively large errors in any individual strong encounter. All 64-bit implementations fp64 as well as Posits (Posits$$) experience difficulty in our tests. One of the implementations of Posits (Universal) gives precision comparable to fp64 but is slow (by at least an orders of magnitude compared to fp64 after correcting for the more efficient hardware support for the latter). The other (CPPPosits) has a speed comparable to fp64 but has systematically larger errors (by about an order of magnitude compared to fp64 with excesses exceeding two orders of magnitude). As a consequence, this implementation leads to a systematic drift in the result space and has difficulty resolving close encounters. Posits and fp64 have difficulty when integrating a dynamical system in a moving reference frame; testing Galileo invariancy. In their current implementation, Posits do not seem to be the ideal alternative for fp64 when integrating chaotic or stiff ordinary differential equations, such as Newton's equations of motion.

authors.name: Simon Portegies Zwart (Leiden Observatory)

papers.title: Exact Scaling Theory of Social Tipping Phenomena in Finite Populations
papers.summary: Granovetter's threshold model provides a classical framework for social mobilization, in which collective action spreads through self-reinforcing cascades as individuals join once the movement size reaches their personal threshold. Here, we investigate social tipping points by treating the initial fraction of instigators, $\rho_0$, as a control parameter in a finite population of $N$ agents with activation thresholds drawn from a Beta distribution with shape parameters $\alpha$ and $\beta$. We characterize the thermodynamic phase diagram, which exhibits both continuous and discontinuous cascade transitions, and develop an exact combinatorial formulation for finite populations. The discontinuous transitions are hybrid, combining a jump in the final active fraction with a square-root critical singularity associated with an interior saddle-node bifurcation. Using the empirical cumulative distribution of quenched thresholds, we develop an asymptotic finite-size scaling theory that identifies the stochastic mechanisms responsible for rounding these transitions. For power-law thresholds ($\alpha>1$, $\beta=1$), the critical window and the mean inactive fraction at criticality both scale as $N^{-1/3}$. For hybrid transitions governed by an interior saddle-node, the critical window scales as $N^{-1/2}$, while the conditional displacement of stalled cascades from the marginal state scales as $N^{-1/4}$. We further derive an explicit Gaussian scaling function for the probability of complete activation and show that convergence to this limiting function is exceptionally slow, with corrections of order $N^{-1/6}$. These results establish the extensively seeded Granovetter model as a tractable framework for investigating finite-population fluctuations and hybrid criticality in irreversible threshold-driven cascades.

authors.name: Bianca Y. S. Ishikawa, Jos\'e F. Fontanari

papers.title: Short spatial mooring-tilt variations from deep Mediterranean observations
papers.summary: Interaction between energy-abundant mesoscale eddies and internal waves can lead to convection-turbulence generation and may prove important for deep-sea life and circulation. However, the size of scales of interacting flows is not well known. In this paper, a diagnostic tool of tilt is tested near the single top-buoyancy of 40 mooring lines 9.5 m apart horizontally and compared with 50-m scale relative vorticity and waterflow above a 2500-m deep flat Northwestern-Mediterranean seafloor. Whilst tilt relates to first order with flow-speed squared induced by mooring-line drag, considerable deviations from this relationship and larger tilt occur when the amplitude of relative vorticity attains values O(f), f the inertial frequency of planetary vorticity. The sign of relative vorticity is of no importance. Such larger-tilt events occur during most intense convection turbulence via warm-water slanting from above. During these events, variations in tilt-angle magnitude are as large as the average tilt O(0.1)degr, thereby reducing variational scales from 50 to 9.5 m. Thus, in a deep-sea environment where flow speeds are <0.07 m/s, O(0.01) m/s flow-speed variations provide important turbulent mixing, under conditions without deep dense-water formation.

authors.name: Hans van Haren

papers.title: Density-gradient effect in high-harmonic generation in gases
papers.summary: High-harmonic generation (HHG) in gaseous targets is the most widespread method to produce coherent extreme-ultraviolet (XUV) pulses with sub-femtosecond duration. However, this process has intrinsically low efficiency, and substantial research and development is devoted worldwide to increase the achievable photon flux through this highly nonlinear light--matter interaction process. In this work, we show the strong interplay of phase matching and absorption in gas-pressure gradients, substantially affecting macroscopic HHG efficiency. Through detailed experimental analysis and supporting numerical studies, we highlight their significance, particularly at the boundaries of the interaction volume. The concluded results have implications in the massively expanding application possibilities of HHG sources requiring high photon flux, for example in the semiconductor industry, in nanoscale imaging of biological and industrial samples, or in nonlinear optics in the XUV regime.

authors.name: Zolt\'an Filus, T\'imea Gr\'osz, Chinmoy Biswas, L\'en\'ard Guly\'as Oldal, Tam\'as Bartyik, Barnab\'as Gilicze, Subhendu Kahaly, Katalin Varj\'u, Bal\'azs Major

papers.title: New rules, old habits: across seven team sports, each league keeps its own way of using the rules
papers.summary: Studies of a rule change usually report one average effect, for one league or several combined. We asked whether a rule change reorders leagues, in 101 leagues of seven sports. When the substitution limit rose from three to five, the leagues already ranked from most substitutions to fewest, as known for the biggest leagues. In their first season under five, the fourteen top leagues kept that order (rank correlation 0.89; one means the same order, zero unrelated orders). That is about as firmly as from one ordinary season to the next. A prediction for twelve second tiers, written before their records were read, held (0.73). They ranked like their country's top league. Across rule changes in other sports, leagues kept their order in four of eight tests. In every sport measured, a league stayed near its place among its sport's leagues from season to season. Under five, clubs inside a league differed more within a season than the leagues did, but their differences lasted less. Rule-makers should judge a change league by league, against each league's own seasons.

authors.name: Gustavo Pedro Ricou

papers.title: Size and shape of condensing steam jets and plumes
papers.summary: Droplet-laden cloud dynamics emerge from coupled phase transitions and turbulent mixing. Combining experiments and mean-field theory, we establish scaling laws for steam-injected clouds in unsaturated air seeded with condensation nuclei. Depending on whether the cloud is confined to the initial momentum-dominated zone of the jet or extends into the buoyancy-dominated plume, two asymptotic regimes arise. In the momentum regime, cloud dimensions scale with the injector radius. In the buoyancy regime, size follows a $\dot{m}^{2/5}$ scaling, where $\dot{m}$ is the injected steam mass flow rate. Assuming interdroplet air remains humidity saturated, our mean-field analysis predicts cloud persistence governed by enthalpy and humidity mixing. These findings bridge microphysical processes and macroscale dynamics, offering a quantitative framework for atmospheric cloud evolution.

authors.name: N. Fourcade, F. Poydenot, P. Langlois, F. Barbe, N. Sinnathamby, P. Claudin, B. Andreotti

papers.title: Shape effects on the Shafranov shift of Solov'ev equilibria with prescribed boundaries
papers.summary: The Shafranov shift, the outward displacement of the magnetic axis of a toroidal plasma, is known analytically for circular and elliptical cross-sections, whereas its dependence on shape in strongly shaped plasmas has not been studied systematically. Here the shift is analyzed for a wide range of prescribed boundaries, at fixed profiles or poloidal beta, using exact Solov'ev solutions of the Grad--Shafranov equation with the boundary imposed in a least-squares sense. For shaped boundaries the shift depends on the point from which it is measured, usually the geometric center, the midpoint of the radial extent of the boundary. Therefore, a straight-cylinder equilibrium with the same plasma shape is introduced as the zero-shift reference state, and the shift is measured from its magnetic axis. With this reference, some known features of the shift measured from the geometric center turn out to be effects of the reference point, whose error depends only on the boundary and can also make the shift negative. Three boundary parametrizations are used to analyze positive and negative triangularity, squareness from square to concave shapes, and non-convex star polygons of arbitrary symmetry order. At fixed poloidal beta the shift depends only weakly on triangularity: the larger shift of negative than of positive triangularity plasmas obtained with the geometric center is an effect of the reference point and nearly disappears with the cylindrical reference. Negative squareness and concavity, instead, reduce the shift itself: for concave plasma cross-sections it is almost half that of elliptical and D-shaped ones.

authors.name: D. Abate

papers.title: A high-order ghost-point immersed boundary method with auxiliary differential equations for time-domain impedance walls
papers.summary: This paper presents a method for performing time-domain simulations of a sound field interacting with a wall having a locally-reacting impedance. The linearized Euler equations are solved using a high-order finite difference method. To impose the impedance condition on a wall that is not aligned with the Cartesian grid, an immersed boundary method (IBM) is employed. It relies on a ghost-point approach with a normal-stencil-based reconstruction, where the impedance is accounted for via auxiliary differential equations (ADEs), which are integrated using the same Runge-Kutta scheme as the governing equations. The method is validated against semi-analytical solutions for a pressure pulse reflecting off a flat or cylindrical wall with an impedance corresponding to a mass-spring-damper system. The cylindrical case solution is derived in the appendix. The measured convergence order is approximately 4 for a flat wall and just slighlty smaller for a curved wall. Long-term stability is verified by the diffraction of a monopole by a cylinder.

authors.name: Abdoulaye Ouattara, David Marx, Christian Prax

papers.title: Hyperfine structure splitting for the triplet $2^{3}S(L = 0)-$state in the two-muonic helium ${}^{3}$He $\mu_{2}$ atom
papers.summary: The hyperfine structure splitting for the triplet $2^{3}S(L = 0)-$state in the two-muonic helium ${}^{3}$He $\mu_{2}$ atom is determined to high accuracy. Such a structure arises as a result of hyperfine (or spin-spin) interaction between the triplet two-muonic shell and non-zero spin of the central helicon nucleus. Our result for the hyperfine structure splitting is $\Delta \approx 2.5811701551505 \cdot 10^{7}$ MHz, where the standard uncertainty has been evaluated as $\pm 10$ Hz.

authors.name: Alexei M. Frolov

papers.title: Breit interaction in elastic scattering of vortex electron on Hydrogen atomic target
papers.summary: The interaction of electron vortex beams with atoms is fundamental to their applications, yet existing studies of elastic scattering have considered only the Coulomb interaction. The role of the Breit interaction, which represents the leading relativistic correction to the Coulomb potential between two electrons, has not been systematically examined. In this paper, we study the elastic scattering of a vortex electron by a hydrogen atomic target, with emphasis on the role of the Breit interaction. Comparisons are made between two situations: the pure Coulomb contribution and the pure Breit contribution. Our results show that the Breit interaction dominates the scattering process when the total angular momentum of the vortex electron is larger than a certain threshold, which challenges the conventional notion that the Breit interaction makes little contribution to electron scattering for low-$Z$ atoms. This phenomenon arises primarily because a vortex electron with large angular momentum possesses a substantial magnetic moment, and the Breit interaction precisely describes the interaction between magnetic moments. The threshold can be adjusted by changing the parameters of the initial vortex electron. Moreover, we further compare the single-atom, mesoscopic, and macroscopic target cases, and show that the target size significantly influences the observability of the Breit-induced effects, with a smaller target size being favorable for observing this phenomenon.

authors.name: Pengcheng Zhao

papers.title: Role of flame localization in wavemaker regions on the suppression of combustion instability in turbulent partially-premixed methane flames
papers.summary: The interaction between flame dynamics & hydrodynamic instabilities plays a fundamental role in determining the stability of swirl-stabilized combustors. In the present study, we investigate the hypothesis that spatial overlap between flame & wavemaker region is a necessary prerequisite for combustion stability in flows characterized by a wavemaker region. To test the hypothesis, a low-momentum secondary methane injection was introduced through circumferential holes located on the centerbody of a swirl-stabilized burner. The injection velocity was maintained below 5\% of bulk flow velocity to minimize momentum-induced modifications of flow field while selectively redistributing heat release. In addition, an equivalent amount of fuel was diverted from primary fuel supply to secondary injection ports, known as fuel-staging, to isolate the effects of flame relocation from those of the total fuel flow rate. The introduction of secondary injection produced a transition of the flame from M-shaped to V-shaped structure, while fuel-staging yielded a similar flame response, demonstrating that observed behavior results primarily from redistribution of heat release. Linear stability analysis revealed that wavemaker region remains near inlet of the combustion chamber. Moreover, flame root transitions from a lifted M-flame to attached V-flame and consistently stabilizes at radial position corresponding to the identified wavemaker region. The coincidence of flame attachment & wavemaker location under stable operating conditions provides strong experimental evidence that flame stabilization is governed by their spatial overlap rather than by a modification of the underlying hydrodynamic instability. The proposed framework provides new insight into the coupling between flame stabilization & hydrodynamic instability & offers practical guidance for the design of stable, low-emission combustion systems.

authors.name: Abhishek Kushwaha, Bjarne Lieth, Isaac Boxx

papers.title: Fluid drags on a sphere at finite Reynolds number--a classical problem examined afresh
papers.summary: Evaluating the drag coefficient Cd for a sphere moving in a fluid at finite Reynolds number Re has become a classical research subject in fluid dynamics, with publications appearing continuously by numerous authors over the years due to the unavailability of closed-form mathematical solutions. To date, mathematical formulas for calculating Cd as a function of Re can only be obtained by correlation curve fitting to experimental data. The consequence is the coexistence of various formulas with different mathematical fitting functions and an increasing number of fitting parameters. The present study focuses on examining the accuracy of Klyachko's 1934 formula for Cd with two common fractions as fitting parameters, which could enable closed form integration of a simplified equation governing rectilinear motion of aerosol spheres. The computed values of root-mean-square relative error from recently developed formulas show reasonable accuracy of the Klyachko formula for Re less than 1000 and its extension to Re less than 2e5 as a piecewise continuous function, with the possibility of significant improvement through a slight modification. Hence, a few demonstrative examples are presented using the extended Klyachko formula in the study of rectilinear acceleration, the calculation of the terminal velocity of aerosol spheres, and so forth, to shed fresh light on how this classical problem can be studied.

authors.name: James Q Feng

papers.title: High-power photoconductive THz emitters for fast parallel electro-optic detection
papers.summary: The terahertz (THz) spectral region is highly attractive for imaging because it penetrates many optically opaque materials and can distinguish them by composition. THz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) is ideally suited for spectroscopic imaging, since it records the full electric-field waveform and thus broadband amplitude and phase information. Translating this capability into fast, wide-field imaging has remained a major challenge, largely because the low average power of conventional TDS sources forces a trade-off between acquisition speed, field of view and sensitivity. Here we demonstrate a fast hyperspectral THz camera based on parallel electro-optic sampling, driven by a large-area photoconductive emitter delivering a record-high 38.3 mW of average power at 400 kHz. A numerical model reproduces the measured emitter scaling and shows that, under 515 nm excitation, electron transfer into low-mobility satellite valleys delays radiation screening, allowing higher pump fluences before its effect dominates. The camera records the full THz waveform, with ~1.5 THz bandwidth, simultaneously at 145,000 pixels over a ~14.5 mm2 field of view at 2 Hz. These results establish high-average-power THz-TDS as a route to broadband, high-speed imaging, for inline material-resolved inspection and for spectroscopic imaging of irreversible, second-timescale processes such as hydration in biologically relevant systems.

authors.name: Mohsen Khalili, Anna Martinez, Robin L\"oscher, Abhishek Singh, Stephan Winnerl, Clara J. Saraceno

papers.title: A Differentiable Surrogate for Loss-Dominated Ion Beam Transport
papers.summary: Radioactive nuclei with extreme proton-to-neutron ratios provide unique probes of nuclear structure, fundamental symmetries, astrophysical processes, and applications such as medicine. However, their short half-lives and low production rates mean that experiments must work with few desired ions, often amid contaminant backgrounds exceeding the signal by six orders of magnitude. Efficiently isolating, transporting, and delivering these ions through multi-stage apparatus is therefore a central challenge. We introduce a differentiable probabilistic surrogate for ion-beam transport in regimes dominated by particle loss. The model jointly captures the survival probability of ions along the beamline and the evolving phase-space distribution of the surviving particles by combining discrete-time survival analysis with conditional normalizing flows. Applied to a high-dimensional electrostatic beamline, the resulting likelihood enables gradient-based optimization of operating voltages and inference of beam properties from sparse detector observations. Once trained, the surrogate provides millisecond-scale differentiable predictions, transforming particle-tracking simulations with hard losses into an inference-ready model for experimental design, beamline optimization, and future digital twins of experiments with rare nuclei.

authors.name: Jose M. Munoz-Arias, Laura Ruiz-Arango, Derick Gonzalez-Acevedo, Fabian C. Pastrana-Cruz, Jackson Hacias, Ronald F. Garcia Ruiz

papers.title: Wave-driven geostrophic vortices in rotating turbulence
papers.summary: We perform direct numerical simulations of rotating turbulence to investigate the mechanisms responsible for the maintenance of large-scale geostrophic vortices. We confirm that the Reynolds stresses generated by inertial waves are consistent with the Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes balance of the large-scale flow and demonstrate the predicted cyclone-anticyclone asymmetry, with cyclones exhibiting stronger azimuthal velocities and more compact cores. Wave-field analysis provides evidence that geostrophic vortices selectively absorb and reflect inertial waves according to the sign of their angular momentum. Wave absorption occurs either at a critical layer encountered as waves propagate radially inward toward the vortex core, before reaching the reflection point, or through enhanced viscous dissipation associated with increasing local wavenumber. As rotation rate increases, inertial waves with opposite angular wavenumbers exhibit increasingly similar dispersion relations, reducing the difference in their absorption. This weakens the net angular-momentum transfer to the vortices and diminishes the strength of the geostrophic flow. Consequently, the fraction of energy contained in geostrophic modes depends non-monotonically on the rotation rate, demonstrating that sufficiently rapid rotation can ultimately suppress, rather than enhance, turbulence two-dimensionalization.

authors.name: Vladimir Parfenyev, Sergey Vergeles

papers.title: A compact six-beam 3D magneto-optical trap based on multifunctional metasurface chips
papers.summary: Magneto-optical traps (MOTs), indispensable to cold-atom-based quantum computing and quantum precision measurement, are increasingly desired in compact and stable form. Particularly, the six-beam 3D-MOT, distinguished by symmetric geometry and superior trapping performance, finds particularly broad applications. Conventional implementations, however, rely on complex and bulky free-space optics, hindering miniaturization, practical assembly, and long-term stability. Here, we demonstrate a compact six-beam 3D-MOT system that employs two multifunctional optical metasurface chips to implement the optical-field functionalities required for cooling and trapping atoms. By combining two metasurface chips and a vacuum cell, a photonic-integrated cell module (PICM) is implemented as the core assembly and the volume is only" 73*73*107 mm^3" . In success, 1.3 * 10^3 Rb atoms are trapped and cooled to the temperature of ~183 {\mu}K. It should be noticed that the laser beam is guided to the metasurface through optical fiber, thus such fully fiber-coupled architecture enables straightforward and stable operations. We believe that this work would pave a practical route toward compact and portable 3D-MOT.

authors.name: Chen Qing, Huijie Sun, Yize Liu, Yuxuan Liao, Yongzhuo Li, Dengke Zhang, Xue Feng, Yidong Huang

papers.title: Self-organizing recruitment cascades couple Levy search to a clustered maximum-entropy resource field
papers.summary: Foraging recruitment is modeled as a contagion: an agent finding a resource triggers a linear-threshold cascade on the group's communication network. Because activation is degree-normalized, crowding shuts the cascade off, causing the swarm to aggregate on a resource and then disperse to explore again. Acting on the cascade moves agents in space, rewiring the network; recruitment and exploration are thus one coupled process, and removing this coupling alone abolishes self-limitation. Recruitment spreads only within a connectivity window bounded below by percolation onset and above by degree-blocking. The swarm self-organizes to the near-critical edge of this window--self-organized quasi-criticality--hovering near but below the critical point without settling onto a size-invariant critical state, with a finite-correlation-time activity spectrum (Lorentzian-like, not 1/f) consistent with local criticality. Recruitment raises harvest up to 2.7x over solitary search on sparse, clustered fields and loses (down to 0.37x) on abundant or uniform ones; because resources generically aggregate, the favourable regime is the common one. The Levy search and resource field are both least-committal: a maximum-caliber walk coupled to a maximum-entropy point process whose generic sign is clustered, with the optimal search exponent tracking the field's fractal dimension. Heavy-tailed Levy exploration crosses sparse voids while recruitment cascades exploit clusters by switching agents to short local steps, binding exploration and recruitment into a single self-organizing cycle.

authors.name: Galen J. Wilkerson

papers.title: Vacuum-Field Squeezing by Molecules in Optical Cavities: An Exact Bound and Linear-Response Theory
papers.summary: The ground state of a molecule coupled to an optical cavity contains virtual photons, and squeezing of the photonic field has been found in exactly solvable models, perturbation theory, and numerical calculations. Here, two exact sum rules for the field quadratures show that, within the dipole approximation, the vector-potential fluctuations of a linearly polarized mode never exceed their vacuum value in the ground state of any molecule at any coupling strength. Consequently, the field is squeezed whenever the mode couples to a dipole-allowed transition from a nondegenerate ground state, and the cavity-induced ground-state energy shift cannot increase with the cavity frequency at a fixed coupling vector, which is an exact constraint on approximate methods. Moreover, the incoherent photon statistics, which exclude the coherent part of the field, are never sub-Poissonian. At weak coupling, an exact resolvent expression reduces the squeezing and the ratio of the anomalous to the normal photon moment to linear-response properties of the isolated molecule, with the ratio set by a mean excitation energy. Time-dependent density functional theory with CAM-B3LYP and PBE0 reproduces exact and QED coupled-cluster references for both quantities to within 5% at 45 benchmark points. A survey of 29 molecules gives mean excitation energies of 9.5-21 eV at a cavity frequency of 2 eV and shows that the most polarizable molecules squeeze the field the most.

authors.name: Kurt R. Brorsen

papers.title: CRAFT-{\epsilon}: A Conformer-Resolved Atom- and Fragment-based Theory for the Static Relative Permittivity of Pure Organic Liquids
papers.summary: The static relative permittivity is an important property in thermodynamic modeling, electrochemistry, and solvent design, but predicting it directly from molecular structure remains challenging because both electronic polarization and molecular dipole orientation contribute to the measured response. Here, we introduce CRAFT-{\epsilon} (Conformer-Resolved Atom- and Fragment-based Theory for {\epsilon}), a conformer-resolved molecular descriptor model for predicting the static relative permittivity of neutral pure liquids. Conformer free energies, molecular dipoles, and atom-resolved polarizabilities are obtained from a GFN2-xTB/ALPB 10 workflow. The molecular dipole is decomposed into chemically defined polar-fragment vectors, allowing fitted corrections to retain both the magnitude and relative orientation of local dipolar contributions. Electronic and orientational polarization are combined with a group-contribution molar volume in the Onsager-Kirkwood-Fr\"ohlich relation. A staged parameterization with 41 parameters is applied to nonpolar, polar, and hydrogen-bonding compounds. For 1393 liquids with permittivities between 1.5 and 183, CRAFT-{\epsilon} reaches a five-fold cross-validated average absolute deviation of 2.40 ({R^2} = 0.93). Conformational averaging 15 is essential for liquids with several polar groups. Compared with an established fragment-based model with 139 parameters, it reaches a similar cross-validated RMSE (3.65 versus 3.41) with about a quarter of the parameters and applies to every liquid of the dataset. The resulting framework provides a computationally inexpensive route from molecular structure to liquid dielectric response and forms a basis for later application to solvent mixtures and electrolyte systems.

authors.name: Simon M\"uller

papers.title: Automated generation and execution of large-scale semidefinite programs for variational two-electron reduced density matrix theory
papers.summary: The variational two-electron reduced density matrix (v2RDM) method provides a wave-function-free approach to the description of strong electron correlation whose computational cost scales polynomially with the number of correlated orbitals. Here, we present an automated pipeline for the generation and execution of semidefinite programs (SDPs) associated with the v2RDM problem. Algebraic constraints encoding ensemble $N$-representability conditions are generated via the p$^\dagger$q second-quantized algebra package, and the p$^\dagger$q-generated expressions are automatically translated into a sparse-matrix representation that can be digested by an appropriate SDP solver. We have implemented a boundary-point SDP (BPSDP) solver in the libsdp package that can execute the v2RDM SDPs on either CPU or GPU hardware. We apply the code in several contexts. First, two-particle conditions are used to describe the 76-orbital model of the iron-molybdenum cofactor (FeMoco) of nitrogenase, the simulation of which requires roughly 25 hours of compute time on a single Nvidia H100 GPU. Second, the performance of high-order (four-particle positivity) conditions is evaluated on a challenging two-dimensional H$_{10}$ cluster problem. Lastly, new classes of positivity constraints for mixed fermion-boson systems are generated and applied within the context of ab initio cavity quantum electrodynamics simulations.

authors.name: A. Eugene DePrince III, Nicholas C. Rubin

papers.title: Physics-informed neural network (PINN) approximations of capillary menisci in polygonal channels
papers.summary: A capillary interface must satisfy both its curvature equation and the contact angle at the container walls. We study how strong-form physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) approximate these conditions when the prescribed equilibrium is geometrically incompatible. In zero gravity, the Concus-Finn critical contact angles for spanning graphs in square and equilateral-triangular cross-sections are respectively 45 degrees and 60 degrees. Below these angles, classical subdomain flux balance yields a certified lower bound on the continuous combined interior and wall residual loss, retaining the sampling densities and wall weight. The subdomain bounds and their sums over disjoint regions tend uniformly to zero as the contact angle approaches the threshold from below at fixed wall weight. The computed PINNs return smooth graphs with finite axial extent in the nonexistence regime: small interior residuals coexist with corner wall-flux deficits, where the adjoining contact-angle conditions demand more flux than a finite-slope graph can supply. At the default wall weight, several degrees into this regime, neural losses computed by quadrature are 1.6-1.8 times the bound from one cut per corner, with higher ratios occurring near the critical angle. Polynomial least-squares comparisons support the same geometric interpretation in a second smooth trial family. The bound supplies a physical scale for the residual compromise and explains why residual assessment must include wall flux and continuum compatibility.

authors.name: Zijian Liu, Julian Olszewski, Jie Xu

papers.title: Yb/Sr optical clock comparison at 2.08E-18 uncertainty over a 1350-km fiber link
papers.summary: Redefining the International system of Units (SI) second requires independent frequency-ratio measurements between clocks based on different laboratories, with an overall uncertainty below 5E-18, to validate individual clock evaluations through consistency checks. Reaching this uncertainty over long distances has remained challenging. So far, comparisons at this level have been achieved only a few times, between co-located clocks, and their results disagree markedly. Previous high-precision comparisons have therefore been limited to local or kilometre-scale links. Here we compare a ytterbium optical lattice clock in Wuhan with a strontium optical lattice clock in Shanghai over a phase-stabilized fiber link spanning 1350 km, and determine the Yb/Sr frequency ratio to be 1.207 507 039 343 337 716 0(26), with a Bayesian statistical uncertainty of 1.14E-18 and a total uncertainty of 2.18E-18. To our knowledge, this is the first intercity long distance frequency-ratio measurement, whose total uncertainty reaches the level required by the redefinition roadmap. The measured ratio exhibits a significant correlation with Earth tides and its response agree with the model within the statistical uncertainty. At intercity scale, this comparison demonstrates the capability of an optical-clock network for frequency comparison and Earths gravitational-potential sensing, a key step toward a wide-area optical-clock network.

authors.name: Lei Hou, Xiang-Pei Liu, Zhuan-Xian Xiong, Fa-Xi Chen, Wen-Xuan Song, Jian-Yu Guan, Qiang Zhu, Yu-Chen Zhang, Xiang Zhang, Bing Wang, De-Zhi Xiong, De-Quan Kong, Jia-Hao Zhang, Long-Fei Liao, Shao-Mao Wang, Xing-Yang Cui, Ping Xu, Peng Liu, Jie Li, Xiao Jiang, Ling-Xiang He, Li-Bo Li, Qi Shen, Youchao Xie, Lei Wang, Sheng-Kai Liao, Juan Yin, Cheng-Zhi Peng, Wen-Bin Shen, Bao-Long Lu, Han-Ning Dai, Yu-Ao Chen, Qiang Zhang, Hai-Feng Jiang, Jian-Wei Pan

papers.title: Integer electron-count cuts in variational second-order reduced-density-matrix theory. I. Molecular dissociation with fixed real-space and orbital partitions
papers.summary: Van Aggelen et al. [Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. 11, 5558 (2009)] showed that variational second-order reduced-density-matrix (2-RDM) calculations with the standard two-index conditions dissociate diatomic molecules into fractionally charged atoms with energies far below the exact limit, a drastic violation of size consistency; the proposed subsystem constraints require auxiliary calculations with the physical fragment Hamiltonians. We show that two long-known ingredients, combined, remove most of this failure without such calculations: the requirement that the number of electrons in a part of the molecule be an integer, imposed as linear conditions on the 2-RDM, and a chemically motivated partition of the molecule into atomic regions bounded at the bond critical point of the Hartree-Fock density. In a minimal basis, compared with full configuration interaction, a single such condition reduces the energy errors of NO$^+$ and CN$^-$ at 6 {\AA} from 108.9 and 80.7 m$E_\mathrm{h}$ to less than 0.02 m$E_\mathrm{h}$. In N$_2^+$, whose fragments have the correct mean population but too small a fluctuation, the region and three-index conditions act complementarily, reducing the error at 4 {\AA} from 138.0 to 1.6 m$E_\mathrm{h}$. At the separated-atom limit, the region cuts make the $P$, $Q$, $G$ energy additive over the fragments to within 0.2 m$E_\mathrm{h}$ in 7 of 10 systems, 3 already nearly additive without cuts; adding the $T_1$ and $T_2$ conditions also makes CO nearly additive, while a nonadditive error remains for N$_2^+$ and CO$^+$. Effective partitions are those whose condition is nearly saturated by the exact state.

authors.name: Maho Nakata

papers.title: LADA: A differential algebra-based simulation package for arbitrary-order charged-particle and light optics
papers.summary: LADA computes charged-particle and light-optical transfer maps by differential algebra in Python, with run-time order selection validated through order nine. It combines these established map methods with ATIMA-based stopping, straggling and scattering, the GLOBAL, CHARGE and ETACHA charge-state models, EPAX fragmentation, six-dimensional integration through measured or computed RF fields with reference-energy rebasing, and section-wise particle tracking with aperture and RF-window losses. Maps retain analytic dependence on external parameters; contraction with input moments gives beam observables and their sensitivities without particle tracking at each setting. Lattice import from COSY, MAD-X, Xsuite and MIRKO provides per-record status and comparisons with available codes. NumPy is the only required dependency. On the HHT benchmark, where the maps of both codes agree in every coefficient through ninth order, the optional compiled DA kernel on eight cores is 1.5 to 1.6 times faster than COSY at orders 3 to 9. Applications include the SIBAF irradiation facility through CALINA, proton microscopy and beam-line studies at GSI and FAIR.

authors.name: Dmitry Varentsov, Sergey Litvinov, Maksym Miski-Oglu, Sergiy Trotsenko

papers.title: Contrast-Enhanced Nonlinear Imaging with Moir\'e Flat-Band Superlattices
papers.summary: Nonlinear metasurfaces offer a compact platform for infrared-to-visible conversion and imaging, yet resonant enhancement is often accompanied by restricted angular acceptance, limiting the range of transverse spatial frequencies that can interact efficiently with the nonlinear modes. Here, we address this challenge using a one-dimensional photonic moir\'e superlattice supporting multiple quasi-flat bands in the near-infrared. These moir\'e modes combine strong near-field enhancement with broad momentum-space accessibility, enabling efficient third-harmonic generation (THG) while maintaining stable excitation over a large angular range. Experimentally, we observe strong THG emission near $467~\mathrm{nm}$ under broadband excitation from $ 1180$ to $ 2000~\mathrm {nm} $. We further employ the nonlinear moir\'e superlattice for infrared imaging by converting an infrared target into visible through the THG process. By encoding image information into displacement-dependent THG signals and decoding their spatial variations, we experimentally resolve weak features and internal textures with improved contrast compared with THG imaging using nonlinear films or conventional nonlinear metasurfaces. These results establish photonic moir\'e superlattices as a versatile platform combining efficient frequency conversion, broad angular acceptance, and mode-sensitive spatial encoding for high-contrast, label-free nonlinear imaging with enhanced feature discrimination.

authors.name: Amin Zamani, Lihang Feng, Jianji Liu, Ze Zheng, Gabriel Sanderson, Mohsen Rahmani, Peilong Hong, Lei Xu

papers.title: Dispersive Corrections to Electromagnetic Energy and Power Flux Are Imprints of Eliminated Degrees of Freedom
papers.summary: In a spatially dispersive medium the electromagnetic energy and flux are given by the frequency and wave-vector derivatives of the constitutive parameters, a result known as the Agranovich--Ginzburg (AG) formulas. Here, we clarify the physical meaning of the derivative terms in these relations and show that they measure the energy and flux carried by the degrees of freedom of the internal field-matter dynamics that the Maxwellian constitutive description hides. We construct an extended state-space model of such dynamics for a wide class of temporally and spatially dispersive media, from which the Maxwellian constitutive relations follow upon elimination of the internal variables, the effective material operator resulting from the Schur complement of the eliminated internal block. A congruence identity relates this complement to the extended state-space description, which allows us to extend the AG formulas to general bianisotropic media and to establish the conditions of their validity in the presence of dissipation. The AG dispersive corrections are thus the imprints of the eliminated degrees of freedom rather than independent constitutive postulates. They hold for fields driven at arbitrary real frequency and wave vector, and not only for eigenmodes, provided that the sources act on the fields alone and that any dissipation is carried by the electromagnetic subsystem. We verify the construction on the Lorentz, Drude, magnetized-plasma, and hydrodynamic models, the last of which describes a nonlocal metal. Additionally, a bianisotropic omega-medium and a capacitively loaded wire medium are treated in the Supplemental Material.

authors.name: Stanislav Maslovski, Constantin Simovski

papers.title: Domain-Adapted Deep Optical Flow for Multiphase Velocimetry in Unsteady Cloud Cavitation
papers.summary: Time-resolved velocimetry inside cloud cavitation is difficult because tracers do not penetrate vapor structures and deforming interfaces distort the particle images that PIV relies on. We present a domain-adapted deep optical flow framework for two-phase velocimetry, a RAFT model fine-tuned on synthetic image pairs rendered from multiphase OpenFOAM simulations (RAFT-CloudCav). It is compared with a pre-trained RAFT model, Farneb\"ack and OpenPIV on 130,000 frames/s recordings of a Venturi at 30 and 48 L/min. As no experimental ground truth exists, validation uses the integrated flow rate against a turbine meter, the liquid-phase velocity divergence and the station-to-station spread of the flow rate. The four methods agree within 2% in the liquid core and integrate to 41.6-43.2 L/min against a metered 48.0 $\pm$ 0.5 L/min, a shortfall common to all four that lies in the measurement and is partly traced to the coarse imaging configuration. RAFT-CloudCav gives the most consistent flow rate between stations (1.8% against 4.2-4.5%). The learned estimators reduce the liquid-phase divergence three- to seventeenfold relative to the classical ones, with the pre-trained model lowest, and OpenPIV under-reads the cavitating near-wall shear layer by up to 38%. Every method resolves the re-entrant jet in the instantaneous field. In a non-cavitating control the boundary layer is captured better as the imaging is refined, from three grid points across a 0.66 mm layer at 49 $\mu$m/pixel to twelve at 13 $\mu$m/pixel. The mean field is recovered without tracer particles to within 13%. Uncertainties are estimated a posteriori from the signed image residual and propagated conservatively.

authors.name: Naga Nitish Chamala, Sanjay Vasanth Kethanur Balasubramaniam, Olivier Coutier-Delgosha

papers.title: Multipole Decomposition of Moving Sources
papers.summary: Cartesian multipole moments are widely used to analyze and engineer radiation, but the usual relations for their radiated fields assume a wavevector-independent source frequency. For moving sources, Doppler shifts make the frequency depend on the wavevector, so the radiated fields predicted from the moments generally carry errors proportional to v/c. From charge conservation in the laboratory frame, we derive a multipole decomposition of moving sources that retains the usual moments but evaluates their contributions at Doppler-shifted wavenumbers and adds a convection-current term. Requiring no rest frame, it applies to moving matter and to excitation patterns in synthetic motion through media at rest, including superluminal ones. The decomposition also extends to nonuniform translation and to nonrigid patterns with curved spectral supports. Exact calculations for moving electric, magnetic, and toroidal dipoles confirm the decomposition and attribute the different radiation of a dipole in moving matter and in synthetic motion to the laboratory moments that each kind of motion induces. For an anapole, these moments decide whether it radiates. An anapole carried by uniformly moving matter remains nonradiating, whereas an excitation pattern with the same electric and toroidal dipoles radiates in synthetic motion. The decomposition thus makes multipolar analysis available for moving matter and for excitation patterns in synthetic motion, and it opens the way to designing their radiation.

authors.name: Shuhang Chen, Yutong Li, Xinmeng Wang, Qi Zhu

papers.title: Thermochemical Rossby waves in rapid rotation: from swallowtail geometry to nonlinear selection
papers.summary: When heat and solute both destabilise a rapidly rotating fluid, do their buoyancies add? Codensity models assume so, giving a straight onset diagonal; spherical shells show curved and kinked thresholds. We study the Busse-Simitev rotating annulus, whose normal modes obey an exact complex cubic dispersion relation. Combining the Bilharz criterion with the neutral-curve envelope yields, in the rapid-rotation limit, an explicit swallowtail wave front, in Arnold's sense, that bends the codensity diagonal into smooth and then kinked thresholds as the diffusivity ratio decreases. Its cusp edges lie inside the unstable domain and its exposed kink ends at the swallowtail singularity; these are singularities of wave-number selection, without coalescence of temporal eigenvalues, and the swallowtail diffusivity ratio has analytical small- and large-Prandtl-number limits. At a kink, broad, fast thermal and narrow, slow compositional Rossby waves become neutral together; hidden arcs mark the birth and merger of unstable wave-number bands. The same geometry enters nonlinear selection: mean-scalar feedback factors through neutral-arc normals and scalar responses, so the mean-profile coexistence margin is positive at every corner of the leading front and vanishes quadratically with the kink angle as the waves merge. Complete cubic coefficients predict robust coexistence at a reference corner and a narrow bistable interval near merger. Periodic-cell simulations away from merger confirm the coexisting waves and their invasion thresholds.

authors.name: Oleg N. Kirillov

papers.title: Distinguishing thyroid nodule malignancy using digital palpation
papers.summary: Accurate pre-operative diagnosis of thyroid nodules remains a major clinical challenge. Current diagnostic techniques rely on fine-needle aspiration and demonstrate high rates of inconclusive results, often leading to avoidable thyroidectomies with lifelong implications. Here, we introduce a mechanics-based diagnostic method that leverages Digital Palpation to determine malignancy and identify tissue subtypes in human thyroid nodules. From a cohort of patients undergoing thyroidectomies, we evaluated ex vivo thyroid specimens and processed the resulting mechanical data from 36 tests in 10 thyroid nodules. Principal Component Analysis reveals that these experimental results are distributed within a three-dimensional space of interpretable scalar features reflecting tissue grittiness, strength, and toughness, which map closely to descriptions of malignant and benign nodules given by clinicians. Our results further demonstrate that malignant nodules exhibit distinct mechanical signatures compared to their benign counterparts. This revealed a statistically significant difference (p = 9 x 10^-4) and separability (95% lower-bound Hedges' g = 1.08) between benign and malignant nodules along a direction in principal component space representing effective stiffness. Preliminary clustering patterns were also observed among malignant subtypes, including follicular, oncocytic, and papillary thyroid carcinomas. Together, these results highlight the potential of Digital Palpation as a novel mechanics-based method for tissue characterization and motivate its further development toward diagnostic applications.

authors.name: Brendan M. Unikewicz, Joseph E. Bonavia, Ekaterina L. Koelliker, Abigail Klein, Katie C. Spaeth, Hannah M. Varner, S. Kiana Naghibzadeh, Yoav Horev, Sareh Parangi, Tal Cohen

papers.title: marineGeochemFoam: A multipurpose framework for simulating reactive transport and biogeochemical cycling in marine sediments and at seawater-groundwater interfaces
papers.summary: We present marineGeochemFoam, an open-source reactive transport modeling framework for simulating early diagenesis, sediment burial, submarine groundwater discharge, and biogeochemical cycling in marine sediments and groundwater-seawater transition zones. The code is implemented in the widely used numerical toolbox OpenFOAM and extends the capabilities of the existing diagenetic models by supporting, among other features, i) coupled reactive transport of dissolved solute and solid species, (ii) a flexible native reaction package, supporting arbitrary reaction networks with n-th order and Monod-type kinetics, and (iii) coupling with an external geochemical code, PHREEEQC, providing access to a wide range of thermodynamically based geochemical processes. We benchmarked different features of the code across various examples with increasing complexity. Successively, the code was applied to two case studies reproducing field observations from the Hanko groundwater discharge site, Finland, and the Santa Barbara Basin, California. Beyond diagenetic applications, the code also serves as a general-purpose reactive transport simulator.

authors.name: Navid Ahmadi, Evgenii Kortunov, Karim Norouzi Moghanjoghi, Joonas J. Virtasalo, Muhammad Muniruzzaman

papers.title: Spontaneous mechanical patterning in active elastic tissues with stress feedback
papers.summary: The active mechanics of biological tissues is often governed by embedded active contractile fibers responding to mechanical feedback. We introduce a minimal model of a solid-like tissue where the mechanics is controlled by feedback of local active and elastic stresses on fiber organization. The resulting tissue generically exhibits a bistable response to external strain and spontaneously segregates into domains of orthogonally aligned fibers. Our theory thus provides a minimal mechanical feedback mechanism generating orthogonal structural alignment ubiquitous in biological tissues.

authors.name: Henrik Weyer, Divyoj Singh, M. Cristina Marchetti

papers.title: Feedback-induced mechanical bistability and perpendicular-domain formation in active elastic tissues
papers.summary: Contractile fibers in muscle tissues are highly aligned over the scale of many cells. Muscle layers surrounding organs with an inner lumen are often arranged in orthogonal directions. Here, we study a minimal mechanism of how structural order and its patterning into orthogonally aligned domains can emerge from mechanical feedback alone. The central idea is that contractile fibers align in the direction of the local active and elastic stresses, a feedback motivated by the maturation of muscle fibers under tension. We thus model muscle tissue as an active nematic solid with stress feedback: an elastic medium with embedded contractile fibers that are reinforced along the directions of the local tissue stresses. We find that the feedback from the contractile fiber stress is self-amplifying and drives spontaneous fiber alignment. Feedback from the elastic stress couples the alignment to the mechanical boundary conditions and tissue geometry. Depending on the mechanical boundary conditions, the elastic-stress feedback stabilizes two orthogonally aligned tissue states, resulting in a structurally and mechanically bistable tissue that shows a hysteretic stress-strain response. In spatially extended tissues, this bistability gives rise to orthogonally aligned domains separated by domain walls. Our results show that stress feedback can pattern structural order by coupling spontaneous alignment to the tissue geometry. Our mechanism thus provides a purely mechanical route to orthogonal fiber patterning in muscle tissues.

authors.name: Divyoj Singh, Henrik Weyer, Harry Kroft, M. Cristina Marchetti

papers.title: Data-driven non-contiguous photon-energy groups for fast multigroup radiation transport in line-dominated plasmas
papers.summary: Radiation transport in line-dominated plasmas, such as extreme ultraviolet (EUV) light source plasma, laser-fusion hohlraums, and stellar interiors, needs too many photon-energy groups for accurate radiation-hydrodynamic simulations. Our data-driven method assigns the bins of an opacity table to $K$ non-contiguous groups with fixed spectral shapes that never couple. Existing multigroup codes can use it by replacing the opacity table.In a radiation-hydrodynamic code, 30 such groups replaced 151 conventional groups; the energy conversion efficiency from laser to EUV changed by less than 0.5\% in absolute value.

authors.name: Shinsuke Fujioka, Yuji Takagi, Nozomi Tanaka, Akira Sasaki, Yu Yamamoto, Muhammad Fauzan Syahbana, Katsunobu Nishihara, Tomoyuki Johzaki, Atsushi Sunahara, Masashi Yoshimura

papers.title: Hybrid Machine Learning for Physically Consistent Prediction of Mutual Diffusion Coefficients in Binary Liquid Mixtures
papers.summary: Experimental data on mutual diffusion coefficients in liquid mixtures are scarce, and existing prediction methods are unreliable for non-ideal mixtures. Building on HADES, our hybrid model for self-diffusion coefficients, we introduce the Enhanced Vignes Equation (EVE), which augments the Vignes equation with a deep-set model. Its inputs are molecular descriptors derived from SMILES and activity-coefficient information from HANNA, a machine-learning model for activity coefficients. EVE predicts Maxwell-Stefan diffusion coefficients; the corresponding Fickian coefficients follow from the thermodynamic factor, likewise obtained from HANNA. Trained and evaluated on 2106 experimental data points for 123 binary mixtures, EVE outperforms all available semi-empirical models, halving the mean absolute relative error for mixtures without experimental infinite-dilution diffusion data. Combined with HADES, EVE yields the complete set of self- and mutual diffusion coefficients of a binary mixture from SMILES and pure-component viscosities alone. EVE and HADES are available at https://ml-prop.mv.rptu.de/, and the code is fully disclosed.

authors.name: Jens Wagner, Thomas Specht, Hans Hasse, Fabian Jirasek

papers.title: An Analytical Model for Fast Design Optimization and Performance Studies of nuSTORM
papers.summary: The concept of generating neutrino beams from stored muons (nuSTORM) has been explored for several decades. A few nuSTORM facilities have been designed for GeV muons, and a design of a sub-GeV nuSTORM, proposed for the European Spallation Source, is now underway. At low energy, the much larger beam divergence can significantly reduce the neutrino flux reaching the detector. Therefore, optimization of facility parameters is essential to avoid additional flux losses. This optimization, however, is not trivial due to the interdependency of the parameters. In this paper, we derive an analytical expression for the absolute neutrino flux incident on the detector front face and show how it can guide the optimization of a nuSTORM facility. The analytical expression is furthermore validated with published data and Monte Carlo simulations from five separate cases. In addition, we show how it can be extended to also predict the neutrino energy distribution at the detector, thus offering a convenient method to estimate the facility performance without time-consuming Monte Carlo simulations of particle transport and decay.

authors.name: ESSnuSB Collaboration, T. W. Choi, M. Olveg{\aa}rd, J. Aguilar, D. Bar\v{c}ot, E. Baussan, A. K. Bhattacharyya, M. Blennow, M. Bogomilov, B. Bolling, E. Bouquerel, F. Bramati, A. Branca, G. Brunetti, I. Bustinduy, C. J. Carlile, J. Cederkall, S. Choubey, P. Christiansen, I. Christodoulou, E. Cristaldo Morales, P. Cupia{\l}, D. D'Ago, H. Danared, J. P. A. M. de Andr\'e, E. Abad D\'iaz, M. Dracos, I. Efthymiopoulos, T. Ekel\"of, M. Eshraqi, G. Fanourakis, A. Farricker, E. Fasoula, T. Fukuda, S. Gago, N. Gazis, Th. Geralis, M. Ghosh, A. Giarnetti, O. Gilanliogullari, G. Vassilopoulos, S. Vihonen, J. Wurtz, V. Zeter, O. Zormpa

papers.title: Xenon energy-deposition widths in silicon: measurements and Geant4 comparisons
papers.summary: Energy-deposition fluctuations determine the isotope-separation capability of multilayer silicon detectors. We measure the central peak widths of $^{124}$Xe signals in 300- and 675-micrometre silicon layers at incident energies of approximately 152-274 MeV per nucleon and compare them with Geant4 11.4.0 electromagnetic option 4 (emopt4) and a calculation with explicit charge exchange. In the 300-micrometre detector, the emopt4 relative width of 1.844% exceeds the unselected experimental width of 1.407% by 31% and the selected width of 1.060% by 74%. For the 675-micrometre detector, selection windows around the downstream-signal peak, each approximately ten fitted first-plane standard deviations wide, give experimental upper estimates of 0.66-0.74%, compared with emopt4 predictions of 1.01-1.24%. Explicit charge-state transport gives widths of 0.889-0.932% for the thinner layer, depending on the incident charge distribution, and 0.59-0.63% for the thicker layer. These predictions are consistent with the experimental upper estimates, while emopt4 overestimates the widths for both thicknesses throughout the studied energy interval.

authors.name: Andrei Azhakin, Ilya Kudryashov, Dmitry Karmanov, Igor Kovalev

papers.title: CCGeant4: charge-state-resolved transport and energy-loss fluctuations of relativistic heavy ions in Geant4
papers.summary: CCGeant4 models energy-loss fluctuations of heavy ions in Geant4, accounting for both charge exchange and relativistic corrections to electron scattering beyond the first Born approximation. We use GLOBAL cross sections for electron capture and loss, ATIMA equilibrium stopping powers and charge-dependent delta-electron spectra calculated from the Dirac equation in a frozen-shell potential. The package also supports tabulated elastic ion-nucleus scattering. The silicon example includes interference between Coulomb and nuclear scattering amplitudes. We compare charge evolution with GLOBAL and energy-loss spectra with MOCADI for matched beams and targets. Experimental comparisons cover published energy-loss measurements and several measurements of energy deposited by xenon ions in silicon. For uranium at 800 MeV/u, the energy-loss variances from our Dirac configuration agree with published screened-ion calculations to within 4% in Be, Al and Pb. Both calculations lie within the reported experimental uncertainties for all three targets, while calculated bismuth spectra in silver are narrower than measured. Calculations in thin silicon layers show that delta-electron escape can make deposited-energy distributions substantially narrower than primary-ion energy-loss distributions, highlighting the importance of secondary-electron transport for detector-response modelling. The distribution includes the Geant4 source patch, the transport tables and their converters, and a runnable example.

authors.name: Andrei Azhakin, Ilya Kudryashov

papers.title: Flow Structure in Idealized Rotating Detonation Combustor with Supersonic Inflow
papers.summary: The work presented investigates the flow structure and stability of an airbreathing rotating detonation engine (RDE) in an idealized combustor. The presented derivation of a modified pressure cutoff injection scheme allows for supersonic injection in an idealized two-dimensional RDE as a function of a specified design Mach number and the pressure ratio across the injection surface. Numerical simulations are conducted using a compressible reacting flow solver with finite-rate chemistry built on an Adaptive Mesh Refinement (AMR) framework. The fuel mixture is set to a stoichiometric hydrogen-air mixture for all simulations. Stable operation occurs for a wide range of inflow conditions with inflow Mach numbers up to 4. The increased total temperature associated with increasing Mach numbers causes burning at the injection surface during the injector recovery process, resulting in unstable operation. Meanwhile, increasing total pressure facilitates sustained supersonic injection. Analysis of the steady flow structure shows a familiar structure with significant changes to the detonation structure when compared with a rocket RDE. With supersonic inflow, an oblique detonation wave (ODW) forms along the injection surface connected to the moving detonation through a slip line. Changes in the oblique detonation wave and normal detonation angle occur with changes in the inflow Mach number, however the overall detonation structure remains similar when supersonic injection occurs.

authors.name: Ruben A. Fernandez, Venkat Raman

papers.title: Dynamics and Statistical Mechanics of Born-Oppenheimer Auxiliary Velocities
papers.summary: In Born-Oppenheimer (BO) dynamics, auxiliary variables such as electron densities, induced polarization and electrode charges follow stationarity conditions, yet their time derivatives, such as currents, are physical observables. Using Mass-Zero constrained dynamics, we interpret these derivatives as explicit dynamical variables and derive the invariant measure giving their equilibrium statistical properties. We illustrate the framework in constant-potential molecular dynamics, where the electrode-charge velocities reproduce BO current fluctuations and the frequency-dependent admittance.

authors.name: Paula Sierra, Benjamin Rotenberg, Sara Bonella

papers.title: UV and deep-UV ultrafast harmonic generation enhanced by resonant gold nano-pillar metasurface
papers.summary: We report experimental observations and full-vector numerical simulations of second and third-harmonic generation from a two-dimensional periodic gold nano-pillar metasurface, for efficient ultrafast light conversion from near-infrared to the UV and deep-UV spectral ranges. The metasurface is designed to support an angle-tunable plasmonic resonance in the near-infrared spectral range, with its resonance wavelength shifting as a function of the pump angle of incidence. Under resonant conditions, strong electromagnetic-field confinement near the nano-pillar corners enhances the nonlinear light-matter interactions. Compared with a flat gold mirror, the nanostructured metal exhibits enhanced nonlinear frequency conversion, with conversion efficiencies of second and third-harmonic generation increased by two and three orders of magnitude, respectively. Full-wave theoretical modeling of linear and nonlinear light-matter interaction in nanoscale structures validates the experimental results. We demonstrate that periodically arranged square gold pillars can be engineered to achieve enhanced second and third-harmonic generation at wavelengths that can be tailored through the structural design, without requiring complex geometries or hybrid structures that pose fabrication challenges. The close agreement between theoretical predictions and experimental measurements further advances our understanding of surface-mediated nonlinear optical processes in metals and highlights the potential of metallic nanostructures as ultrafast light sources in the UV and deep-UV.

authors.name: Shroddha Mukhopadhyay, Yuxuan Chen, Hooman Barati Sedeh, Natalia M. Litchinister, Michael Scalora, Jose Trull, Maria Antonietta Vincenti, Crina Cojocaru

papers.title: Modeling stellar convective transport with plumes : II. Transport Properties of Locally and Non-locally driven Convection
papers.summary: We perform three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations of two idealized convection setups: a cooling-driven model (Model C) and an entropy-gradient-driven model (Model S). The two setups exhibit clear differences: while Model S develops large, relatively stationary eddies excited at depth, Model C is dominated near the surface by intermittent plume-like downflows that produce broad non-Gaussian velocity distributions and a turbulent energy flux that exceeds that in Model S by nearly an order of magnitude in the upper convection zone. Conventional gradient-diffusion (GD) closures reproduce the transport in Model S but significantly underestimate it in Model C, demonstrating that the plume-dominated transport realized in our cooling-driven setup cannot be reproduced by a local, gradient-based model. To address this, we introduce a Time-Space Double Averaging (TSDA) method that extracts coherent fluctuations, yielding a diagnostic variable $\tilde{\mathbf{u}}$ that peaks where the flux is largest. Building on this insight, we propose a modified GD closure in which the turbulent diffusivity is corrected by a plume-mediated term, achieving quantitative agreement with simulation results. Although the closure requires a calibrated model parameter and a careful choice of the averaging window, it provides a physically transparent framework that links coherent plume dynamics to mean-field transport and offers a pathway toward improved subgrid models for non-equilibrium stellar convection zones.

authors.name: Youhei Masada, Tomoya Takiwaki, Nobumitsu Yoko

papers.title: An auto-initializing algorithm to determine electronic ground states from random Slater determinants
papers.summary: Accurate quantum many-body calculations often depend on reliable reference states or good human-designed ans\"atze, yet such knowledge can become unreliable in hard problems like strongly correlated systems. Here we show that high-accuracy many-body ground states can be discovered directly from random Slater determinants. We introduce the Trimmed Configuration Interaction (TrimCI) method, which self-refines by iteratively expanding and trimming configurations in the variational space. TrimCI matches state-of-the-art accuracy using orders of magnitude fewer determinants and computer time: $10^6$-fold fewer than a recent quantum computing calculation on an iron-sulfur cluster, $10^5$-fold fewer than a leading classical method on a larger iron-sulfur cluster in nitrogenase, and over 99% of the ground-state energy of a strongly correlated lattice system from $10^{-28}$ of its Hilbert space, exceeding quantum Monte Carlo accuracy by orders of magnitude in some regimes. TrimCI thus provides an auto-initializing, accurate and highly efficient framework for quantum many-body systems, whose compact explicit wavefunctions enable direct and rapid evaluation of observables.

authors.name: Hao Zhang, Matthew Otten

papers.title: Towards superior van der Waals density functionals for molecular crystals
papers.summary: Ubiquitous van der Waals (vdW) interactions play a subtle yet crucial role in determining the precise atomic arrangements in solids, particularly in molecular crystals where these weak forces are the primary link between constituent building blocks. Within density functional (DF) theory, the most natural approach to address them is the use of vdW-inclusive density functionals. Through a detailed analysis of the underlying formalism, we have developed a computational scheme that combines vdW functionals of type DF1 and DF2 providing a readily tunable framework to improve the theoretical description and prediction of molecular crystals and other sparse materials. The proof of principle is demonstrated by benchmarking our method on the X23 dataset of molecular crystals.

authors.name: Dmitry V. Fedorov, Nikita E. Rybin, Mikhail A. Averyanov, Alexander V. Shapeev, Artem R. Oganov, Carlo Nervi

papers.title: Measuring Mixed-State Topological Invariant in Open Photonic Quantum Walk
papers.summary: Pure-state manifestations of geometric phase are well established and have found applications across essentially all branches of physics, yet their generalization to mixed-state regimes remains largely unexplored experimentally. The Uhlmann geometric phase offers a natural extension of pure-state paradigms and can exhibit a topological character. However, observation of this invariant is impeded by the incompatibility between Uhlmann parallel transport and Hamiltonian dynamics, as well as the difficulty of preparing topologically nontrivial mixed states. To address this challenge, we report an experimentally accessible protocol for directly measuring the mixed-state topological invariant. By engineering controlled nonunitary dynamics in a photonic quantum walk, we prepare topologically nontrivial mixed states from a trivial initial state. Then, by machine learning the full density matrix in momentum space, we directly extract the quantized geometric phase of the nontrivial mixed states. Furthermore, we observe that this transition of the quantized mixed-state topological invariant from a trivial to a nontrivial value is closely associated with the emergence of a topological kink structure. These results highlight a geometric phase framework that naturally extends to open quantum systems both in and out of thermal equilibrium.

authors.name: Qin-Qin Wang, Xiao-Ye Xu, Yong-Jian Han, Chuan-Feng Li, Guang-Can Guo

papers.title: Electronic structure, phase stability, and transport properties of the AlTiVCr lightweight high-entropy alloy: A computational study
papers.summary: We investigate the thermodynamics and phase stability of the AlTiVCr lightweight high-entropy alloy using a combination of ab initio electronic structure calculations, a concentration wave analysis, and atomistic Monte Carlo simulations. In alignment both with experimental data and with results obtained using other computational approaches, we predict a $\textrm{B2}$ (CsCl) chemical ordering emerging in this alloy at comparatively high temperatures, which is driven by Al and Ti moving to separate sublattices, while V and Cr express weaker site preferences. The impact of this $\textrm{B2}$ chemical ordering on the electronic transport properties of the alloy is investigated within a Kubo--Greenwood linear response framework and it is found that, counter-intuitively, the alloy's residual resistivity increases as the material transitions from the $\textrm{A2}$ (disordered bcc) phase to our predicted $\textrm{B2}$ (partially) ordered structure. Our results give fresh insight into the atomic-scale structure and consequent physical properties of this well-studied, technologically relevant material.

authors.name: Christopher D. Woodgate, Hubert J. Naguszewski, Nicolas F. Piwek, David Redka

papers.title: Adaptive dynamics of eco-evolutionary repeated games: Effect of reward and punishment
papers.summary: Long-term evolutionary processes can strongly influence common-pool resource conservation by generating new traits or behaviours that modify the feedback between population strategies and the resource state. Here we develop an eco-evolutionary framework in which individuals repeatedly interact with the same opponent and follow direct reciprocity through reactive strategies. The strategic dynamics is coupled to a renewable common resource and analyzed using adaptive dynamics. After our exhaustive non-linear dynamical analysis of $2\times2$ strategic games, we focus on comparative and combined usefulness of institutional incentives in the form of rewards and punishments in preventing the Tragedy of the Commons even when defection dominates in the replete resource state. We also report possibility of robust stable oscillations -- emerging via Hopf bifurcation -- in resource state and population strategies.

authors.name: Prosanta Mandal, Suman Chakraborty, Vaibhav Madhok, Sagar Chakraborty

papers.title: Quantum Algorithm Framework for Phase-Contrast Transmission Electron Microscopy Image Simulation
papers.summary: We present a quantum algorithmic framework for simulating phase-contrast transmission electron microscopy (CTEM) image formation using a fault-tolerant, gate-based quantum circuit model. The electron wavefield on an $N\times N$ grid is amplitude-encoded into a $2\log_2 N$-qubit register. Free-space propagation and objective-lens aberrations are implemented via two-dimensional quantum Fourier transforms (QFTs) and diagonal phase operators in reciprocal space, while specimen interaction is modeled under the phase-object approximation (POA) in a single-slice multislice formulation as a position-dependent phase grating. We validate projected potentials, contrast transfer function (CTF) behavior, and image contrast trends against classical multislice simulations for MoS$_2$ over experimentally relevant parameters, and provide resource estimates and key assumptions that determine end-to-end runtime. Extracting a complete $N\times N$ intensity image by direct sampling requires $O(N^2/\epsilon^2)$ repetitions, which rules out a generic polylogarithmic-cost image-generation algorithm. We therefore analyze end-to-end cost, including state preparation, repeated execution, measurement precision, and the best classical calculation of the same output, and identify the conditions under which limited-output tasks could be candidates for quantum advantage; the present benchmarks establish implementation agreement and do not demonstrate such an advantage. This framework provides a physics-grounded mapping from CTEM theory to quantum circuits and establishes a baseline for extending toward full multislice and inelastic scattering models.

authors.name: Sean D. Lam, Roberto dos Reis

papers.title: Nuclear interference by electronic de-orthogonalisation
papers.summary: Interference is a universal consequence of superposition, yet in composite quantum systems it can encode correlations between subsystems. We show that in coupled electron-nuclear dynamics, interference in the nuclear density can arise dynamically even when it is initially absent. Starting from a superposition of orthogonal Born-Oppenheimer electronic states, we demonstrate within the exact factorisation framework that genuine non-adiabatic electron-nuclear correlations induce de-orthogonalisation of the electronic factors, thereby generating interference terms in the nuclear density. Such interference has no counterpart in adiabatic evolution. Unlike conventional nuclear wave-packet interference or interference that merely reflects electronic coherence in a chosen basis, the effect identified here is a manifestation of the compositeness of the full electron-nuclear state. Nuclear density interference thus emerges as a direct dynamical signature of correlated quantum motion in composite systems.

authors.name: Matisse Wei-Yuan Tu, Angel Rubio, E. K. U. Gross

papers.title: Optical Magnus effect on gravitational lensing
papers.summary: The optical Magnus effect refers to a transverse shift of a trajectory of light caused by its polarization and arises as a correction to geometrical optics at the linear order in wavelength. Here, we start from Maxwell's equations in a curved spacetime to derive the equations of motion for a wave packet of circularly polarized light, which confirm the known results involving the helicity-dependent anomalous velocity with some generalization and clarification. We then study possible consequences of the optical Magnus effect on gravitational lensing in the Schwarzschild spacetime as well as in an expanding spacetime with a weak gravitational potential. Among others, by formulating a lens equation modified to incorporate the optical Magnus effect, the Einstein ring is found impossible to emerge from a point source for any axially symmetric thin lens. Analytic solutions to the modified lens equation are also obtained for simple lens models, illuminating how image formation is affected by the optical Magnus effect.

authors.name: Yusuke Nishida

papers.title: Scalable Hessian-vector products for tensor networks with application to quantum circuit compression
papers.summary: Optimizing tensor networks with standard first-order methods often leads to slow convergence and getting trapped in local minima.
