We show that a reference tetrad, that is a section of the tetrad solution space seen as a principal bundle over the metric one, always provides a lift free of this cocycle, so that the tetrad residual symmetry algebra is the semi-direct sum of the metric one and the ideal of field-dependent residual Lorentz transformations. The construction is independent of the gauge conditions, of the residual group, of the first-order Lagrangian, and reduces to the Kosmann lift on metric isometry generators. We illustrate it on a Weyl BMS-type solution space with time-dependent boundary metric, described in tetrad variables with a residual U(1) Lorentz freedom, for which the cocycle of a naive lift is computed and then explicitly removed.

authors.name: Antoine Vincenti

papers.title: Carroll Double Copy
papers.summary: We construct a double copy for Carroll gravity as the ``square'' of Carroll Yang-Mills theory at the linearised level. Starting from the convolutional double copy prescription in Lorentzian spacetime, we take the Carrollian limit $c \rightarrow 0$ to establish a double copy dictionary compatible both with symmetries and the corresponding equations of motion. Since this limit yields two distinct sectors, namely the electric and magnetic Carroll theories, we systematically investigate double copy constructions involving all possible combinations of these parent theories. To accommodate the time-independent on-shell configurations of the magnetic Carroll fields, we introduce a suitable regularisation procedure for the convolutional double copy. In addition, the covariance of the double copy under Carroll boosts requires an appropriate dressing of the fields, leading to the inclusion of a Goldstone-type object in the construction. We first develop the formalism using toy models involving scalar fields and then apply it to the double copy between linearised Carroll Yang-Mills theory and Carroll gravity.

authors.name: Sucheta Majumdar, Silvia Nagy, Giorgio Pizzolo

papers.title: Instant Folded Strings: Fractal Decay and ANEC Saturation
papers.summary: Instant Folded Strings (IFSs) present a puzzle. On the one hand, they appear to be an intrinsic part of string theory: they are fundamental closed strings nucleated classically in backgrounds in which the string coupling grows toward the future, and they have been argued to play an important role in black-hole interiors and cosmology. On the other hand, their energy-momentum tensor violates the Averaged Null Energy Condition (ANEC), placing IFSs in tension with standard causality and unitarity arguments. We show that finite string coupling resolves this tension by triggering a decay cascade that saturates the ANEC in Minkowski spacetime. The remnant of the original IFS persists indefinitely, continuously seeding a self-similar fragmentation cascade that produces infinitely many strings over its full history. In the semiclassical regime, the cascade is governed by a single Malthusian exponent, $\kappa_{\mathrm{IFS}}=2\sqrt{2}-2$, which controls the branching growth, pressure decay, cutoff-ANEC convergence, and anomalous non-integer dependence on the string coupling. The complete state has vanishing total energy and momentum while remaining highly excited and carrying negative integrated pressure on every finite time slice. This provides a concrete example of genuinely stringy low-energy dynamics in which microscopic null-energy consistency coexists with macroscopic negative pressure.

authors.name: Nissan Itzhaki, Uri Peleg

papers.title: The Shape of the Strongly Coupled MQM Ground State
papers.summary: We study a surprisingly efficient family of variational ansatze for the ground state of bosonic matrix quantum mechanics at large $N$. These are ansatze whose norm-squared probability distributions are themselves matrix integrals with single-trace actions, and so have their own independent `t Hooft expansions. They are efficient in the sense that optimizing over a small number of parameters produces many digits of accuracy for the energy, single-trace moments, and connected correlators. For infinite-$N$ planar data our results rapidly converge to within published bootstrap intervals and stabilize to a few digits of precision beyond them. We also demonstrate that we can efficiently capture $1/N$ corrections by computing connected two-point functions. These are matched against resummed quantum perturbation theory and Monte Carlo simulations.

authors.name: Alexander Frenkel

papers.title: Self-interacting $p$-forms and the shear-free anisotropic cosmological model
papers.summary: The cosmological principle may require more than observations demand: what is needed is isotropic expansion without vorticity. Extended Friedmann-Lemaitre-Robertson-Walker (eFLRW) cosmologies realise this with a non-vanishing anisotropic spatial curvature that is balanced by an anisotropic stress while the shear vanishes. Thorsrud and others investigated such scenarios for free differential $p$-forms. Here we extend the analysis to non-Abelian $p$-forms ($p=0,\dots,4$) with self interactions. The balance requires the anisotropic stress to decay as $a^{-2}$, $a$ being the cosmological scale factor, which we combine with the gauge-field continuity equation. The general results indicate that, in the presence of a potential, fine-tuning of the same is needed in order to balance the curvature. Notably, this is not the case for a $3$-form field $\underline{H}^a$ with a potential term $V(\underline{H}^2)=A+B\,\underline{H}^2$, where $A$ and $B$ are constants: in Bianchi class A, an uncharged 3-form balances the curvature with this potential without any tuning, and a charged one does so for a suitably chosen connection. This is the only candidate we have found where the potential does not require tuning. It is also an interesting candidate as it can be interpreted as a cosmological constant in combination with a dark-matter sector mimicking curvature.

authors.name: Nicolas Hernandez (Universidad Industrial de Santander, Centro de Investigacion Cientifica y de Educacion Superior de Ensenada), Ben D. Normann (Norwegian University of Science and Technology), Yeinzon Rodriguez (Universidad Industrial de Santander, Universidad Antonio Narino)

papers.title: Relaxation of Quantum Observables in a 4D Black Hole that forms from Collapse of a Null Shell
papers.summary: The vacuum polarization and luminosity are computed in a four-dimensional spacetime where a spherically symmetric null shell contracts to form a black hole. This is done by computing the contribution of the spherically symmetric modes of a massless minimally coupled scalar field to the quantities $\la \phi^2 \ra_{\rm in} - \la \phi^2 \ra_U$ and $L_{\rm in} - L_U$. Here the subscript ``in'' denotes the {\it in} vacuum state for the null shell spacetime and the subscript ``U'' denotes the Unruh state in Schwarzschild spacetime. The computation is done outside the null shell and outside the event horizon where the spacetime geometry is the Schwarzschild geometry. It is found that, as expected, these differences approach zero at late times. However, they do so significantly more slowly than in the two-dimensional case where there is no scattering of the mode functions. In both cases, the difference is dominated by a quasinormal mode at intermediate times and a tail term at late times that decays quartically in time. For the luminosity difference, an analytic calculation verifies the late-time result for the tail term.

authors.name: Shohreh Gholizadeh Siahmazgi, An{\i}l Zengino\u{g}lu, Paul R. Anderson, Alessandro Fabbri

papers.title: Gauge aspects of teleparallel gravity and Noether's second theorem
papers.summary: We examine the gauge structure of the Teleparallel Equivalent of General Relativity (TEGR) from the perspective of Noether's second theorem. We show that diffeomorphisms and local Lorentz transformations are the gauge symmetries of TEGR, as these are the only variational symmetries that give rise to Noether identities. We then discuss the distinct roles of these two symmetries and their implications for the gauge-theoretic interpretation of gravity. Finally, we discuss consequences of these observations for the role of translations in gauge theories of gravity and the coupling of matter in TEGR. In particular, we demonstrate that the matter coupling prescription is uniquely determined and coincides with that of general relativity, including in the case of spinor fields.

authors.name: Sebastian Brezina, Martin Kr\v{s}\v{s}\'ak

papers.title: Kalb-Ramond black bounces: throat-blind shadows and throat-sensitive neutrinos
papers.summary: Regularizing a black hole removes its singularity, but which observations could detect the regularized core? We address this question for a Simpson-Visser black bounce built on the power-law hairy black hole that a Lorentz-violating Kalb-Ramond background produces. Measured in the areal radius, the bounce leaves the metric function untouched and changes only the radial measure. This single fact sorts the observables into two classes. The shadow, the innermost stable orbit, orbital frequencies and gravitational redshifts are blind to the throat. The instability of the photon ring, the brightness of its subrings, the oscillation phase of neutrinos and the energy deposited by neutrino pair annihilation respond to it through one universal factor. We derive an exact law for the subring demagnification that holds for any metric function. We also show that the throat enters the weak-field neutrino phase and the light deflection with different weights, so that combined photon and neutrino lensing can separate the mass from the throat. Ray-traced polarized images of a turbulent thin disk confirm that the direct image hides the throat while the first subring reveals it. For neutrinos emitted near a stellar-mass compact object the throat reshapes the flavor survival pattern and enhances the annihilation energy deposition. Two independent computations reproduce each headline number.

authors.name: Faizuddin Ahmed, Ahmad Al-Badawi, \.{I}zzet Sakall\i

papers.title: Metric perturbations in Einstein-Hilbert gravity: An alternative perturbative formulation
papers.summary: We derive the ordinary gauge-fixed quadratic operators of the four-dimensional Einstein--Hilbert action in exponential and inverse-metric-density variables on an arbitrary reference background. With a single nonlinear background-harmonic gauge transported through the exact field map, the density operator is the trace-reversed Lichnerowicz operator, while the exponential operator contains an additional algebraic Ricci-curvature term. This difference arises from the nonlinear transformation of the background tadpole and vanishes on Ricci-flat backgrounds; a cosmological-constant check gives the corresponding cancellation at Einstein saddles. The construction retains the exact determinant contribution and specifies the associated Faddeev--Popov operator. At the first interacting order on a flat background, we show that the two gauge-fixed cubic actions differ by a term proportional to the free field equation, and independently evaluate the same nonzero three-point coefficient in both variables, with its normalization matched to the Einstein-gravity interaction. An exact Schwarzschild configuration satisfies the same background-harmonic gauge and is stationary under unrestricted exterior variations of the gauge-fixed action. Its density and exponential reconstructions are checked together with the bulk and boundary terms; a separate radial variation illustrates the loss of an equation after imposing a restricted ansatz. These results provide an explicit comparison of established field coordinates at the classical and tree levels; quantum loop calculations additionally require a common measure, regulator and source prescription.

authors.name: Sergey Bondarenko, Raghvendra Singh

papers.title: Thermodynamics and interior structure of density-responsive regular black holes
papers.summary: This work studies regular black holes motivated by the scalar sector of density-responsive gravity (DRG). An algebraic prescription with phenomenological local running maps a Gaussian matter profile to a diagnostic density profile. A pressure check shows that this profile does not solve the full static DRG equations. It serves only to select an effective metric family with two horizons. The extremal mass is calibrated to $M_{\min} = \sqrt{1+A/2}\,M_{\mathrm{P}} \simeq 1.006\,M_{\mathrm{P}}$, where $A=0.024$ is the historical scalar response amplitude. A fit to $\rho(r) = \rho_0\exp[-(r/r_c)^n]$ selects $n=2$. The temperature is nonmonotonic, reaching $T_H^{\max}=0.02547\,M_{\mathrm{P}}$ at $M=1.332\,M_{\mathrm{P}}$ before vanishing at $M_{\min}$. The calculation verifies the generic scaling near extremality $\mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{tr}}\propto(M-M_{\min})^{-1/2}$ of a static lapse diagnostic for $n=2,3,4,6$ and for the Hayward and Bardeen controls. A regulated integral of coordinate time between the horizons provides a static cavity diagnostic, not a prediction of echoes of gravitational waves. The remaining area entropy equals the area entropy already lost at $M_{\mathrm{cross}}/M_0=0.707107\simeq1/\sqrt{2}$. This geometric crossing does not establish a Page curve or unitarity. The endpoint area entropy is below $2.6\%$ of the initial Bekenstein-Hawking entropy for $M_0 = 5\,M_{\mathrm{P}}$ and below $0.03\%$ for $M_0 = 50\,M_{\mathrm{P}}$. An inverse source reconstruction confirms an isotropic core of de Sitter type but retains the pressure mismatch. An exploratory collapse calculation with an imposed bounce factor produces bounded configurations with $1-2m/r<0$ without establishing formation of the calibrated geometry. The robust results are the calibrated thermodynamics and generic scaling near extremality.

authors.name: Martin Drobczyk

papers.title: Holographic Einstein rings of a covariant quantum corrected AdS black hole
papers.summary: We investigate holographic Einstein rings in a covariant quantum corrected Schwarzschild--AdS$_4$ spacetime using a massless scalar probe. At fixed horizon radius $r_h$, the deformation parameter $\zeta$ leaves the metric mass parameter, coordinate surface gravity, and photon sphere radius unchanged, while increasing the photon potential maximum and the asymptotic lapse coefficient $A=1+\zeta^2$. The critical coordinate impact parameter approaches $A^{-1/2}$ for large black holes, whereas the corresponding incidence angle in the normalized boundary frame approaches $\pi/2$. Ray tracing and local WKB barrier data recover the same geometric scale. Quasinormal spectra computed with AdS boundary conditions provide a comparison at finite multipole number. These results separate the finite radius effect of the deformation from the change in boundary time normalization.

authors.name: Zhenglong Ban, Xiaomei Liu, Rong-Jia Yang

papers.title: Nonperturbative lattice simulation of the nucleation rate in thermal first-order phase transitions
papers.summary: We present a nonperturbative lattice study of vacuum decay through bubble nucleation in a three-dimensional real scalar field theory at finite temperature. The vacuum decay rate is computed by combining an expanded-ensemble multicanonical hybrid Monte Carlo approach, which samples the critical bubble configurations, with real-time Langevin dynamics, which follows the subsequent bubble evolution. We extrapolate the nucleation rate to the continuum limit and compare it with the corresponding one-loop perturbative prediction, finding a discrepancy of about \(8\%\).

authors.name: Jing Zhou, Ligong Bian

papers.title: Skyrmions coupled to the sigma meson
papers.summary: We propose a geometric coupling of the Skyrme model of nuclei to the scalar--isoscalar sigma meson by identifying the sigma field with the radial length of the chiral four-vector while preserving the topological protection of the baryon number. Restricting to the $B=1$ hedgehog ansatz, an asymptotic analysis of the field equations shows that the in-vacuum sigma mass $m_\sigma$ is replaced inside the nucleon by an effective in-medium mass $m_{\sigma,{\rm eff}} = 2m_\pi$. Full numerical integration via a double-shooting method and parameter optimization demonstrate that including the sigma meson leads to a remarkable improvement in the description of nucleon observables and to a pion decay constant very close to its physical value.

authors.name: Christoph Adam, Carlos Naya, Thomas Winyard

papers.title: Beyond the Onsager matrix: All-order resummation of relativistic particle and energy diffusion
papers.summary: We study the coupled diffusion of particle number and energy carried by ultrarelativistic probe particles propagating through a material medium. The probes undergo elastic scattering, which randomizes their direction, and inelastic scattering, which exchanges energy with the medium while preserving particle number. We compute exactly the full $2\times2$ frequency- and wave-number-dependent diffusivity matrix, resumming the constitutive gradient expansion to all orders. In a particularly natural Onsager-normalized basis of conserved densities, the resummed matrix is found to be diagonal at arbitrary frequency and wave number, even though particle and energy transport remain coupled and the conventional Onsager matrix has nonzero thermoelectric cross coefficients. Beyond the hydrodynamic limit, the resummed diffusivities resolve microscopic relaxation timescales and the ballistic kinetic continuum that are invisible to the ordinary Onsager coefficients.

authors.name: Lorenzo Gavassino

papers.title: Asymptotic stability of axisymmetric perturbations of near-horizon extremal Kerr with a Schwarzian-deformed throat
papers.summary: We study the asymptotic stability of axisymmetric gravitational perturbations of the near-horizon geometries of (near-)extremal Kerr black holes and consider the family of backgrounds in which the AdS$_{2}$ factor of NHEK is deformed by a Schwarzian mode. Requiring the Killing parameter to be local in the background makes the Gelfand--Dikii polynomials natural solutions of the Killing equation, and that locality requirement brings stationary solutions of the Korteweg-de Vries equation. The hierarchy selects a family of backgrounds, which remain $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R})\times \mathfrak{u}(1)$ throughout them: the first level gives NHEK and near-NHEK, the second, solitons that depart from one of these geometries and return to it. We linearize Einstein's equations around this family, where the axisymmetric sector reduces to a wave equation on the nearly-AdS$_{2}$ base, and analyze this equation by energy and virial methods. For NHEK we obtain a conserved energy, an integrated local energy estimate and asymptotic stability in a weighted norm; for a nonconstant Schwarzian the energy becomes a Lyapunov functional whose monotonicity is dictated by the sign of its derivative, yielding uniform bounds for integrable ones, and mild local decay along the KdV soliton. We also find a monotone horizon-localized norm, which is not of Aretakis type, showing that stability properties are directly sensitive to the near-horizon structure encoded in the Schwarzian background. We compute the associated Regge--Teitelboim charges at a late-time corner of the throat using a radial ADM foliation of the spacetime.

authors.name: Marcela C\'ardenas, Benjam\'in Cuevas-Tapia, Claudio Mu\~noz, Jessica Trespalacios, Hanne Van Den Bosch

papers.title: The fate of hidden symmetries under magnetic Harrison transformations
papers.summary: Solution-generating transformations construct new geometries from known seeds, raising the question of whether and to what extent the resulting solutions inherit the hidden symmetries underlying the seeds' integrability and separability. We have established universal perturbative inheritance laws for CKTs and massless scalar separability directly at the level of magnetic Harrison transformations, encompassing both magnetization of Carter-type seeds and demagnetization of conformal Carter-type seeds. In both magnetized Kerr and demagnetized Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson, this perturbative inheritance coexists with the loss of exact Carter-type separability, while seed-connected conformal Killing-Yano structures are already obstructed at the same perturbative order. These results reveal a hierarchy in the perturbative survival of hidden symmetries and provide a framework for investigating their inheritance in more general theoretical settings and under other solution-generating transformations.

authors.name: Shoulong Li, Fangkang Yu, Hong-Da Lyu

papers.title: Two-scale system: compactified ambient metrics and Scri/Spi/Ti
papers.summary: We show that certain geometric constructions, including the Fefferman-Graham ambient metric, Brinkmann spaces, and ultrastatic vacuum spacetimes, admit natural conformal compactifications and can be unified within a single framework arising naturally from conformal geometry. The framework is based on a two-scale system comprising two weight-one conformal scalars satisfying almost-Einstein equations and certain regularity conditions. As a particular instance of this unifying framework, we obtain a new ambient construction for Spi and Ti, the extended spatial and temporal infinities of Ricci-flat spacetimes. A remarkable feature of this construction is that Spi/Ti and the null infinity of the corresponding spacetimes are naturally realised as a boundary face and the corner of the two-scale ambient space, respectively. We also demonstrate how the two-scale system can serve as a background ambient geometry for studying the asymptotic behaviour of (gauge) fields at spatial, temporal, and null infinity.

authors.name: Xavier Bekaert, Maxim Grigoriev, Mikhail Markov

papers.title: Unruh-induced decoherence and entanglement degradation in Ramsey interferometry
papers.summary: We propose a modified Ramsey interferometric protocol to probe decoherence associated with the Unruh effect through fringe visibility. The scheme employs Unruh-DeWitt detectors coupled to a massless scalar field in the Minkowski vacuum through an interaction that induces pure dephasing without transitions between their internal energy levels. For a uniformly accelerated detector with finite spatial extent, an analytical dephasing function separates inertial vacuum fluctuations from the thermal Unruh contribution. When the thermal contribution dominates, fringe visibility decays exponentially with a rate proportional to the proper acceleration. The bipartite extension considers two detectors initially prepared in a Bell state, one inertial and the other uniformly accelerated, while retaining correlations mediated by the scalar field. In particular, we find that the joint fringe visibility coincides exactly with concurrence when the cross-term contribution disappears. This suggests that the entanglement degradation can be quantified directly from the interference contrast.

authors.name: E. D. C Brand\~ao, O. P. de S\'a Neto, F. C. E. Lima, H. A. S. Costa

papers.title: A Stable Vector Bounce
papers.summary: We construct a geodesically complete bounce in cubic generalised Proca theory with a free canonical scalar as the matter field. The temporal vector evolves along its algebraic constraint and supports the transition from contraction to expansion while matter obeys the null energy condition. This evolution permits nonzero derivative mixing at the bounce. The kinetic coefficients are positive at every finite time for all nonzero comoving wavenumbers, and short-wavelength perturbations are stable throughout the solution. Following the linear equations to both infinite-time limits also shows that local perturbations are bounded for all nonzero comoving wavenumbers.

authors.name: Nils A. Nilsson

papers.title: $Q$-operators, cluster mutations, and flavored Toda chain
papers.summary: We construct Baxter $Q$-operators for a family of quantum cluster integrable systems, that we call the flavored Toda chains, associated with quivers $\mathcal{Q}_N[F]$, where $F\subseteq\{2,\dots,N\}$ specifies data of $\vert F \vert$ additional nodes compared to $\mathcal{Q}_N[\varnothing]$ for the ordinary $N$-particle open $q$-deformed Toda chain. A distinguished sequence of quantum cluster mutations yields an ordered product of Faddeev's quantum dilogarithms. We prove that these operators form a commuting family and that their shifted quotients are transfer matrices whose coefficients are commuting Hamiltonians. We identify these transfer matrices with matrix elements of products of explicit local Lax matrices of rank two. Local cluster transformations move flavor insertions along the chain while preserving their ordered flavor parameters and the transfer matrix together with the canonical transformation. We also derive integral kernels for the $Q$-operators and evaluate an associated Fourier transform as a factorized scalar $Q$-function. Finally, we relate the quivers to the BPS quivers of five-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ gauge theories in the decoupling limit and identify the normalized scalar $Q$-function with the perturbative contribution of a canonical codimension-two defect wrapping a squashed three-sphere.

authors.name: Saebyeok Jeong, Taro Kimura, Norton Lee

papers.title: Black holes in Myrzakulov $F(R,T)$ gravity
papers.summary: We investigate vacuum black-hole solutions in metric-affine Myrzakulov $F(R,T)$ gravity (MG-I), where $R$ is the affine Ricci scalar and $T$ is a quadratic torsion invariant, not the trace of the matter energy-momentum tensor. For the polynomial model $F(R,T)=\alpha R+\beta T+\gamma T^3$, with $\alpha\neq0$, we first vary the metric and all components of the independent affine connection, and only then specialize to metric-compatible geometry with totally antisymmetric torsion. Nonzero axial torsion admits an exceptional branch $\alpha+\beta+3\gamma T_*^2=0$, on which the metric satisfies the Einstein equations with effective cosmological parameter $\Lambda_*=\gamma T_*^3/\alpha$. We establish a local existence result and construct torsionful Schwarzschild-(anti-)de Sitter representatives that are smooth through a selected future Killing horizon. Within the spherically symmetric axial ansatz, we characterize Ricci-symmetric affine connections by the condition $(fV-U)'=0$ and compare a constant-$W=fV-U$ family with a constant-$U$ family. Although these connections share the same metric and torsion scalar, their affine curvature invariants generally differ. Independent coordinate-level curvature contractions and component tests of the unrestricted metric and connection variations corroborate the identities used in the construction; these checks complement the analytic variational derivation. Finally, we identify null directions of the restricted axial quadratic form and distinguish this degeneracy from a complete metric-affine stability analysis. Our conclusions are local and do not establish global extendibility, physical inequivalence of all torsion profiles, or dynamical stability.

authors.name: Alexandre Landry, Ratbay Myrzakulov

papers.title: A Numerical Approach to Quantization
papers.summary: We introduce a numerical approach that simultaneously searches for matrix quantizations and compatible Poisson structures on classical geometric surfaces. Our method identifies irreducible Hermitian matrix representations and a trainable Poisson multiplier by minimizing a loss function that penalizes violations of the Casimir and commutation constraints. Through numerical investigations and subsequent theoretical analysis, we establish a no-go theorem showing that, for Weyl quantized fuzzy spheres with nondegenerate axial spectrum, the matrix dimension cannot exceed the degree of the nonconstant polynomial axial Poisson multiplier. We further extend our approach to nonpolynomial Poisson multipliers, demonstrating its versatility and potential to drive novel discoveries. Although here we focus on Weyl quantized fuzzy spheres, the framework is extensible to general geometric manifolds and quantization schemes. Our approach also provides a practical starting point for investigating Schild string theory and the quantization of spacetime histories.

authors.name: Grace Murray, Siyue Zhu, Angeline Hu, Kaitlyn S. Yasumura, Ioannis G. Kevrekidis, Trung V. Phan

papers.title: Fate of chiral and $U(1)_A$ symmetries in hot QCD matter under background magnetic fields
papers.summary: We summarize our recent lattice QCD study of chiral and singlet $U(1)_A$ symmetry breaking in background magnetic fields. The magnetic field explicitly reduces the non-singlet flavor symmetry through the unequal light-quark electric charges. We therefore study two neutral-channel susceptibility differences: $\chi_{\pi^0}-\chi_\sigma$ for chiral symmetry breaking and $\chi_{\pi^0}-\chi_{\delta^0}$ for singlet $U(1)_A$ symmetry breaking. The calculation uses fixed-scale $(2+1)$-flavor HISQ ensembles with $m_l=m_s^{\mathrm{phys}}/10$, corresponding to a zero-field pion mass of $M_\pi\simeq220\,\mathrm{MeV}$. Magnetic fields enhance both susceptibility differences at low temperatures. Near the crossover, sufficiently strong fields instead suppress both differences. The suppression sets in at larger magnetic fields and is milder for the singlet-axial susceptibility difference than for the neutral chiral susceptibility difference.

authors.name: Dan Zhang, Heng-Tong Ding, Jos\'e Javier Hern\'andez Hern\'andez

papers.title: Quasinormal Modes and Environmental Trapping around Charged Letelier Black Holes with Perfect-Fluid Dark Matter and Quintessence
papers.summary: We compute the massless scalar quasinormal spectra of charged Letelier black holes surrounded by logarithmic perfect fluid dark matter (PFDM) and quintessence, for $\Lambda=0$ and for asymptotically anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetimes, together with the test Maxwell spectra for $\Lambda=0$. For $\Lambda=0$, sixth order WKB values with Pad\'e resummation agree with independent time domain evolutions to within $0.06\%$ for the fundamental modes. Stronger string cloud and quintessence lower both the oscillation frequencies and the damping rates, while a larger charge or a larger positive PFDM parameter $\beta$ raises both. In our convention $\beta>0$ means negative PFDM energy density; negative $\beta$ gives a positive density and reverses the shift. The angular frequency and Lyapunov exponent of the unstable circular null orbit reproduce the eikonal trends and approximate the $\ell=2$ WKB frequencies at the percent level. For $\Lambda<0$ the scalar potential diverges at the AdS boundary and the single barrier WKB formula does not apply. We therefore solve the eigenvalue problem with a Chebyshev pseudospectral method in ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates, with regularity at the horizon and a Dirichlet condition at the boundary, and check the modes against time domain evolutions and Schwarzschild-AdS benchmarks. The AdS spectrum contains long-lived modes trapped between the photon sphere barrier and the reflecting boundary, with damping rates spanning about five orders of magnitude. The damping correlates with the ratio of the oscillation frequency to the barrier top frequency, consistent with leakage through the barrier. No growing modes are found in the test field sectors and parameter ranges studied, which does not establish the stability of the fully coupled system.

authors.name: Semra Gurtas Dogan, Abdullah Guvendi, Hassan Hassanabadi

papers.title: Casimir-like wormholes
papers.summary: We investigate spherically symmetric spacetimes sourced by matter with energy density $\rho \propto 1/r^{4}$ and equation of state $p_r = \omega \rho$. We derive the most general solution of Einstein's equations for this class of sources, obtaining black holes, naked singularities and traversable wormholes, parametrized by the integration constants and $\omega$. We show that only two classes of matter can support traversable wormholes: Casimir-type matter with $\omega > 0$ and phantom matter with $\omega < -1$, while quintessence and conventional dark energy are excluded by the flare-out condition. For the Casimir value $\omega = 3$, the transverse pressure approaches $p_t \to -\rho$ near the central singularity, so the full algebraic structure of the Casimir stress-energy tensor, $\rho \propto -1/r^{4}$, $p_r = 3\rho$, $p_t = -\rho$, is not imposed but emerges from Einstein's equations. Treating the amplitude of the energy density as a free classical parameter, we obtain wormholes with throat radii from microscopic to astrophysical scales. These Casimir-like configurations share the functional form of the Casimir tensor but are not generated by the physical Casimir effect; Garattini's Planck-scale Casimir wormhole is recovered when the quantum Casimir energy scale is imposed. The total amount of exotic matter is finite for arbitrary $\omega$ and scales linearly with the throat radius. Analyzing the traveler's acceleration, tidal forces and transit times, we show that radial free fall satisfies all human traversability conditions for $r_0 \gtrsim 10^{8}$ m. Finally, embedding diagrams illustrate three geometric regimes depending on $\omega$.

authors.name: Mauricio Cataldo

papers.title: Lean-Verified No-Go Theorems for $R$-Symmetries and Modular Symmetries in 4D GUTs
papers.summary: $R$-symmetries are instrumental in supersymmetric model building. However, a no-go theorem restricts us from using them in a large class of four-dimensional (4D) grand unified theories (GUTs). Specifically, it has been shown that a supersymmetric 4D GUT based on SU(5), with finitely many chiral multiplets, cannot be broken spontaneously to the exact minimal supersymmetric standard model (MSSM) while preserving a discrete $\mathbb{Z}_M^R$, with $M \geq 3$, or continuous U(1) $R$-symmetry. We use Lean 4 to formalize this proof. In the process, we identify and close a gap in the general case of the published argument. Further, we discuss the implications for GUT models with modular symmetries. We point out that modular symmetries are inevitably $R$-symmetries in a supersymmetric framework that also describes gravity. At certain critical points in moduli space, discrete $R$-symmetries are linearly realized. In the context of 4D GUTs, the no-go theorem then implies that exotic states become massless at these points, provided the GUT-breaking vacuum preserves these symmetries. In the vicinity of these critical points, these exotics are parametrically light, which may spoil gauge coupling unification.

authors.name: Mu-Chun Chen, Xiang-Gan Liu, Michael Ratz, Alexander Stewart

papers.title: ECPack.wl: A Mathematica Package for Elliptic Curves over the Rationals and Finite Fields
papers.summary: We present a Mathematica package entitled ECPack.wl, where we implement many important properties and commands relevant to the study of elliptic curves over the rationals and finite fields, namely $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\mathbb{F}_q$, where $q=p^r$ and $p$ is prime. By streamlining the analysis of general elliptic curves and their transformations, ECPack.wl offers foundational computational tools for applications in high-energy physics, including elliptic Feynman integrals. This package significantly extends the functionalities of a package due to McGee in so far as we are able to study all versions of elliptic curves, such as the long Weierstrass, quartic and Legendre forms. We implement suitable transformations that are required for the general case, as well as those associated with fields of characteristic 2 and 3. Furthermore, the package computes many curve properties, such as point arithmetic, minimality checks, rank bounds and analytic rank, group structure, invariants, and the Weil and Tate pairings, over both $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\mathbb{F}_p$, as well as the Kodaira classification of the singular fibres of one-parameter families of elliptic curves, with the associated F-theory data. The package and its accompanying notebooks are available at https://github.com/DhamakedarDarsh/Mathematica-Code-and-worked-out-notebooks-for-Elliptic-Curves

authors.name: B. Ananthanarayan, Darsh R. Bhatt, Parastoo Taghizadeh Asl

papers.title: Hyperbolic string vertices as geometric chains
papers.summary: For 0<L<=2arcsinh(1), the hyperbolic string vertices of Costello and Zwiebach consist of the bordered hyperbolic surfaces with geodesic boundary of length L whose interior simple closed geodesics have length at least L. We show that the corresponding regions in moduli space are compact oriented orbifolds with corners whose boundaries are, including orientations and automorphism groups, the spaces of twisted sewings. Hence their generating chain satisfies the master equation without the bracket term exactly in a complex of geometric chains. The usual connected form cannot hold exactly for geometric chains; we determine its exact form, show that it holds modulo gluing and covering relations in a complex computing the homology of the moduli spaces, and that the vertex currents are the unique top-dimensional solution. Finally we compare with Costello's homotopical framework. In a strict model given by hyperbolic surfaces with marked boundary points, every solution of his master equation with his initial condition integrates exactly to the vertex currents, up to the sign (-1)^(3g-3+n); such solutions exist, are unique up to homotopy, and correspond to the hyperbolic vertices. Under a continuity assumption on the comparison map and granting the inputs of Costello's homology computation, the hyperbolic vertices represent his homotopy class of solutions, for a completed notion of homotopy.

authors.name: Hao Yu

papers.title: Boson Stars with Ay\'{o}n--Beato--Garc\'{i}a nonlinear electrodynamics
papers.summary: In this paper, we study spherically symmetric boson star solutions in Einstein gravity minimally coupled to Ay\'{o}n--Beato--Garc\'{i}a nonlinear electrodynamics and a massive complex scalar field. We find that these solutions exist only when the electric charge $q$ is below a critical value. Within this range, solutions with relatively small charges can exhibit a gravitational blueshift, and the radial mass function becomes negative in some regions while the ADM mass remains positive. For larger charges, frozen boson-star solutions emerge as the scalar-field frequency $\omega$ approaches zero. In these configurations, the metric function $1/g_{rr}$ and $-g_{tt}$ become very small near a special position $r_{\mathrm{ch}}$, and the spacetime resembles an extremal black hole from the perspective of an observer at infinity. Moreover, timelike trajectories in these frozen boson stars are strongly deflected near $r_{\mathrm{ch}}$, and particles require a longer coordinate time to traverse the same radial distance than they do in ordinary boson stars.

authors.name: Long-Xing Huang, Yong-Qiang Wang

papers.title: Polynomial twisted periods and affine vertex algebras
papers.summary: We prove the conjecture of Kang, Lawrie, and Song that Zhu's $C_2$-algebra of a simply-laced boundary admissible affine vertex algebra is isomorphic to the Jacobian ring of an invariant potential obtained by lifting a polynomial twisted period from a Cartan subalgebra via the Chevalley isomorphism. We further identify the $C_2$-algebras of the corresponding Drinfeld-Sokolov reductions with the Jacobian rings of the restrictions of this potential to Slodowy slices. We also extend the Jacobian presentation to non-simply-laced principal boundary admissible affine vertex algebras, where the restriction of the potential to the Cartan subalgebra satisfies a Dunkl-singularity equation with root-length-dependent multiplicities.

authors.name: Tomoyuki Arakawa, Wenbin Yan

papers.title: Cosmological Collider Signals from Fermion Bubble Loops with a Chemical Potential
papers.summary: We present the first systematic analytical calculation of the local and nonlocal cosmological collider (CC) signals generated by massive fermion bubble loops in the presence of an effective chemical potential during inflation. Working in the de Sitter approximation, we investigate the four-point correlator of inflaton perturbations in the single-squeezed limit. By combining CC cutting rules, late-time expansions, and partial Mellin-Barnes (MB) techniques, we derive analytical expressions for both local and nonlocal signals. In particular, we identify two distinct contributions to the local signal, arising from spectrum and integer poles and from ultraviolet poles of the loop-momentum integral. We further investigate the three-point limit, where the separately extracted local and nonlocal contributions develop apparent folded singularities. By reorganizing the MB representation, we demonstrate that these singularities cancel in the complete signal and obtain a convergent double-MB integral suitable for numerical evaluation. Independent calculations using complementary MB representations provide nontrivial consistency checks of our results. We find that the chemical potential can significantly enhance the oscillatory signal while increasing its logarithmic oscillation frequency. Our analytical results provide a foundation for further studies of chemical-potential-enhanced fermionic CC signals, including fermion triangle loops.

authors.name: Chengcheng Han, Zhanhong Lei, Zhehan Qin, Wuzhou Yin

papers.title: A consistent (3D) EFT expansion of the bubble nucleation rate. Part I: scalar theories
papers.summary: Precise predictions of bubble nucleation are essential for connecting cosmological phase transitions to their potential observational signatures. In this first paper of a two-part series, we develop a general, fully perturbative framework for incorporating higher-dimensional operators (HDOs) into nucleation calculations in scalar high-temperature effective field theories. Our approach consistently includes their effects on the bounce and the fluctuations around it, including interactions with higher derivatives. We prove that the resulting statistical rate is invariant under field redefinitions, and establish sufficient conditions for the existence of the perturbative bounce solution in the presence of HDOs. We illustrate the framework by applying it to a model containing a scalar and a fermion, where we find modest HDO corrections in its regime of moderately strong transitions. We thus extend the systematic study of HDO effects beyond critical thermodynamics and provide a controlled method for determining their impact on bubble nucleation.

authors.name: Luis Gil, Javier L\'opez Miras

papers.title: Static Bounds on Thermal Fast Scrambling
papers.summary: Scrambling, the process by which initially localized quantum information spreads across an interacting many-body system, is a hallmark of quantum chaos and plays a central role in understanding black hole dynamics. In thermal systems, the chaos bound of Maldacena, Shenker and Stanford limits the exponential growth rate of out-of-time-order correlations to $2\pi/\beta$, assuming that time-ordered correlation functions factorize after a dissipation time. Establishing the corresponding rigorous logarithmic lower bounds on scrambling times at arbitrary fixed temperature has remained an open problem, most notably in disordered systems, where the Gibbs state depends on the same random couplings that drive the dynamics. Here we prove such bounds at every fixed temperature for the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model and for random $k$-local spin systems, without assuming real-time factorization. Our approach uses the operator-size distribution of the square root of the Gibbs state to quantify how local probes modify its structure. This static information bounds the thermal correlator uniformly in time along the edges of its analytic strip in complex time, and analyticity then limits how rapidly scrambling can develop. For both families of models, we prove that with probability tending to one the scrambling time is at least $(1-\epsilon)[\beta/(2\pi)]\log N$ for any $0<\epsilon<1$, with the coefficient $\beta/(2\pi)$ suggested by the chaos bound. The bound holds for each fixed pair of distinct Majorana modes in the SYK model and for the target average of any fixed single-site source in the spin model. These results place the thermal fast-scrambling timescale on a rigorous footing and show how static properties of the Gibbs state can constrain real-time information spreading.

authors.name: Yixuan Ma, Weikang Li, Dong-Ling Deng

papers.title: Global bound-state spectrum and spin- and angular-momentum-dependent confinement in an inverse-$3/2$ magnetic quantum dot
papers.summary: We investigate the bound-state spectrum and confinement thresholds of a two-dimensional electron governed by the Schr\"{o}dinger--Pauli equation in an inverse-$3/2$ radial magnetic-field profile. The radial problem reduces to the biconfluent Heun equation, but instead of restricting the solution to the quasi-exact polynomial sector, we impose the bound-state condition globally through a spectral Wronskian between the endpoint-selected Frobenius solution and the subdominant asymptotic solution. The resulting spectrum contains continuous nonpolynomial bound-state branches on which the known quasi-exact solutions appear as isolated exact points. In this global description, the polynomial index $N$ remains a termination index within the quasi-exact sector but does not uniquely label the spectral branches. An independent exact analysis of the continuum edge yields spin- and angular-momentum-dependent critical couplings that can lie below the quasi-exact restriction $U_0a>4$, where $U_0$ is the Coulomb-strength parameter and $a$ is the magnetic-profile length scale. These results establish quasi-exact solvability as a set of special analytic points embedded in a broader biconfluent-Heun spectrum with spin- and angular-momentum-dependent confinement thresholds.

authors.name: Luis B. Castro

papers.title: Maximum entropy reconstruction of the black hole greybody factors from its Korteweg-de Vries integrals
papers.summary: The dynamics of perturbed non-rotating black holes (BHs) can be described by master wave equations with a potential barrier. Recent work has shown that these equations possess an infinite number of symmetries generated by the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) hierarchy, leading to conserved quantities (KdV integrals) that fully determine the BH greybody factors via a moment problem. In this paper, we introduce and validate a new method to solve this moment problem using the maximum entropy principle. The method reconstructs, at each order of truncation, the least-biased transmission probability compatible with a finite set of KdV integrals, guaranteeing positivity by construction. We first validate the technique against the exactly solvable P\"oschl-Teller potential. We then apply it to the Regge-Wheeler potential governing axial perturbations of a Schwarzschild BH, where no exact solution is available; the resulting reconstruction agrees closely with the fourth-order Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) approximation across several multipoles. This is the first application of the maximum entropy method to the reconstruction of BH greybody factors, demonstrating that a modest number of KdV integrals is sufficient to recover them accurately.

authors.name: Noah Alberca (Departament de Matem\`atiques, Universitat Aut\`onoma de Barcelona, Institute of Space Sciences), Michele Lenzi (Physique Th\'eorique et Math\'ematique, Universit\'e Libre de Bruxelles), Carlos F. Sopuerta (Institute of Space Sciences, Institute of Space Studies of Catalonia)

papers.title: Entropy of Noncommutative Spaces
papers.summary: We give an overview of the second quantisation of spectral triples and compute the entropy of the noncommutative space described by it in terms of a spectral action. This reviews earlier work by Chamseddine, Connes and the second author, but presented here concisely, including the procedure of second quantisation using infinite-dimensional Clifford algebras. We exemplify the theory by considering noncommutative metric spaces consisting of $N$ points. The entropy of these discrete spaces is explicitly computed, and we study the resulting entropic force as well as the evolution of the spaces in time.

authors.name: Cisca Kalmijn, Walter D. van Suijlekom

papers.title: Torsional Hall Viscosity of Massive Chern Insulators: Finite Temperature and Chemical Potential
papers.summary: We study the torsional Hall viscosity $\zeta_{\rm H}$ of Chern insulators at finite temperature and chemical potential. Our analysis considers the massive Dirac fermion and two deformations: a constant out-of-plane magnetic field and a momentum-dependent mass described by the single-block Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang (BHZ) Hamiltonian. For the massive Dirac theory, we show that temperature and chemical potential lead to UV-finite corrections and that a chemical potential outside the bulk gap modifies $\zeta_{\rm H}$ even at zero temperature. In a constant magnetic field, the response of massive Dirac fermions is dictated by the relativistic Landau-level spectrum, leading to a plateau structure at zero temperature that is smoothed at finite temperature. The jumps are proportional to the Dirac mass and inversely proportional to the squared magnetic length and the newly occupied Landau-level energy. Finally, we present a detailed study of the correction to $\zeta_{\rm H}$ in the single-block BHZ continuum model due to temperature and chemical potential. For parameters relevant to (Hg,Mn)Te quantum wells, the magnitude of the jump across a mass domain wall retains its vacuum enhancement due to the BHZ deformation as long as the chemical potential lies sufficiently deep inside the gap compared with the thermal energy. Our results extend the theory of torsional Hall viscosity to experimentally relevant conditions and may facilitate its future detection.

authors.name: Weizhen Jia, Ioannis Matthaiakakis, David Rodr\'iguez Fern\'andez, Zhuo-Yu Xian, Johanna Erdmenger, Ewelina M. Hankiewicz, Ren\'e Meyer

papers.title: Detectability of Eccentric Intermediate Mass-Ratio Inspiral in the Decihertz Band
papers.summary: The proposed decihertz gravitational-wave (GW) band $(\sim 10^{-2}-1\,\Hz)$ will observe the late inspiral of intermediate mass-ratio inspirals (IMRIs), binaries with mass ratios $10^2 \lesssim q \lesssim 10^4$ that assemble dynamically in dense stellar environments and are expected to retain measurable eccentricity. Search and parameter-estimation pipelines are predominantly built around circular templates, and we test this assumption. Using black-hole perturbation theory waveforms from \textsc{FastEMRIWaveforms} for a representative IMRI ($M=10^4\,\modot$, $q=100$, observed for its final $10\,\hr$), we compute fitting factors between eccentric signals and circular templates, maximizing over the template's total mass and mass ratio with a differential-evolution search, for the B-DECIGO, LGWA-Si, and IndIGO-D noise curves and a flat PSD. The mismatch grows with initial eccentricity $e_0$ and crosses the standard $3\%$ threshold at $e_0\simeq3\times10^{-2}$, well within the range allowed by the waveform model and expected from dynamical formation. The best-fitting circular templates also bias the total mass and mass ratio by several percent at $e_0=0.1$. Combining the mismatch with the signal-to-noise-dependent distinguishability criterion, we find that for a source at $1\,\mathrm{Gpc}$, eccentricities as small as $e_0\simeq5\times10^{-4}$ (B-DECIGO and IndIGO-D) and $5\times10^{-3}$ (LGWA-Si) are resolvable, one to two orders of magnitude below where detection efficiency degrades. The loss of match arises from the excitation of radial Teukolsky harmonics, which spread power into sidebands that circular templates cannot represent, and from the slower orbital decay of eccentric binaries at fixed initial semi-latus rectum. Robust detection and parameter estimation of IMRIs with DECIGO, LGWA, and IndIGO-D will require eccentric waveform models and template banks.

authors.name: Devesh Giri, Sajal Mukherjee, Apratim Ganguly, Sanjit Mitra

papers.title: Non-factorisable Yangian Lax matrices through oscillators
papers.summary: We construct oscillator realisations of Yangian Lax operators in type $A$, with particular interest in non-factorisable operators associated with prime snake modules. Our construction applies to finite-dimensional skew representations of $Y(\mathfrak{gl}_n)$. We prove that these representations are generated by the tensor vacuum in suitably ordered tensor products of oscillator representations. Their Lax operators are obtained by restricting the corresponding products of linear oscillator Lax operators to these submodules. We determine the vacuum eigenvalues and Drinfeld polynomials, and give a determinant formula for the dimensions directly in terms of the highest loop weights. A $21$-dimensional example illustrates the construction, including an explicit basis and a transfer-matrix identity.

authors.name: Rouven Frassek, Henrik J\"urgens

papers.title: Non-Canonical Q-balls in Polyattractor Inflation Models
papers.summary: We show that Q-balls can exist in supergravity-based polyattractor inflation models that interpolate between $\alpha$-attractor T-models and polynomial attractor models. We consider both the original polyattractor potential and a natural generalisation. We find that Q-balls solutions exist when the model deviates significantly from the T-model $\alpha$-attractor, whereas in the T-model limit no Q-balls exist. These are non-canonical Q-balls due to the non-canonical kinetic term of the complex inflaton field. Such Q-balls could have significant cosmological consequences if they are produced at the end of inflation. In particular, if the global $\mathrm{U}(1)$ symmetry of the supergravity-based polyattractor model is unbroken, the Q-balls can be absolutely stable and could account for dark matter.

authors.name: Kimberley Siret, Rhys Abercromby, Kit Lloyd-Stubbs, John McDonald

papers.title: Geometry of squeezed states. The phase-space metric, relative vacua and cosmology
papers.summary: Geometry enters quantum theory in two places. The space of quantum states carries a symplectic form, which generates unitary evolution, and a metric, which governs uncertainties and transition probabilities. The classical phase space acquires a metric of its own when a vacuum is chosen: quantizing a linear system amounts to choosing a compatible complex structure, equivalently a compatible metric $g$. We take this second metric as the primary object and show that it plays, on phase space, the role that the quantum metric plays on the space of states: fluctuations of linear observables are $g$-norms of Hamiltonian vector fields, and along coherent states $g/2\hbar$ \emph{is} the quantum metric. Squeezed states then have a simple description. A squeezed vacuum is the vacuum of another metric, and squeezing is a property of a pair of metrics, a relative vacuum, whose invariants are the eigenvalues $e^{\pm2r_i}$ of $L=g_0^{-1}g$. We work out the harmonic oscillator in detail, including why a rotated squeezed state no longer minimizes the product of the displayed uncertainties. Quadratic evolution deforms the metric, and only the part of the generator that is self-adjoint with respect to the reference changes the $r_i$, at a rate we give exactly. For fields, a vacuum is unitarily implementable relative to a reference exactly when it lies at finite distance from it in the space of vacua. For a massless field in de Sitter space we revisit the two canonical charts compared by Grain and Vennin: relative to the reference of the standard squeezing formalism the Bunch--Davies state has $\sinh r_k=1/(2|k\eta|)$, and relative to the vacuum that a radiation era beginning at time $\eta$ would select it has $\sinh r_k=1/(2k^2\eta^2)$. The second comparison squeezes twice as fast and is unitarily implementable; the first is not.

authors.name: Alejandro Corichi, Jer\'onimo Cortez

papers.title: The Skyrme-Dilaton and Nucleon Observables
papers.summary: We extend the Skyrme model by incorporating the $\sigma/f_0(500)$-meson as a dilaton. The motivation is twofold: the $\sigma$-meson is the lightest scalar resonance in QCD and is therefore the natural extensions to the pions of the classical Skyrme model, while its interpretation as a pseudo-Goldstone boson of spontaneously broken scale symmetry is supported by recent studies of gravitational form factors and related developments. Although the $\sigma$-meson is a broad resonance, for static observables it can be treated as real particle since its line-shape is not expected to be essential. A combined fit to static nucleon observables yields $\chi^2/\mathrm{dof} $ close to unity, with substantial improvement over the original Skyrme model, while simultaneously reproducing the physical value of $F_\pi$, the overall scale of the model.

authors.name: Thomas Fischbacher, Roman Zwicky

papers.title: Axioms for relative entropy
papers.summary: For normal states of arbitrary von Neumann algebras, we characterize positive finite multiples of Araki relative entropy among non-degenerate divergences. The axioms are monotonicity under normal unital completely positive maps, tensor additivity, superadditivity for product second states, and separate lower semicontinuity in the predual norm. Alternatively, a conditional-expectation identity replaces the two tensor assumptions. The proof uses order bounds and asymptotic estimates on tensor powers. An appendix proves the known analytic estimates needed here, using standard modular theory and Haagerup L^p spaces. We also obtain the corresponding characterization in the C* algebraic setting.

authors.name: Roberto Longo

papers.title: On the Asymptotic Expansion of Massive Fields in Spherically Symmetric Systems
papers.summary: The behavior of massive real scalar fields, when sourced by a central object, is usually assumed to follow a Yukawa falloff towards radial infinity. In this paper, we show that this is generically not the case, even for minimally coupled fields. Further, while the point-particle action provides a coordinate-invariant definition of the central object's scalar charge, we show that the coefficient one usually extracts at asymptotically large radii in the case of massive scalar fields is neither coordinate invariant nor identical to the scalar charge appearing in the point-particle action. We resolve this issue perturbatively by constructing matched asymptotic expansions and investigate the non-perturbative structure using numerical methods.

authors.name: Robin Fynn Diedrichs, Iris van Gemeren

papers.title: Exceptional cubics on 7-manifolds
papers.summary: A $G_2$-structure $\varphi$ on a $7$-manifold $\mathcal M$ determines a two-dimensional space of invariant totally symmetric cubic forms on each fiber of the rank-$27$ bundle $S^2_0T^*\mathcal M$ of traceless symmetric $2$-tensors. This space is spanned by the trace cubic $C_0$ and a cubic $C_\varphi$ that, up to a constant factor, is the pointwise integrand of the Yukawa coupling on the $G_2$ moduli space. We determine the exact infinitesimal stabilizers over $\mathbb C$ of all nonzero cubics in this family. For $C_0+\lambda C_\varphi$, the stabilizer has dimension $78$ precisely at the two non-real values $\lambda_\pm=(1\pm i\sqrt7)/8$. Its dimension is $21$ for $C_0$ and $14$ in all other cases. At $\lambda_\pm$, the stabilizer is simple of type $E_6$, and the corresponding cubic is linearly equivalent to the complex Albert algebra cubic norm. The two cubics at $\lambda_\pm$, which we call critical, define complex-conjugate $E_6$-reductions of the complexified bundle. At any element with nonzero critical norm, the corresponding cubic determines a complex Albert algebra with basepoint stabilizer $F_4$; a line subbundle of the tangent bundle selects a smooth bundle of these algebras with tensorial operations and a Euclidean real form. The induced Levi-Civita connection preserves either critical cubic exactly when the $G_2$-structure is torsion-free. Its orthogonal projections onto the two exceptional reductions coincide with the connection induced by the minimal $G_2$-connection.

authors.name: Sergey Grigorian

papers.title: A separation criterion for chiral systems and its application to Pleba\'nski--Demia\'nski perturbations
papers.summary: We give a constructive criterion for local separation of first-order chiral systems coupling two complex doublets. It combines a Gram decomposition of the coupling sources with separate coordinate dependence and a differential transport test. For recoverable, nondegenerate source families, the criterion is necessary and sufficient within the specified class of mode-independent complex matrix transformations with unit determinant. For a fixed differential operator and admissible Gram decomposition, we identify conditions under which the sources uniquely determine the Hermitian coefficient matrix required for separation. As an application, we construct an explicit algebraic transformation and derive separated radial and angular equations for coupled radiative Einstein--Maxwell perturbations of rotating, charged Pleba\'nski--Demia\'nski backgrounds with acceleration, NUT charge, and a cosmological constant, on specified local patches. Its Gram decomposition is unique under additional generic assumptions. We also derive angular endpoint indices for Bonnor and Misner identifications with conical deficits or excesses. Under the stated regularity assumptions, each specified self-adjoint angular realization at fixed real mode parameters has a discrete spectrum and a complete orthonormal eigenbasis.

authors.name: Hideo Furugori, Daisuke Yoshida

papers.title: Boundary to bound dictionary for generic Kerr orbits
papers.summary: We establish a new relation between classical observables for scattering and bound orbits of a massive probe particle in a Kerr background. We find an exact representation of the Hamilton-Jacobi action in terms of the conserved charges which admits an analytic continuation, both for the radial and polar contribution, for a general class of geodesics beyond the equatorial case. Remarkably, this allows to extend the boundary to bound dictionary and it provides an efficient method to compute the deflection angles and the time delay for scattering orbits, as well as frequency ratios for bound orbits, in the probe limit but at all orders in the perturbative expansion.

authors.name: Riccardo Gonzo, Canxin Shi

papers.title: Black Hole Chemistry Knows Extra Dimensions
papers.summary: We study black hole chemistry in the eight-dimensional Einstein-Yang-Mills-Maxwell theory, where the stabilized size of the compact internal space dynamically determines the four-dimensional thermodynamic pressure. Analyzing AdS black holes, we show that larger extra dimensions lower phase-transition temperatures and broaden the range of thermodynamically excluded black hole sizes. Additionally, we investigate a geometric representation of the thermodynamic volume by defining a volume-constrained minimal surface using a lapse-weighted volume functional. This codimension-two surface minimizes its area under the constraint that its enclosed volume exactly matches the thermodynamic volume. This surface prescription naturally reproduces the event horizon for dyonic and Schwarzschild-AdS black holes. We also apply this to the Kerr--AdS black hole and find an off-horizon surface numerically and analytically for finite and small angular momenta. In addition, we interpret the thermodynamic volume in terms of an effective number of disentanglers in a MERA system.

authors.name: Kyung Kiu Kim, Jeongwon Ho, Seungjoon Hyun, Taehyeon Song

papers.title: Entropic force in matrix theory
papers.summary: We consider the entropic force in matrix theory. We find the gravity in bulk can be emergent from the entropic force.

authors.name: Wei-shui Xu

papers.title: Higher genus twistor spaces and the celestial torus
papers.summary: This paper studies novel four-dimensional integrable field theories that are deformations of self-dual Yang-Mills. They are engineered by considering holomorphic Chern-Simons and BF type theories on covers of twistor space obtained by pulling back the vector bundle $\mathcal{O}(1)^2\to\mathbb{CP}^1$ to hyperelliptic or elliptic curves. Compactifying to 4d yields an integrable theory, which in the examples I study, are determined to leading order. The form of the higher-order corrections are bootstrapped, and I argue that the index structure and coefficients of these terms are fixed by integrability. The celestial chiral algebras of these theories are shown to live on hyper-elliptic and elliptic curves, respectively. Symmetry reducing these integrable deformations to 2d yields an example of a hyperelliptic and elliptic integrable model governing a deformation of Hitchin's equations.

authors.name: Seraphim Jarov

papers.title: Hamiltonian Truncation Framework for Gauge Theories on the Interval
papers.summary: In this work, we investigate gauge theories in two dimensions nonperturbatively using the Hamiltonian truncation approach. Working on a spatial interval and adopting the axial gauge, we remove all gauge field degrees of freedom and express the interacting Hamiltonian in the eigenbasis of the free Dirac theory, truncated at a finite energy. As a benchmark we analyse the Schwinger model, where our numerical spectra agree closely with the exact results from bosonization across a wide range of couplings, validating the construction of the Hamiltonian. We then generalize the formulation to nonabelian gauge groups and apply it to SU(3) gauge theory with a single massless Dirac fermion. These results demonstrate that gauge theories can be explored nonperturbatively using a truncated Hamiltonian that generates evolutions in ordinary time, offering a complementary alternative to lattice field theory.

authors.name: Rachel Houtz, James Ingoldby

papers.title: A geometrical invitation to BMS group theory
papers.summary: In these lecture notes, a group-theoretical introduction to BMS symmetries is provided in a self-contained manner. More precisely, all definitions and structures are purely based on geometrical and group-theoretical notions defined at null infinity and valid in any dimension (four or higher), in a way that circumvents its traditional bulk realisation as asymptotic symmetries. The topics which are reviewed are: the definition of BMS transformations as conformal Carrollian isometries of null infinity, the semidirect structure of the BMS group, the holographic reconstruction of Minkowski spacetime in terms of good cuts, the one-to-one correspondence between good cut subspaces and Poincar\'{e} subgroups (aka vacua), as well as a basic introduction to the unitary representations of the BMS group.

authors.name: Xavier Bekaert, Yannick Herfray, Lea Mele, No\'emie Parrini

papers.title: BPS vortex from nonpolynomial scalar QED in a $\mathbb{C}\mathrm{P}^1$-Maxwell theory
papers.summary: We investigate a generalized gauged $\mathbb{C}\mathrm{P}^1$-Maxwell theory in which the electromagnetic sector acquires a field-dependent magnetic permeability generated dynamically through fermionic vacuum polarization. We couple a Dirac fermion with an effective mass to a gauged $\mathbb{C}\mathrm{P}^1$ sigma model whose target space carries the Fubini-Study metric. Integrating out the Dirac fermion at one loop induces a logarithmic correction to the Maxwell kinetic term. This dependence is retained in the planar effective theory after dimensional reduction. Within this framework, one builds a generalized $\mathbb{C}\mathrm{P}^1$-Maxwell model by admitting Bogomol'nyi-Prasad-Sommerfield (BPS) configurations. Taking this into account, we solved the self-dual equations that describe vortex-like solutions with quantized magnetic flux.

authors.name: F. C. E. Lima

papers.title: Conformal Vacua in Boundary-Glued AdS$_3$
papers.summary: We argue that the purely topological gluing of AdS$_3$ spacetimes, which are otherwise independent due to Dirichlet boundary conditions, can still produce non-trivial spaces after a quotient. In this direction, we extend the study of a recently discovered non-orientable AdS$_3$, which is a $\mathbb Z_2$ quotient of two AdS$_3$ spaces glued along their conformal boundaries. We find that this space is compact and boundaryless and that the quotient sends the gluing surface to a torus comprised of a null lattice with halved periods. However, the bulk wraps around both its sides, which means that as an embedded space this gluing surface forms a one-sided torus. We discover that it supports a permutation-twisted sector of two CFT$_2$s with shared Dirichlet boundary conditions and conjecture that conformal maps can be extended across this gluing surface. Using this extension, we show that the vacuum of pairs of Rindler wedges, which share a boundary in this non-orientable AdS$_3\times$S$^2$ space, are conformal to static patch vacua, which are supported on two dS$_4\times \mathbb R$ glued together at their conformal boundaries.

authors.name: Lucas K. Kovalsky, Shivesh Pathak, Kyle Ritchie

papers.title: Effective Field Theory for Superconducting Phase Transitions
papers.summary: Employing the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, we formulate an effective field theory for s-wave superconducting phase transition, where the dynamical variables consist of electromagnetic gauge field and complex scalar order parameter. Symmetry-constrained effective action allows systematic handling of dissipations and fluctuations. In particular, we explore the physical implications of higher-order terms, including those involving additional dynamical fields as well as higher time derivatives, on the real-time dynamics near the superconducting critical point. When appropriately truncated, the effective field theory reproduces the phenomenological Ginzburg-Landau equations. Upon crossing the critical temperature into the low-temperature phase, the electromagnetic gauge symmetry undergoes spontaneous breaking induced by the condensate of the order parameter. Collective excitation analysis reveals that the Higgs mode behaves as an overdamped diffusive mode near the critical point, while the phase fluctuation is absorbed into the gauge field via the Higgs mechanism. For complex kinetic coefficients, we derive the coupled linearized equations for amplitude, phase, and longitudinal gauge fluctuations, and distinguish propagation from damping through their complex poles. The holographic Schwinger-Keldysh construction provides an explicit realization and a nontrivial consistency check of the effective action, and determines its Wilsonian coefficients within a specific strongly coupled model. Holographic results reveal a complex relaxation parameter that indicates oscillatory dynamics characteristic of strongly coupled systems.

authors.name: Yanyan Bu, Zexin Yang

papers.title: Entanglement inequalities for timelike intervals within dynamical holography
papers.summary: This paper extends our previous work (arXiv:2504.14313) of a single timelike subregion to two, in the framework of AdS$_3$-Vaidya holography. We confirm the positivity of timelike mutual information and the statement of weak monotonicity when the subregions are non-overlapping. We also study entanglement inequalities such as Araki-Lieb inequality and strong subadditivity when the intervals start to overlap. In line with the recent findings in the literature, we provide explicit working examples showing that the timelike version of the strong subadditivity is generally violated in these setups, even though the statements of subadditivity and Araki-Lieb inequality hold true.

authors.name: Gaurav Katoch, Debajyoti Sarkar, Bhim Sen

papers.title: A gravity interpretation for the complex saddles of the ABJM and spindle indices
papers.summary: The superconformal index is a grand-canonical partition function that counts the 1/16-BPS states in the theory, and its Legendre transform with respect to reduced chemical potentials accounts for the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of electrically charged rotating black holes in anti-de Sitter spacetime. However, the superconformal index of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory appears to allow shifts in chemical potentials, and the contributions of the shifted terms diverge exponentially. We resolved this puzzle by showing the instability of wrapped D3-branes corresponding to shifts in the gravitational on-shell action. Analogously, we study the M5-brane instability criterion of the ABJM index and the spindle index.

authors.name: Minwoo Suh

papers.title: Filtering out Erratic Observables: Wormholes from Gauging Nonlocal Symmetries
papers.summary: The wormhole contribution to the gravitational path integral may be interpreted as smooth remnant of correlations among the erratic large-$N$ behaviors of dual CFTs. In this work, we investigate this idea in (2+1)-dimensional gravity. We show that one-sided boundary gravitons are intrinsically incomplete in the sense that the associated observable algebra has a nontrivial center regardless of choices of boundary conditions. Based on asymptotic symmetries, we bootstrap a general Poisson bracket to construct completions of the boundary gravitons. In the simplest completion, the commutant of the boundary graviton observable algebra is given by an observable algebra of monodromy data which we interpret as an effective description of one-sided black holes. We show that, to describe Lorentzian multi-boundary wormholes, only the monodromy data with a positivity restriction is needed. The positivity restriction results in emergent erratic large-$N$ behaviors for some observables. We filter out the erratic observables by restricting to a subspace on which they act trivially. The monodromy observables generate nonlocal symmetries lack of corresponding local currents. We show that gauging the nonlocal symmetries is equivalent to filtering out the erratic observables. For one CFT, gauging the nonlocal symmetries at the quantum level removes all black hole states. Filtering the partition function of CFTs leads to an apparent ensemble averaging. For two CFTs, a Hilbert subspace describing wormholes survives after gauging global part of the nonlocal symmetries. The filtered partition function of the two CFTs is an ensemble average over quantum gates entangling the monodromy degrees of freedom of the two CFTs. The correlation between the erratic observables of the two CFTs is preserved, which contributes to the filtered partition function as a wormhole term.

authors.name: Qi-Feng Wu

papers.title: Stress Tensor Deformations in dS/CFT: Mixed Boundary Conditions, Spectrum Flow and Pseudo Entropy
papers.summary: We formulate a local semiclassical source--response prescription for derivative-free stress-tensor deformations in dS/CFT. The metric flow determines the deformed boundary metric and stress tensor, encoding the deformation through mixed boundary conditions at future infinity. In Kerr-dS$_3$/CFT$_2$, the holographic charges reproduce the field-theory spectral flow, providing an internal consistency check. For general deformations in this class, we derive a holographic pseudo-entropy formula in terms of the flowed boundary data, nonperturbative in the deformation parameters within a specified complex-geodesic prescription. We evaluate this formula explicitly for the $T\bar{T}$ and root-$T\bar{T}$ deformations. On the non-rotating principal branch, an analytically continued replica calculation reproduces the interval-dependent corrections at first order in the couplings and leading semiclassical order. Agreement of the interval-independent terms additionally requires a source-frame regulator identification.

authors.name: Feng Hao, Hao Ouyang, Xi-Yang Ran

papers.title: O(N) BCFT: new data from conformal partial wave expansions
papers.summary: The $\mathsf{O}(N)$ $\mathsf{BCFT}$ is analyzed in the large $N$ expansion in a generic bulk dimension $2<d+1<4$. Focus is on boundary conditions corresponding to the ordinary transition, however techniques used can be generalized to special or extraordinary transitions. We study the system of bulk $2$-pt functions $\langle \phi\phi\rangle$, $\langle \phi^2 \phi^2\rangle$ and $\langle \sigma\sigma \rangle$, where $\sigma$ is the Hubbard--Stratonovich field. They are expanded in bulk/boundary conformal partial waves. The coefficient functions of this expansion -- the spectral functions -- encode $\mathsf{BCFT}$ data and determine bulk/boundary conformal block expansions. We prove conjectures about boundary spectral functions in Dujava et al. [arXiv:2503.16345] and reproduce the bulk expansion of $\langle \phi\phi \rangle$ in Giombi et al. [arXiv:2007.04955]. The bulk expansion of $\langle\sigma\sigma\rangle$ is new and allows to extract the leading large $N$ expression for an unknown OPE coefficient $C_{\sigma\sigma\sigma^3}$ (the computation outputs as a byproduct also a mixing coefficient, which matches an existing result by Derkachov et al. [arXiv:hep-th/9705020], providing further support for the main result). Besides these derived data infinitely many constraints are produced, though due to operator mixing growing in complexity as degeneracy increases, they cannot be disentangled without further input.

authors.name: Jozef Csipes, Petr Va\v{s}ko

papers.title: On the Schubert calculus of the quantum K-theory for partial flag manifolds: a 3d A-model perspective
papers.summary: We further investigate the 3d gauged linear sigma model (GLSM)/~quantum K-theory correspondence for partial flag manifolds $X \equiv {\rm Fl}(\boldsymbol{k};n)$. This is a 3d uplift of the 2d GLSM/quantum cohomology correspondence with the 3d theory compactified on $\mathbb{R}^2\times S^1_\beta$. Recently, a set of half-BPS line operators, called Schubert line defects, were constructed that correspond to the Schubert classes in the K-theory ring of $X$. Utilizing algebro-geometric algorithms, we compute $2$-point and $3$-point correlation functions of these line operators in the 3d A-model regime of the theory. These are interpreted as genus-$0$ K-theoretic Gromov--Witten invariants, and they produce the K-theoretic Littlewood--Richardson coefficients of the quantum K-theory ring of $X$. We show how this works explicitly in examples, going beyond the existing results in the literature. Taking the small $\beta$ limit, we apply these techniques to the resulting 2d GLSM. We explicitly compute the quantum cohomology ring relations of $X$ for some cases and match with existing results in the literature in examples.

authors.name: Zhihao Duan, Osama Khlaif, Hao Zou

papers.title: Diagonally gauged anomaly-free 6D supergravities and their vacua
papers.summary: We study anomaly-free six-dimensional $N=(1,0)$ supergravities with $n_T=1$ and diagonal $U(1)_{R+}$ or $Sp(1)_{R+}$ gauging. The diagonal group combines R-symmetry with a commuting action on hypermultiplets. We perform bounded searches for anomaly-free models with one or two additional simple gauge group factors of rank at most 30, impose string-charge lattice and positive kinetic term conditions, and tabulate the resulting spectra. The main scans cover $q_{\max}\leq2$ and $d_{\max}\leq3$, where $q_{\max}$ is the largest absolute hyperino charge and $d_{\max}$ the largest diagonal $Sp(1)$ representation dimension, with supplementary searches at larger values.
