The updated model provides the correct thermal equilibrium limit of the heavy quark system with the medium background, and improves the accuracy in describing the nuclear modification factor and elliptic flow coefficient of $D$ mesons observed at RHIC and the LHC. Nuclear modification of different chemical components of charm hadrons, including $D^0$, $D_s^+$, $\Lambda_c^+$, $\Xi_c^0$, and $\Omega_c^0$, is investigated. Their spectrum ratios are found sensitive to not only the hadronization mechanism of charm quarks but also the medium-modified charm quark spectrum in heavy-ion collisions, offering additional constraints on the heavy quark dynamics inside a color-deconfined nuclear medium.

authors.name: Shu-Qing Li, Wen-Jing Xing, Shanshan Cao, Guang-You Qin

papers.title: Phenomenology of neutrino mass ordering synergies in reactor, accelerator, and atmospheric neutrino experiments, and the role of the detector response
papers.summary: The neutrino mass ordering is one of the main open questions of neutrino physics, addressed by reactor, accelerator, and atmospheric experiments and by their combination. When the data are fitted under the wrong ordering, each experiment returns its own value of $\Delta m^2_{31}$, its wrong-ordering solution. We show that this solution is a weighted average of the values preferred by the individual bins of the measured event spectra, in reconstructed energy and, for atmospheric neutrinos, also zenith angle, with weights set by their statistical precision. Both the values and the weights depend on the detector response. In the plane of $\Delta m^2_{31}$ fitted under the two orderings, the solutions lie on lines of slope close to $-1$, so that each experiment is described by one intercept. The weighted bin average extends the mass ordering sum rule to any oscillation experiment, including atmospheric neutrinos in Earth matter. It recovers the known closed forms for short-baseline reactors and for accelerators in vacuum, and for JUNO it equals a closed form evaluated at one effective energy, which depends on the energy resolution. Above the MSW resonance the frequency of atmospheric $\nu_\mu$ disappearance becomes nearly independent of $\delta_{CP}$, and the $\nu_\mu$ disappearance solution moves mainly with $\theta_{23}$. The atmospheric intercept depends on the energy and direction resolutions, the energy window, and the event classes, and differs between detectors. The synergy of two experiments is determined by the separation of their intercepts relative to their precisions on $|\Delta m^2_{31}|$. With JUNO, this separation depends strongly on $\delta_{CP}$ for an accelerator and is nearly independent of $\delta_{CP}$ and $\theta_{23}$ for IceCube DeepCore using all channels.

authors.name: Vanessa Cerrone, Marco Grassi

papers.title: Mono-Z Signatures of Vector Dark Matter Detection at Future Electron-Positron Colliders: FCC-ee and ILC
papers.summary: We investigate the mono-$Z$ signature of a vector dark matter (VDM) model at future electron-positron colliders. In this model, a stable vector boson, arising from an extended $U(1)$ gauge symmetry, serves as a viable DM candidate that interacts with the Standard Model (SM) through a Higgs portal. We perform a detailed cut-based analysis for the mono-$Z$ channel at the FCC-ee (with $\sqrt{s}=240$ and $365$ GeV) and the ILC (with $\sqrt{s}=1$ TeV), considering both leptonic and hadronic decays of the $Z$ boson. Signal significances are evaluated for benchmark points using fast event simulation with MadGraph5, PYTHIA8, and Delphes3. Our results demonstrate that future $e^+e^-$ colliders provide excellent sensitivity to Higgs-portal VDM, with the ILC's beam polarization offering an additional handle to suppress SM backgrounds. This study highlights the potential of lepton colliders in probing DM interactions.

authors.name: Seyed Yaser Ayazi, Saeid Paktinat Mehdiabadi, Rouzbeh Rouzbehi

papers.title: Pulsar Timing Correlations Induced by Stochastic Spin-2 Ultralight Dark Matter
papers.summary: Ultralight dark matter (ULDM) can generate time-dependent gravitational perturbations, providing a potential signal for pulsar timing arrays (PTAs). In Galactic halos, the velocity dispersion of ULDM gives rise to finite spatial coherence, which influences the correlations between pulsar timing signals. In this work, we derive the timing-residual cross-correlations induced by rapid metric oscillations of spin-2 ULDM, allowing for general polarization statistics. Under equipartition among the five polarization modes, the intrinsic angular kernel contains monopole and quadrupole components and exhibits an angular profile closely resembling that of spin-1 ULDM, suggesting a potential degeneracy between the two ULDM candidates in PTA observations.

authors.name: Hao-Xuan Shi, Yu-Mei Wu, Chang Liu

papers.title: Generalized transverse-momentum-dependent parton distributions of a photon and orbital angular momentum
papers.summary: The coefficients of generalized transverse-momentum-dependent distributions (GTMDs) that encode the canonical fermion orbital angular momentum and spin--orbit correlation do not contribute to the direct transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) and generalized-parton-distribution (GPD) projections. We present, to our knowledge, the first explicit calculation of the leading-twist, time-even, chiral-even fermion GTMDs of an on-shell real photon at zero skewness and order $\alpha$. The coefficients $\mathcal{F}_A$ and $\mathcal{G}_A$, which multiply the $k_\perp\times\Delta_\perp$ structure, yield the fermion orbital angular momentum $\ell_z^f$ and spin--orbit correlation $\mathcal{C}_z^f$. For photon helicity $+1$, both are obtained in closed form in the leading fermion--antifermion sector and obey $\mathcal{C}_z^f=-\ell_z^f/2$ for a common transverse regulator independent of $x$, because the channel with the active fermion's spin anti-aligned with its orbital motion carries three times the integrated weight of the aligned channel. The projections reproduce the known photon TMDs and leading-logarithmic photon-to-fermion kernels, and energy-momentum-tensor overlaps reproduce the known one-loop photon gravitational form factors $F_1$, $F_2$, and $F_3$. Our result provides an analytic benchmark for fermionic orbital and spin--orbit structure in the real photon.

authors.name: Sujit Jana, Asmita Mukherjee, Sreeraj Nair

papers.title: Inclusive Heavy Quarkonium Production in Lepton-Hadron Scattering in a Joint QCD+QED Factorization Approach
papers.summary: The Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) will provide an opportunity for precision studies of heavy quarkonium production in electron-proton ($ep$) and electron-nucleus ($eA$) collisions. Comparing production in $ep$ and $eA$ collisions provides a clean, well-controlled experimental environment to study interactions between a heavy quark pair and nuclear matter and the formation of quarkonia in a nuclear medium. In this talk, we present the first calculation of heavy quarkonium production in both $ep$ and $eA$ collisions at EIC energies using a joint QCD+QED factorization framework that treats collision-induced QCD and QED radiation on equal footing, and discuss the role of the nuclear medium in exploring how a physical quarkonium is emerged from a produced heavy quark pair. We also systematically extend our calculation to include next-to-leading power contributions in the inverse power expansion of quarkonium transverse momentum, and discuss the matching of our calculations to fixed-order calculations in the nonrelativistic Quantum Chromodynamics (NRQCD) approach.

authors.name: Jian-Wei Qiu, Kazuhiro Watanabe, Jia-Yue Zhang

papers.title: Heavy double-gluon quarkonium and $\overline{b}ggc$ mesons
papers.summary: We investigate heavy double-gluon hybrid mesons, built from a heavy quark-antiquark pair and two valence gluons, using the two-point QCD sum rule method. The charmonium-like $\bar{c}GGc$ and bottomonium-like $\bar{b}GGb$ states are considered with $J^{PC}=0^{\pm\pm}$ and $1^{\pm\pm}$, whereas the open-flavor $\bar{b}GGc$ states are classified by $J^{P}=0^{\pm}$ and $1^{\pm}$. The currents with $J^{PC}=0^{+-}, 0^{--}, 1^{++}$, and $1^{-+}$ vanish identically, so sum rules are derived for the remaining four channels. The operator product expansion is carried out up to dimension twelve, and the Borel parameter and continuum threshold are fixed so that the pole contribution dominates and the OPE converges. The resulting masses lie in the ranges $M\simeq 6.2$--$6.7$~GeV for $\bar{c}GGc$, $M\simeq 12.0$--$12.2$~GeV for $\bar{b}GGb$, and $M\simeq 9.2$--$9.6$~GeV for $\bar{b}GGc$, and the current couplings are obtained for all channels. These predictions provide a basis for analyzing the strong decays of double-gluon hybrids and for interpreting future experimental data in the heavy-quark sector.

authors.name: G. Daylan Esmer, B. Barsbay, K. Azizi, H. Sundu, S. T\"{u}rkmen

papers.title: Effects of Parton Pair Correlations on Direct-Photon Yields and Elliptic Flow in Heavy-Ion Collisions
papers.summary: Direct photons escape heavy-ion collisions with little rescattering, carrying information from the full emission history. Yet describing the measured direct-photon yield and the sizable elliptic flow $v_2$ together remains a long-standing challenge. Here we explore how correlations between emitting partons may affect both observables. The local $2\to2$ photon rate depends on the joint distribution of incoming partons, so a connected correlation between them can change photon emission without changing the one-particle distribution of medium particles. Once folded over the evolving medium in Au+Au and Pb+Pb collisions, the correlation raises the photon yield toward the fitted PHENIX and ALICE data and increases $v_2$ mainly at intermediate $p_T$. The fitted temperature dependence accounts for most of the net flow increase in this region, suggesting that the correlation changes the relative contributions between hotter and cooler regions.

authors.name: Xingjian Lu, Shuzhe Shi

papers.title: Composition-dependent ultralight dark matter detection with a tetrahedral superconducting gravity gradiometer
papers.summary: Tetrahedral superconducting gravity gradiometers designed as full-tensor gravitational-wave detectors, such as the ground-based mSOGRO design and the proposed lunar LANGO observatory, reconstruct the acceleration-gradient tensor from four test masses. We show that giving the four test masses two compositions in a $2+2$ arrangement adds a composition-dependent ultralight dark matter (ULDM) channel to that same tensor readout, with no separate dark-matter sensor and no dark-matter-specific readout. A coherently oscillating scalar accelerates each mass in proportion to its dilaton charge, and the tensor reconstruction leaves the charges only in a mean, rejected with the common mode, and a single vector $\qv$ proportional to the charge contrast $\Delta\abaralpha_{AB}$ between the two materials. The response is the rank-one tensor $\K_{\ULDM}(t)=\gv_\phi(t)\otimes\qv$, whose amplitude is set by the halo, independent of $m_\phi$. The axis of $\qv$ is fixed in advance by the material assignment, so the response obeys the null condition $\K_{\ULDM}(\mathbf{I}-\Pq)=0$ at every instant, for any $\gv_\phi$ including a virialized field with a stochastic gradient---an exact tensor discriminator against gravitational-wave signals; for a single composition $\qv=0$. With the gravitational-wave noise model, the coupling sensitivity for copper and lead test masses reaches $d_{\hat m}-d_g\simeq3.4\times10^{-8}$ for the baseline instrument and $4.9\times10^{-10}$ with upgraded accelerometers. The rank-one factorization and the null condition are summarized in a companion Letter; the present paper gives the derivations and the detector-level analysis.

authors.name: John J. Oh, Ho Jung Paik

papers.title: Determination of $V_{ud}$ from superallowed $\beta$ decays using effective field theory
papers.summary: A precision determination of $V_{ud}$ from superallowed $\beta$ decays requires exquisite control over radiative corrections, including nuclear-structure-dependent effects whose evaluation has traditionally relied on nuclear models. To assess the uncertainties inherent in the nuclear matrix elements, an alternative strategy based on effective field theory (EFT) has been established in recent years. Here, we present material progress in this program, in terms of a first EFT calculation of the crucial correction $\bar\delta_\text{NS}$ for 12 superallowed transitions ranging from $^{10}$C $\rightarrow$ $^{10}$B to $^{54}$Co $\rightarrow$ $^{54}$Fe. These main results rely on nuclear ab initio calculations using the coupled cluster method, benchmarked against Quantum Monte Carlo evaluations for light nuclei. The global fit to superallowed decay rates reveals that the precision in $V_{ud}$ is currently limited by short-distance contributions that in the EFT are parameterized as two-nucleon contact interactions, leading to an uncertainty $\delta V_{ud}\simeq 6\times 10^{-4}$. We discuss the consequences for the status of the first-row unitarity test of the CKM matrix as well as a roadmap how to reduce the uncertainty in $V_{ud}$ in the future.

authors.name: Samuel Novario, Graham Chambers-Wall, Vincenzo Cirigliano, Wouter Dekens, Jordy de Vries, Stefano Gandolfi, Martin Hoferichter, Emanuele Mereghetti

papers.title: Ab initio calculations of ${\bar\delta_\text{NS}}$ and extraction of ${V_{ud}}$ using effective field theory
papers.summary: Radiative corrections limit the precision of $V_{ud}$ extractions from superallowed $\beta$ decays. In particular, the model dependence in the nuclear matrix elements (NMEs) is difficult to assess without a clear organizing principle, which is provided by effective field theory (EFT). We report substantial progress in this program based on ab initio nuclear calculations using the coupled cluster method. Benchmarking results against Quantum Monte Carlo calculations for light nuclei, we evaluate all two-body NMEs that enter the correction $\bar\delta_\text{NS}$ across 12 superallowed transitions relevant for $V_{ud}$, including an estimate of truncation and Hamiltonian uncertainties. We find that certain three-body NMEs at ${\mathcal O}(\alpha^2)$ play an important role, due to a combination of large numerical prefactors and coherent scaling with $Z^2$. We develop a formalism to estimate such NMEs based on nuclear densities to complete the EFT evaluation of $\bar\delta_\text{NS}$, validating the corresponding two-body NMEs against ab initio calculations. We further identify the corrections in the traditional phase-space factor that are captured by the EFT and remove them consistently, which renders the individual transitions mutually consistent. Profiting from a recent calculation of ${\mathcal O}(\alpha^2 Z)$ ultrasoft photons, we find that the scale uncertainty in the EFT is now negligible, while the remaining uncertainty is dominated by contact terms required to renormalize the magnetic Gamow-Teller NMEs. One combination of low-energy constants can be determined from a global fit to the superallowed data, but the second one proves strongly correlated with $V_{ud}$, necessitating additional input to resolve the nuclear-structure effects. We argue that such short-distance contributions currently imply an uncertainty in $V_{ud}$ at the level of $\delta V_{ud}\simeq 6\times 10^{-4}$.

authors.name: Samuel Novario, Graham Chambers-Wall, Vincenzo Cirigliano, Wouter Dekens, Jordy de Vries, Stefano Gandolfi, Martin Hoferichter, Emanuele Mereghetti

papers.title: Spatiotemporal K-Shape: Reconstructing inhomogeneous condensate profiles on the lattice
papers.summary: Spatially modulated chiral condensates can affect the phase structure of dense QCD effective models. Understanding such order requires characterizing its real-space structure as well as detecting a modulation. Spatial two-point correlators retain the ensemble-averaged power spectrum but discard relative Fourier phases, leaving the configuration shapes undetermined in general. We propose the Spatiotemporal K-Shape method to extract representative shapes from lattice Monte Carlo ensembles without assuming a functional form. The method extends K-Shape clustering to periodic lattice fields, aligning configurations modulo translations and, optionally, a global sign or phase before extracting cluster centroids. Comparisons across clusterings assess whether one representative shape suffices. Controlled tests recover distinct profiles with identical correlators and separate mixtures of different shapes. Applied to the $(1+1)$-dimensional Gross-Neveu model with $N_f=8$, the method extracts non-sinusoidal profiles with two sign changes at two chemical potentials and separates multiple shape families at a third, where a single centroid is insufficient. Including the discrete chiral sign symmetry in the alignment can fold domain-length fluctuations into an asymmetric centroid without implying a preferred ensemble asymmetry. The method thus complements correlator diagnostics with representative real-space shapes and information on their diversity. The application to the Gross-Neveu model provides a testing ground for configuration-based studies of inhomogeneous order relevant to the QCD phase diagram.

authors.name: Keita Horie, Rin Kagami, Chiho Nonaka

papers.title: Constraining neutrino masses with localized fast radio bursts: Current bounds and future prospects
papers.summary:
The dispersion-measure (DM)--redshift relation of fast radio bursts (FRBs) provides independent low-redshift cosmological information for neutrino-mass inference. In this work, we perform joint analyses with cosmic microwave background (CMB) data, using 120 localized FRBs with reliable host-galaxy redshifts and larger mock samples, to investigate the effects of sample size and the dark-energy model on constraints on the sum of neutrino masses, $\sum m_
u$. In the $\Lambda$CDM+$\sum m_
u$ model, CMB+FRB gives $\sum m_
u<0.21\,\mathrm{eV}$, substantially relaxed relative to the current CMB+DESI result. With 1000 simulated events, CMB+FRB1(mock) gives an upper limit of $0.12\,\mathrm{eV}$, which decreases to $0.035\,\mathrm{eV}$ for CMB+FRB2(mock) with 10000 events. The latter is more stringent than the CMB+DESI limit, demonstrating the potential of large localized FRB samples to constrain neutrino mass. When the model is extended to $w_0w_a$CDM+$\sum m_
u$, both the observed and mock samples yield upper limits of approximately $0.3$--$0.4\,\mathrm{eV}$, indicating that the assumed dark-energy model remains a dominant factor in these constraints. As localized FRB samples grow and the modeling of the individual DM contributions becomes more accurate, FRBs may provide further independent low-redshift information for constraining neutrino mass.

authors.name: Yin-Long Cao, Ji-Guo Zhang, Guo-Hong Du, Tian-Nuo Li, Jing-Fei Zhang, Xin Zhang

papers.title: Study on net-proton number fluctuations in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{\textit{s}_{\text{NN}}}$ = 7.7-27 GeV with the SMASH model
papers.summary: Higher-order cumulants ($C_n$) of the event-by-event net-proton number ($\Delta N_{\mathrm{p}} = N_{\mathrm{p}} - N_{\bar{\mathrm{p}}}$) distributions are sensitive observables in the search for the QCD critical point. A reliable quantitative baseline for non-critical effects is essential for interpreting these observables. We calculate $C_2/\langle N_{\mathrm{p}} + N_{\bar{\mathrm{p}}}\rangle$, $C_3/C_1$, and $C_4/C_2$ in Au+Au collisions at collision energies $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 7.7$-$27$ GeV with the SMASH hadronic transport model. The collision-centrality, rapidity-window, and collision-energy dependences are reported. The cumulant ratios are predicted below the independent-Poisson baseline, with the suppression increasing toward more central collisions and larger rapidity windows. In 70-80% collisions, SMASH calculations lie above the STAR measurements for all three ratios, whereas in 0-5% collisions, the STAR $C_4/C_2$ value at 19.6 GeV lies below the SMASH reference with a pull of approximately $-2.7$. These results provide an independent non-critical hadronic baseline for assessing the model dependence of the observed data-model discrepancies.

authors.name: Fengxi Yan, Ting Liu, Rongrong Ma, Yunshuang Qin, Shule Wu, Shenghui Zhang, Fan Si

papers.title: Global analysis of the $\rho$ resonance in lattice QCD
papers.summary: We present a lattice-QCD study of the $\rho$ resonance in which we address the quark-mass and lattice-spacing dependence in a novel way using a global analysis of four $N_f=2+1$ ensembles. We parametrize discretization effects in the lattice energy levels and not in the scattering amplitude, which is defined in the continuum. We describe the amplitude using a $K$-matrix parameterization, which contains the light- and strange-quark mass dependence. By varying the parameterizations of quark-mass and lattice-spacing dependence, we examine the sensitivity of the physical-limit $\rho$ pole position to these choices and obtain the result $\sqrt{s}_\rho = 744(11)(7) - i\,69(7)(3)~\text{MeV}$ from a model average.

authors.name: Luka Jevsenak, Luka Leskovec, Stefan Meinel, John Negele, Srijit Paul, Andrew Pochinsky

papers.title: Heavy-quark gluon radiation in transversely flowing QCD matter: First-subeikonal corrections
papers.summary: We investigate medium-induced gluon radiation from energetic heavy quarks propagating through a finite-size QCD medium with transverse collective flow. Within the DGLV framework, we calculate the radiation spectrum at first order in opacity and to first-subeikonal accuracy, retaining finite heavy-quark and effective gluon masses. Subleading corrections to the longitudinal propagator poles generate mass-dependent modifications of both the residue denominators and formation phases. For rotationally symmetric transverse-momentum integration domains, all contributions linear in the transverse flow velocity vanish after full azimuthal integration, while a nonzero static first-subeikonal correction remains. For representative medium parameters, this correction increases the integrated fractional radiative energy loss by approximately $10$--$20\%$, depending on the quark mass, initial energy, and path length. At the differential level, transverse flow produces a dipolar angular anisotropy, enhancing radiation along the flow direction and suppressing it in the opposite direction.

authors.name: Bojana Ilic, Magdalena Djordjevic

papers.title: $T_{cc}$ and Hidden Charm Tetraquarks $1^+$ and $0^+$in QCD sum rules and Heavy-Quark Spin Symmetry
papers.summary: In this work, $T_{cc}$ double charm tetraquark and $1^{+}$ and $0^{+}$ hidden charm tetraquarks are studied within the QCD sum rules framework. In the heavy-quark limit, the $1^+$ and $0^+$ tetraquarks are degenerate and the difference in their masses is an $1/m_c$ effect. It is shown that, although the uncertainty in the mass predictions of each of these hadrons is ${\cal O}(100\;\mathrm{MeV})$, when the mass differences are studied, the uncertainty is reduced to less than ${\cal O}(10\;\mathrm{MeV})$. Hence, it is concluded that if one of the exotic hadrons is observed and its mass is used as input, the masses of the other hadrons can be determined with a precision of ${\cal O}(10\;\mathrm{MeV})$ using the QCD sum rules method.

authors.name: Semra Sari Ferah, Altug Ozpineci

papers.title: Higgs production from anomalous gluon dynamics
papers.summary: We present a two-loop analysis of the contributions to Higgs production via gluon-gluon fusion arising from the triple-gluon operator in the Standard Model effective field theory (SMEFT). Our discussion covers all aspects of renormalization group (RG) improved perturbation theory, including matching and running within the SMEFT. This study can therefore be seen as a blueprint of the intricacies and subtleties that arise in RG improved SMEFT calculations for collider processes beyond the leading order.

authors.name: Ulrich Haisch

papers.title: Left-Chiral Neutrino Secret Interactions Probed by High-Energy Neutrinos Surviving the Cosmic Neutrino Background
papers.summary: This work explores the potential of astrophysical neutrinos to probe neutrino secret interactions ($\nu$SI) through their propagation in the Cosmic Neutrino Background (C$\nu$B). Using representative energies and distances for SN 1987A, NGC 1068, TXS 0506+056 and PKS 0735+178, together with distance hypotheses for KM3-230213A, we derive single-event survival benchmarks for the mediator mass and coupling. We focus on scenarios that do not populate right-handed neutrino states in the early Universe and therefore avoid the strongest cosmological constraints: a massive spin-one mediator with a left-chiral coupling to Dirac neutrinos and a scalar mediator coupled to Majorana neutrinos. We also consider scalar exchange with Dirac neutrinos, a common benchmark in propagation studies, and demonstrate that on the standard relic background its resonance is helicity suppressed, with a strength controlled by the relic-neutrino mass. The analysis covers a broad range of mediator masses, including the light-mediator, resonant and heavy-mediator regions, and accounts for the effects of the relic-neutrino masses and of cosmological evolution along the propagation path. We illustrate the main features of each scenario in a common-mass approximation, with analytic expressions for the non-relativistic and ultra-relativistic relic background, and then extend the analysis to realistic non-degenerate neutrino mass spectra. Owing to its energy, the KM3-230213A event shifts the resonant sensitivity to heavier mediators, while distant-source hypotheses increase the propagation sensitivity in this mass range.

authors.name: Maria Petropavlova

papers.title: Scalar and spin polarizabilities of singly heavy baryons within heavy baryon chiral perturbation theory
papers.summary: We present a systematic study of the scalar electromagnetic and spin polarizabilities of spin-1/2 singly charmed baryons at $\mathcal{O}(p^4)$ within the framework of heavy baryon chiral perturbation theory. Our results show that the higher-order corrections to the electric polarizability are small, while those to the magnetic polarizability are relatively larger due to the small mass splitting of singly charmed baryons and are closely related to transition magnetic moments. Furthermore, we find that the spin polarizabilities of singly charmed baryons, except for $\gamma_{M1M1}$, are much smaller than those of the nucleons. We have also calculated the polarizabilities for singly bottom baryons, with the results showing generally larger values than those of singly charmed baryons.

authors.name: Zi-Jun Li, Zhan-Wei Liu, Ping Chen

papers.title: Calculating extremely high energy bremsstrahlung in matter
papers.summary: Ultra-relativistic electrons initiate electromagnetic showers in ordinary matter that evolve through bremsstrahlung and pair production. At very high energy, the quantum mechanical duration of bremsstrahlung becomes longer than the mean free time to elastically scatter from the medium, leading to a significant suppression known at the Landau-Pomeranchuk-Migdal (LPM) effect. For some ranges of bremsstrahlung photon and initial electron energies $(k_\gamma,E)$, the duration becomes so long that it will also overlap with subsequent pair production by the bremsstrahlung photon, disrupting LPM suppression and drastically changing LPM predictions. We have previously calculated this change for extremely high energies ($k_\gamma \gg 2$ TeV or more, depending on the medium), for which the electron mass and medium-induced photon mass could be ignored. In this paper, we extend that analysis to lower (but still ultra-relativistic) energy by accounting for those masses, leading to a rich map of behavior in different regions of $(k_\gamma,E)$.

authors.name: Peter Arnold, Joshua Bautista, Omar Elgedawy, Shahin Iqbal

papers.title: Minimal Majoron Dark Matter
papers.summary: We study Majoron dark matter (DM) in its minimal realization, based on the Type-I seesaw framework extended by a SM-singlet complex scalar. Remaining agnostic about the origin and value of the Majoron mass, we evaluate the DM abundance from both the freeze-in and misalignment mechanisms, and identify the viable parameter space consistent with observational constraints. Without fine-tuning of the initial misalignment angle, we find that the Majoron mass is bounded by $m_J \lesssim \mathcal{O}(10)~\mathrm{MeV}$. We also discuss compatibility with thermal leptogenesis. Successful leptogenesis with two right-handed neutrinos favors misalignment-dominated production with the Majoron mass $m_J \lesssim \mathcal{O}(100)~\mathrm{eV}$, while freeze-in dominated production is compatible with leptogenesis only with a mild fine-tuning of the initial misalignment angle, $\theta_i \lesssim \mathcal{O}(0.01)$.

authors.name: Kensuke Akita, Koichi Hamaguchi, Haruto Kitagawa, Tatsuya Yokoyama

papers.title: Investigating the mass spectra of $1F$-wave singly heavy $\Sigma_{Q}$, $\Xi^{\prime}_{Q}$, and $\Omega_{Q}$ baryons
papers.summary: In this work, we enumerated the mass spectra of the experimentally unobserved $1F$-wave states with the the orbital angular momentum $L$ = 3 for the singly heavy $\Sigma_{Q}$, $\Xi^{\prime}_{Q}$, and $\Omega_{Q}$ $(Q=c, b)$ baryons in the framework of quark-diquark configuration using the Regge trajectory model and the scaling rules. To determine the effective masses of the heavy quark and two light quarks, the relativistic effective mass formula are employed by combining the Coulomb potential. Within the spin-dependent Hamiltonian, we construct the mass shift forms as a non-diagonal symmetric $6\times 6$ matrix for the $1F$-wave states of $\Sigma_{Q}$, $\Xi^{\prime}_{Q}$, and $\Omega_{Q}$ baryons. Our analysis of mass spectra provides valuable insights to guide future experimental investigations, and enhances the understanding of the spectroscopic properties of unobserved $1F$-wave orbital excitations for these singly heavy baryons.

authors.name: Ji-Si Pan, Ji-Hai Pan

papers.title: Isospin-breaking effects on the threshold cusp structures in $\Lambda N$-$\Sigma N$ scattering
papers.summary: We discuss the isospin-breaking effects on threshold cusp structures in multichannel scattering near two-body thresholds. In hadronic systems with isospin symmetry, two or more nearly degenerate thresholds can appear, and their small splitting due to isospin breaking can generate multiple cusp structures in a narrow energy region. In this paper, using the $K$-matrix representation, we derive a general expression for the scattering amplitude near the thresholds and show that the cusp structures can be classified by the signs of the slopes of the cross section above and below threshold. We also show that additional restrictions appear in two- or three-channel systems and in the Flatt\'e amplitude. For three-channel scattering with two nearby thresholds, we clarify how the two cusp structures are related when the threshold splitting is small and how they merge into a single cusp in the degenerate limit. Finally, we discuss the cusp structures in the $\Lambda p$ elastic cross section in the coupled $\Lambda N$-$\Sigma N$ system with charge $Q=+1$. We show that, when isospin breaking is small, the two cusp structures are constrained by isospin symmetry. We also perform quantitative calculations using both simplified examples and realistic input based on N$^2$LO chiral effective field theory, and find that isospin breaking can significantly modify the relative sharpness of the cusps and may even change the cusp type itself.

authors.name: Katsuyoshi Sone, Yudai Ichikawa, Tetsuo Hyodo

papers.title: Constraints on a Light Leptophilic Scalar from Dark-Sector Couplings
papers.summary: We study a minimal framework where a Majorana fermion dark matter particle interacts with a light scalar mediator coupled mainly to electrons. We examine both freeze-out and freeze-in production to determine the regions of parameter space that yield the correct relic abundance with particular emphasis on a detailed comparison with results in the recent literature. The analysis includes cosmological and astrophysical constraints as well as laboratory bounds from electron-recoil experiments, fixed target searches, and precision measurements. The combined results identify a narrow but viable parameter region, favoring sub-GeV dark matter, and define clear targets for future experimental tests. This highlights the strong complementarity between direct-detection experiments and collider searches. We additionally investigate the mediator-mass region around 17 MeV, motivated by the hints reported by the ATOMKI experiment and the PADME collaboration, including couplings between the mediator and light quarks. Direct searches already constrain a large region of the parameter space, even when dark matter is produced via freeze-in, pointing again to sub-GeV dark matter.

authors.name: Marco Graziani, Giacomo Landini, Federico Mescia, Claudio Toni, Ludovico Vittorio

papers.title: Axial-Vector Lattice Benchmarks Reveal a Common Medium Response of Meson Screening in Hot QCD
papers.summary: Meson screening masses trace the evolution of hadronic correlations toward quasi-free quark--antiquark screening in hot QCD. Combining lattice QCD (LQCD) benchmarks with a symmetry-preserving Dyson--Schwinger baseline, we identify a flavor-dependent axial-vector quasi-free onset, $x^\ast_{fg}=T^\ast_{fg}/T_c$: an operational matching scale based on the proximity of the axial-vector screening mass to its free-field reference, where $T_c$ is the pseudocritical temperature. On the finite interval $1\le T/T_c\lesssim x^\ast_{fg}$, independent light/strange and charm-containing lattice benchmarks are organized by a common medium-response function with one flavor-sector parameter. One axial-vector point fixes this parameter; the remaining axial-vector data test the temperature dependence of the response, and vector screening masses validate it without vector input. A reduced-mass interpolation then yields lattice-testable predictions for quasi-free onset scales and vector and axial-vector screening spectra in light--charm and open-bottom sectors.

authors.name: Jie Ren, Chen Chen, Fei Gao, Si-xue Qin

papers.title: $\lambda$, $\rho$, and $\sigma$ Regge trajectories for the hexaquark ${(\bar{u}(cc))(b(\bar{b}\bar{b}))}$ in the triquark-antitriquark picture
papers.summary: We propose Regge trajectory relations for the hexaquark ${(\bar{u}(cc))(b(\bar{b}\bar{b}))}$ by using the Regge trajectory relations for diquarks and triquarks. With these newly derived relations, we investigate five series of hexaquark Regge trajectories: the $\lambda$-, $\rho_1$-, $\rho_2$-, $\sigma_1$-, and $\sigma_2$-trajectories. We demonstrate that, apart from the simplest $\lambda_1$-trajectories, the $\rho_1$-, $\rho_2$-, $\sigma_1$-, and $\sigma_2$-trajectories cannot be constructed by merely mimicking the meson Regge trajectories, since mesons possess no internal substructures. To derive these trajectories, one must account for the structure and internal substructure of the hexaquark. Without this structural information, the $\rho_1$-, $\rho_2$-, $\sigma_1$-, and $\sigma_2$-trajectories could only be obtained through direct fits to available theoretical predictions or future experimental data. We demonstrate that the $\rho_1$-, $\rho_2$-, $\sigma_1$-, and $\sigma_2$-trajectories for the hexaquark do not correspond respectively to the Regge trajectories for the triquark, antitriquark, diquark, and antidiquark. Nevertheless, their behaviors match those of the Regge trajectories for the triquark $(\bar{u}(cc))$, the antitriquark $(b(\bar{b}\bar{b}))$, the diquark $(cc)$, and the antidiquark $(\bar{b}\bar{b})$, in that respective order. Furthermore, we present rough mass estimates for the excited states corresponding to the $\lambda$-, $\rho_1$-, $\rho_2$-, $\sigma_1$-, and $\sigma_2$-trajectories.

authors.name: Xin-Ru Liu, Qi Liu, Jiao-Kai Chen

papers.title: Dynamical criterion for biased domain-wall formation
papers.summary: In the presence of a bias term, the conventional condition for forming a domain-wall network is $p_{\rm fv}>p_c\simeq 0.31$, with $p_{\rm fv}/(1-p_{\rm fv})=\exp(-\Delta V(0)/V_b(0))$, where $p_{\rm fv}$ is the false-vacuum fraction immediately after the phase transition, $\Delta V(0)$ is the zero-temperature energy splitting between the false and true vacua and $V_b(0)$ is the zero-temperature barrier height measured from the true vacuum. This criterion, however, cannot be generally valid, since it is insensitive to the dynamics of the phase transition. In this work, we derive a dynamical criterion for domain wall formation in the presence of a bias term. We evaluate $p_{\rm fv}$ at the freeze-out temperature of the false-vacuum correlation volumes $T_{\rm fo}$, obtaining a substantially stricter criterion. The same dynamical picture also yields a necessary consistency condition for applying scaling-regime gravitational-wave estimates, $T_{\rm fo}>T_{\rm ann}$, where $T_{\rm ann}$ is the annihilation temperature inferred from the scaling-regime dynamics.

authors.name: Wen-Yuan Ai

papers.title: Toponium effects on quantum steering and Bell nonlocality of top quarks
papers.summary: We investigate quantum steering and Bell nonlocality in top-quark pair production at the LHC near threshold. The toponium contribution strengthens the spin-singlet component and substantially enhances the entanglement between the two quark spins. With current LHC data, quantum steering appears to be observable at the $5\sigma$ level provided systematic uncertainties are at 5\% or below. For Bell nonlocality, the statistical significance can also be high close to threshold, but systematics are expected to limit a possible measurement to around $2\sigma$ sensitivity.

authors.name: J. A. Aguilar-Saavedra, S. Rodr\'iguez-Ben\'itez

papers.title: Phenomenology of genuine twist-three distributions from a global QCD analysis
papers.summary: We present an extraction and phenomenological study of genuine twist-three parton distribution functions (PDFs) through a global QCD analysis of the structure function $g_2$ in deep-inelastic scattering (DIS), its moment $d_2$, and single-/double-spin asymmetries in semi-inclusive DIS (SIDIS). The unified description of these processes clearly confirms the universality of genuine twist-three PDFs and the validity of QCD factorization theorems at this subleading level. The extraction is accompanied by several validation tests, tests of sum rules, comparisons with earlier literature, computation forces and average transverse momentum of partons. As a by-product, we also obtain Sivers and worm-gear-T transverse momentum dependent (TMD) distributions, which allows us to construct a tomographic picture of the proton based on substantially broader data.

authors.name: Guillermo Portela, Alexey Vladimirov

papers.title:
Connecting $B	o K^{(\ast)}
u
u$ and $K	o \pi
u
u$ decays with neutrino physics
papers.summary:
We investigate the contributions of Lepton Number Violating (LNV) effective operators to the rare decays $B	o K^{(\ast)}
u
u$ and $K	o \pi
u
u$. Such operators can modify the kinematic distributions of these processes, providing distinctive probes of physics beyond the Standard Model. Through a renormalization-group analysis, we show that the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) operators responsible for these effects are subject to stringent indirect constraints from neutrino physics. In particular, we find that the mild excess reported by Belle-II in the $B^+	o K^+
u
u$ channel cannot be explained by LNV SMEFT operators without introducing significant fine-tuning in neutrino masses. We then show that these constraints can be evaded in the SMEFT minimally extended by a light right-handed neutrino, allowing for sizable effects in rare meson decays. Finally, we explore the implications of this viable scenario for low-energy processes, including neutrinoless double-beta decays.

authors.name: Asmaa Abada, Claire Chevallier, Luighi P. S. Leal, Anna Llaurad\'o, Olcyr Sumensari, Renata Zukanovich Funchal

papers.title: Form-Factor-Constrained Non-Factorized Transition-GPD Tomography of $N\to\Delta(1232)$ Multipole Structure
papers.summary: A form-factor-constrained non-factorized transition-GPD reconstruction is developed for the $N\to\Delta(1232)$ electromagnetic transition. The production input consists of the published CLAS magnetic multipole amplitude and electric and scalar/Coulomb quadrupole ratios. Additional external low-$Q^2$ ratio data are retained only as a separate ratio-sector diagnostic. The electroproduction quantities are propagated replica by replica and converted to the dimensionless Jones--Scadron transition form factors $G_M^*$, $G_E^*$, and $G_C^*$. AICc model selection yields a modified dipole for $G_M^*$, a dipole for $G_E^*$, and a cubic $z$ expansion for $G_C^*$. These fits define the imposed positive-$x$ normalization $F_\alpha(t)=2G_\alpha^*(-t)$ for factorized, correlated exponential, Regge-like, and double-distribution-inspired transition-GPD profiles. The upper boundary of the impact-parameter transform is fixed by the largest measured absolute-form-factor point, $Q^2=6~\mathrm{GeV}^2$, so that no high-$Q^2$ continuation beyond the measured range enters the production reconstruction. The primary transverse localization observable is therefore defined from the small-$Q^2$ slope of the modeled transition GPD, with finite-window radial moments retained only as secondary core-shape diagnostics. For the slope-defined width, the transition form factor contributes an $x$-independent channel-dependent offset, while the entire $x$ dependence is fixed by the chosen longitudinal--transverse profile ansatz. The factorized profile is $x$-independent and the three non-factorized families generate distinct modeled $x$ dependences. The resulting reconstruction separates measured transition-form-factor information from model-dependent longitudinal structure and provides a controlled framework for assessing structural and covariance sensitivity in $N\to\Delta(1232)$ transition tomography.

authors.name: R. M. Marinaro III

papers.title: Unbiased Data-Driven Determination of the Nuclear Dipole Amplitude in the Color Glass Condensate
papers.summary: Gluon saturation limits the growth of parton densities at small Bjorken-$x$ and is expected to be most pronounced in heavy nuclei. Yet quantitative extractions of the nuclear gluon dipole amplitude have long relied on parametrized initial conditions, introducing uncontrolled model dependence that obscures genuine nuclear effects. We introduce a physics-informed neural-network framework that embeds the collinearly improved Balitsky-Kovchegov evolution equation directly into the training objective, allowing the impact-parameter-averaged dipole amplitude to be determined from data without assuming a functional form for its initial condition. Applying this framework to forward-hadron nuclear-modification-factor and coherent $J/\psi$ photoproduction data, we extract the $^{208}$Pb dipole amplitude at $x_0=0.01$ with QCD evolution and momentum-space positivity enforced throughout training. The evolved amplitude reproduces the measured cross sections across the available kinematic range and yields a saturation-scale ratio $Q_{s0,\mathrm{Pb}}^2/Q_{s0,p}^2 = 3.17^{+0.17}_{-0.10}$, consistent with simple geometric scaling. The extracted Pb initial condition is well described by a McLerran-Venugopalan-type form, in contrast to the proton, reflecting the higher color-charge density of a large nucleus. Using the same amplitude, we predict the rapidity dependence of the transverse-momentum ratio in $pp$, $p$Pb, and Pb$p$ collisions, finding agreement with recent LHCb measurements at low multiplicity without any system-dependent parameters. This work provides the first unbiased, data-driven determination of nuclear structure in the saturation regime and establishes a general strategy for embedding nonlinear evolution equations into machine-learning extractions of dynamically constrained observables.

authors.name: Si-Wei Dai, Haowu Duan, Long-Gang Pang, Guang-You Qin, Shu-Yi Wei, Han-Zhong Zhang, Wenbin Zhao

papers.title: Thermal Evolution and Hydrodynamic Filtering of Pseudoscalar Dark Matter
papers.summary: Filtered dark matter provides a mechanism for producing massive dark matter particles during a first order phase transition. The resulting abundance can be modified by plasma hydrodynamics. We investigate this effect in a complex singlet extension of the Standard Model, focusing on the deflagration regime. The entropy normalized dark matter abundance $Y_\chi$ is calculated using both analytic and numerical methods. As the dark matter mass increases, we identify three patterns of abundance evolution before nucleation, ranging from thermal equilibrium to thermal suppression and freeze-out. For $\xi_w=0.01$, the numerical results show that hydrodynamic effects increase the final $Y_\chi$ by factors of approximately $4.1$, $5.7$, and $31.6$ for $m_\chi=1.78$, $2.30$, and $5.03~\mathrm{TeV}$, respectively. For the two lighter masses, the numerical and analytic results agree within $5\%$, and the difference is reduced to about $1\%$ or less when hydrodynamic effects are included. The heaviest case requires a numerical treatment because dark matter freeze-out before nucleation. Our results show that hydrodynamic reheating can enhance $Y_\chi$ even when dark matter has already frozen out before the phase transition. In this regime, $Y_\chi$ is determined by the dark matter abundance established before nucleation and hydrodynamic filtering at the bubble wall.

authors.name: Xiu-Fei Li, Hongxin Wang, Lei Wang

papers.title: Inelastic from the Other Side: Xenon Excitation Signals in Light of the LZ High-Recoil Event
papers.summary: The LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment recently reported a single event consistent with a nuclear recoil of $E_{\rm NR}\sim248$~keV in an extended-energy search. We study the accompanying inelastic-xenon channel, $\chi+Xe\to\chi+Xe^{*}$, as a complementary test of dark matter (DM) interpretations of such high-recoil events. Using the non-relativistic effective-field-theory (NREFT) framework, we compute the inelastic-xenon rates for representative scenarios including accelerated DM populations and inelastic dark matter. Their signal patterns in the S1--S2 plane are reconstructed. The nuclear de-excitation shifts these signals toward the electronic-recoil band, where they may overlap with clustered isotope backgrounds. We then propose a schematic, physics-motivated background model to estimate their detectability. For many benchmarks, the inelastic-xenon rates are $\mathcal{O}(0.1)$ of the elastic rates or below, and the projected sensitivity remains weak even at $200~{\rm tonne\,yr}$ for the scenarios investigated. Our results provide additional inelastic-xenon signal predictions for various DM scenarios and motivate improved high-energy background modeling and detector calibration for future searches.

authors.name: Guanhua Gu, Lingfeng Li, Shao-Song Tang, Yongheng Xu

papers.title: Flavour decomposition of the chiral-odd form factors of the nucleon
papers.summary: We compute the chiral-odd form factors $H_T$, $E_T$ and $\tilde{H}_T$ of the nucleon within light-cone QCD sum rules, separately for the $u$ and $d$ quarks, over $1\le Q^2\le 10$ GeV$^2$, and organise their values at $Q^2=0$ into the tensor monopole, dipole and quadrupole moments $g_T$, $\kappa_T$ and $Q_T$. The flavour components of the quadrupole moment and the isoscalar channel have not previously been obtained in this framework. The form factors are read from a basis of Lorentz structures that becomes independent only after a canonical ordering of the Dirac strings, and three of the eight surviving structures give the three form factors separately. Two statements follow from the analytic expressions. The $d$-quark contributions to $E_T$ and $\tilde{H}_T$ are equal and opposite in the chiral limit, the breaking being proportional to the quark mass and to the twist-six amplitude $\mathcal{V}_6$. At the level of the least suppressed momentum-fraction integral, the isoscalar tensor charge receives no leading-twist contribution, the twist-three terms of the two flavours cancelling. Neither statement is visible without resolving the flavours. At $\mu^2=1$ GeV$^2$ we obtain, for the two distribution-amplitude sets, $g_T^{u-d}=1.27(7)$ and $1.08(6)$, $\kappa_T^{u-d}=1.35(62)$ and $1.58(59)$, $Q_T^{u-d}=-4.40(83)$ and $-4.20(73)$, $g_T^{u+d}=0.39(7)$ and $0.38(6)$, $\kappa_T^{u+d}=4.47(62)$ and $4.32(59)$, and $Q_T^{u+d}=2.41(53)$ and $1.56(30)$. The mean-field relation $2\tilde{H}_T^{u-d}=-E_T^{u-d}$ holds in sign and in order of magnitude, the ratio being $0.64(16)$ and $0.67(15)$. In the impact-parameter plane the two flavour distributions are displaced in opposite transverse directions by nearly equal amounts, $\langle b_y\rangle=0.37$ and $-0.37$ fm, and both are elongated across the polarisation axis, the $d$ quark some five to six times more strongly than the $u$ quark.

authors.name: U. \"Ozdem

papers.title: Warm-Inflation: a software for first-principles integration of warm inflation power spectra
papers.summary: As part of a PhD thesis entitled `Scalar perturbations in warm inflation and during reheating' we present a software for computing warm inflation observables. In particular, our Mathematica implementation computes the power spectrum, spectral tilt, and tensor-to-scalar ratio for a given momentum scale. Compared with other implementations, we start in a Bunch-Davies state deep inside the horizon, ideally at a time when thermal noise is exponentially suppressed. We integrate gauge-invariant equations for three curvature perturbations across horizon exit. We continue deep enough outside of horizon so that all curvature perturbations agree. Results are illustrated for Standard Model embedded warm inflation, and we also provide notebooks for several other popular potentials and friction coefficients. The theoretical foundations for the code can be found in the main part of the thesis or in earlier papers [1,2]. Specifically, part II derives gauge-invariant, model-agnostic evolution equations, as well as the noise autocorrelator interpolating between quantum and classical domains. Part III presents the general ideas behind the numerical implementation, while part IV presents selected results. The code is described, line-by-line, in Appendix A. The published PhD thesis is available at https://doi.org/10.48620/101166 while the notebooks can be downloaded from https://github.com/alicarogeljblackhole/Warm-Inflation.

authors.name: Alica Rogelj

papers.title: Evidence for Kaluza-Klein excitations of the graviton, gluon and quark at LHC
papers.summary: Following our paper showing evidence for a tower of Kaluza-Klein gravitons, we interpret the massive 4 jet excesses observed by CMS. They could come from the decay of two heavy KK gluons gkk(3.6TeV) and gkk(8.6TeV) into pairs of KK quarks qkk(1TeV) and qkk(2.1TeV). Present limits on gkk into top pairs seem to exclude gkk(3.6TeV) but these limits assume a dominant decay into top pairs, which can be questioned as was the case in our study of KK graviton decays. The cross section predicted for gkk(8.6) requires a BR into a pair of qkk(2.1TeV) or order 10% which is not unlikely. We also discuss the issue of a hierarchy between the KK graviton masses and the vector boson masses and the solution provided by the RS multi-brane models. Prospects for reaching a 6 s.d. level local evidence with RUN3 data are promising for 3 channels. KK excitations of the Z boson are discussed and appear also promising. Indirect evidences for these particles are also presented.

authors.name: Alain Le Yaouanc, Fran\c{c}ois Richard

papers.title: Holographic Approaches to Hadron Structure
papers.summary: We give an introduction to and an overview of holographic approaches to QCD and hadron structure. After an introduction to the string-theoretic foundations of holographic QCD, we review the predictions of top-down and bottom-up models for the phenomenology of mesons, baryons, and glueballs. We focus on the top-down model following from probe flavor branes in the Witten model of low-energy Yang-Mills theory and, in the more phenomenological approach of bottom-up models, mostly on minimal models based on five-dimensional anti-de Sitter space, which also implement global symmetries and their anomalies consistently, but allow the high-energy behavior to better match real QCD.

authors.name: Luigi Cappiello, Anton Rebhan, Shigeki Sugimoto

papers.title: A dual-moment phenomenological framework for gravitational,electromagnetic and strong interactions
papers.summary: The unification of fundamental interactions remains an outstanding open problem in fundamental physics. Most existing unification schemes rely on extra dimensions, exotic symmetries, or unobserved dynamical degrees of freedom. Here we construct a minimal classical phenomenological framework built on primitive charges and motion-induced kinetic dual moments. Gravitational, electromagnetic, and strong interactions are coherently formulated within a unified inverse-square-law structure. We postulate a universal coupling relation connecting source-charge couplings and moment-mediated couplings across these interaction sectors. Although weak-charge degrees of freedom can be formally accommodated within the formalism, full quantitative treatment of weak-interaction dynamics is left for future work. The model recovers well-established low-energy limits for planetary orbits, atomic systems, and heavy-quark hadrons. Importantly, it yields distinguishable corrections to light deflection by rapidly spinning compact objects, and three independent experimental schemes are proposed to test these predictions.

authors.name: Zhiguang Tan, Shengjie Wang, Hua Zheng

papers.title: Novel method for measuring the isovector partner of X(3872)
papers.summary: The predicted isovector partner of the $X(3872)$, denoted as $W_{c1}$, is expected to produce only a relatively weak structure near the charged $D \bar{D}^*$ threshold, making its experimental identification challenging. In this work, we explore the triangle singularity (TS) mechanism as a means of enhancing the sensitivity to the $W_{c1}$ in the decays $B^0 \to \pi K \bar{D}^0 D^{*0}$. We investigate the $D_{s1}(2536) \bar{D}^*$ triangle rescattering mechanism, incorporating the coupled-channel $D \bar{D}^*$ scattering amplitudes obtained from the Lippmann-Schwinger equation. The interplay between the TS and the coupled-channel dynamics produces characteristic structures in the $K \bar{D}^0 D^{*0}$ invariant mass distributions associated with the $X(3872)$ and its isovector partner $W_{c1}$. In particular, the charged-channel contribution exhibits a distinct structure sensitive to the nearby $W_{c1}$ pole. Our results demonstrate that the TS mechanism provides a promising way to probe the otherwise weak manifestation of the $W_{c1}$, offering a complementary experimental strategy for searching for this predicted state at Belle II and LHCb.

authors.name: Qiu-Lin Tan, Mao-Jun Yan, Chun-Sheng An, Cheng-Rong Deng, Xiao-Hai Liu

papers.title: Connecting Electroweak Fine-Tuning, Tens-of-GeV Dark Matter, and Exotic Higgs Decays in the GNMSSM
papers.summary: In the general next-to-minimal supersymmetric standard model (GNMSSM), we connect electroweak fine-tuning, a singlino dark matter candidate with mass around tens of GeV, and Exotic Higgs Decays, identifying a natural region characterized by the mass hierarchy $m_{\tilde{S}}<m_{\tilde{B}}<m_{\tilde{H}}$ and $\mu_{\rm tot}\in [200, 500]$ GeV. For fine-tuning measure $\Delta \leq 40$, the branching ratio $\mathrm{Br}(h\to a_sa_s)$ falls in the range 7\%$-$25\%, with the pseudoscalar mass $m_{a_s}$ lying mostly between 10 and 20 GeV. This region splits into two viable scenarios consistent with LZ 2024 direct detection: one where the lightest CP-even Higgs $h_1$ is SM-like ($h_1$ case), and another where the second-lightest $h_2$ is SM-like ($h_2$ case). LHC searches for $h\to a_sa_s \to b\bar{b}\tau^+\tau^-$ exclude 12\% (10\%) of samples with 12 GeV $\leq m_{a_s} \leq$ 15.5 GeV in the $h_1$ ($h_2$) case, while a substantial fraction remains accessible at the HL-LHC in the $h_2$ case. Our analysis unifies naturalness, dark matter, and observable exotic Higgs decays, yielding concrete targets for future experiments.

authors.name: Zhaoxia Heng, Fei Li, Haijing Zhou

papers.title: Low-lying doubly charmed strange baryons via QCD sum rules
papers.summary: We systematically investigate the masses of the low-lying doubly heavy baryons and their $B^*(3/2^+)\to B(1/2^+)\gamma$ radiative transitions within QCD sum rules and light-cone sum rules (LCSR). By constructing mixed interpolating currents, we obtain $M_{\Xi_{cc}}=3.62^{+0.14}_{-0.15}$ GeV, $M_{\Xi_{cc}^*}=3.72^{+0.14}_{-0.13}$ GeV, $M_{\Omega_{cc}}=3.72^{+0.13}_{-0.15}$ GeV, and $M_{\Omega_{cc}^*}=3.82^{+0.13}_{-0.15}$ GeV, together with their doubly bottom partners around $10.27$--$10.34$ GeV. The extracted masses are compatible with the observed $\Xi_{cc}$ and $\Omega_{cc}$ states and predict hyperfine splittings of about $101^{+27}_{-11}$ MeV and $99^{+11}_{-12}$ MeV for the $\Xi_{cc}$ and $\Omega_{cc}$ systems, respectively. Using these inputs, we derive the LCSR for the electromagnetic form factors and obtain radiative widths $\Gamma(\Xi_{cc}^{*++}\to\Xi_{cc}^{++}\gamma)=5.25^{+8.57}_{-3.62}$ keV, $\Gamma(\Xi_{cc}^{*+}\to\Xi_{cc}^{+}\gamma)=0.31^{+0.84}_{-0.25}$ keV, and $\Gamma(\Omega_{cc}^{*+}\to\Omega_{cc}^{+}\gamma)=0.41^{+0.67}_{-0.30}$ keV, while the corresponding doubly bottom widths are at the $0.002$--$0.01$ keV level. We find that the magnetic-dipole contribution dominates, whereas the electric-quadrupole form factor is numerically small. The light- and heavy-quark photon-emission terms can interfere or enhance significantly, and the heavy-quark contribution cannot be neglected in radiative transitions. These results provide useful theoretical guidance for future searches for spin-$3/2$ doubly heavy baryons through radiative decay modes at LHCb, Belle II, and other experimental facilities.

authors.name: Hui-Min Yang, Hua-Xing Chen, Xuan Luo

papers.title: Short Gravitational-Wave Transients as Probes of Cosmic Domain Walls
papers.summary: GW190521 and GW231123 have been reported as short-duration gravitational-wave transients consistent with very massive binary black hole (BBH) coalescences whose inferred parameters, i.e., exceptionally high total masses and spin magnitudes, challenge standard isolated binary stellar evolution. We test a topological dark matter (TDM) interpretation invoking cosmic domain walls by fitting a physically motivated domain wall template to the LIGO Hanford and Livingston strain data. The BBH hypothesis is individually favored, with $\log_{10}\mathcal{B}_{\rm BBH/TDM}=12.2$ and $11.3$ for GW231123 and GW190521, respectively. However, these values are lower than those typically recovered from matched maximum a posteriori BBH waveforms injected into nearby noise segments. We further perform, for the first time, a joint fit in which domain wall signals from a single underlying scalar field are constrained simultaneously by both events. Although not favored over BBH signals, we find the two events are consistent with a common scalar field, with shared TDM parameters agreeing across independent noise realizations and sky locations. We further find that injected TDM transients are systematically recovered under the BBH hypothesis with large spin parameters, revealing a morphological degeneracy that could mask genuine domain wall signals. This analysis demonstrates that multi-event parameter consistency tests provide a new discriminant for domain wall dark matter searches in upcoming observing runs.

authors.name: Tore Boybeyi, Doga Veske, David Maibach

papers.title: Fermi-eROSITA cross-correlations suggest annihilation lines of $\sim70$ GeV WIMPs
papers.summary: The deep potential wells of galaxy clusters provide some of the strongest constraints on the velocity-dependent ($p$-wave) annihilation of weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) dark matter. Cross-correlating high-latitude Fermi-LAT 16.3-year data with the western Galactic hemisphere eROSITA map facilitates high-sensitivity tests. A blind composite matched-filter scan of the cross-correlated spectrum for the $\chi\chi\to\gamma\gamma$, $\gamma Z$, and $\gamma h$ annihilation-line triad of a single WIMP $\chi$ finds $m_\chi c^2\simeq71.9$ and $67.5$ GeV (observer-frame) triads, each with a local $Z$-score $\sim3$ and a (henceforth global) $1.7$-$2.1\sigma$ (trial-corrected), insensitive to details of detrending, sky masks, and filters. The leading nonad (equidistant three triads) corresponds to $66.4$ and $71.9$ GeV cross-annihilating WIMPs ($2.5\sigma$). The leading $\sim72$ GeV triad coincides with the mass implied by interpreting the reported $\sim43.2$ GeV $\gamma$-ray line in three nearby clusters as its $\gamma Z$ channel. At this externally fixed mass, the triad reaches $3.0\sigma$ alone, and $5.1\sigma$ when combined with the reported line ($3.8\sigma$ under alternative assumptions; similar values for the nonad). This triad, absent from the ambient (X-ray-uncorrelated) spectrum, presents in different Galactic sectors, strengthens under cosmological (positive) but not negative redshift broadening $\Delta z$, and peaks at $\Delta z\simeq 0.05$, consistent with galaxy clusters; its two non-$43$ GeV channels reach $2.4\sigma$ by themselves. Measured (not loss-corrected) intrinsic cross sections are a few $10^{-19}$ cm$^3$ s$^{-1}$ for WIMPs tracing the X-ray gas.

authors.name: Uri Keshet

papers.title: First Lattice Calculation of Structure-Dependent Radiative Corrections to Lepton-Flavor-Universality Ratios in Leptonic Decays
papers.summary: The ratio of electronic to muonic leptonic decay widths, $R_{e/\mu}$, for the light mesons $\pi$ and $K$, provides a clean test of lepton flavor universality (LFU) and a sensitive probe of physics beyond the Standard Model. Its Standard-Model prediction is exceptionally precise, with the leading uncertainty associated with the structure-dependent (SD) radiative correction of $O(0.1\%)$. As experiments such as PIONEER and NA62 aim for unprecedented precision, this SD correction has become an essential ingredient in precision experiment--theory comparisons. We present the first lattice QCD$+$QED calculation of this SD correction at the physical pion mass and in the continuum limit. We employ the infinite-volume reconstruction (IVR) method with Coulomb-gauge photons, significantly reducing both statistical errors and finite-volume effects. We obtain the Standard-Model predictions, $R_{e/\mu}=1.23516(10)\times10^{-4}$ for $\pi$ and $R_{e/\mu}=2.47661(31)\times10^{-5}$ for $K$. Our results reduce the hadronic uncertainty in $R_{e/\mu}$, provide the most precise Standard-Model predictions to date, and establish first-principles benchmarks for future high-precision tests of LFU.

authors.name: Peter Boyle, Norman H. Christ, Xu Feng, Taku Izubuchi, Luchang Jin, Christopher T. Sachrajda, Xin-Yu Tuo

papers.title: Quark-mass dependence of two-nucleon scattering
papers.summary: Understanding how the properties of the visible Universe depend on the parameters of the Standard Model of particle physics requires \emph{ab initio} theoretical computations. To that end, we investigate the quark-mass dependence of low-energy nucleon-nucleon scattering in the deuteron and dineutron channels. We perform lattice-QCD calculations at pion masses $M_\pi\approx 200$ and $280$ MeV and compare their results to phenomenology at the physical point and to a previous calculation at $M_\pi\approx 710$ MeV. Scattering amplitudes, phase shifts, and threshold parameters are determined from finite-volume spectra using quantization conditions that explicitly incorporate long-distance effects from one-pion exchange. We analyze the pion-mass dependence of scattering lengths and effective ranges using chiral effective field theory with Weinberg and Kaplan-Savage-Wise power countings. From this, we estimate the pion-mass derivatives of the inverse scattering lengths and binding momentum, at the physical point. Both power countings indicate that the deuteron unbinds near $M_\pi\approx 220$ MeV.

papers.title: Sensitivity of the SHiP experiment at CERN to sterile-neutrino-induced oscillations
papers.summary:
The SHiP experiment, approved for the high-intensity beam-dump facility in the ECN3 hall at the CERN SPS in the North Area, will record neutrino interactions both in its scattering and neutrino detector (SND) and, about \SI{70}{m} further downstream, in its calorimeter system. We show that the baseline SHiP detector configuration therefore forms a two-baseline experiment for oscillations induced by a sterile neutrino. From a 	extsc{Geant4} simulation of 	extsc{Genie}-generated interactions we derive the energy response of both stations to $
ue$ and $
umu$ charged-current (CC) interactions and the separation of $
ue$~CC events from the neutral-current $\pizero$ background, and fold them into a near/far disappearance analysis with a $20\%$ flux-shape uncertainty and a $1\%$ far/near normalisation uncertainty. For $6	imes10^{20}$ protons on target, the projected $95\%$~CL median sensitivities are $\Umufour\simeq\UmuLimit$ at $\mfour\simeq\UmuLimitMass$~eV and $\Uefour\simeq\UeLimit$ at $\mfour\simeq\UeLimitMass$~eV. In the muon channel this lies below existing $
umu$-disappearance limits for $\DnineLow\lesssim\mfour\lesssim\DnineHigh$~eV.

papers.title: Quantum-correlation of neutral charmed mesons at BESIII
papers.summary: Quantum-correlated $D\bar D$ pairs give direct access to the strong-phase differences between $D^0$ and $\bar D^0$ decays, which are essential inputs to the CKM angle $\gamma$ and charm mixing. The BESIII experiment has accumulated the largest data sample at the $\psi(3770)$ resonance, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $20.3\,\text{fb}^{-1}$. The neutral $D\bar D$ pairs produced at $\psi(3770)$ are in a $C$-odd state. We report new and improved measurements of the strong-phase differences in $D\rightarrow K_{S,L}\pi^+\pi^-$, $D\rightarrow K^+K^-\pi^+\pi^-$, $D\rightarrow K^-\pi^+\pi^+\pi^-$ and $D\rightarrow K^-\pi^+\pi^0$ decays, alongside a measurement of the $CP$-even fraction in $D\rightarrow K^+K^-\pi^+\pi^-$. Furthermore, we present a novel method that studies the $D\bar D$ quantum correlations using data collected at centre-of-mass energies from $4.13$ to $4.23\,$GeV, where the $D\bar D$ pairs are produced in $C$-even or $C$-odd states, according to the number of accompanying photons. This gives the first observation of $C$-even $D\bar D$ pairs and a new measurement of the strong-phase difference in $D\rightarrow K^-\pi^+$ decays.

authors.name: Shenghui Zeng (on behalf of the BESIII collaboration)

papers.title: High-Statistics Study of Antiproton Annihilation at Rest on Argon in a LArTPC
papers.summary: This paper reports a high-statistics study of antiproton--argon ($\bar{p}\text{--}\text{Ar}$) annihilation at rest in the J-PARC T98 experiment using a single-phase Liquid Argon Time Projection Chamber (LArTPC). A dataset comprising over $10^{5}$ annihilation events was acquired together with comprehensive calibration data. In parallel, a dedicated Geant4-based simulation framework was developed to model the secondary beam transport and detector response. Together, these experimental and computational resources provide a foundation for benchmarking hadronic interaction models and for future LArTPC-based antimatter searches, such as GRAMS. As an initial application of this framework, we compare the measured annihilation topologies, localized energy profiles, and spatial cluster multiplicities with predictions from three hadronic interaction generators: Fritiof, INCL++, and GiBUU. While all models reproduce the overall features of the total energy deposition, GiBUU provides the most consistent empirical description of localized energy deposition near the annihilation vertex and spatial cluster multiplicities at larger radii, reflecting the key roles of secondary nucleon knockout and in-medium pion absorption. These results provide a high-statistics experimental benchmark for modeling low-energy antiproton interactions in liquid argon.

papers.title: First observation of the decay $D_{s1}(2460)^{+} \to D_{s}^{*+}\gamma$ and measurement of the branching-fraction ratio $\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+} \to D_{s}^{*+} \gamma]/\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+} \to D_{s}^{+} \gamma]$
papers.summary: We report the first observation of the radiative decay $D_{s1}(2460)^{+} \to D_{s}^{*+} \gamma$ with a significance greater than 10 standard deviations. The signal is found in $e^{+}e^{-} \to c\bar{c}$ production using data samples with integrated luminosities of 980 and 572~$\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ collected by the Belle and Belle~II detectors operating at the KEKB and SuperKEKB asymmetric-energy $e^{+}e^{-}$ colliders, respectively. The branching-fraction ratio $\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+} \to D_{s}^{*+} \gamma]/\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+} \to D_{s}^{+} \gamma]$ is measured to be $0.74 \pm 0.05 ({\rm stat.}) \pm 0.06 ({\rm syst.)}$. This result helps discriminate between different theoretical models regarding the internal structure of the charm-strange meson $D_{s1}(2460)^{+}$.

papers.title: Hunting dark matter: the present and future of direct particle detection
papers.summary: The nature of dark matter remains one of the major open questions in particle physics and cosmology. Direct detection experiments aim to identify dark matter particles through their interactions with ordinary matter, but despite substantial improvements in experimental sensitivity, no conclusive detection has been achieved. In this review, we provide a comprehensive overview of the present status and future prospects of direct particle detection, focusing on searches for dark matter particles from the Galactic halo. We introduce the theoretical framework for interpreting experimental results, including nuclear and electron scattering, collective excitations, particle absorption, and time- and direction-dependent signatures. We review the detection technologies employed in these searches, highlighting their operating principles, advantages, and limitations, as well as the calibration techniques and background mitigation strategies required to achieve high sensitivity. Particular emphasis is placed on experimental results reported since 2020, covering nuclear and electron recoil searches, annual modulation measurements, and directional detection. We also discuss experiments under construction and proposed future detectors, ranging from large-scale noble-liquid experiments to low-threshold technologies targeting sub-GeV dark matter. Finally, we examine the challenges that will shape the next generation of experiments, including the need for increasingly low energy thresholds, improved background understanding and discrimination, and the growing importance of neutrino-induced backgrounds. The diversity and complementarity of detector technologies will remain essential for exploring the dark matter parameter space and establishing the nature of any potential signal.
