None of our targets show detectable rotational broadening or chromospheric activity. Conclusions. The Li-rich stars analysed here are unevolved, ruling out in-situ Li production. Planet engulfment is very unlikely in GCs, and we detect no present-day rotation or activity. By exclusion, the most plausible remaining scenarios involve different types of interaction with a companion, including dynamical interactions, mass transfer, and mergers. Currently, we have not detected a companion.

authors.name: F. Lucertini, E. Pancino, L. Monaco, L. Sbordone, I. Baeza, D. A. Alvarez Garay, S. Villanova, A. Mucciarelli, N. Sanna

papers.title: Gravitational Waves from Population III Black Hole Mergers in Primordial Gas Disks: Constraining Astrophysical Scenarios with the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna and the Einstein Telescope
papers.summary: The first generation of metal-free Population III (Pop~III) stars provides a possible formation channel for the black hole (BH) seeds in the early Universe. Their remnants may grow through gas accretion and mergers, producing gravitational wave (GW) signals detectable by future observatories. We develop a semi-analytical model of fragmentation in a primordial self-gravitating gas disk within minihaloes at $z > 15$, motivated by high-resolution cosmological simulations. The resulting Pop~III stars form around a central primary, some leaving massive BH remnants that migrate towards the central BH through dynamical friction from gas and dark matter, while the central BH grows through accretion and mergers. For a $10^6~{\rm M_\odot}$ halo at $z=20$, we explore how the initial mass function (IMF) and BH accretion efficiency affect detectability with the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) and the Einstein Telescope (ET). We find that both detectors can potentially reveal mergers of Pop III remnant BHs, but favor different astrophysical conditions. LISA pinpoints more massive central BHs ($\sim10^3$-$10^4 {\rm M_\odot}$), grown rapidly through mutual mergers alongside efficient gas accretion ($f_{\rm Edd}=1$), and a relatively top-heavy IMF ($\alpha=0.8$). In contrast, detectability with ET favors lower-mass BHs, with less efficient accretion ($f_{\rm Edd}=0.01$) and a steeper IMF ($\alpha=1.5$). These results highlight the potential of LISA and ET to probe Pop~III BH formation, growth, and mergers across different regions of parameter spaces, jointly constraining Pop~III star formation and early BH seed evolution.

authors.name: Maulik Bhatt, Lucio Mayer, Pedro R. Capelo, Simona Gallerani, Andrea Pallottini

papers.title: Compositions of Exoplanetary Debris Shaped by Milky Way Stellar Abundance Patterns
papers.summary: Galactic chemical evolution (GCE) predicts large-scale variations in exoplanet compositions with host star elemental abundances, reflecting the Milky Way's history of star formation and elemental enrichment from stellar feedback. We investigate the impact of GCE on the compositions of exoplanetary bodies using polluted white dwarfs (WDs), which probe the bulk elemental abundances of planetary debris. Using a literature sample of 70 polluted WDs, we calculate iron mass fractions for the accreted bodies and compare these to tracers of the WD progenitor's initial abundances, including age and kinematics. We demonstrate predicted trends using a sample of main sequence stars, and we show that these are generally reflected in the polluted WD sample. In particular, H-dominated WDs show preferentially larger iron mass fractions amongst younger and less dynamically excited systems. This trend is weaker amongst He-dominated WDs, and we show that this may be attributed to uncertainties in their observed phases of accretion. Continuing to combine WD pollution compositions with stellar parameters and kinematics could be a valuable way to constrain large-scale versus local drivers of planetary compositions.

authors.name: Isabella L. Trierweiler, Kendra Nguyen, Lou Baya Ould Rouis, Pratik Gandhi, Laura K. Rogers, Carey M. Lisse, Malena Rice, Damanveer S. Grewal, Edward Young

papers.title: Rest-frame annihilation lines of $\sim70$ GeV WIMPs in 23,000 stacked galaxy clusters
papers.summary: Weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) annihilation features were reported as a 43 GeV line in three Fermi-LAT galaxy clusters ($\mathtt{S}_3$), as triad $\{\gamma\gamma, \gamma Z,\gamma h\}$ lines from $\sim70$ GeV WIMPs in LAT data cross-correlated ($\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$) with western eROSITA X-rays, and as a nonad (combining three triads) of two cross-annihilating WIMPs in $\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$. A blind scan of LAT 16.3-year data around 23,343 high-latitude clusters in their rest frames finds three triads, at 70 GeV ($2.8\sigma$ trial-corrected, henceforth), $72$ GeV ($1.3\sigma$; strengthening to $2.7\sigma$ if mass-fixed by $\mathtt{S}_3$, $4.0\sigma$ combined with $\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$ masked around the clusters, $5.7\sigma$ if also combined with $\mathtt{S}_3$), and 74-75 GeV: a triplet not only rare ($3.5\sigma$) but also forming a $\{70,74\}$ GeV nonad ($3.4\sigma$; strengthening to $4.0\sigma$, $4.6\sigma$, and $6.1\sigma$, respectively). The spectral features, robust in and out of the $\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$ region and $\mathtt{S}_3$ clusters, appear in all Galactic quadrants and only in the cluster rest frame (vanishing upon redshift rescaling or permutation), fade away from cluster centers, are absent from their surrounding stacked fields, and like $\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$ indicate intrinsic few $10^{-19}$ cm$^3$ s$^{-1}$ cross sections (uncorrected) across samples. All features are largely explained by cross-annihilating $69.7^{+0.4}_{-1.0}$ and $74.5^{+1.1}_{-0.6}$ GeV WIMPs.

authors.name: Uri Keshet

papers.title: Global Fit Inference for LISA with samsara++
papers.summary: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will observe a superposition of gravitational-wave signals, requiring joint inference of an unknown number of sources, parameters, and instrumental noise. To disentangle these contributions, that overlap in both time and frequency, a Global Fit (GF) analysis is needed. We present samsara++, a C++/CUDA sampler designed to address this trans-dimensional GF problem. Building on the continuous-time MCMC framework of samsara, the algorithm combines birth-death processes for adding and removing sources, with mutation moves for parameter estimation. Birth and death are selected through posterior-dependent rates. Shared-memory parallelism, incremental likelihood updates, and indexed storage reduce the computational and memory costs, while parallel tempering improves the exploration of multimodal posteriors. We assess the performance using simulated one-year LISA datasets containing Galactic double white dwarf binaries and stationary Gaussian instrumental noise. Analyses of populations containing 143 and 866 binaries start from empty source models, without preliminary searches or proposals tailored to the injected population. These tests demonstrate source reconstruction and catalog generation, highlighting, at the same time, the importance of source-count, overlapping signals, and incomplete mixing on joint source and noise inference. Then we perform a separate stress test, initialized at the injected parameters, exploring a population of 16,435 binaries, corresponding to 131,480 source parameters. This run completes 15 million iterations in approximately 16 hours using about 3 GB of RAM. All together, these benchmarks show the computational feasibility of birth-death sampling for large Galactic-binary populations, and provide a foundation for extending samsara++ toward a comprehensive LISA global fit.

authors.name: Lorenzo Valbusa Dall'Armi, Gabriele Astorino, Riccardo Buscicchio, Angelo Ricciardone, Walter Del Pozzo

papers.title: Microcausality Bounds on Dispersion Laws
papers.summary: Microcausality holds in any state, including those that spontaneously break Lorentz invariance, and requires the poles (and other singularities) of the retarded Green's function to satisfy $\mathrm{Im}\,\omega \le |\mathrm{Im}\,k|$ throughout the complex plane. Building on the work of Heller, Serantes, Spali\'nski and Withers, we study its consequences for dispersion relations that are linear at small $k$, like Goldstone bosons, assuming tree-level, non-dissipative dynamics. We show that microcausality is equivalent to requiring that $k \pm \omega(k)$ be typically real functions. This yields two-sided bounds on all higher-order coefficients of $\omega(k)$ in units of its radius of convergence $R$, the scale at which the linear Goldstone description breaks down. The optimal constraints are characterised by an infinite hierarchy of Toeplitz determinants. We derive analogous bounds on $\omega^2(k)$, whose radius of convergence $\tilde R$ marks the scale at which new states must appear. The bounds shrink to zero as the sound speed $c_s$ approaches 1: for a fixed higher-derivative correction, both $R$ and $\tilde R$ become parametrically smaller than naive dimensional analysis suggests. In particular, in the EFT of Inflation all higher-derivative quadratic operators must vanish as $c_s \to 1$. We test the bounds in several models: a $U(1)$ superfluid, light in a dielectric medium, photon propagation in a strong magnetic field, colour-flavour-locked quark matter, and a homogeneous solid. Finally, we extend the bounds to gapped modes.

authors.name: Paolo Creminelli, Michael Mancini, Warin Patrick McBlain

papers.title: Bayesian Time-Varying Spectral Estimation for LISA with P-Splines
papers.summary: We model the evolutionary spectrum of a slowly time-varying process by a linear combination of products of time- and frequency-dependent B-splines, placing a Gaussian tensor-product penalty prior on the coefficients. The posterior distribution is obtained by updating the prior using a Whittle-type likelihood approximation of the Wilson-Daubechies-Meyer time-frequency coefficients. Separate regularisation in time and frequency allows non-stationary spectral structure to be inferred. An adaptive coarse-grained likelihood reduces the computational cost while preserving fine resolution around sharp spectral features. We first validate the method using repeated simulations of a locally stationary process with known spectrum, showing lower reconstruction errors and narrower posterior intervals as the sample size increases. We then apply it to a year-long simulated LISA data set with stationary instrumental single link spectra, an evolving time-delay interferometry (TDI) response, and a modulated Galactic foreground. We compare a flexible total power spectral density (PSD) model with models incorporating progressively stronger physical information and examine both continuous and gapped observations. Allowing time variation substantially improves reconstruction relative to a stationary model, while incorporating physical information about the TDI response further improves recovery, particularly near its moving spectral features. The results illustrate the trade-off between spectral flexibility, physical assumptions, and posterior uncertainty in non-stationary LISA noise estimation.

authors.name: Avi Vajpeyi, Giorgio Mentasti, Ollie Burke, Renate Meyer, Patricio Maturana-Russel, Quentin Baghi

papers.title: Relativistic precession around rotating neutron stars. I. Slow rotation: Hartle--Thorne spacetimes, particle orbits and the QPOs of atoll and Z sources
papers.summary: We study the relativistic precession model (RPM) of quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in the spacetimes of slowly rotating neutron stars computed from the equation of state (EOS). For four EOSs (WFF1, G3, FSUGarnet and IOPB-I) we solve the Hartle--Thorne equations to second order in the angular velocity and compute the orbital and epicyclic frequencies of the exterior metric without expanding in the spin or the quadrupole. At $1.9\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ the spin-induced quadrupole is 2--4 times that of a black hole with the same spin; it lowers the nodal precession frequency by up to 25 per cent near the innermost stable circular orbit and limits the nodal frequency that any spin can produce. An eccentric, tilted geodesic around a $1.92\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ star spinning at 363~Hz precesses at the epicyclic rates, and the power spectrum of a hot spot on it peaks at the orbital, periastron and nodal precession frequencies. Applied to the atoll sources 4U 1636$-$53 and 4U 1728$-$34, the RPM gives masses of 2.02--$2.15\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ and 1.88--$1.92\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$. For 4U 1728$-$34 the low-frequency QPO favours stars with large moments of inertia, $I\simeq2.5\times10^{45}$~g\,cm$^{2}$. Without an EOS the QPOs give $M=1.920^{+0.014}_{-0.012}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$, $j=0.162^{+0.023}_{-0.011}$ and $\bar Q=2.2^{+1.1}_{-0.8}$; a Kerr spacetime with the same nodal frequency would underestimate the moment of inertia by 22 per cent. For the Z sources GX 5$-$1 and GX 340+0 the horizontal-branch oscillations cannot be twice the nodal precession frequency for any of the four EOSs: the fits are driven to spins of 730--745~Hz and to the maximum mass.

authors.name: A. C. Khunt

papers.title: Scalar charge of neutron stars and accreting black holes in Starobinsky gravity: quasi-universal relations, the trace anomaly and gravitational-wave sensitivity
papers.summary: The Starobinsky scalaron is sourced by the trace of the stress--energy, so its exterior charge is set by the matter around an object and not by the object's vacuum geometry. We derive a master formula for that charge for any static, spherically symmetric source, evaluate it first for neutron stars, where the interior is known, and then for accreting black holes, where it is not. For a star the pressure subtracts: on the interior metric with the Eardley sensitivity, and the charge is a quasi-universal function of the compactness. Six realistic equations of state confirm the relation but lie above the coefficient calibrated on polytropes; the refit reproduces their mean to 0.007. The trace $\rho-3p$ changes sign in the cores of massive stars, and the charge also tracks the tidal deformability and the moment of inertia to a few parts in 1000 and 100. Solving the Einstein-frame structure equations self-consistently moves a star along this relation and leaves its charge at fixed compactness within 4 per cent of the test-field value. We compare the charge with NICER radii and the GW170817 tidal deformability, and use the published massless dipole constraint from GW230529 to calibrate a Fisher estimate of the sensitivity of a similar binary to a finite scalaron range, projected to the Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer; the range is a free parameter, and the laboratory bound on pure $R+\alpha R^2$ is confronted explicitly. A vacuum black hole has q=0; a hole with a disc has $q=\sinh(m_\phi r_d)/(m_\phi r_d)$, controlled by the disc's outer edge, which makes it the counterpart in which the same integral is dominated by matter far from the centre; light is blind to the charge at leading order, and the correction beyond it is negligible for any self-consistent disc.

authors.name: Yashmitha Kumaran, Il\'idio Lopes

papers.title: A hybrid log-likelihood-ratio statistic for single-detector SPIIR gravitational-wave searches
papers.summary: Periods with only one detector operating accounted for 13.3 percent of the third LIGO-Virgo observing run (O3) and 29.7 percent of the first part of the fourth observing run (O4a). We present the first dedicated single-detector implementation of the Summed Parallel Infinite Impulse Response (SPIIR) pipeline for binary neutron star (BNS) and neutron star-black hole (NSBH) merger searches. Our hybrid log-likelihood ratio combines signal-consistency models for non-Gaussian glitches with a profile likelihood ratio for the signal-to-noise ratio under a Gaussian-noise model. We calibrate the glitch model by source category and trigger-rate class. We assign false alarm rates (FARs) using the measured background from the same detector and analysis chunk, extrapolating its high-ranking tail. We check the FAR assignments by comparing observed and expected cumulative background counts for BNS in O3a and NSBH in O3b at LIGO Hanford (H1) and LIGO Livingston (L1). Using O3 data and the GWTC-3 injection set, we find that, at a threshold of one false alarm per two months, the BNS sensitive distances are $136.5^{+2.9}_{-3.0}$ Mpc in L1 and $120.2^{+3.1}_{-3.3}$ Mpc in H1. These central estimates are approximately 24 and 38 percent higher, respectively, than the GWTC-3 GstLAL values of $110.5^{+3.2}_{-3.4}$ Mpc and $87.2^{+3.6}_{-3.9}$ Mpc over the same data and injection parameter ranges. GstLAL provides the only published single-detector results in GWTC-3. For NSBH, SPIIR reaches $164.1^{+6.7}_{-7.3}$ Mpc in L1 and $134.9^{+6.3}_{-7.0}$ Mpc in H1, compared with $165.1^{+6.7}_{-7.3}$ Mpc and $156.0^{+5.9}_{-6.4}$ Mpc for GWTC-3 GstLAL, respectively. Targeted searches recover triggers associated with GW190425, GW200105_162426, and GW230529_181500 with assigned FARs below the same threshold.

authors.name: SPIIR Collaboration, Weichangfeng Guo, Sunil Choudhary, Victor Oloworaran, Linqing Wen, Jayden Doan, Qingyuan Liang, Tim Davies, Luke Davis, Irina Dvorkin, Apratim Ganguly, Shang-Jie Jin, JeongCho Kim, Yu-Chiung Lin, Ngai-Chun Lung, Alistair McLeod, Khun Sang Phukon, Andreas Wicenec

papers.title: Probing superradiant cloud level transitions in stellar-mass black hole binaries with milli-Hertz and multiband gravitational wave observations
papers.summary: We investigate superradiant cloud level transitions in stellar-mass black hole binaries with milli-Hertz and multiband gravitational-wave observations. Under the adopted cloud formation and survival conditions, the $\lvert322\rangle\rightarrow\lvert31-1\rangle$ fine transition can imprint phase corrections in the LISA band, while Bohr transitions occurring after the milli-Hertz band observation can be probed through shifts in the merger time. Modeling the coupled cloud-orbit evolution, we find that cloud depletion can begin before resonance and that ionization can advance rather than delay coalescence. For a representative nearby binary, a vacuum injection-recovery analysis yields a cloud-mass-fraction posterior concentrated at $M_c^i/M\lesssim10^{-6}$. Comparing the LISA-predicted coalescence time with a subsequent ground-based measurement provides a complementary test of later cloud evolution. These results motivate complementary searches for ultralight bosons with milli-Hertz and multiband gravitational-wave observations.

authors.name: Si-Tong Peng, Anson Chen, Si-Yang Pu, Jun Zhang

papers.title: Repeated Gravitational-Wave Lensing from Binary Black Holes on Eccentric and Precessing Orbits around Spinning Supermassive Black Holes
papers.summary: Gravitational waves (GWs) from a stellar-mass binary black hole (BBH) orbiting a supermassive black hole (SMBH) can experience repeated gravitational lensing as the BBH passes behind the SMBH. Our previous studies of orbit-induced GW modulation motivate this investigation of repeated lensing in evolving hierarchical triple systems. We investigate how eccentricity, inclination, and relativistic precession of the outer orbit affect successive lensing events and parameter inference. The outer orbit follows post-Newtonian dynamics, and the inspiral waveform includes moving-source effects and de Sitter precession. An event-local point-mass lensing model tracks the changing source--lens alignment and GW frequency. For a one-year LISA observation, we examine lensing-event identification, Fisher-matrix estimates of parameter uncertainties, and waveform residuals when lensing is omitted. Our results show that outer-orbit evolution changes the timing and amplification of successive lensing events and can bring initially unfavorable configurations into the lensing region. A fixed circular, nonprecessing approximation misses all lensing events for a substantial fraction of the selected lensed systems. The median fractional reductions in uncertainty are largest for the outer-orbit inclination and SMBH spin. For some systems above the adopted detection threshold, lensing-induced waveform differences persist after local adjustments to the parameters of the unlensed model. Repeated lensing can thus provide complementary constraints on SMBH properties and outer-orbit geometry in LISA observations of hierarchical BBHs.

authors.name: Jie Wu, Mengfei Sun, Jin Li, Zhoujian Cao

papers.title: Simultaneous tests of post-Newtonian inspiral using GW250114 and GW250207
papers.summary: We perform the one of the most general tests of post-Newtonian (PN) inspiral in binary black holes to date by allowing all eight phase coefficients up to 3.5PN order to vary simultaneously from their general-relativistic values. Using two of the loudest binary black hole events observed to date, GW250114 and GW250207, we carry out Bayesian inference with the IMRPhenomXPHM_SpinTaylor waveform model augmented by parametrized deviations in the post-Newtonian phasing. We then identify the combinations of phase coefficients most strongly constrained by the data through a principal component analysis of the eight-dimensional deformation space. We find that the data constrain the three leading principal components beyond their priors, and that all three are consistent with the predictions of general relativity. These results demonstrate that exceptionally loud gravitational-wave events enable robust, high-dimensional tests of inspiral dynamics and provide direct access to the measurable subspace of post-Newtonian deformations.

authors.name: Saurabh Kumar, Parthapratim Mahapatra, Ish Mohan Gupta, M. Saleem, B. S. Sathyaprakash, K. G. Arun

papers.title: An Empirical Calibration of the Tip of the Red Giant Branch Distance Method in the Near Infrared. II. JWST NIRCam Wide Filters
papers.summary: The tip of the red giant (TRGB) is a standardizable candle and is identifiable as the discontinuity at the bright extreme of the red giant branch (RGB) stars in color-magnitude diagram (CMD) space. The TRGB-based distance method has been calibrated and used to measured distances to galaxies out to $D\leq20$ Mpc with the $I$-band equivalent Hubble Space Telescope ($HST$) $F814W$ filter, and as an important rung in the distance ladder to measure the Hubble constant, $H_0$. In the infrared (IR), the TRGB apparent magnitude ranges from $1-2$ magnitudes brighter than in the optical, and now with the IR James Webb Space Telescope ($JWST$) observatory the feasible distance range of the TRGB method can be extended to $\sim50$ Mpc. However, in the IR the TRGB luminosity depends to varying degrees on stellar metallicity and age. In this study we standardize the TRGB luminosity using stellar colors as a proxy for metallicity/age to derive color-based corrections for the $JWST$ Near-Infrared Camera (NIRCam) short wavelength (SW) filters $F090W$, $F115W$, $F150W$ and the long wavelength (LW) filters $F277W$, $F356W,$ and $F444W$. We provide recommended filter combinations for distance measurements depending on the requisite precision. For science requiring high precision ($\leq1\%$ in distance) and robustness we recommend measuring the TRGB in $F090W$ vs $F090W-F150W$ or $F115W$ vs. $F115W-F277W$ with the caveat that even with $JWST$ long integration times will be necessary at further distances. If lower precision ($>1.5\%$ in distance) can be tolerated, or if shorter integration times are desirable, we recommend measuring the TRGB in either $F115W$ or $F150W$ paired with $F356W$. We do not recommend $F444W$ for precision TRGB measurements due to its lower angular resolution.

authors.name: Max J. B. Newman, Kristen B. W. McQuinn, Evan D. Skillman, Martha L. Boyer, Roger E. Cohen, Andrew E. Dolphin, O. Grace Telford

papers.title: The Palomar 5 Stellar Stream in DESI Legacy Surveys DR10: Wide-field Morphology and Constraints on the Inner Halo Potential Shape
papers.summary: The Palomar 5 stellar stream probes the gravitational potential of the inner Milky Way, where the disk, dark halo, and time-dependent perturbations all contribute substantially to the force field. Using the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys Data Release 10 (DR10), we map the wide-field morphology of the stream over $-25^\circ<\phione<20^\circ$ and $-5^\circ<\phitwo<10^\circ$. Our analysis combines a cluster-calibrated PARSEC color--magnitude diagram filter, a continuous main-sequence turnoff plus RR Lyrae distance relation, and a field star response tied to local imaging depth. After applying the response correction, we recover the stream clearly over $-15.5^\circ\le\phione\le7.0^\circ$ and reveal no coherent low-surface-brightness extension beyond this range within our DR10 search footprint. Mock stream fits to the measured centroid and width yield an NFW potential flattening parameter $\qphiz=0.82^{+0.13}_{-0.11}$, assuming a static Hernquist bulge, a Miyamoto--Nagai disk, and a potential-flattened NFW halo with fixed $r_s=20\,{\rm kpc}$ and fixed $V_c(R_0)=232\,\kms$ at the Solar radius. The posterior favors an oblate effective inner halo potential, with a minor dependence on the assumed progenitor mass. The DR10 stream morphology therefore provides a homogeneous observational reference well suited for future joint analyses that incorporate density information, proper motions, line-of-sight velocities, and time-dependent perturbations.

authors.name: Yun-Ao Xiao, Hu Zou, Lu Feng, Jinfu Gou, Wei-Jian Guo, Niu Li, Wen-Xiong Li, Shu-Fei Liu, Haoming Song, Ji-Peng Sui, Xi Tan, Jingyi Zhang

papers.title: Baryonification II: Constraining feedback with X-ray and kinematic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich observations
papers.summary: Baryonic feedback alters the matter distribution on small and intermediate scales, posing a challenge for precision cosmology. The new, component-wise baryonification (BFC) approach provides a self-consistent framework to model feedback effects for different observables. In this paper we use this framework to fit kinematic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (kSZ) observations from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) alongside halo X-ray gas fractions from eROSITA, investigating baryonic feedback in a cosmological context. We first show that the kSZ data from ACT is consistent with the gas fractions from eROSITA, both suggesting a feedback model that is stronger than what is assumed in most hydrodynamical simulations. This finding is in contrast to older, pre-eROSITA gas fraction measurements that point towards weaker feedback in tension with the kSZ results. We suspect these discrepancies to be due to selection bias in the pre-eROSITA sample, or differences in halo mass estimation between the two data sets. In a further step, we use the BFC model to predict the baryonic suppression of the matter power spectrum. Based on our combined fit to data from ACT and eROSITA, we find a power spectrum suppression that exceeds the percent-level at modes above $k=0.3-0.6 \,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$, growing to 2-8 percent at $k=1\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$, and to 20-25 percent at $k=5\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$, consistent with strong-feedback hydrodynamical simulations. Finally, we compare our best-fitting model to the observed gas density and pressure profiles of massive galaxy clusters from the X-COP sample, finding excellent agreement. These results show that BFC provides a self-consistent picture of feedback across mass- and length scales as well as different cosmological observables, thus making it promising for applications to multiwavelength studies to jointly constrain cosmology and baryonic effects.

authors.name: Michael Kova\v{c}, Andrina Nicola, Jozef Bucko, Aurel Schneider, Robert Reischke, Sambit K. Giri, Romain Teyssier, Matthieu Schaller, Joop Schaye

papers.title: When the Shadow Meets Its Measure: Assessing the Feasibility of Submillimeter Black Hole Shadow Imaging in Megamaser-disk Active Galactic Nuclei
papers.summary: Well-modeled water megamaser disks offer a path to black hole shadow (BHS) tests of strong-field gravity beyond Sgr A* and M87*: their very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) angular dynamics precisely constrains $M_\bullet/D$, the maser-disk orientation, and the dynamical center within the maser reference frame, thereby predicting the fiducial Schwarzschild BHS angular size without an externally adopted distance. We assess 21 megamaser galaxies as BHS targets using published maser measurements to calculate BHS angular sizes and baseline requirements. We combine new Submillimeter Array (SMA) continuum observations with archival Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) and Very Large Array (VLA) measurements to estimate arcsecond-scale 230 GHz flux densities and identify the strongest nuclear-region sources for higher-resolution follow-up. We also estimate the maximum dust and extended-jet contributions, examine limited variability measurements, and, for the leading candidate NGC 4258, evaluate the astrometry required to detect a spin-dependent offset between the BHS center and the maser dynamical center. Only NGC 4258 has an adopted BHS angular size resolvable with an Earth--L2 baseline; the other adopted sizes require longer baselines, while an Earth--L4/L5 separation would be sufficient for all. Five sources reach $S_{230}\gtrsim10$ mJy. However, whether the observed 230 GHz emission arises on BHS scales and is sufficiently optically thin to reveal a BHS remains unknown throughout the sample. NGC 4258's submillimeter excess is consistent with a thin disk transitioning to an advection-dominated flow; its spin-offset test remains infeasible with present maser astrometry.

authors.name: Roman N. Burridge, Geoffrey C. Bower

papers.title: Pulsar timing arrays: the emerging gravitational-wave landscape
papers.summary: Pulsar Timing Array (PTA) experiments have found evidence for a nanoHertz gravitational wave (GW) background (GWB). The challenge is now to turn evidence for a GWB into an understanding of the sources and physics that produce it. This review connects the physics of the Hellings--Downs correlation to the interpretation of the GWB spectrum and anisotropy, asking whether supermassive black hole binary populations consistent with electromagnetic observations can explain the signal. Searches for individual binaries take these questions further: multi-messenger observations and pulsar terms can reveal the evolution of these binary systems. Realizing this potential requires reliable noise models and candidate validation. We explain how pulsar noise, unresolved sources, and incomplete sky coverage limit these inferences. The same PTA observations also probe cosmic strings and ultralight dark matter, while fitted timing parameters extend GW searches to picohertz frequencies and enable measurements of Galactic acceleration. Rapid data combination and the larger, more precisely timed arrays expected from the Square Kilometre Array Observatory and Deep Synoptic Array will increase the sensitivity of these searches and measurements, sharpening our view of the emerging GW landscape.

authors.name: C. M. F. Mingarelli, J. A. Casey-Clyde, Y. T. Chang, E. Eisenberg, F. Hutchison, N. Khusid, B. Larsen, A. Moran, F. Semenzato, L. Willson, Q. Zheng

papers.title: Constraints on the Physical Association between ICECAT1 Neutrinos and Fast Radio Bursts Using the Second CHIME/FRB Catalogue
papers.summary: We present a search for neutrino counterparts to fast radio bursts (FRBs) using temporal and spatial cross-matching between the 1423 non-repeating FRBs of the Second CHIME/FRB catalogue and the 73 alerts of the IceCube high-energy alert-track catalogue ICECAT1 from 2018 July 25 to 2020 December 31. Because current FRB-neutrino models do not agree on the emission order, we adopt a two-sided temporal hypothesis and define the significance criterion from the expected number of chance coincidences before the search. We find no statistically significant association: no pair lies within the $3\sigma$ and $5\sigma$ coincidence windows of $3.50 \times 10^2$ s and $7.43 \times 10^{-2}$ s, and the pair closest in time, FRB20190630C-IC190629A, is consistent with a chance coincidence ($p = 0.254$, $0.66\sigma$). Using a population-level stacking analysis, we derive 90% upper limits on the neutrino-to-radio luminosity ratio of FRBs, $\xi \lesssim 1.4 \times 10^{11}$ for a neutrino spectral index $\gamma=1.0$ to $6.8 \times 10^{12}$ for $\gamma=3.0$, assuming neutrino emission within the burst duration. For a neutrino number spectrum $dN/d\epsilon \propto \epsilon^{-2}$, the corresponding limit on the neutrino fluence per burst is about a factor of 4 below those of previous stacking searches. For $\gamma=2$, the limits on the isotropic neutrino energy, $10^{49}$-$10^{52}$ erg, lie more than five orders of magnitude above the predictions of magnetar-driven shock models, so the present data do not constrain these models. Nevertheless, our blind significance criterion and population-stacking limits provide a baseline for future multi-messenger searches.

authors.name: Hiroto Masaoka, Tetsuya Hashimoto, Shotaro Yamasaki, Yuhei Iwata, Tomoki Wada, Tomotsugu Goto, Shintaro Yoshiura, Kazuaki Hashiyama, Mareki Honma, Takuya Akahori, Kohei Kurahara

papers.title: OJAL\'A: Optimizing J-PAS Astronomy for Large-scale Analysis. A transformer-based model for source classification and physical-parameter inference
papers.summary: The advent of large-scale surveys requires efficient machine learning techniques to exploit massive datasets. We present OJALA, a transformer-based autoregressive model that classifies astronomical objects and infers their physical parameters from 54-band J-PAS photometry combined with broad-band data from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys and WISE. The model is trained on approximately 20 million synthetic SEDs generated from DESI DR1 spectra and validated using a cross-matched sample of approximately 121,000 J-PAS and DESI objects. OJALA classifies stars, galaxies, and QSOs and estimates photometric redshifts for galaxies and QSOs. It recovers galaxy stellar masses and star formation rates, predicts optical emission-line equivalent widths and extinction-corrected H$\alpha$ luminosities, and reproduces the BPT and WHAN diagnostic diagrams. It also estimates stellar atmospheric parameters, including effective temperature and metallicity. Comparisons with dedicated multilayer perceptrons show that a single OJALA model generally matches or outperforms specialized predictors and remains robust under incomplete photometric coverage. We release the code, model weights, and a Value Added Catalog for the J-PAS Early Data Release.

authors.name: G. Mart\'inez-Solaeche, R. M. Gonz\'alez Delgado, R. Garc\'ia-Benito, A. Hern\'an-Caballero, I. P\'erez-R\`afols, L. A. D\'iaz-Garc\'ia, L. Raul Abramo, J. E. Rodr\'iguez-Mart\'in, A. M. Conrado, I. Breda, H. Dom\'inguez S\'anchez, I. M\'arquez, M. Pieri, D. L\'opez-Cano, V. M. Placco, L. Nakazono, A. del Pino, V. Marra, J. Alcaniz, N. Benitez, S. Bonoli, S. Carneiro, A. J. Cenarro, D. Crist\'obal-Hornillos, S. Daflon, R. A. Dupke, A. Ederoclite, C. Hern\'andez-Monteagudo, J. Liu, C. L\'opez-Sanjuan, A. Mar\'in-Franch, C. Mendes de Oliveira, M. Moles, F. Roig, L. Sodr\'e, K. Taylor, J. Varela, H. V\'azquez Rami\'o, J. M. V\'ilchez, J. Zaragoza-Cardiel

papers.title: Two-dimensional, time-dependent approximate NLTE unified model atmospheres with winds for hot, massive stars
papers.summary: Multi-dimensional unified model atmospheres with winds of massive stars have so far been studied under the assumption of equal flux, Planck, and energy weighted mean opacities, which effectively means these models have been in local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE). Although LTE may be a valid approximation in deeper atmospheric layers, it breaks down in the extended outflowing parts. As such, the opacities governing the heating and cooling of the gas are neither the same nor equal to flux-mean opacity in those regions. We present an approximate NLTE procedure that accounts for scattering in the computation of energy and Planck-mean opacity from a multitude of spectral lines in an accelerating medium. The formalism evaluates the opacities using Sobolev escape probabilities and effective thermalization parameters from a line database consisting of ~4 million spectral lines. RHD simulations are calculated as before with a hybrid opacity scheme combining Rosseland means with line opacities in an accelerating medium. Due to their high velocity dispersion, upon interaction, they produce localized shock fronts with the gas temperature exceeding the photon temperature. Due to improved treatment of heating and cooling in outflowing parts, the radiation and gas temperatures in the wind are no longer the same, as was the case in previous multi-dimensional simulations. Instead, gas gets heated at shock fronts, but due to strong radiative cooling remains localized. The net result is a multi-component wind structure not only in density and velocity, but also in temperature. This likely has important consequences for the formation and interpretation of observed O-type star wind spectra.

authors.name: Dwaipayan Debnath, Jon O. Sundqvist, Nicolas Moens, Luka G. Poniatowski, Cassandra Van der Sijpt, Andreas A. C. Sander

papers.title: The hydrodynamical response of cold circumgalactic clouds to quasar radiation
papers.summary: Recent simulations increasingly resolve the small-scale structure of the circumgalactic medium (CGM), but the dynamical impact of ionising radiation on its cold $10^4$ K component remains poorly understood. We investigate the evolution of cold gas structures exposed to quasars' EUV radiation. We develop an analytical framework to describe the evolution of such clouds, introducing a new threshold that defines when a cloud becomes radiation-shielded. The framework is validated using radiation-hydrodynamic simulations of single static clouds. It predicts three evolutionary paths: (i) an optically thin regime, in which radiation uniformly ionises the cloud; (ii) a radiation-shielded regime, where the cloud remains largely unaffected; and (iii) a rocket-effect regime, in which the propagation of the ionisation front ionises the illuminated side while compressing the opposite side, later accelerating the surviving cold clump. In the latter regime, the cloud's Ly$\alpha$ luminosity can be up to one order of magnitude higher than the optically thin case. Such luminosities are as high as $70\%$ of the values obtained from a fluorescent regime without considering hydrodynamical response. Unless the cloud is shielded, at least $\sim 50$-$60\,\%$ of Ly$\alpha$ emission arises from recombination. Applying this framework to both a ray crossing a population of clouds, and a ray propagating inside a cold stream, we find that the cold CGM around bright quasars ($L_{\mathrm{\nu,LL}} \sim 10^{31.6} \, \mathrm{erg\, s^{-1}\, Hz^{-1}}$) is likely fully ionised, whereas the one around faint quasars ($L_{\mathrm{\nu,LL}} \sim 10^{28.6} \, \mathrm{erg\, s^{-1}\, Hz^{-1}}$) predominantly experiences a rocket-effect regime. These results imply that the hydrodynamical response of cold CGM structures to quasar radiation must be considered when deriving their physical properties, particularly for faint quasars.

authors.name: Nicolas Ledos, Sebastiano Cantalupo, Titouan Lazeyras, Gabriele Pezzulli, Kentaro Nagamine, Shinsuke Takasao, Marta Galbiati, Andrea Travascio, Giada Quadri, Weichen Wang, Antonio Pensabene

papers.title: The Lumina Project: The Demographics of Active Galactic Nuclei from Quasars to Little Red Dots at $z\geq 3$
papers.summary: High-redshift active galactic nuclei (AGN) serve as powerful probes of early black-hole growth, galaxy formation, and the evolving intergalactic medium (IGM). In this work, we use Lumina, a cosmological radiation-hydrodynamic simulation spanning the epochs of hydrogen and helium reionization, which combines a large $(500\,{\rm cMpc})^3$ volume with $2\times 6000^3$ resolution elements, to explore high-redshift AGN. The simulation self-consistently follows hundreds of millions of galaxies and supermassive black holes (SMBHs), together with their impact on the ionization and thermal state of the IGM. We exploit this uniquely large dynamic range to predict multi-band AGN luminosity functions (LFs) at $z \geq 3$, from hard X-rays to the mid-infrared. These predictions encompass both moderately luminous quasars and the faint ``Little Red Dots'' (LRDs) uncovered by JWST. We develop an empirical model that maps simulated SMBHs onto observed AGN using bolometric and extinction/absorption corrections for canonical AGN and LRDs, and in which SMBHs with $M_{\rm BH}\leq 10\,M_{\rm seed} \sim 10^{7}\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$ stay in the LRD phase with a duty cycle of $30\%$. This simple framework reproduces the observed LFs and clustering of LRDs. Meanwhile, the pre-JWST quasar LF constraints are recovered, although we find that a $\sim 0.3$ dex log-normal scatter in bolometric luminosity is required to reproduce the bright end. We place the simulated AGN population in the cosmological context by quantifying the redshift evolution of AGN and LRD number densities, and their contributions to the integrated BH mass densities. The same AGN population is the dominant driver for the HeII reionization modelled self-consistently in Lumina. This empirical AGN model paves the way for general population-synthesis models of high-redshift AGN, including LRDs, in a unified cosmological framework.

authors.name: Xuejian Shen, Oliver Zier, Aaron Smith, Rongrong Liu, Rahul Kannan, Teodora-Elena Bulichi, Sonja M. Koehler, Volker Springel, Mark Vogelsberger, Lars Hernquist, Rohan P. Naidu, Anna de Graaff, Elia Pizzati, David M. Alexander, Luis C. Ho, Vasily Kokorev, Gene Leung, Anna-Christina Eilers, Ryan C. Hickox

papers.title: Deep optical spectroscopic monitoring of the pulsating ULX NGC 1313 X-2 with long-slit Gemini observations
papers.summary: This study reports the nature of the companion star to the pulsating ULX NGC 1313 X-2, using long-slit spectroscopic data from Gemini-South observations, based on archival data from 2009. After stacking flux-calibrated spectra from ten nights of observations and fitting the spectra with stellar templates, we find a possible Balmer break in the GMOS-S spectrum below 4000 Angstroms, which is suggestive of an A-type supergiant donor. Using the inferred stellar radii, we report updated constraints on the orbital parameters of the system and on the nature of the binary. We also add some information on the accretion disc size scale by studying the X-ray and optical variability using the lag-frequency spectrum and corroborate on results from earlier studies for the gas bubble expansion rates by modelling the [O III] emission line profiles, allowing constraints on the kinetic power of the wind/jet relative to the accretion power. This study also expands on previous efforts to study the formation history of the binary using multi-wavelength observations.

authors.name: Rajath Sathyaprakash, Timothy. P. Roberts

papers.title: KRONOS II: Solar-like Umbra and Penumbra Properties on the Young Sun V1298~Tau
papers.summary: Transiting exoplanets provide a unique laboratory for studying stellar surface heterogeneities via starspot or facular occultations. When observed at multiple wavelengths, this configuration enables spectroscopic characterization of spot thermal contrasts, distributions, and morphology. In this work, we leverage JWST NIRISS/SOSS transit observations of the 20--30 Myr planets V1298~Tau~bcd to study the surface properties of their solar analog host star V1298~Tau. We identify 14 starspot crossing events across two visits. We derive $0.8-2.8\mu$m starspot contrast spectra and demonstrate the contrasts are best explained when accounting for the umbral and penumbral components of the starspots, robust to which stellar model grid is assumed. The spot temperatures are broadly consistent between visits, suggesting that V1298 Tau ($T_\mathrm{phot}=4866\pm33$ K) has starspots with $T_{\mathrm{umbra}}$ = 3200--3400 K umbrae and $T_{\mathrm{penumbra}}$ = 4400--4600 K penumbrae, and are $\sim$25--30\% umbrae by area. The differences between these spot components and the stellar photosphere are consistent with sunspots. Additionally, the relation between the spot contrast and the ratio of umbral to penumbral area is similar to that of the Sun. Combining these JWST observations with long baseline multi-band photometry from the Las Cumbres Observatory, we also estimated the global unocculted spot distribution, revealing at least 5 additional large unocculted active regions assuming no facular contribution. Altogether, these measurements suggest that while the total spot coverage evolves in time, the relative temperatures of surface heterogeneities on Sun-like stars may be consistent throughout their lifetimes. Furthermore, these results demonstrate that JWST exoplanet transit observations can be useful for starspot substructure characterization.

authors.name: Matthew M. Murphy, Adina D. Feinstein, Meir E. Schochet, Benjamin V. Rackham, Luis Welbanks, Darryl Z. Seligman, Girish M. Duvvuri, Eva-Maria Ahrer, John H. Livingston, Saugata Barat, Jean-Michel D\'esert, Rafael Luque, Catriona Murray, Matthew C. Nixon, Sydney Petz, Michael Radica, Hinna Shivkumar

papers.title: A Log-Uniform Initial Magnetic Field Distribution Explains Pulsar and Magnetar Populations through Magnetic Inclination Alignment
papers.summary: The origin of the gap in the observed magnetic field distribution between pulsars and magnetars raises a challenge to understanding these populations within a unified framework. We analytically show that the gap can be naturally explained by the alignment of the magnetic inclination angle between the magnetic and spin axes. Based on coupled evolution of spin-down and magnetic inclination angle in the plasma-filled magnetosphere, the alignment timescale follows $\tau_\alpha \propto B^{-2}$. Thus, strongly magnetized neutron stars including high-$B$ pulsars and magnetars align more rapidly than pulsars with $10^{12}\,\mathrm{G}$, reducing their beaming fraction and thereby suppressing their observed numbers. However, magnetars are primarily identified through X-ray activity and are therefore relatively less affected by beaming. Taking into account both beaming fraction and luminosity corrections, we reconstruct the initial magnetic field distribution from the observed distribution. We show that pulsars and magnetars do not dictate intrinsically distinct initial distributions, but can instead be understood within a single continuous initial magnetic field distribution, such as a log-uniform distribution.

authors.name: Takumi Shimasue, Kenta Hotokezaka, Paz Beniamini

papers.title: Response of a Pulsar Timing Array to an Internal Gravitational-wave Source
papers.summary: Millisecond pulsars (MSPs) are abundant in globular clusters (GCs) and probably also in galactic nuclei. They offer the potential to form a miniature pulsar timing array (mini-PTA) to detect nanohertz gravitational-wave (GW) sources located inside the array. Since the size of such an array is comparable to the wavelength of GW, the conventional plane-wave approximation becomes invalid, and near-field effects, including wavefront curvature, non-radiative self-field of the GW source, and direct perturbation of pulsar by GW, become significant. In this work, we incorporate these effects in a comprehensive model to calculate the timing residual induced by a GW source inside a mini-PTA. We also consider realistic GW source configurations in GCs (M15 and $\omega$ Centauri) and in galactic nuclei (Sgr A* and M31), and find that for MSPs located sufficiently close to the GW source (within a few wavelengths), the residual can reach $1~\mu\mathrm{s}$ in GCs and up to milliseconds in galactic centers, within the potential detection reach of current radio telescopes. Crucially, when the pulsar lies within a few GW wavelengths of the source, the non-radiative field dominates and causes the residual to rise much more steeply (between $1/r_e^2$ and $1/r_e^4$, where $r_e$ is the distance to the source) than the conventional far-field scaling ($1/r_e$). These results demonstrate that mini-PTAs in GCs or galactic nuclei can serve as powerful probes of otherwise invisible GW sources, including intermediate-mass and supermassive black hole binaries.

authors.name: Houyuan Qi, Xian Chen, Lin Wang, Kuo Liu

papers.title: Gas-induced gravitational-wave dephasing and accretion periodicities of live post-Newtonian massive black hole binaries: warm disk
papers.summary: We perform 3D hydrodynamical simulations of an equal-mass quasi-circular live $10^6 {\rm M}_\odot$ massive black hole binary (MBHB) embedded in a prograde, locally isothermal circumbinary disk (CBD) with 0.1 aspect ratio. The binary evolves under the effect of gaseous torques and 2.5 post-Newtonian dynamics. We follow the gravitational-wave (GW) driven inspiral from 53 Schwarzschild radii ($r_s$) down to merger, over 1.5 years. Comparing the GW inspiral rate with the viscous inflow, we find the binary to decouple from the CBD just $\approx 2$ days before merger. We measure gas torques (gravitational and accretion) with and without concurrent GW emission, finding that their sums agree to within $\lesssim 5\%$ down to $25 r_s$. We then measure a gas-induced GW phase shift that peaks at $\approx 5\times10^{-4}$ rad near $45 r_s$, as the gas torque slows the inspiral, and then changes sign as the accreted mass accelerates it. It is LISA-detectable only at $z\lesssim 0.1$. We further characterize the mass accretion rate modulations. All three fundamental periodicities, associated with the "lump" at the inner cavity edge, the binary orbital period, and half of it, are shifted to lower frequencies by precession. We measure the shift at the orbital period, due to relativistic apsidal precession, in an inspiraling binary for the first time, and newly identify the other two as due to the precession of the eccentric cavity. Our results have implications for multi-messenger astronomy, since observation of accretion rate modulation by LSST/Roman surveys and phase-shift by LISA will provide crucial information on the complex environment surrounding MBHBs.

authors.name: Mudit Garg, Alessia Franchini, Alessandro Lupi

papers.title: Micron-Scale Technosignatures: How a Cubic Metre of Lunar Regolith May Begin to Constrain the Number of Past Technological Civilisations in the Galaxy
papers.summary: Building on Arkhipov's proposal that technogenic artefacts may survive natural interstellar transport and accumulate on Solar System surfaces, we examine the prospects for identifying micron-scale engineered particulate material within the lunar regolith. We analyse the transport of micron and submicron grains through the interstellar medium, including gas drag, sputtering, and ISM phase-dependent survival, and show that refractory particles with characteristic radii of order 0.3 microns may traverse kiloparsec scales over residence times of 0.1-1 Gyr. Solar radiation pressure and heliospheric filtering define a dynamically constrained slow-arrival channel in which a small fraction of grains reach the Earth-Moon system at relative velocities compatible with survival upon impact. Combining these properties with regolith-mixing constraints yields quantitative upper limits on the cumulative undirected technomaterial output of large-scale spacefaring civilisations: a null detection in a cubic metre of regolith excludes scenarios in which Solar-type stars typically disperse more than approximately 0.10 Earth mass equivalents of long-lived artificial particulate debris over Galactic history. Deliberate targeting of the inner Solar System with artificial particulate matter defines a complementary regime characterised by the visitation frequency and deposited mass of such releases, for which the probabilities of detection may be orders of magnitude higher. We outline a multi-modal detection strategy integrating machine-vision triage with laboratory forensic techniques to identify anomalous grains within a well-characterised natural background. Particulate technosignatures thus establish an experimentally accessible form of exo-archaeology, capable of placing meaningful constraints -- and, in favourable cases, yielding direct material evidence -- of the Galaxy's technological history.

authors.name: Lewis J. Pinault, Brian C. Lacki, Ian A. Crawford, Andrew P. V. Siemion

papers.title: Dust Formation in Common Envelope Binary Interactions -- III. Lightcurves
papers.summary: Luminous red novae are transient events thought to arise from common envelope binary interactions. In this paper, we perform post-processing light-curve calculations for two, 3D hydrodynamic simulations of common envelope events between 1.7 $M_\odot$ and 3.7 $M_\odot$ asymptotic giant branch stars and a 0.6 $M_\odot$ compact companion, simulated for 44 years under adiabatic conditions, with dust nucleation included. In both our simulations, we observe a bright, hot peak lasting 3--5 years, primarily due to photospheric expansion before and during inspiral. Additional peaks appear for different viewing angles due to the interaction's asymmetry. Dust forms about 1--3 years after the beginning of the simulated interaction, and shortly afterwards, followed by a partial recovery and a plateau with a colour temperature of $\sim$ 400 K. The dust photosphere reaches a size of $\sim$ 250 au by the end of the simulations, but would become optically thin at visible wavelengths in 2000--6000 years, revealing an inner, warmer photosphere. Our results are most reliable around the time of peak and the immediate light decline; outside this window, they remain largely qualitative due to two well-quantified but substantial uncertainties---insufficient surface resolution in the first 1--2 years and the adiabatic assumption in the later years. We finally contextualise our simulations within a group of observed luminous red nova transients, drawing particular attention to the outburst of OGLE-2002-BLG-360 and AT 2025abao, which are the only two luminous red novae to date understood to be the interaction of a companion with low-to-intermediate-mass giant stars.

authors.name: Chunliang Mu, Orsola De Marco, Luis C. Berm\'udez-Bustamante, Ryosuke Hirai, Daniel J. Price, Lionel Siess, Miguel Gonz\'alez-Bol\'ivar, Mike Y. M. Lau, Nadejda Blagorodnova

papers.title: Effect of post-recombination accretion on primordial binary black hole mergers within virialized dark matter halos
papers.summary: Gravitational waves from binary black hole mergers remain among primary sources for ground-based and space laser interferometers. Primordial binary black holes (PBHs) can form binaries in the early Universe or at the matter-dominated stage in virialized dark matter halos at redshifts $z\sim 7-15$. We study enhancement of primordial binary PBH merger rate in virialized dark matter halos due to baryon accretion in the post-recombination epoch within two accretion models onto individual PBH -- Bondi-Hoyle-Littleton (BHL) and Park-Ricotti (PR), representing two extreme cases of the accretion efficiency. We calculate modification of the initial PBH mass function and their fractional contribution to dark matter. A significant enhancement in the binary PBH merger rate is found for the late three-body channel, which was previously treated as subdominant. In the case of delayed virialization onset at $z<10$, merger rates of dynamically formed PBH binaries are limited by the existing LVK binary BH detections. An increased merger frequency is revealed for PBH binaries with highly asymmetric mass ratios. We also calculate expected detection rates of binary PBH mergers for the TianQin space-based gravitational-wave interferometer and show them to be optimistic in the BHL accretion case even for very low initial PBH abundances $f_\text{PBH}\sim 10^{-6}$.

authors.name: A. Konovalov, K. Postnov

papers.title: Structural Diversity Among the Milky Way's Dwarf Spheroidal Satellites
papers.summary: We fit a flexible double power-law (`$\alpha\beta\gamma$') model to the stellar density fields observed for the Milky Way's known dwarf spheroidal satellite galaxies. We show that where standard criteria for model selection are decisive, the $\alpha\beta\gamma$ model is favored over the special case of the Plummer model, and also over the \sersic\ model and its special case, the exponential. The Milky Way's dSph population exhibits a diverse range of stellar density profile shapes, as quantified by the values we infer for outer and inner power-law indices $\beta$ and $\gamma$. Several of the most massive dSphs (e.g., Eridanus II, Fornax, Leo I, Leo II) have steeply-declining outer profiles, with $\beta\gtrsim 8$; others (e.g., Sextans, Bo\"otes I) fade slowly, with $\beta\lesssim 4$. The inner profiles of dSphs with stellar mass $\gtrsim 10^5 M_{\odot}$ are consistent with `cores' of uniform stellar density ($\gamma\approx 0$). At lower masses the slopes of inner density profiles are poorly constrained, except in a few ultrafaint dSphs (e.g., Hercules, Ursa Major II) where we infer steep stellar cusps, with $\gamma\gtrsim 1.5$. Owing to the $\alpha\beta\gamma$ model's flexibility, the inferred halflight radii and total stellar masses are significantly more uncertain than previous estimates, with halflight radii larger by up to an order of magnitude in some cases. Finally, we demonstrate that allowing for flexibility in the shape of the stellar density profile is crucial for dSph mass modeling, where systematic errors associated with choice of stellar density profile can outweigh random errors in the observed velocity dispersions.

authors.name: Matthew G. Walker, Rapha\"el Errani, Andrew B. Pace, Jorge Pe\~narrubia, Sofia Splawska, Eduardo Vitral

papers.title: HAMCOR: inferring X-ray coronal geometry from reverberation lags with a Hamiltonian formulation and exact photon transfer in Schwarzschild and Kerr spacetimes
papers.summary: X-ray reverberation lags probe the geometry of the corona around accreting black holes, but are usually interpreted with parametric geometries such as a lamppost. We present HAMCOR, a geometry-agnostic method that infers the coronal emissivity distribution from reverberation lags. The corona is a non-negative emissivity field on a grid; the solution minimises a Hamiltonian combining a smoothness prior with lag likelihoods and the measured illumination fraction. Photon transfer is computed by exact null-geodesic integration in Schwarzschild and Kerr spacetimes, including the energy shifts of the reflected spectrum, and the model passes through the same cross-spectral estimator as the data, with dilution and an intrinsic continuum lag. Lag-frequency spectra constrain about four combinations of the emissivity; centroids are recovered within 2-6 r_g, maps only partially. In eight XMM-Newton observations of Mrk 335, 1H 0707-495, IRAS 13224-3809 and MCG-6-30-15, six reflection fractions exceed the maximum reachable around a non-spinning hole; at a=0.998 seven become reachable and require compact coronae (R_c ~ 2-3 r_g), in tension with the lags in three epochs of Mrk 335. Lag-energy spectra fitted with the energy-resolved transfer quadruple the number of constrained parameters. A lamppost allowed down to the horizon is preferred by the Akaike criterion in all cases but one, Mrk 335 in 2006 at maximal spin, where it is disfavoured only if the reflection fraction is known to better than 0.03, whereas alternative spectral models spread it by 0.1. Current data are consistent with, but do not require, an extended corona; excluding a lamppost requires a reflection fraction measured to a few per cent independently of the spectral model together with a high-coherence lag-energy spectrum. The code is publicly available.

authors.name: Fabio Buffoli

papers.title: SPH methods in the modelling of compact objects
papers.summary: We review the current status of compact object simulations that are based on the Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) method. The first section of this review is dedicated to SPH as a numerical method for Newtonian, ideal gas dynamics and it should be fairly self-contained. It begins with the basics of the method, but also describes recent advances including various meshless derivatives or methods for treating shocks. A separate chapter summarizes general relativistic SPH, including its special relativistic limit, and it explains in some detail the recent development of full numerical relativity in SPH where matter is evolved together with a dynamical spacetime. The remainder of the review has an astrophysical focus, here we discuss the status of the simulations of white dwarf--white dwarf, neutron star--neutron star and neutron star--black hole systems. For each type of system the emphasis is on gravitational-wave-driven mergers, but we also briefly summarize dynamical collisions that can occur in locations with large stellar densities.

authors.name: Stephan Rosswog

papers.title: Discrepancies between Chandrasekhar's theory of relaxation and $N$-body simulations
papers.summary: Globular clusters are systems which are known to be particularly well described by two-body relaxation. In recent decades many studies have shown that Chandrasekhar's orbit-averaged theory is able to reproduce many features of numerical simulations. However, it has been claimed that differences between the theory and simulation remain, such as an amplitude mismatch of the rate of change of the distribution function. In this paper we compare the theoretical predictions of Chandrasekhar's theory for anisotropic clusters to precise $N$-body data. We show that more careful $N$-body measurements are able to reduce the claimed mismatch. Nevertheless, we observe a dependency of the remaining mismatch on both position and anisotropy. While the dependence on anisotropy may be understood qualitatively on theoretical grounds, the radial dependence implies that spatial inhomogeneities, and therefore collective effects, may become unavoidable to resolve the residual mismatch between theory and simulations.

authors.name: Kerwann Tep, Douglas C. Heggie

papers.title: PANTERA. I. Hunting for the Most Metal-Rich Stars in the Solar Neighborhood with High-Resolution Spectroscopy
papers.summary: We present PANTERA (Project for Astrophysical Nucleosynthesis and Targeted Exploration of metal-Rich Abundances), a high-resolution spectroscopic survey of the most metal-rich stars in the solar neighborhood. In this first paper, we report iron abundances for 56 metal-rich stars, selected from Gaia DR3 XP spectrophotometric metallicities. These targets were observed with the PEPSI spectrograph on the Large Binocular Telescope (LBT), the Levy spectrograph on the Automated Planet Finder (APF) telescope, and the HIRES spectrograph on the Keck telescope. We derive [Fe/H] from an equivalent-width analysis of iron lines, with the effective temperature taken from photometry and the surface gravity from the Gaia parallax. We verify our measurement using Gaia benchmark stars, observing some sources with more than one spectrograph, using a second synthesis code, and an independent equivalent-width measurement. We find that the Gaia-XP metallicities over-predict [Fe/H] for part of our sample: they agree with our values for the dwarfs, though a selection bias limits what this agreement can show, and exceed our [Fe/H] by $0.15\pm0.02$ dex on average for the cool giants. We attribute the over-prediction in part to the strong blue line blanketing of the cool metal-rich giants and to the survey labels on which the XP metallicities were trained. We find that 25 of the 56 stars have [Fe/H] $> +0.4$, with the most iron-rich stars reaching [Fe/H]$=+0.58$. We discuss the implications of our result on studying metal-rich populations.

authors.name: Serat M. Saad, D. M. Rowan, K. Z. Stanek, Ilya Ilyin, Benjamin J. Fulton, Howard Isaacson, Jessica R. Lu

papers.title: The eROSITA X-ray luminosity function of active galactic nuclei
papers.summary: The X-ray luminosity function (XLF) of active galactic nuclei (AGN) provides an observational probe of the growth of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) across cosmic time. With its large survey grasp, Spectrum Roentgen Gamma (SRG)/eROSITA samples the luminosity--redshift plane with a depth--area balance complementary to pencil-beam surveys, providing the volume needed to detect rare luminous AGN, previously limited by small-number statistics. We measure the soft XLF, leveraging an eROSITA sample spanning approximately eight orders of magnitude in luminosity out to $z\simeq6$. This enables us to study luminosity-dependent evolution with improved constraints, and to infer both the SMBH accretion history and optical/UV missed AGN population. We introduce a new redshift-dependent smoothly broken power-law parameterisation in which all XLF model parameters are allowed to evolve continuously with redshift. We find lower space densities for moderately and very luminous AGN at low redshift, while the abundance is higher than previously found at the highest redshifts. Comparisons to optical/UV quasar LFs converted to rest-frame $2\!-\!10\,\mathrm{keV}$ show that the UV-missed fraction decreases with luminosity, and, in the most luminous bin, increases with redshift. Integrating the XLF yields a black-hole accretion-rate density peaking at $z \simeq 1.5$, with the corresponding cumulative black-hole mass density indicating $\sim80^{+11}_{-23}\%$ obscured growth relative to locally-inferred BH mass estimates derived from scaling relations and missed by the soft X-ray selection of our sample. With this work, we release the eROSITA DR2 AGN catalogue, including counterparts and their redshift information. We then discuss how these results can inform future spectroscopic, photometric, and X-ray survey strategies aimed at improving AGN demographic constraints.

authors.name: W. Roster, J. Buchner, M. Salvato, R. Shirley, A. Merloni, T. Dwelly, J. Aird, A. Georgakakis, P. Boorman, Z. Igo, M. Brusa, W. N. Brandt, B. Trakhtenbrot, B. Laloux, P. Baldini, C. Andonie, C. Aydar, C. Ricci, S. F. Anderson, P. Chakraborty, R. J. Assef, D. P. Schneider, E. Kyritsis, M. Kluge, E. Bulbul, K. Nandra, J. Weller

papers.title: Tomographer: End-to-end Redshift Distribution Estimation for Source Catalogs and Intensity Maps
papers.summary: Redshift information is central to nearly every extragalactic and cosmological application of sky surveys, yet only a small fraction of cataloged sources, and none of the photons forming diffuse backgrounds, have spectroscopic redshifts. Clustering-based redshift inference estimates the redshift distribution of an arbitrary dataset through spatial cross-correlation with a reference sample of known redshifts. It relies only on positional information, making it applicable to any tracer of large-scale structure, including source populations and diffuse intensity maps. Its broader adoption, however, has been limited by technical barriers: assembling and characterizing spectroscopic references, expensive pair-counting computations, theoretical corrections, and systematic control. To remove these barriers, we introduce Tomographer, an end-to-end clustering-redshift framework. The key design feature is a set of precomputed "activation maps" encoding the spatial pair information of 3 million Sloan Digital Sky Survey spectroscopic galaxies and quasars up to $z\sim4$ over $10{,}000\,{\rm deg}^2$. This eliminates user-end pair counting, reducing computational scaling from $O(N\log N)$ to $O(1)$ map multiplications. Given a source catalog or intensity map, Tomographer returns the bias-weighted redshift distribution, $b(z)\,{\rm d}N/{\rm d}z(z)$ or $b(z)\,{\rm d}I/{\rm d}z(z)$. We validate the framework against samples with known redshifts, demonstrate accurate uncertainty estimates, and show robustness to survey footprint, spatially varying selection functions, beam smoothing, and foreground contamination. We showcase applications to source catalogs selected by flux, color, photometric redshift, morphology, or variability, and to intensity maps from radio to X-rays. Future Tomographer releases will incorporate additional wide-field spectroscopic reference samples as they become available.

authors.name: Yi-Kuan Chiang, Yu Voon Ng, Yu-Ren Lin, Manuchehr Taghizadeh-Popp, Brice M\'enard

papers.title: The Zero-Age Massive Stellar Population of W49A from VLA Observations
papers.summary: We use all-configuration VLA data at 3.3 cm with a physical resolution of ~2000 AU to infer the embedded zero-age massive stellar population of the W49A protocluster, as traced by its compact, ultracompact (UC), and hypercompact (HC) H II regions. Our method consists of visual source identification, the derivation of stellar ionizing-photon rates from the observed emission measure, and the further derivation of stellar masses and luminosities using state-of-the-art stellar calibrations. Considering the 101 robust detections, maximum-likelihood estimation fitting of the high-mass end (M > 10.9 M_\odot) of the sample yields power-law slopes Gamma >= 2.40 for the logarithmic representation of the stellar initial mass function (IMF): dN/d(log M) proportional to M^{-Gamma}. The result is robust considering different assumptions for the ionizing stellar systems. The slopes remain at Gamma >= 1.88 after correction for optical depth effects at 3.3 cm. Therefore, the inferred distribution of stellar masses presents a clear deficit in the high-mass end as compared to the standard stellar IMF (Gamma = 1.35). We propose that this is due to a shorter lifetime of the radio-detected H II regions produced by higher-mass stars, but evolutionary effects in the mass distribution of star formation within embedded protoclusters cannot be discarded.

authors.name: M. Ju\'arez-Gama, R. Galv\'an-Madrid, G. Su\'arez, C. G. De Pree, J. J. Tobin, G. Bruzual, A. Ginsburg, J. E. Mendoza-Torres, H. B. Liu, D. Wilner, T. Nony, A. Parra-L\'opez, R. Rivera-Soto, A. F. McLeod, N. Cunningham, X. Lu, E. F. Jim\'enez-Andrade

papers.title: The instantaneous mass accretion rate of novae in quiescence: - an archival ultraviolet optical spectral analysis
papers.summary: Based on archival spectra, we derive the quiescent instantaneous mass transfer rates in novae using synthetic disk spectra generated with tlusty, Gaia parallax-derived distances, and updated color excess values. Our results for nine novae, based on ultraviolet spectra and on a number of optical spectra, yield mass accretion rates that are higher than those derived from simple integration of the UV and optical luminosity. HR Del, 20 years after its eruption, has a mass transfer rate of $4\times 10^{-7}M_\odot$/yr, and is likely burning the accreting H-rich material. V842 Cen, thought to be a low mass transfer system, has a comparable mass accretion rate. For both novae, the enhanced mass transfer must be self-sustained by a feedback loop. RR Pic, with $\dot{M}\approx 5\times 10^{-8}M_\odot$/yr, is better fitted with an accretion disk where the outer region is heated up to 12,000 K, in agreement with H and He emission lines coming from the outer disk and a large emission region on the leading side of the disk. Such a heated disk also gives a good fit to the spectra of CP Lac, and DI Lac with $\dot{M}\sim4.5$ and $9\times 10^{-9}M_\odot$/yr. V1974 Cyg and V533 Her, with an accretion rate of $\sim 3\times 10^{-9}M_\odot$/yr, have a rather flat spectrum. V446 Her and BK Lyn, caught in a state of low accretion, have the lowest mass accretion rates with $\dot{M} \sim 10^{-9}$ and $\sim 10^{-10}M_\odot$/yr respectively. The higher mass transfer rate systems, with $\dot{M}\approx \sim 10^{-7}M_\odot$/yr, agree with the standard disk model; the remaining systems are better fitted when the outer disk is heated to $\sim 12,000$~K. We suggest that irradiation from the heated WD, inner disk, together with tidal interaction, the bright spot, and material overflowing the disk edge, can increase the temperature of the outer disk.

authors.name: Patrick Godon, Edward M. Sion, Tim Naylor, Frederick A. Ringwald

papers.title: The Atacama Cosmology Telescope: Passband Measurements with an Analysis of Systematic Errors
papers.summary: We present measurements of the spectral response of the four Advanced ACTPol (AdvACT) multichroic detector arrays, which observed in frequency bands centered near 30, 40, 90, 150, and 220 GHz. The passbands were measured with a Fourier transform spectrometer (FTS) combined with coupling optics that direct and match the output of the FTS to the AdvACT receiver. We perform optical simulations of the FTS and coupling optics in order to model frequency-dependent systematic effects in this system, examining the systematics of each individual measurement component in detail. We use these simulations to apply corrections to the measurements and evaluate the remaining systematic uncertainty. We combine these systematic estimates with statistical errors to determine the measured passbands and their uncertainties from our FTS measurement, which are typically $0.75$ to $1.5\%$ per detector array for the central frequency. We present the passband characteristics for all measurements made by ACT in a common framework. Additionally, we discuss in detail limits set by the systematics in our measurements as well as ways to minimize the systematics of each component to improve passband measurements in the future.

authors.name: Thomas Alford, Rahul Datta, Erminia Calabrese, Steve K. Choi, Mark Devlin, Shannon M. Duff, Adriaan J. Duivenvoorden, Rolando D\"unner, Joseph Golec, Matthew Hasselfield, J. Colin Hill, Johannes Hubmayr, Jeffrey McMahon, Michael D. Niemack, Lyman A. Page, Suzanne T. Staggs, Alex Thomas, Cristian Vargas, Yuhan Wang, Edward J. Wollack

papers.title: JW-FD_V2: A 15-Year Multimodal Dataset for Solar Flare Forecasting
papers.summary: Solar flares drive severe space weather hazards, and forecasting their occurrence remains a central challenge for both heliophysics and operational space weather services. Data driven methods require long horizon datasets in which images, magnetic features, and flare labels are coregistered in space and time. We present JW-FD (JinWu-Flare Dataset), a 15 year multimodal release spanning 1 January 2011 through 31 December 2025, constructed from SDO/HMI line of sight magnetograms, NOAA Solar Region Summary reports, and NOAA X-ray flare event lists. The dataset comprises 3,083 independent active regions and 2,003,969 coregistered magnetogram crops, together with FITS, PNG, CSV, and MP4 modalities. Each sample provides 29 magnetic features linked to configurable flare labels under a strict pre-eruption window spanning seven forecast horizons and four GOES intensity thresholds. An 8:1:1 split at the active region level, obtained by stratified rejection sampling (seed 3970), keeps each active region in a single partition to prevent temporal leakage and balances rare M- and X-class positives between validation and test. PNG branches are released at ten magnetic saturation thresholds. A Swin ablation over all ten clips finds >C1.0 skill nearly insensitive to Bth, whereas >M1.0, >M5.0, and >X1.0 lock different clips. We therefore adopt Bth = 800 G as a compromise PNG working point rather than the optimum of any one task, and report four-model 24 h baselines at that clip. Skill remains modest as the class becomes rarer. The open source construction pipeline is available at https://github.com/Xiaoxuan-1/JW-FD, and the released dataset (version v2) at https://doi.org/10.57760/sciencedb.019mg.

authors.name: Shao Mingfu, Lin Jiaben, Wang Hui, Tong Liyue, Yang Chen, Zhang Yin, Li Yuyang

papers.title: Constraining neutron-star properties with ensembles of thermonuclear bursts: application to SRGA J144459.2-604207
papers.summary: Deducing the properties of the host neutron stars from thermonuclear (type-I) X-ray bursts remains a challenge, due to incomplete data, multidimensional parameter space, and dearth of suitable models and analysis tools. Here we describe further development of the BEANSP package, with a new "ensemble" analysis mode utilising the consistent and regular "clocked" bursting exhibited by some sources. This mode requires only one model evaluation per epoch, and so is much more efficient than the previous "train" mode. We apply the code to the best-known source exhibiting "clocked" bursting, GS 1826-24, utilising a grid of KEPLER models pre-calculated for this purpose, and find good agreement with a previous study. We performed experiments on simulated data, and recovered input parameters related to the burst ignition with reasonable accuracy, but less so for the system distance, emission anisotropy and neutron star mass and radius. Finally, we assembled a set of 14 daily burst epochs covering the 2024 outburst of the accretion-powered millisecond pulsar SRGA J144459.2-604207, and attempted to constrain the system properties of this object by comparing to SETTLE model predictions. We find reasonably good agreement between the observations and model predictions for a mildly sub-solar fuel composition, with H-fraction $X\approx0.54$ and CNO metallicity $Z_{\rm CNO}\approx0.01$. However, we note that the inferred H-fraction is in excess of the limit of 0.4 established separately, and the adopted model may not provide sufficiently accurate predictions for this burst ignition regime. The inferred distance depends on assumptions about the system inclination and corresponding anisotropy of the persistent emission, and is likely in the range 6-11 kpc. Future applications with more physically realistic models are a promising avenue for this and other sources with H-rich bursts.

authors.name: Duncan K. Galloway (Monash University, Australia, IGDORE), Serena Jones (ICRAR Curtin), Luke Waterson (Monash University, Australia), Tao Fu (Xiangtan University, China), Adelle J. Goodwin (ICRAR Curtin), Zhaosheng Li (Qingdao University of Technology, China)

papers.title: Fractional Bose-Einstein Condensate Dark Matter Cores: Numerical GPP Solutions and SPARC Rotation Curves
papers.summary: We investigate a fractional Bose Einstein condensate dark matter scenario in which an ultralight bosonic component forms a self gravitating core embedded in a predominantly cold dark matter halo. The stationary GPP system solved numerically beyond the TF approximation leads to energetically bound equilibrium configurations and good phenomenological fits to the selected rotation curves from 30 SPARC galaxies.

authors.name: Akila Labadi, Mohamed Benarous, Ahmed Hocine

papers.title: One Precessing Jet Pair, Diverse Core-Collapse Supernova Remnant Morphologies
papers.summary: We produce a diverse set of observed core-collapse supernova (CCSN)-type morphologies using a precessing pair of opposite jets within the jittering-jets explosion mechanism (JJEM) framework. We conduct a three-dimensional hydrodynamical simulation of a precessing pair of jets that explode a massive star, and find that a single precessing pair of opposite jets can generate S-shaped structures, pipe-spout-blowout features as observed in the Cygnus Loop, multiple apparent pairs of opposite protrusions similar to some morphological features in S147, and H-shaped structures with a prominent bar, similar to the one observed in the 3C 397 remnant.
