papers.summary: For every finite level of the Navascu\'es-Pironio-Ac\'in (NPA) hierarchy, we construct correlations that satisfy all its constraints but violate information causality. At each fixed level, one use of a binary-outcome correlation and one classical bit suffice for a violation that grows without bound as the number of measurement settings increases. Information causality bounds the information gained about independent database bits, summed over possible requests, by the length of the message. Quantum correlations obey the one-bit bound; the optimal information gain at any fixed NPA level grows logarithmically with the number of settings. The violation remains unbounded even when all outcome probabilities are positive and, for any fixed number of measurement settings on each side, every choice of those settings admits a local model. One communicated bit therefore exposes an unbounded gap between information causality and every finite NPA level.

authors.name: Anubhav Chaturvedi, Marcin Paw{\l}owski

papers.title: Vanishing Relative Distance of Uniformly Random CSS LDPC Codes Built from Permutation Matrices
papers.summary: Classical random regular low-density parity-check codes can have minimum distance growing linearly with block length. We study CSS check matrices formed as full $J\times L$ arrays of arbitrary $P\times P$ permutation matrices, sampled uniformly subject to commutation. For fixed column weight $J\ge3$ and fixed even row weight $L>2J$, we prove that the relative minimum distance converges to zero in probability as $P\to\infty$, with block length $n=LP$. We analyze the weight enumerators that count all nontrivial logical representatives after excluding stabilizers. A coefficientwise lower bound shows that, at every fixed relative weight $0<\alpha<1$ along even-weight sequences, exponentially many such representatives exist with high probability. Their typical and mean counts have exponent lower bound $h_2(\alpha)/2$, where $h_2$ is the binary entropy function. We compare this bound with the classical LDPC and dense CSS mean weight-distribution exponents. The existence, with high probability, of a logical operator below every fixed target weight $\delta n$ yields the distance conclusion.

authors.name: Kenta Kasai

papers.title: Quantitative measurement of microwave power at millikelvin temperatures: Comparison between dispersively and directly coupled superconducting qubits
papers.summary: The Rabi frequency of a two-level system is directly proportional to the electric field amplitude being incident on this system. Taking advantage of this relationship, it is possible to use two-level systems as quantitative sensors of electric fields. Here, we apply this concept to superconducting qubits and use them for quantitative measurement of microwave power at millikelvin temperatures. Our superconducting circuit design includes three transmon qubits directly coupled to the central microwave feedline and three transmon qubits coupled dispersively via readout resonators to the feedline. We compare both coupling schemes to assess their reliability for microwave power sensing. Further, we describe the modeling behind each power-sensing method, including an uncertainty estimation based upon repeated measurements. By combining dispersively coupled and directly coupled qubits on the same device, we are able to explore different power ranges: from $-155\;$dBm to $-130\;$dBm for the directly coupled qubits and from $-95\;$dBm to $-55\;$dBm for the dispersively coupled qubits. When determining the microwave-line attenuation for a frequency of $6.0\;$GHz from room temperature to the millikelvin stage of the cryostat, we obtain best estimates and uncertainties for the directly coupled transmons of $(74.7\pm 0.2) \;$dB and for the dispersively coupled transmons of $(75.4\pm 6.8) \;$dB. The larger uncertainty of the dispersively coupled qubit measurements indicates that these qubits are less reliable for power sensing than the directly coupled qubits, most likely, due to the additional coupling resonator, whose transfer function is difficult to estimate accurately. Our results constitute the first step towards validation of qubit power sensing in dilution fridges, leading towards traceability for cryogenic microwave measurements.

authors.name: Asen L. Georgiev, Christoph Kissling, Fabian Kaap, Victor Gaydamachenko, Lukas Gr\"unhaupt, Mark Bieler

papers.title: Sharp $L_p$-Regularity for Quantum Markov Semigroups
papers.summary: We determine the sharp universal constants in positive-input $L_p$-regularity for finite-dimensional quantum Markov semigroups with a faithful invariant state. For $1<p<\infty$, they are $p\sin(\pi/p)/(2(p-1))$ under KMS symmetry and $\frac{p}{2(p-1)}\tan(\frac{\pi}{2}\min\{1/p,1-1/p\})$ without a symmetry assumption, with the endpoint values at $p=1$ given by $\pi/2$ and $\pi/4$, respectively.

authors.name: Lijun Wang

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning designs Quantum Repeater Protocols on Networks beyond the Chain Scenario
papers.summary: Small-scale quantum repeater protocols have been shown to distribute entanglement over existing telecommunication infrastructure by means of short range quantum communications and long range classical messages. For larger networks, there are a number of theoretical proposals about how to operate the network to achieve a good performance under varying metrics. Moreover, since the dimension of the space of possible protocols grows exponentially with network size, plenty of those proposals are based on heuristics that reduce the search space. One of these is entanglement routing, which simplifies the problem on non-linear networks by allocating a series of disjoint paths and running chain protocols simultaneously on them. However, in this work we claim routing leads to suboptimal protocols. In fact, inspired by works on linear chains, we apply reinforcement learning to non-linear networks and optimize over the larger non-routing protocol space. Then, we find protocols that outperform a routed extension of the swap-ASAP protocol, even in the parameter regimes where the latter is widely recognized as the state of the art. These results indicate that routing must be discarded in favor of non-routing methods, while they pave the way towards the design of a sensible Quantum Internet architecture.

authors.name: Andr\'es Agust\'i Casado, \'Alvaro Troyano Olivas, Javier Faba Garc\'ia, Luis M. Robledo, Vicente Mart\'in, Laura Ortiz

papers.title: Rethinking Entropic Uncertainty: How measuring without a trace leads to longer keys
papers.summary: In recent years, the entropic uncertainty relation (EUR) has been one of the most prominent tools to obtain tight key rates secure against general coherent attacks for a broad class of quantum key distribution (QKD) protocols. Despite its success, the fundamental question of how to incorporate the statistics of more than two mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) directly into the EUR is yet to be answered. Here, we introduce a simple yet powerful shift of perspective: Instead of the usual tripartition into the systems of Alice, Bob and Eve, we treat Alice and Bob as one joint system and introduce an additional register as the third system. This register contains the results of appropriately chosen virtual measurements that leave no trace in the real branch of the protocol, but act as a conditioning on the counterfactual phase error measurements. We show that this allows us to obtain tight key rates for QKD protocols using an arbitrary number of MUBs directly and natively from the EUR. Moreover, we demonstrate that this approach has a much broader relevance beyond the inclusion of multiple MUBs, allowing for improvements in many existing security proofs and the treatment of previously unexplored aspects for a wide range of protocols.

authors.name: Philipp Kleinpa{\ss}

papers.title: Plenitude of ideal correlations explains quantum theory
papers.summary: We show that the Hilbert-space formalism and the Born rule of quantum theory are singled out by the following principle: every correlation that is possible in a theory in which every observable admits an ideal measurement is physically realizable. An ideal measurement is one that yields the same outcome when repeated and does not disturb any compatible observable.

authors.name: Ad\'an Cabello

papers.title: Experimental simulation of a Hilbert-space inner-product change
papers.summary: We simulate an effective change in a single qubit's inner product (IP) by implementing the channel $\mathcal{F}^\eta$ on a superconducting quantum processor. Whereas previous experiments simulated parity-time (PT)-symmetric dynamics with a fixed IP, this experiment implements the IP-change channel itself for metrics associated with PT-symmetric systems. Building on an earlier adversarial verification approach, we derive a process-fidelity threshold that rules out mixtures of qubit unitary operations with random discarding of runs. We test the channel for 40 metrics using a single qutrit and a two-qubit Stinespring dilation. The measured fidelities exceed the threshold in 24 of 40 qutrit instances after readout error mitigation, compared with 16 of 40 unmitigated two-qubit instances. Without mitigation, 14 of 40 qutrit instances pass. These results demonstrate a direct simulation of an effective Hilbert-space IP change and its verification against a specified adversarial class, while showing the importance of readout treatment in comparing the encodings.

authors.name: Vinh San Dinh, Salini Karuvade, Abhijeet Alase, Silvia Zorzetti, Barry C. Sanders

papers.title: Quantum Networks with Realistic Photonic Memories
papers.summary: Ensemble based photonic memories paired with photon pair sources are the essential ingredient for many quantum networking protocols. Most protocols and theoretical analyses focus on networks of identical nodes, however, realistic networks consist of nodes that may vary from device to device. We investigate a network of non-identical memories and develop mitigation strategies for the variation in performance. We find that by strategically distributing the memories among the nodes and individually adapting the emission probabilities based on the memory efficiency the effect of the variance on fidelity and duration can to a large extend be mitigated. Generally, our analysis shows the importance of accounting and compensating for device variations to avoid deteriorating the performance. Lastly, we also link our results to memories where efficiency decays as a function of storage duration. Here, we show that our approach provides a visible improvement for networks with non-identical and decaying memories.

authors.name: Benedikt Tissot, Sophia Carmen Simon, Anders S{\o}ndberg S{\o}rensen

papers.title: Entanglement distillation, nonlocal magic, and state sharing in an isospectral non-Hermitian bipartite model
papers.summary: An invertible nonunitary similarity deformation leaves a two-qubit Hamiltonian's spectrum unchanged while varying a selected normalized right eigenstate in the fixed physical inner product. We embed this state in a two-parameter maximally correlated family that includes local dephasing and noisy circuit preparation. Hashing and a matching diagonal relative-entropy bound give the exact distillable entanglement and the PPT comparison distances at every finite tensor power. Correlated PPT catalysts cannot improve the Bell-pair distillation rate. The optimized CHSH value is \(2\sqrt{1+t^2}\): every state with nonzero coherence violates CHSH, while complete dephasing is separable. A calibrated finite-sample bound and two equal-fidelity preparations clarify which noise parameters determine the rate. For pure inputs, the binomial Schmidt spectrum gives logarithmic collectively optimized nonlocal magic with vanishing density, despite a positive entanglement density and extensive pairwise-frame magic. Fixed Clifford decoding gives six- and eight-copy CCZ concentration probabilities \(P_6=\frac12(1-2^{-\mathcal M_\gamma})\) and \(P_8=1-2^{-\mathcal M_\gamma}\). The same family permits explicit swapping recursions, symmetry-resolved entanglement, and a comparison of qubit stabilizer and fermionic Gaussian resources. These calculations keep the relevant operation classes separate when comparing many-copy limits.

authors.name: Chenhuan Wu

papers.title: Exponential Quantum Memory Advantage for Late-Graph Smoothness and Spectral Estimation
papers.summary: Graph signal processing tests how smoothly the decisions of next-generation massive sensor networks with $N$ nodes vary over their neighbour graph. Memory becomes the bottleneck when the neighbour graph arrives only after data erasure, a late-graph setting motivated by dispersed sensor networks and telemetry. We analyse three collection scenarios, reliable rounds, continuous broadcast and ordered capture, and test the Dirichlet energy $\mathcal E_G=\mathbf z^{\mathsf T}\mathbf L\mathbf z/N$ of the fused decision map $\mathbf z\in\{\pm1\}^N$, with late-graph Laplacian $\mathbf L$, against two thresholds. Hidden Matching uses $O(\log N)$ qubits on fused bits, but in reliable rounds and continuous broadcast, where nodes report $b$ sub-bits separately, a classical record buffer before it uses $O(N b)$ bits; classical methods need $\Omega(\sqrt N)$ bits in the worst case. The recently introduced Quantum Oracle Sketching builds quantum oracles from random data streams without storing them. We combine coherent loading of separately reported sub-bits, exact in reliable rounds and by Quantum Oracle Sketching in continuous broadcast, with nonlinear fusion and Hidden Matching readout. The register count $R$ does not grow with $N$, and the memory is $O(\log N)$ logical qubits and classical bits, at fixed $b$, graph bounds, thresholds and error targets: an exponential memory advantage over every classical receiver and over Hidden Matching with that buffer. We prove unbiasedness in reliable rounds, preparation bounds in continuous broadcast, classical lower bounds and, for a planner-supplied multi-hop coefficient stream, spectral error bounds. Broadcast simulations match analytic averages at $N=1024$, without resolved bias growth up to $N=2^{20}$. Fault-tolerant hardware, gate rates and, in continuous broadcast, report counts remain open.

authors.name: Burhan G\"ulbahar

papers.title: The speed limit of gravitational entanglement and the cost of noise
papers.summary: Is gravity quantum? A proposed test lets two small masses, each in a superposition of two places, become entangled through their mutual gravity. Gravity is weak, so the masses must stay coherent for seconds while random forces disturb them. Here we ask how fast gravity can entangle two masses, and what noise costs. Without noise we find the maximum rate exactly: it falls as the inverse cube of the separation, and two positions per mass achieve it. Above a noise level set by the masses and their separation, gravity's leading pull can be imitated by classical signals, and every strategy is limited to a rate falling at least as the inverse fourth power. Exact, continuous error correction shields the masses from noise but hides them from each other: the best rate falls as the inverse seventh power, and six positions on a hexagon come within 10% of it at large separation.

authors.name: Ekta Panwar, Anubhav Chaturvedi

papers.title: Optimal Quantum Sensing Algorithms for Discrete-Frequency Spectroscopy
papers.summary: Spectroscopy is a versatile tool that drives scientific discovery and underpins modern technologies. Quantum sensing offers promising opportunities to advance spectroscopy through enhanced sensitivity and spectral and spatial resolution. However, existing approaches largely focus on improving general measurement capabilities, often overlooking the structure of specific sensing tasks and leaving potential performance gains untapped. Here, we develop an algorithmic approach to quantum sensing tailored to various spectroscopic tasks, providing new avenues for improvement. Specifically, we consider general time-varying signals supported on a known set of $N$ candidate frequencies, a setting we call discrete-frequency spectroscopy. We formulate three types of practically motivated sensing tasks---Detection, Search, and Learning---that require progressively more spectral information. For all tasks, we design optimal quantum sensing algorithms achieving a $\sqrt{N}$ speedup over conventional frequency-scanning approaches. Optimal Detection and Search need only a single-qubit sensor under $\pi$-pulse control, whereas optimal Learning provably requires coherent processing with a quantum computer. End-to-end numerical simulations incorporating various experimental imperfections predict up to two-orders-of-magnitude speedup in Detection. As an example, we analyze the feasibility of our Detection and Search algorithms for real-world molecular screening based on state-of-the-art nitrogen-vacancy centers. We also show how quantum-computing-enhanced Learning enables wireless communication in a weak-signal regime where conventional methods fail. Our results establish a practical route toward realizing quantum advantages via designing task-specific sensing algorithms.

authors.name: Yu-Jie Liu, Richard R. Allen, Ruohan Shen, Bingtian Ye, Timothy T. Chang, Joonhee Choi, Soonwon Choi

papers.title: Resolving and Suppressing Temporally Correlated Noise in Quantum Error Correction
papers.summary: Scaling fault-tolerant quantum error correction (QEC) requires suppressing errors in both space and time, yet standard logical memory experiments primarily probe spatial faults. Here, we use a 105-qubit Willow superconducting quantum processor to realize and scale the surface code stability experiment, which is alternatively sensitive to temporal error chains. Scaling from patch sizes of $3 \times 3$ to $7 \times 7$, we realize a timelike block suppression factor of $\mu_T = 1.47 \pm 0.25$, demonstrating the ability to maintain temporal error suppression as the number of qubits increases. By extending the stability experiment for many cycles, we uncover a sum-of-exponentials behavior in error suppression caused by a temporally correlated error: data-qubit heating to the third excited state $|3\rangle$. We fully capture this effect with a parameter-free, device-level leakage model incorporating higher-state transport during syndrome extraction cycles. To suppress this error, we develop and realize a walking stability circuit, reaching a logical error probability floor of $\le 3.20\times 10^{-8}$ at 60 cycles---two orders of magnitude below the standard construction---and limited by ionizing radiation error bursts. Finally, by adaptively terminating syndrome extraction based on decoder confidence in an offline analysis, we reduce spacetime logical error by 38% and time overhead by 34% compared to the optimal fixed-cycle strategy.

papers.title: Gravitational field of spinors with torsion and matter$-$antimatter asymmetry
papers.summary: The conservation law for the orbital plus spin angular momentum of a free Dirac particle in curved spacetime requires that the affine connection has the antisymmetric part: the torsion tensor, which extends general relativity to the Einstein$-$Cartan theory of gravity. In spacetime with torsion, the Dirac equation becomes a nonlinear, cubic equation in the spinor wave function. Under charge conjugation, the nonlinear term changes sign relative to the mass term. A Dirac spinor and its charge conjugate therefore satisfy different field equations. We use the spinor connection formalism to derive the Dirac equation for a spherical spinor in its centrally symmetric gravitational field with torsion. We determine the energy$-$momentum tensor for this spinor and show that the energy contribution from torsion is negative for matter particles and positive for antimatter particles. Consequently, the ground state of a fermion has a lower energy than the ground state of the corresponding antifermion. We also derive the Einstein$-$Cartan$-$Dirac equations for this spinor; they indicate the existence of particle-like soliton solutions exhibiting matter$-$antimatter energy asymmetry.

authors.name: Nikodem Pop{\l}awski

papers.title: Quantum Cooling by Classical Shadows
papers.summary: Cooling to ground states of many-body Hamiltonians by imaginary-time evolution is central to quantum simulation, but its non-unitary aspect prevents direct implementation on a quantum computer. Existing routes restore it by importing structure from outside the intrinsic quantum dynamics, e.g. by parameter estimation on many copies or recursive compilation. Here, we show that a single randomized snapshot of the quantum many-body system is sufficient to steer the state along the cooling direction on average. Our algorithm, shadow chain, uses randomized measurements to collapse the state to its classical record, which fixes the next unitary update. Snapshots across steps form a trajectory that is a quantum-executable sample of an auxiliary-field path integral; fluctuations among trajectories are exponentially suppressed in system size. With the randomness supplied intrinsically by the Born measurement rule, the trajectories sample themselves rather than going through external accept-reject steps. The resulting algorithm is ansatz-free and exact upon extrapolation to the continuous limit, with the exponential cost confined only to system size rather than temperature.

authors.name: Xuepeng Wang, Debanjan Chowdhury

papers.title: Gapless Nature of Spin Liquid in the $S=1/2$ Kagome Heisenberg Antiferromagnet with Neural-Network Quantum States
papers.summary: Whether the spin-$1/2$ kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet hosts a gapped $\mathbb{Z}_2$ or a gapless $U(1)$ Dirac spin liquid remains a central open question in frustrated magnetism. Here, we address this question by directly computing the triplet gap with a neural-network quantum state that does not presuppose any specific spin-liquid structure. Applying a time-reversal symmetric transformer-based ansatz to clusters of up to $768$ sites, we obtain state-of-the-art variational energies on two-dimensional lattices with periodic boundary conditions and estimate an energy per site of $-0.43873(12)$ in the thermodynamic limit. Finite-size scaling of the magnetic order parameter and triplet excitation gap shows that both extrapolate to zero in the thermodynamic limit. Together, these results provide independent and direct evidence of a gapless spin-liquid ground state, consistent with the $U(1)$ Dirac spin liquid. More broadly, they demonstrate that neural-network quantum states can resolve ground-state properties of frustrated quantum magnets that remain challenging for conventional numerical methods.

authors.name: Andreas Raikos, Alessandro Sinibaldi, Riccardo Rende, Giuseppe Carleo, Federico Becca, Luciano Loris Viteritti

papers.title: Flexible ground-state search algorithm on hybrid Clifford-tensor network manifolds
papers.summary: Tensor network algorithms face challenges in highly entangled regimes, such as systems with periodic boundary conditions (PBC), long-range interactions, or higher dimensions, where the required bond dimension quickly renders computations infeasible. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a novel approach that integrates the stabilizer formalism directly into the traditional density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) algorithm. While previous methods have used Clifford unitaries to minimize ground-state entanglement, fundamentally limited to distilling that away utilizing local two-qubit operations, our framework optimizes Clifford transformations to minimize the state's energy. We benchmark our method against standard DMRG at fixed bond dimensions for the Ising model on a ring (including long-range interactions) and on a torus. We observe systematic gains in models with local interactions - as drastic as a factor of 40 decrease in bond dimension in two dimensions. Our algorithm is readily implementable in standard DMRG codes and provides a practical way to substantially reduce algorithm costs, paving the way for large-scale simulation at volumes beyond what is presently achievable.

authors.name: Hari Timsina, Antonio Francesco Mello, Meghadeepa Adhikary, Marcello Dalmonte, Mario Collura

papers.title: Landauer erasure and horizon information in an expanding universe
papers.summary: We investigate the thermodynamic cost of information erasure in Friedmann--Robertson--Walker cosmology by combining Landauer's principle with the thermodynamics of the apparent horizon. Adopting the apparent-horizon temperature as an effective cosmological temperature, we find that for standard non-phantom expansion, the minimum heat required to erase one bit decreases while the entropy-equivalent information content of the horizon increases. We further compare the Landauer heat with the Misner--Sharp energy and show that, despite their simple thermodynamic relation, they have distinct physical meanings. These results provide a simple connection between information erasure, horizon thermodynamics, and gravitational energy in an expanding universe.

authors.name: Babak Vakili

papers.title: Finite-time quenches across first-, second-, and infinite-order transitions in XXZ spin chains
papers.summary: We investigate how equilibrium quantum phase transitions manifest themselves in small systems driven out of equilibrium by quantum quenches. We consider linear ramps of the anisotropy in spin-1/2 and spin-1 XXZ chains, which host transitions of first, second, and infinite (Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless, BKT) order. We consider system sizes available in current quantum simulators and investigate how the order of the transition, the symmetries, and the ramp duration affect the decomposition of the time-evolved state into the instantaneous eigenbasis. The order of the transition determines the dynamics: across the BKT transition, moderately slow ramps already keep the system close to its ground state, corresponding to an adiabatic evolution, whereas for the second-order Haldane-N\'eel transition a ramp roughly three times slower is required to reach the same regime. Across the first-order transition, since the dynamics conserves the magnetization of the initial state, we observe the formation of ferromagnetic domains, separated by a single domain wall for slow ramps and by multiple walls for faster ones. Interestingly, shortly after the transition, the state evolves as a coherent beating between domain-wall states, a behavior captured by the recently proposed quantum-state texture.

authors.name: Luiz Felipe Santos Dittberner, Luigi Berber, Maria C. O. Aguiar, Krissia Zawadzki, Helena Bragan\c{c}a

papers.title: Quasi-particle sector hybridization and the onset of chaos in spin ladders
papers.summary: How quasiparticle numbers influence the emergence of quantum chaos is a fundamental question in interacting many-body systems. We investigate this interplay in a spin-$1/2$ XXZ ladder, where the strong-rung regime supports an approximate organization of many-body eigenstates into quasi-particle(triplon) number sectors. Using spectral statistics, triplon-based observables, and von Neumann entanglement entropy, we characterize the microscopic hybridization of triplon-number sectors as the leg coupling increases. We find that the crossover toward Gaussian orthogonal ensemble statistics shifts to weaker couplings with increasing system size, whereas the characteristic crossover scale associated with triplon-sector hybridization exhibits a much weaker size dependence. Furthermore, eigenstate-to-eigenstate fluctuations exhibit scaling consistent with the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis even while remnants of the strong-rung structure persist, suggesting that spectral chaos does not necessarily require complete sector hybridization.

authors.name: Arnav Pushkar, Abhik Kumar Saha

papers.title: Asymptotic efficiency of tests for quantum statistical models
papers.summary: In classical statistics, local asymptotic normality provides a general framework for characterizing optimal testing power and constructing asymptotically efficient procedures. Extending this framework to quantum statistical models introduces additional challenges arising from the noncommutativity of observables and the need to optimize over quantum measurements. In this paper, we develop a theory of asymptotic efficiency for quantum hypothesis testing using quantum local asymptotic normality and the asymptotic representation theorem. We establish sharp nuisance-maximin power bounds for one-sided tests and two-sided tests within the unbiased class by reducing the corresponding classical--quantum Gaussian shift experiments to classical testing problems. This reduction is justified through a quantum Hunt--Stein argument that accommodates both commuting and noncommuting Gaussian coordinates. Under suitable asymptotic invariance conditions, the resulting bounds transfer to the original quantum experiments and are attained by scalar symmetric logarithmic derivative tests. We further develop a two-stage adaptive construction that achieves the same local asymptotic power without knowledge of the reference parameter. As an application, we study testing of smooth spectral functionals of quantum states. We compare scalar symmetric logarithmic derivative tests with the weak Schur sampling plug-in test and with optimally weighted linear statistics of its fluctuations. This comparison distinguishes loss from the plug-in weighting from a gap between the best such spectral statistic and the scalar score procedure. We characterize equality of the corresponding variances and illustrate the two gaps through explicit examples.

authors.name: Rathindra Nath Karmakar, Samriddha Lahiry, Koichi Yamagata

papers.title: Live Noise Fingerprints for Quantum Program Analysis
papers.summary: Quantum programs are probabilistic in nature, and noisy execution due to current imperfect hardware further complicates their analysis. In this paper, we study abstract semantics for analysing quantum programs under these conditions. We introduce noise fingerprints, compact descriptions of the observable effects of noise relative to a finite interface of input states and output measurements. We use them to define our abstract domain with respect to the concrete noise-related behaviour. We relate the concrete and abstract domains through a probabilistic Galois connection, extending the Galois-connection framework to distribution-valued interpretations. We study the resulting abstraction in terms of observational soundness, conciseness, efficiency, and ability to adapt to changing noise. We show that polynomial-size interfaces yield exponentially smaller fingerprints than full noise models while preserving the chosen observations, and that fingerprint distance characterises the largest observational discrepancy over the chosen interface. Further, we develop ChanShadow, which reuses noise fingerprints of commonly used short program fragments to analyse noisy execution of whole programs and provides a uniform finite-sample error bound. We construct working examples showing how fingerprints support program analysis. We evaluate fingerprint precision, representation cost, measurement requirements, and behaviour under noise drift. On a synthetic benchmark, fingerprints retain $(99 \pm 1)\%$ of the noise strength information of a full noise model. On simulated noise drift, reusing earlier measurements reduces the number of fresh measurement rounds needed to reach an error tolerance of $0.10$ by a factor of $2.3$ at $95\%$ confidence and by a factor of $27$ under the median-error criterion.

authors.name: Avner Bensoussan, Karine Even-Mendoza, Debalina Banerjee, Elena Chachkarova, Sophie Fortz, Vasileios Klimis, Mohammad Reza Mousavi

papers.title: Fragmentation in Non-Hermitian Many-Body Systems
papers.summary: In non-Hermitian (NH) fermionic chains with spatially random imaginary gauge fields, single-particle eigenstates exhibit erratic NH skin localization with strongly fluctuating, subexponential decay, distinct from both conventional skin accumulation and Anderson localization. At finite filling, Pauli exclusion suppresses macroscopic accumulation and instead leads to fragmentation of the particle density, in sharp contrast to Hermitian disordered systems. Using exact free-fermion methods, we show that the density organizes into disconnected regions of high and low occupancy, forming spatially separated Fermi domains whose number $N_{\mathrm{FS}}$ scales subextensively with system size $L$. Remarkably, fragmentation is not only an equilibrium property but also emerges dynamically in the NH evolution, unlike in Hermitian systems where such structures are not dynamically selected. This behavior admits a Coulomb-gas description in a stochastic potential, establishing a direct link between erratic NH skin localization and real-space fragmentation of many-body states.

authors.name: Stefano Longhi

papers.title: When the Boundary Changes the Bulk: Topological Edge Modes in Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions
papers.summary: For dynamical quantum phase transitions (DQPTs) in open chains it has been noted that the boundary can change the bulk: in time windows bounded by DQPTs, exponentially localized edge modes of the Loschmidt matrix produce a finite change in the intensive return rate. These modes have been attributed to topological properties of the initial and final Hamiltonians. Here we show that it is not the topology of the Hamiltonians but rather that of the non-Hermitian Loschmidt matrix which protects these edge modes. In particular, we show that topological edge modes can exist in class A, where both Hamiltonians are topologically trivial. For classes A, BDI, and AIII we show that these modes are protected by $\mathbb{Z}$ indices of a Toeplitz operator and that K-splitting theorems provide a precise bulk-boundary correspondence. In class D, they are protected instead by a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ index that records whether the quench has flipped the fermion parity at the edge. The bulk invariant for class D can be formulated either as a ratio of the Loschmidt amplitudes for periodic and anti-periodic boundary conditions or as a winding number that counts phase vortices in momentum and time. We discuss examples and provide numerical data for all four topological classes.

authors.name: N. Sedlmayr, J. Sirker

papers.title: A Quantum Metric Approach to Stabilizer Codes
papers.summary: We associate a spectral triple with each stabilizer code in a projective error model arising from a nice error basis and equipped with a length function. The spectral triple records the dimension of the code as well as the minimum code distance. For Pauli stabilizer codes of dimension greater than one with Hamming weight, Latr\'emoli\`ere's dual propinquity provides a pseudometric which allows us to compare codes of different physical and logical dimensions. We show that in the resulting topology, minimum distance of a code is locally constant for qubits and for qudits of dimensions three and five. Thus correction of all errors up to a prescribed weight is a local property in these cases. Moreover, for each prime $p$, we classify the underlying $C^*$-algebras in the metric closure as a subclass of AF algebras, namely those arising as tensor products of $C((\mathbb{Z}_p)^r)$, for $r \in \{0,1,2, \ldots , \infty\}$, with matrix algebras of $p$-power order or the UHF algebra of type $p^\infty$. Every such $C^*$-algebra not isomorphic to $M_{p^k}(\mathbb{C})$ for any $k\geq 1$ occurs as the underlying algebra of a point in the metric boundary. In particular, we obtain the CAR algebra as a metric limit of qubit stabilizer codes.

authors.name: Are Austad, Jonas Eidesen

papers.title: A Universal Algebraic Construction of Hilbert-Space Fragmentation
papers.summary: We present a mechanism for obtaining Hilbert-space fragmentation from arbitrary quantum lattice Hamiltonians acting on finite-dimensional local spaces. We first express the Hamiltonian in an algebraic form using supersymmetry (SUSY) and parasupersymmetry (paraSUSY) generators. Enlarging their representations defines a lifting procedure, which we study in two forms, site-wise and bond-wise lifting. Site-wise lifting introduces immobile zero modes that generate exponentially many invariant sectors while retaining the original dynamics in the fully active sector. We determine the sector structure and establish strong fragmentation for uniform lifts at fixed intermediate zero-mode density. For nearest-neighbor chains, correlation functions reveal restricted propagation and, in the mixed-field example, persistent local memory. Bond-wise lifting produces mobile conserved strings, pair-flip dynamics and fluctuating dimers, and extends to fragmented unitary circuits. Different representations and embeddings realize different fragmentation mechanisms. Some of the fragmented models obtained by this method include lifted permutation and Ising spin chains, a lifted toric code, the \(XXC\) families of spin chains, and fragmented extensions derived from the integrable \(H_{1,11}\) and \(H_{1,3}\) seed densities. The last two models are derived from Hietarinta's classification of constant $4\times 4$ Yang-Baxter solutions.

authors.name: Pramod Padmanabhan, Vladimir Korepin

papers.title: Bright-Dark State Interplay Governs Vibronic Decoherence in Molecular Aggregates
papers.summary: In this study, we establish a spectroscopy-driven framework that connects optically bright vibronic eigenstates to their subsequent decoherence dynamics in excitonic molecular aggregates. Combining the Multiparticle Holstein Formalism with explicit system--bath interactions, we demonstrate that relaxation-induced purity loss is governed by three interconnected factors: (i) the bath spectral window, which determines the accessibility of intra- and interband relaxation pathways; (ii) the local network of dark vibronic states surrounding the optically prepared bright state; and (iii) the energetic placement of the bright state, which controls downhill relaxation. Remarkably, states with different excitation energies exhibit nearly identical purity dynamics when their local relaxation networks are similar. The resulting H--J asymmetry further reveals the importance of energetic directionality. These findings establish a reliable connection between optical spectroscopy, vibronic band structure, and state-selective loss in purity.

authors.name: Sreeja Loho Choudhury, Abhradeep Sarkar, Raja Ghosh

papers.title: Chiral Majorana Charge Kondo Criticality
papers.summary: Unambiguous identification of chiral Majorana edge modes remains challenging because the transport signatures proposed for them can also arise from conventional mechanisms. Here we identify the chiral Majorana charge Kondo (CMCK) critical point as a more discriminating many-body route to detect chiral Majorana edge modes. This criticality arises in a charged island hosting a single chiral Majorana edge mode, where Majorana self-conjugacy locks normal and anomalous tunneling amplitudes, so that each physical lead provides two Kondo screening channels without fine tuning. Ordinary subgap states generically break this locking and drive the system toward conventional charge Kondo (CK) behavior. In the simplest two-terminal geometry, CMCK and conventional CK share the critical conductance $G^*=e^2/2h$, but their leading conductance corrections scale as $T^{1/3}$ and $T$, respectively. Their residual entropies also differ, as do the crossover exponents under gate detuning and contact asymmetry. For $N$ leads, CMCK conductance corrections scale as $T^{1/(N+1)}$, and for $N\geq3$ even the critical conductance differs from that of conventional CK with the same number of leads. These universal signatures are testable using established charge-Kondo measurement techniques.

authors.name: Xiao Xiao

papers.title: Compact Projected Pfaffian States for Rydberg-Blockaded Quantum Spin Systems
papers.summary: We numerically demonstrate that a compact projected Pfaffian ansatz effectively describes the ground state of the nonintegrable PXP model. The variational wave function is obtained by applying separate Gutzwiller and Rydberg-blockade projectors to a general fermionic paired state, and each blockade-allowed configuration has an amplitude given by the Pfaffian of a configuration-selected pairing matrix. The exact blockade-projected product state of a known frustration-free deformation of the PXP model lies within the variational manifold and provides a physically motivated initial state for the variational Monte Carlo optimization toward the ground state of the pure PXP model. For a one-dimensional system of $N$ sites, optimizing all symmetry-allowed pairings in an $O(N)$-parameter wave function yields a near-exact ground state with a normalized energy variance (V-score) of order $10^{-9}$ despite the exponentially large blockade-constrained Hilbert space. On the square lattice, an $O(N)$-parameter wave function with the same amplitude structure yields relative energy errors below $0.2\%$ for clusters accessible to exact diagonalization and produces magnetizations consistent with available benchmarks. These results show that the same projected Pfaffian construction can be applied to blockade-constrained systems in both one and two dimensions.

authors.name: Ryui Kaneko

papers.title: Unstable Periodic Orbit Localization in a Nonlinear System-Environment Model
papers.summary: The role of unstable periodic orbits (UPOs) is investigated in the chaotic dynamics of a nonlinear system-environment model composed of a central two-level system coupled to an environment of two-level systems. Families of UPOs embedded in chaotic regions are identified and their local instability is characterized. Their behavior is examined under variations of the environment size, energy, and system symmetry, allowing the model to serve as a controlled testbed in which the dimensionality and dynamical conditions can be systematically modified. Characteristic UPO-based dynamical quantities are used to assess the influence of these periodic orbits on nearby chaotic trajectories, including occupation of the UPO tube, its persistence at late times, return fidelity enhancement, and recurrence timing. Across the different model variations considered, trajectories initialized close to the UPOs retain statistically detectable spatial and temporal signatures associated with the periodic orbits. These results indicate that unstable periodic orbits can retain a measurable organizing influence on surrounding chaotic trajectories across changes in dimensionality, energy, and system symmetry, giving rise to scar-like dynamical signatures in a simple nonlinear system--environment model.

authors.name: Daniel Martinez-Gil

papers.title: An isolated complex Hadamard matrix with nonzero defect
papers.summary: We exhibit a complex Hadamard matrix of nonzero defect which is isolated among complex Hadamard matrices, up to Hadamard equivalence. This counterexample is realized by a Butson-type Hadamard matrix of size $13$, with entries roots of order $6$ of unity. In the language of commuting squares, this shows that the span condition, previously introduced by the second author as a sufficient condition for isolation, is not a necessary condition for isolation.

authors.name: Shannon Hall, Remus Nicoara

papers.title: Lieb-Robinson Bounds for Electric Quantum Walks
papers.summary: We derive Lieb-Robinson type bounds with optimal propagation velocity for shift-coin and split-step quantum walks in rational electric fields. The velocity decays exponentially fast in the period of the field, showing long intervals of suppressed spreading. The proof rests on bounds for the imaginary part of the analytically continued dispersion relation of the electric walk. We show that the infimal Lieb-Robinson velocity coincides with the asymptotic velocity for these walks, while a nonhomogeneous example demonstrates that the two types of velocity need not agree in general. We also obtain an exponential tail estimate on the probability of a walk to lie outside the effective light cone.

authors.name: Houssam Abdul-Rahman, Christopher Cedzich, G\"unter Stolz

papers.title: Postselection on Halting and Reductions to the Halting Problem
papers.summary: A probabilistic Turing machine is an ordinary Turing machine that may also toss fair coins, with no limit on its running time or memory. If it always halts, it decides only computable problems. Aaronson et al. studied machines that may run forever on some coin tosses, with the answer read only from the runs that halt. Suppose the correct answer must be more than twice as likely as the wrong one. They showed that these machines decide exactly the problems solvable with a fixed list of questions about the halting problem. They asked what happens when the correct answer need only be the more likely one. We show that the machines then decide exactly the problems solvable by asking such questions one after another, each chosen after the earlier answers. We also show that the factor two can be replaced by any fixed factor greater than one. A machine may promise two numbers: a lower bound on its probability of halting, and a lower bound on its probability of being right when it halts. From these two numbers we compute exactly how many questions fixed in advance the machine can replace. The main idea is that probability acts as a budget for how often a computable guess may change its mind. The results extend to oracle machines and to machines nested inside each other. Quantum machines decide the same problems.

authors.name: Saman Farhat, Farzad Didehvar

papers.title: A boson representation of the electronic structure calculation based on the quantum Krylov subspace algorithm
papers.summary: Quantum calculations are expected to broaden the range of strongly correlated phenomena in solids accessible to first-principles calculations. The quantum Krylov diagonalization method, or in a broader sense, the quantum subspace expansion method (QSE) offers an advantage over other variational methods in terms of numerical stability. In this work, we propose a boson representation of electronic systems with the aim of reducing QSE quantum circuit depth, where electron-hole pair bosons serve as the fundamental degrees of freedom. We benchmark the boson representation in comparison with a corresponding fermionic QSE and CCSD for an equidistant and a dimerized configuration of a periodic hydrogen chain \ce{(H2)_n}. Despite the drastic approximation we reveal the boson QSE scheme provides practically useful accuracy in the ground state energy. Our results support its applicability to realistic quasi-two- and three-dimensional electronic systems.

authors.name: Hiroki Katow, Hisao Nakamura

papers.title: Localization transition in a spin chain with an exact Fock-space tree
papers.summary: Many-body localization is often pictured as Anderson localization on the graph of many-body configurations. Strongly correlated disorder and a dense net of loops, however, make this graph hard to analyze. We introduce a local disordered spin-1 chain in which a single domain wall explores an exact binary tree of configurations. Random fields create strongly correlated disorder on this tree, as in generic interacting systems, while the absence of loops keeps the problem tractable. We rigorously bound the spreading of the domain wall at strong disorder, and efficient numerics on exponentially large trees indicate a localization transition at finite disorder strength.

authors.name: Bernhard Jobst, Simone Warzel, Alexander Altland, Frank Pollmann

papers.title: Peak state transfer in trees and the cost of distance
papers.summary: There is peak state transfer between vertices $u$ and $v$ in a graph $G$ if there exists a time $t$ for which $|(\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm i t M})_{u,v}|$ saturates the triangle inequality imposed by its spectral decomposition and $M$ is either the adjacency or Laplacian matrix. We show that peak state transfer at distance $d$ requires $\frac{d^3}{24}(1 + o(1))$ edges in the adjacency case, $\Omega(d^2)$ edges in the Laplacian case, and that the leading coefficient in the former is tight. We find a family of graphs with Laplacian peak state transfer at distance $d$ and $\Theta(d^5)$ edges, showing that peak state transfer is achievable in a polynomial graph size. In contrast, Laplacian perfect state transfer costs at least $\Omega(2^{d/2})$ edges when the distance partition of vertices around one vertex is almost equitable. Finally, we show that Laplacian peak state transfer in trees requires $\Omega(d!)$ edges, and we characterize all trees of diameter $\leq 4$ admitting Laplacian peak state transfer, thus answering a pair of questions posed by Coutinho, Guo, and Schmeits.

authors.name: Andrew Osborne, Andrew A. Houck

papers.title: Double quantum dots as dynamical impurities in one-dimensional transport
papers.summary: We study single-electron scattering in a tight-binding chain capacitively coupled to double quantum dots, which act as dynamical two-level-system impurities with electrically tunable level splittings. For a single impurity, we solve the scattering problem exactly and show Feshbach-like perfect elastic reflection, whose resonant condition distinguishes the initial two-level state. For several impurities in a strongly reflecting chain, transmission peaks at an intermediate mean level splitting. At small splittings, energy exchange with the impurities can weaken constructive interference between backscattered paths, consistent with the initial rise in transmission. As excitation channels close, virtual transitions can enhance reflection and drive transmission below its purely elastic value $T_0$. At larger splittings, these virtual processes weaken and transmission approaches $T_0$. We discuss how gate-controlled transmission measurements in quantum-dot arrays could test these predictions.

authors.name: Yang-Zhi Chou

papers.title: Tensor Network Based HOBO Solver
papers.summary: In the field of quantum computing, combinatorial optimization problems are typically addressed using QUBO (Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization) solvers. However, these solvers are often insufficient for tackling higher-order problems. In this paper, we introduce a novel and efficient solver designed specifically for HOBO (Higher-Order Binary Optimization) problem settings. Our approach leverages advanced techniques to effectively manage the complexity and computational demands associated with high-dimensional optimization tasks. The proposed solver is a promising tool with significant potential for future extensions in terms of formulation. This solver holds promising potential for a wide range of applications in quantum computing.

authors.name: Yuichiro Minato

papers.title: Two-Step QAOA: Enhancing Quantum Optimization by Decomposing K-hot Constraints in QUBO Formulations
papers.summary: The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) has shown promise in solving combinatorial optimization problems by leveraging quantum computational power. We propose a simple approach, the Two-Step QAOA, which aims to improve the effectiveness of QAOA by decomposing problems with k-hot encoding QUBO (Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization) formulations. By identifying and separating the problem into two stages, we transform soft constraints into hard constraints, simplifying the generation of initial conditions and enabling more efficient optimization. The method is particularly beneficial for tackling complex societal problems that often involve intricate constraint structures.

authors.name: Yuichiro Minato

papers.title: Near-Optimal Techniques for Distributed Entanglement Generation and Purification
papers.summary: We develop a purification-aware optimization framework for distributing high-fidelity entangled states over quantum networks. In repeater-based architectures, the framework jointly selects entanglement swapping, fusion or graph-state growth, and purification operations to maximize generation rate under a fidelity threshold. Different purification models can be incorporated through their fidelity-update, success-probability, and latency rules. We introduce purification-augmented generation trees and dynamic programming (DP) algorithms for entangled-pair (EP) distribution. Hypergraph-flow linear programming (LP) formulations support level-based structures and concurrent generation across multiple trees and demands. We extend the framework to GHZ states and arbitrary graph states constructed from remote EP resources, introduce graph-state construction primitives, and derive closed-form fidelity-vector updates for GHZ fusion and purification and graph-state growth and purification. We provide optimal formulations under the adopted models, discretization, and purification bounds, together with efficient DP and LP heuristics. We bound fidelity- and rate-discretization errors and establish convergence for fixed constructions under stated regularity conditions. NetSquid simulations of EP generation using our LP approach show an average 160% increase in generation rate over the compared prior approaches, with gains up to 330% in some scenarios. GHZ and graph-state simulations demonstrate the heuristics' effectiveness in balancing generation rate, output fidelity, and computational overhead.

authors.name: Yukun Yang, Xiaojie Fan, C. R. Ramakrishnan, Himanshu Gupta

papers.title: Quantum-to-classical transition and the emergence of trajectory level Darwinism with measurements distributed in time: a path integral approach
papers.summary: We present a path-integral formulation of the emergence of classical dynamics that incorporates continuous measurements. Each Feynman path picks up a random phase due to measurements, and we give conditions under which the dominant contribution comes from the vicinity of the classical paths. This information proliferates across the environment, as in quantum Darwinism, via scattering of probes by the system. The scattering which decoheres a trajectory also heats it. This bounds how redundantly an individual classical trajectory can be recorded before back-action turns it into Brownian motion.

authors.name: Harsh Arora, Bishal Kumar Das, Baladitya Suri, Vaibhav Madhok

papers.title: Graph-Cover-based Characterization of the Bethe Partition Function of Double-Edge Factor Graphs
papers.summary: For standard factor graphs (S-FGs), whose local functions are nonnegative-real valued, a popular approximation of the partition function is given by the Bethe approximation, which is also known as the Bethe partition function. Vontobel gave a combinatorial characterization of the Bethe partition function with the help of graph covers. The proof of this characterization heavily relied on the method of types. In this paper, we study double-edge factor graphs (DE-FGs), whose local functions are complex valued and satisfy certain positive-semidefinite constraints. DE-FGs and their partition functions are particularly relevant to quantum information processing. Approximating the partition function of a DE-FG is more difficult than approximating the partition function of an S-FG because the DE-FG partition function is a sum of complex values rather than nonnegative-real values. We develop a Bethe approximation of the partition function of a DE-FG based on sum-product-algorithm (SPA) fixed points. However, one cannot directly apply the method of types to prove a similar graph-cover-based combinatorial characterization of the Bethe partition function as in the case of S-FGs. Despite this, we establish such a combinatorial characterization for a class of DE-FGs that satisfy an easily checkable condition. Towards proving this characterization, we apply a suitable loop-calculus transform (LCT) to DE-FGs. Originally, the LCT was introduced by Chertkov and Chernyak as a special linear transform for S-FGs and later extended by Mori. Our proposed LCT is applicable to both S-FGs and DE-FGs and generalizes prior versions by handling zero-valued SPA fixed-point message components, which are common in DE-FGs. Supported by numerical results, we conjecture that the graph-cover-based combinatorial characterization of the Bethe partition function holds more broadly for DE-FGs.

authors.name: Yuwen Huang, Pascal O. Vontobel

papers.title: Online Quantum State Tomography via Stochastic Gradient Descent
papers.summary: We study online quantum state tomography (QST), where the matrix representation of an unknown quantum state is reconstructed by sequentially measuring the unknown states with respect to a batch of observables and updating the state estimate using only the measurement outcomes and observable information from the current round. Motivated by recent advances in non-convex optimization algorithms for solving low-rank QST, we propose non-convex mini-batch stochastic gradient descent (SGD) algorithms to solve online QST, which leverage the low-rank structure of the unknown quantum state and are well-suited for practical applications. Our main technical contribution is a rigorous convergence analysis of these algorithms. With proper initialization, we demonstrate that the squared error contracts locally in conditional expectation up to a finite-shot noise floor, and the iterates converge geometrically to this floor with high probability. Our algorithms achieve nearly optimal sample complexity up to condition-number and logarithmic factors, while remaining highly memory-efficient. In particular, their time complexities are better than the state-of-the-art non-convex QST algorithms, in terms of the rank and the logarithm of the dimension of the unknown quantum state.

authors.name: Jian-Feng Cai, Yuling Jiao, Yinan Li, Xiliang Lu, Jerry Zhijian Yang, Juntao You

papers.title: Temporal Complexity Hierarchies in Solvable Quantum Many-Body Dynamics
papers.summary: The influence matrix (IM) provides a powerful framework for characterizing nonequilibrium quantum many-body dynamics by encoding multitime correlations into tensor-network states. Understanding how its computational complexity relates to underlying dynamics is crucial for both theoretical insight and practical utility yet remains largely unexplored despite a few case studies. Here, we address this question for a family of brickwork quantum circuits ranging from integrable to chaotic regimes. Using tools from geometric group theory, we identify three qualitatively distinct scalings of temporal entanglement entropy, establishing a hierarchy of computational resources required for accurate tensor-network representations of the IM for these models. We further analyze the memory structure of the IM and distinguish between classical and quantum temporal correlations. In particular, for certain examples, we identify effectively classical IMs that admit an efficient Monte Carlo algorithm for computing multitime correlations. In more generic settings without an explicit classical description of the IM, we introduce an operational measure of quantum memory with an experimental protocol, and discuss examples exhibiting long-time genuinely quantum correlations. Our results establish a new connection between quantum many-body dynamics and group theory, providing fresh insights into the complexity of the IM and its intricate connection to the physical characteristics of the dynamics.

authors.name: He-Ran Wang, Ilya Vilkoviskiy, Dmitry A. Abanin

papers.title: Harmonic Control of Dynamical Freezing in Programmable Rydberg Atom Arrays
papers.summary: Periodic driving enables the engineering of complex quantum matter, yet in interacting systems it generically leads to energy absorption, which limits the lifetime of the engineered states. To address this challenge, dynamical freezing has been proposed as a mechanism for stabilizing non-equilibrium states over parametrically long timescales. While theory predicts robust freezing under simplifying assumptions, realistic platforms inevitably include additional interaction processes that alter its stability. Here, we report the experimental observation of dynamical freezing in programmable Rydberg atom arrays of up to 100 atoms in one and two dimensions. We find that while single-frequency driving produces pronounced suppression of excitation dynamics, the freezing behavior is restricted to a narrow parameter regime due to interaction-induced heating channels present in realistic simulators. Using a perturbative Floquet analysis of the fully interacting atomic system, we identify the dominant microscopic heating processes responsible for this destabilization. Leveraging this understanding, we design a dual-parameter modulation of detuning and Rabi frequency that coherently suppresses these absorption pathways and substantially broadens the freezing regime, making it also robust across different geometries. Our results reveal how heating processes shape the stability of dynamical freezing in interacting Floquet systems and demonstrates a route to control driven many-body dynamics in realistic experimental platforms.

authors.name: Madhumita Sarkar, Ben Zindorf, Bhaskar Mukherjee, Sougato Bose, Roopayan Ghosh

papers.title: Efficient Hamiltonian-aware Quantum Natural Gradient Descent for Variational Quantum Eigensolvers
papers.summary: The Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) is one of the most promising algorithms for current quantum devices. It employs a classical optimizer to iteratively update the parameters of a variational quantum circuit in order to search for the ground state of a given Hamiltonian. The efficacy of VQEs largely depends on the optimizer employed. Recent studies suggest that Quantum Natural Gradient Descent (QNG) can achieve faster convergence speed than vanilla gradient descent (VG), but at the cost of additional quantum resources to estimate the Fubini-Study metric tensor in each optimization step. The Fubini-Study metric tensor used in QNG is related to the entire quantum state space and does not incorporate information about the target Hamiltonian. To take advantage of the structure of the Hamiltonian and address the limitation of additional computational cost in QNG, we propose Hamiltonian-aware Quantum Natural Gradient Descent (H-QNG). In H-QNG, we propose to use the Riemannian pullback metric induced from the lower-dimensional subspace spanned by the Hamiltonian terms onto the parameter space. We show that H-QNG inherits the desirable features of both approaches: the low quantum computational cost of VG and the reparameterization-invariance of QNG. We also validate its performance through numerical experiments on molecular Hamiltonians, showing that H-QNG achieves faster convergence to lower energy while requiring fewer quantum computational resources.

authors.name: Chenyu Shi, Hao Wang

papers.title: Observation of an anomaly in the statistics of Kibble-Zurek defects
papers.summary: The Kibble-Zurek mechanism quantifies defect formation during finite-rate passage across a continuous phase transition, providing key insights into universality in quantum many-body systems. We explore counting statistics of defects in finite-rate ramp experiments on long 1D Rydberg atom chains. The experiments reveal an anomaly in the defect number distribution at long ramp times, challenging the hypothesis of defect formation through independent domain mergers. Numerical simulations reproduce the anomaly and support an interpretation in terms of post-critical coarsening during the ramp, while prepare-and-hold experiments reveal no subsequent secular growth of the measured correlations. Our results show the limits of classical or integrable system descriptions of Kibble-Zurek defect formation for interacting quantum systems.

authors.name: Jan Balewski, Alexey Khudorozhkov, Siva Darbha, Omar A. Ashour, Fangli Liu, Ermal Rrapaj, Sheng-Tao Wang, Pedro L. S. Lopes, Katherine Klymko, Milan Kornja\v{c}a, Daan Camps

papers.title: Noise-Induced Thermalization in Quantum Systems
papers.summary: In the current Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum era, noise is widely regarded as the primary obstacle to achieving fault-tolerant quantum computation. However, certain stages of the quantum computing pipeline can, in fact, benefit from this noise. In this work, we exploit the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis to show that noise generically accelerates a fundamental task in quantum computing -- the preparation of Gibbs states. We demonstrate this behavior using classical and quantum simulations with Haar-random and phase-flip noise, respectively, on a spin-1/2 chain with a local Hamiltonian. Our non-integrable model sees ~3.5x faster thermalization in the presence of noise, while our integrable model, which would not otherwise thermalize, reaches a thermal state due to noise. Since certifying a local Gibbs state is relatively easy on a quantum computer, our approach provides a new practical solution to a key problem in quantum computing. More broadly, these results establish a new paradigm in which noise can be harnessed on quantum computers, enabling practical advantages before the years of fault-tolerance.

authors.name: Sameer Dambal, Yu Zhang, Eric R Bittner, Pavan Hosur

papers.title: On-Demand Millisecond Storage of Spectrotemporal Multimode Telecom Photons
papers.summary: The realization of scalable quantum networks for distribution of entanglement over long distances hinges on quantum repeaters. To outperform the exponential transmission loss in optical fibers, quantum repeaters must employ multiplexing schemes in the temporal, spectral, or spatial domain. The performance of such a multiplexed scheme is contingent on efficient quantum memories offering both extended storage times and large multimode capacities. Towards this goal, we experimentally demonstrate a memory platform operating at telecom wavelength using an Er$^{3+}$:Y$_{2}$SiO$_{5}$ crystal. We record on-demand storage and recall of weak coherent pulses for up to $1$ ms, exceeding by an order of magnitude that of previously reported demonstrations based on Er$^{3+}$. The memory exhibits an efficiency of 10.36 % at 300 $\mu$s storage time with a signal-to-noise ratio of $10.9$, mainly limited by spontaneous emission noise. We also store two spectral modes representing a frequency-bin encoding and retrieve the state with an overlap of 81.8 %. Furthermore, we demonstrate multimode capacity by simultaneously storing 20 temporal and 3 spectral modes with on-demand and selective recall capabilities, serving as a promising step toward a scalable quantum repeater architecture.

authors.name: Anuj Sethia, Nasser Gohari Kamel, Daniel Oblak

papers.title: Correcting quantum errors one gradient step at a time
papers.summary: Probabilistic approximate quantum error correction (PAQEC) lets a recovery fail with some probability, in exchange for higher fidelity when it succeeds. Prior PAQEC code searches keep the codewords orthonormal with penalty terms and tune the code without its best recovery. We propose a gradient method with three new parts. First, the codewords move on the complex Stiefel manifold, so they are orthonormal at every step without penalties. Second, every code is trained against its best recovery, which we solve for at each step rather than learn. Third, a fast Petz recovery that we can differentiate even for symmetric codes gets the search close, and the exact semidefinite program finishes it. We train a single five-qubit code over generalized amplitude damping noise. At weak noise ($\gamma = 0.1$, $p = 0.05$) and equal success probability, it has $23$ times lower infidelity than the permutation-invariant code of prior work, and $9$ times lower than that work's numerically optimized code. At equal fidelity it succeeds $91\%$ of the time, against $76\%$ for the permutation-invariant code.

authors.name: Manav Seksaria, Anil Prabhakar

papers.title: Simulation of noisy quantum circuits using frame representations
papers.summary: One of the core research questions in the theory of quantum computing is to find out to what precise extent the classical simulation of a noisy quantum circuits is possible and where potential quantum advantages can set in. In this work, we introduce a unified framework for the classical simulation of quantum circuits based on frame theory, encompassing and generalizing a broad class of existing simulation strategies. Within this framework, the computational cost of a simulation algorithm is determined by the one-norm of an associated quasi-probability distribution, providing a common quantitative measure across different simulation approaches. This enables a comprehensive perspective on common methods for the simulation of noisy circuits based on different quantum resources, such as entanglement or non-stabilizerness. It further provides a clear scheme for generating novel classical simulation algorithms. Indeed, by exploring different choices of frames within this formalism and resorting to tools of convex optimization, we are able not only to obtain new insights and improved bounds for existing methods -- such as stabilizer state simulation or Pauli back-propagation -- but also to discover a new approach with an improved performance based on a generalization of the Pauli frame. We, thereby, show that classical simulation techniques can directly benefit from a perspective -- that of frames -- that goes beyond the traditional classification of quantum resources.

authors.name: Janek Denzler, Jose Carrasco, Jens Eisert, Tommaso Guaita

papers.title: Elementary Quantum Gates from Lie Group Embeddings in $U(2^n)$: Spectral Geometry and Intrinsic Factorization Lengths
papers.summary:
We study intrinsic factorizations of quantum gates using determinant-one unitaries supported on arbitrary two-dimensional subspaces of $\C^N$, where $N=2^n$. For $U\in U(N)$ write $r=\operatorname{rank}(U-I)$. When $r\ge2$, we characterize all factors that lower the active rank by two through traceless compressions of the Cayley transform on $\Ran(U-I)$. For the ordered active eigenangles $\vartheta_j\in(0,2\pi)$, existence is equivalent to $\vartheta_1+\vartheta_2\le2\pi\le\vartheta_{r-1}+\vartheta_r$. For $U\in SU(N)$, combining this construction with eigenangle merging realizes the classical reflection-length formula in two-level form: $\ell^{SU}(U)=\max\{
u(U),r-
u(U)\}$, where $
u(U)$ is the positive eigenangle sum divided by $2\pi$. On the full-rank open set, the age indexes $N-1$ connected components with constant intrinsic length. We place these factorizations within the spectral description of the dictionaries formed by faithful $SU(2)$ and $U(2)$ embeddings. For $n\ge2$, these dictionaries are Haar-null of Hausdorff dimensions $N^2-N+1$ and $N^2-N+2$; the former is compact and the latter dense. Distances to compact sectors reduce to eigenvalue matching. Further results concern ambient minimality of embedded geodesics and a first-order sharp spectral bound on coherence production.

authors.name: Antonio Falco, Daniela Falco-Pomares, Hermann G. Matthies

papers.title: Hamiltonian Decoded Quantum Interferometry for General Pauli Hamiltonians
papers.summary: We study Hamiltonian Decoded Quantum Interferometry (HDQI) for general Pauli Hamiltonians $H = \sum_i c_i P_i$ on an $n$-qubit system, where $c_i \in \mathbb{R}$ and the $P_i$ are Pauli operators. Given access to a suitable decoding oracle, we construct efficient quantum algorithms that prepare the state $\rho_{\mathcal P}(H) = \frac{\mathcal P^2(H)}{\text{Tr}[\mathcal P^2(H)]}$ for any univariate polynomial $\mathcal P(x)$, which in turn approximates the Gibbs state of $H$ for appropriate choices of $\mathcal P$. The central technical ingredient is a matrix product state (MPS) representation of the reference state, which enables handling the asymmetric coefficient structure that arises for general real coefficients. Our results substantially extend the scope of HDQI beyond stabilizer-like Hamiltonians, providing a unified method for Gibbs state preparation and Hamiltonian optimization across a broad class of physically and computationally relevant quantum systems.

authors.name: Kaifeng Bu, Weichen Gu, Xiang Li

papers.title: Multivariate Multicycle Codes for Complete Single-Shot Decoding
papers.summary: We introduce multivariate multicycle (MM) codes, a Koszul-complex formulation of abelian multicycle (AMC) codes, which are multidimensional scalar lifted-product codes over a finite abelian group algebra, that unifies bivariate bicycle, multivariate bicycle, abelian two-block group algebra, generalized bicycle, trivariate tricycle, and toric codes. MM codes are Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) codes defined from length-$(t+1)$ chain complexes, and for $t\geq4$ they possess metachecks for both types of checks, which can be used for single-shot decoding. We offer a framework that facilitates the construction of long-length chain complexes through the use of the Koszul complex. In particular, obtaining explicit boundary maps (parity check and metacheck matrices) is particularly straightforward in our approach. We also determine when an MM code encodes logical qubits, count the independent check relations not generated by its metachecks, and show that middle-degree codes with even $t$ have equal $X$ and $Z$ distances. This simple but very general parameterization of codes permitted us to efficiently perform a numerical search, where we identify several MM code candidates with high rates and high code distances. Examples of new codes with parameters $[[n,k,d]]$ include $[[96,12,8]]$, $[[144,12,12]]$, $[[486,24,12]]$, $[[630,70,9]]$, and $[[648,60,9]]$. For selected codes, we report confinement profiles and study single-shot and few-shot decoding under phenomenological and circuit-level noise. Our codes also include explicit collapsed 5D through 9D instances, and our 5D instances have check weights lower than those of recent small instances of quantum Tanner codes.

authors.name: Feroz Ahmed Mian, Owen Gwilliam, Stefan Krastanov

papers.title: Unified $(q,s)$-concurrence: a two-parameter family of bipartite entanglement measures
papers.summary: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental resource in quantum information processing, yet its quantitative characterization remains challenging, especially for mixed states. In this work, we introduce a two-parameter family of entanglement measures, referred to as the unified $(q,s)$-concurrence, which generalizes both the standard concurrence and the recently proposed $q$-concurrence. This measure is inspired by the unified entropy and provides a flexible framework for quantifying bipartite entanglement. By combining the positive partial transposition and realignment criteria, we derive an analytical lower bound for this measure for arbitrary bipartite mixed states, revealing a connection to strong separability criteria. Explicit expressions are obtained for the unified $(q,s)$-concurrence in the cases of isotropic and Werner states under the constraint $q>1$ and $qs\geq 1$. Furthermore, we explore the monogamy properties of the unified $(q,s)$-concurrence for $q\geq 2$, $0\leq s\leq 1$ and $1\leq qs\leq 3$, and establish an entanglement polygon inequality for any multipartite qudit system when $q\geq 1$ and $qs\geq 1$. Our results provide a unified and versatile tool for entanglement quantification, with potential applications in quantum communication and multipartite entanglement theory.

authors.name: Chen-Ming Bai, Yu Luo

papers.title: Topological initial state independence in Boundary Time Crystals
papers.summary: Boundary time crystals (BTCs) break time-translation symmetry and exhibit long-lived, robust oscillations insensitive to initial conditions. We show that collective spin BTCs can admit emergent topological winding numbers in operator space. Expanding the density operator in a spherical tensor basis, we map the Lindblad dynamics onto an effective local hopping problem, where collective degrees of freedom label sites of an emergent operator space lattice. Whenever the emergent winding number is non-zero, topological obstructions prevent the localization of operator modes on the lattice and instead enforce their delocalization across operator space. This delocalization enables non-unital sourcing from the identity sector to propagate across operator space and continuously feed the observable sector in an initial state independent manner, thereby generating robust oscillatory responses in the time crystal phase. Our results frame BTC dynamics as a form of topologically constrained operator space transport and suggest a close connection to non-Hermitian skin effects.

authors.name: Dominik Nemeth, Ahsan Nazir, Alessandro Principi, Robert-Jan Slager

papers.title: Digital Quantum Simulation of the Holstein-Primakoff Transformation on Noisy Qubits
papers.summary: Quantum simulation of many-body systems offers a powerful approach to exploring collective quantum dynamics beyond classical computational reach. Although spin and fermionic models have been extensively simulated on digital quantum computers, the simulation of bosonic systems on programmable quantum processors is often hindered by the intrinsically large Hilbert space of bosonic modes. In this work, we study the digital quantum simulation of bosonic modes using the Holstein-Primakoff (HP) transformation and implement this protocol on a cloud-based superconducting quantum processor. Representative bosonic dynamics, including the driven harmonic oscillator, bosonic squeezing, and the Jaynes-Cummings (JC) model, are simulated on quantum hardware. Using data obtained from the quantum simulations, we systematically examine the interplay between algorithmic and hardware-induced errors to identify optimal simulation parameters. The dominant algorithmic errors arise from the finite number of qubits used in the HP mapping and the finite number of Trotter steps in the time evolution, while hardware errors mainly originate from entangling-gate infidelity, decoherence, and readout errors. We demonstrate two-excitation JC dynamics and squeezed-state generation involving qubit-qubit interactions under the HP transformation, extending the simulations beyond the simple single-excitation regime. Furthermore, we show that quantum error mitigation substantially improves the fidelity of the quantum simulations on current hardware. Our results demonstrate the feasibility and limitations of HP-based digital simulation of bosonic degrees of freedom on current quantum processors and provide a framework that can be extended to more complex spin-boson and multimode cavity models.

authors.name: Kelvin Yip, Alessandro Monteros, Sahel Ashhab, Lin Tian

papers.title: Thermodynamics of Coupled Transport: Quantum Dots as a Model System
papers.summary: This review presents a thermodynamic perspective on quantum coupled transport processes in nanoscale systems. Our analysis is formulated within the framework of the entropy production rate, the central quantity governing non-equilibrium processes and expressed through conjugate force-flux pairs. Although thermodynamic laws are universal across classical and quantum domains, the discussion is developed within a microscopic open quantum system framework, focusing on quantum dots (QDs) coupled to electronic reservoirs.
