We first examine elementary single transport processes and highlight their strong thermodynamic constraints in the near-equilibrium regime. This motivates the study of coupled transport, where multiple force-flux pairs coexist and interact, leading to richer thermodynamic behaviour. Using entropy production as the guiding principle, we analyse coupled energy and particle transport in a minimal two-terminal single-QD setup and show how conventional thermoelectric phenomena, including Seebeck and Peltier effects as well as thermoelectric heat engines and refrigerators, naturally emerge as thermodynamic cross-effects. We then extend the framework to a three-terminal coupled quantum dot (CQD) geometry, which provides a versatile platform for studying coupled transport and reduces, under suitable constraints, to the well-known S\'anchez-B\"uttiker configuration. Beyond standard cross-effects, we discuss the phenomenon of inverse currents in coupled transport (ICC), where a current flows against mutually parallel thermodynamic forces without violating the second law. We show that ICC requires breaking the symmetry between energy and particle transport and identify the conditions for its realization in coupled quantum-dot systems with attractive interdot interactions.

authors.name: Shuvadip Ghosh, Sounak Bandyopadhyay, Arnab Ghosh

papers.title: Connection between the contextuality breaking and incompatibility breaking qubit channels
papers.summary: Contextuality and measurement incompatibility are two fundamental aspects of nonclassicality, and their manifestations in observed quantum correlations are often deeply interconnected. Recently, measurement incompatibility has been studied in connection with nonlocality, particularly in terms of their robustness under various quantum channels. This line of investigation helps to establish a connection between the channels that break nonlocality and those that break incompatibility. In this study, we focus on an asymmetric bipartite Bell scenario involving three and four inputs on Alice's and Bob's sides, respectively, with each of these inputs having dichotomous outcomes. Under the assumption of locality, the observed statistics in this asymmetric scenario obey the elegant Bell inequality (EBI). Here, we use a different version of the EBI that relies on the assumption of preparation noncontextuality. By taking the violation of this noncontextual version of EBI as a witness of preparation contextuality we establish a connection between the channels that break contextuality and the channels that break triplewise measurement incompatibility. Our results suggest that any channel which breaks EBI contextuality will also break Clauser Horne Shimony Holt contextuality; however, the reverse does not hold. We also show that a depolarizing channel that breaks N wise incompatibility can also break a certain form of contextuality, witnessed by a generalized inequality involving N measurements on one wing of a bipartite Bell scenario.

authors.name: Swati Kumari, Sumit Mukherjee, R. Prabhu

papers.title: Information-theoretic bound on thermodynamic efficiency and the generalized Carnot theorem
papers.summary: We derive a bound on the efficiency of thermal engines that can be sharper than Carnot's limit. It is a function of statistical correlations between the engine internal state and Hamiltonian, can be saturated even in finite-time cycles, and applies to both classical and quantum engines. Specifically, the bound establishes the exact maximal efficiency of engines operating with multiple baths, tightening the upper limit set by Carnot's theorem. Then, we show that an engine made of a quantum dot coupled with fermionic baths can achieve the bound, even when operating beyond the quasistatic regime. The bound relates thermodynamic efficiency to statistical correlations of the working medium and identifies conditions for its saturation in classical and quantum cycles.

authors.name: Anna Gabetti, Fabrizio Dolcini, Davide Girolami

papers.title: Stabilization of finite-energy grid states of a quantum harmonic oscillator by reservoir engineering with two dissipation channels
papers.summary: We propose and analyze an experimentally accessible Lindblad master equation for a quantum harmonic oscillator, simplifying a previous proposal to alleviate implementation constraints. It approximately stabilizes periodic grid states introduced in 2001 by Gottesman, Kitaev and Preskill (GKP), with applications for quantum error correction and quantum metrology. We obtain explicit estimates for the energy of the solutions of the Lindblad master equation. We estimate the convergence rate to the codespace when stabilizing a GKP qubit, and numerically study the effect of noise. We then present simulations illustrating how a modification of parameters allows preparing states of metrological interest in steady-state.

authors.name: R\'emi Robin, Pierre Rouchon, Lev-Arcady Sellem

papers.title: AI-Enabled Qubit Loss Detection and Replenishment Strategy for Atom Array Quantum Computing
papers.summary: Qubit loss is a major source of error in atom-array quantum computing and invalidates the algebraic structure of the standard stabilizer formalism for quantum error-correcting codes. On the one hand, it complicates decoding; on the other hand, it introduces tochastic flicker patterns in stabilizers as a hallmark of qubit loss. Here, we develop an artificial-intelligence-enabled decoder based on a spatiotemporal graph neural network (STGNN) architecture to extract spatial and temporal correlations from syndrome histories. Our decoder performs a dual-head task, simultaneously correcting standard Pauli errors and identifying the locations of qubit loss. Our decoder achieves significantly higher logical accuracy than both the traditional minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) algorithm and even delayed-erasure MWPM decoders that use qubit-loss information from the final round as input. Furthermore, we integrate the decoder into a sliding-window framework for dynamic qubit replenishment. We emphasize that our approach does not involve any additional physical measurements beyond stabilizer measurements, and detects qubit loss and determines its replacement strategy through a purely software-based AI policy. We demonstrate that our approach bounds the accumulation of lost qubits and fully restores the fault-tolerant scaling behavior. For realistic near-term error rates, this work provides a robust and scalable framework for correcting qubit-loss errors, paving the way for more efficient fault-tolerant quantum computation.

authors.name: Yuqing Wang, Xiaotian Nie, Jiale Dai, Zhongyi Ni, Tao Zhang, Hui Zhai, Linghui Chen

papers.title: Thermalization Regimes in a Chaotic Tavis-Cummings Model
papers.summary: This work investigates the emergent thermalization regimes in a chaotic Tavis-Cummings (TC) model and their implications in quantum spectroscopy. While the TC model is a cornerstone of cavity quantum electrodynamics, traditional treatments often overlook many-body effects that arise in the thermodynamic limit. We utilize the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis to demonstrate that a non-integrable excitonic Hamiltonian within the material manifold drives local thermalization. By tuning the polariton splitting $g$, we observe two dynamical regimes: a thermalizing regime at low interactions driven by quantum chaos and ergodicity, and a non-thermalizing regime at high interactions where strong coupling suppresses ergodicity. We further show that these regimes have direct implications on output photon statistics, specifically influencing the correlation times $\tau_c$ of the cavity population and the second-order correlation function $g^{(2)}(t+\tau)$. We propose that entangled-biphoton spectroscopy serves as an ideal experimental platform to probe these effects and to allow the characterization of the underlying many-body exciton-coupling disorder $\sigma$ through coincidence measurements of the output. Taken together, these results exploit a naturally occurring many-body phenomenon to bridge theoretical predictions with experimental observables.

authors.name: Sameer Dambal, Eric R. Bittner

papers.title: Multirate characterization of relaxation mechanisms for two nonequivalent nuclear spins 1/2 in a liquid using maximally entangled pseudo-pure quantum states
papers.summary: Multirate characterization of spin responses in nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) is a promising approach to fingerprinting complex molecules in the presence of multiple relaxation mechanisms. Here we present experimental and theoretical investigations simultaneously accessing 8 relaxation rates describing the density matrix of two adjacent non-equivalent nuclear spins 1/2 (1H and 13C) belonging to a molecule in a liquid. The selected nuclear pair is stable with respect to chemical exchange. Some of the rates are obtained from conventional measurements of inversion recovery and nuclear Overhauser effect, while other, less conventional ones, are extracted from the relaxation initialized by the maximally entangled pseudo-pure Bell states (Bell PPSs) of the spin pair. The Bell PPSs are created using a hereby introduced method based on a detuned Hartmann-Hahn double resonance condition. Microscopic theory behind the measured relaxation rates is presented, and its consistency is demonstrated by several parameter-free tests. In particular, it is shown both theoretically and experimentally, that the eigenmodes of the off-diagonal relaxation of the two-spin density matrix can be selectively initialized using Bell PPSs. Our multirate analysis suggests that the measured off-diagonal relaxation is partly due to an unconventional mechanism arising from very weak J-couplings of the spin pair with fluctuating distant nuclear spins. Furthermore, we identify a dimensionless ratio of diagonal relaxation rates, which is determined exclusively by intra-pair magnetic dipolar interaction and hence possesses a universal value for a broad class of nuclear spin pairs. This value is consistent with both our experiments and other experiments reported in the literature.

authors.name: Georgiy Baroncha, Alexander Perepukhov, Boris V. Fine

papers.title: Classifying Informative Subsets in Qudit Encrypted Cloning via Congruence Systems
papers.summary: Encrypted cloning offers a means of introducing redundancy into quantum storage while respecting the no-cloning theorem: an unknown state is encoded into multiple signal-noise pairs, and only authorized subsets can recover the original information. However, the leakage properties of unauthorized subsets, particularly for higher-dimensional systems (qudits), have remained unexplored. In this work, we systematically classify the informative subsets of the storage register in the qudit encrypted-cloning protocol. We focus on unauthorized subsets of size $n$ that contain exactly one qudit from each signal-noise pair. We show that the presence or absence of information leakage is determined by the solution set of a system of congruences whose coefficients depend on the dimension $d$ and on the numbers of signal and noise qudits in the subset. The reduced state is completely uninformative if and only if the congruence system admits only the trivial solution; otherwise, it retains a residual dependence on the input state through specific generalized Pauli operators. Low-dimensional examples ($n=1,2,3$) are worked out explicitly, and the complete classification is expressed in terms of a greatest-common-divisor condition. Our results extend the parity-based classification known for qubits ($d=2$) to arbitrary finite dimensions, revealing a dimension-dependent boundary of confidentiality in encrypted cloning. Finally, the modified protocol makes the joint quantum--classical state of every unauthorized subset independent of the input. For the aligned unauthorized subsets containing exactly one qudit from each signal--noise pair, the quantum marginal is, in addition, maximally mixed.

authors.name: Chen-Ming Bai, Xin-Liang Zhou, Yu Luo

papers.title: Excitation Flow, Positivity, and Fisher Information for Open Subsystems of an $N$-Qubit Network
papers.summary: An observer of an autonomous quantum system has no privileged initial time, reference state, or subsystem boundary, so the natural framework for the open dynamics is an ensemble of propagators over many subsystems and time windows. We derive such an ensemble analytically for a closed $N$-qubit network with homogeneous all-to-all coupling and a single conserved excitation, giving the propagator of any $K$-qubit subsystem over any time window. To keep the analytical calculation tractable, we exclude excitation flow in sectors of two or more excitations. A single transition amplitude underlies excitation flow, positivity, entanglement entropy, and quantum Fisher information. Positivity and complete positivity reduce to the direction of the excitation flow, so the two coincide for every subsystem size. Both hold for a propagator if and only if it contracts the subsystem state toward a fixed point shared by its dynamical class. Neither the entanglement entropy nor its change over the time window corresponds to this contraction. The ensemble constrains global parameters inaccessible to any single subsystem, such as the size and coupling of the rest of the network. A band of states lies inside the domain of positivity of every single-qubit propagator, yet the reduced state never visits the band. In completely positive divisible dynamics, by contrast, any propagator may act on any state. The quantum Fisher information decomposes into a bounded state contribution and a secularly growing process contribution. The total is minimal when all future propagators are nonpositive and near its maximum when they are positive.

authors.name: Tommy Chin, Sarah Shandera

papers.title: Encrypted Cloning, Absolute Maximal Entanglement and Quantum Secret Sharing
papers.summary: The no-cloning theorem prohibits the creation of identical copies of quantum information, imposing fundamental constraints on quantum technologies. A recently proposed protocol, encrypted cloning, introduced by Yamaguchi and Kempf, showed that perfect qubit clones can be produced if they are simultaneously encrypted with a single-use key. They also observed a connection between this scheme and quantum secret sharing (QSS). However, it remained an open question whether encrypted cloning could be generalised to arbitrary dimensions, and the broader relationship between the two schemes had not been formally established. In this work, we address both questions by framing encrypted clones as Absolutely Maximally Entangled (AME) states. In parallel with recent work by Cear\'a that utilises Zadoff-Chu sequences, we independently develop a complementary framework for arbitrary dimensions based on Weyl-Heisenberg displacement operators, both tracing back to the original qubit construction by Yamaguchi and Kempf. We analytically compute the encrypted state and prove that an encrypted qudit system comprising two signal-noise qudit pairs is equivalent to a five-party AME state in any dimension, provided the input state is uniform. We then formalise the connection to QSS by proving that a threshold QSS scheme can achieve the fundamental objectives of encrypted cloning, establishing QSS as the natural general framework within which encrypted cloning can be contextualised.

authors.name: Zheng Liang Lim, Hoi-Kwong Lo

papers.title: Quantum mechanics in configuration space in context
papers.summary: The formalism of quantum mechanics in configuration space (QMCS) [Bukhari et al., New J. Phys. 27, 084501 (2025)] has been introduced to unify the modelling of photons and quantum mechanical particles. In this paper, we illustrate that QMCS also increases the continuity between quantum and classical mechanics, since it can be used to obtain both their predictions. Being based on a physically motivated quantisation of Newtonian mechanics, QMCS makes a clear distinction between the velocity observable v and the generator for spatial translations, i.e. the momentum operator p, of mechanical particles. In contrast, standard quantum mechanics, which is based on Hamiltonian mechanics, relates velocity directly to momentum rather than treating them as independent observables. Despite having many formal similarities with Hilbert space formulations of classical mechanics, QMCS is a quantum theory. To illustrate this and to further explore the relations between QMCS and alternative approaches, this paper studies quantum mechanical particles moving in free space as an example.

authors.name: Arwa Bukhari, Margherita Moro, Max Davies, Alastair Wilson, Almut Beige

papers.title: Pauli-Z Moment Matrices in the Variational Quantum Power Method: Goemans-Williamson Rounding, Qubit Locking, and a Correlation-Based Circuit-Cutting Heuristic
papers.summary: The matrix of single- and two-qubit Pauli-Z expectation values of any quantum state is the moment matrix of its computational-basis outcome distribution; it therefore lies in the cut polytope and, in particular, is a feasible point of the degree-2 Sum-of-Squares (Goemans-Williamson, GW) relaxation. Applying GW random-hyperplane rounding to this matrix yields cuts of expected weight at least alpha_GW times the state's energy. This observation and the resulting bound are not new: the bound is the GW inequality applied to the circuit's covariance matrix, and it was stated and used in exactly this form by Martinez, Fawzi and Stilck Franca, who interpret it as showing that a classical surrogate nearly reproduces the circuit and add noisy-circuit guarantees and hardware experiments; relax-and-round of QAOA correlation matrices, with spectral rather than hyperplane rounding, was introduced earlier by Dupont and Sundar. The bound is also not stronger than what direct computational-basis sampling of the state already gives in expectation. In this note we revisit the bound as a post-processing of the two-point data produced by variational algorithms such as QAOA and the Variational Quantum Power Method (VQPM), and give an energy-leakage bound for VQPM qubit locking. We further discuss a heuristic that uses the connected Z-correlation matrix to propose candidate qubit bipartitions for circuit cutting, in the spirit of existing correlation- and mutual-information-based partitioning methods, together with product-state error bounds in terms of quantum mutual information. Pairwise Z-correlations neither certify product structure of the state nor factorization of the underlying unitary, and the error bounds require quantities not available from Z-data alone.

authors.name: Ammar Daskin

papers.title: Ultraviolet structure of entanglement harvesting from energy density and other quadratic couplings
papers.summary: We study entanglement harvesting with particle detectors coupled to the renormalized energy density of a massless scalar field. Our analysis identifies the distributional mechanism underlying the persistent ultraviolet divergences previously observed for quadratic detector couplings and shows that the energy density coupling exhibits the same underlying structure. We show that these divergences are controlled by the switching correlation at coincident interaction times and, for smeared detectors, by local derivatives of the spatial overlap. Consequently, pointlike detectors are UV finite whenever the switchings do not overlap. For smooth, rapidly decreasing switchings, they are also UV finite at any fixed nonzero separation. For Gaussian-smeared detectors, the harvesting correlations are automatically finite in 1+1 and 2+1 dimensions, while in higher dimensions the remaining divergences are removed by non-overlapping switchings. Finally, we derive general expressions for arbitrary zero-mean Gaussian Hadamard states and illustrate the formalism with a thermal field state.

authors.name: Matheus H. Zambianco, Boris Ragula, Eduardo Mart\'in-Mart\'inez

papers.title: The Norton Theorem for Quantum Circuits and Systems
papers.summary: It is well known that classical analog circuits and systems benefit from the powerful Thevenin and Norton theorems. These theorems enable rigorous and exact mathematical simplification and representation of the effect of the rest of a system on the part we want to focus on. We show that there are corresponding versions of a "Quantum Norton Theorem" that enable exact simplification and reduction for quantum circuits and systems, not just for one port, but also for multiport and even open quantum systems. We demonstrate the method on two level systems, chains, system environment partitions, Lindblad examples, and Grover search. The Grover examples show how the reduced network isolates the bright pole governing ideal search and exposes how diagonal disorder transfers spectral weight into dark poles that degrade performance. By partitioning finite dimensional Schrodinger dynamics into retained and eliminated sectors, we show that Gaussian elimination gives an exact reduced equation in which the eliminated subsystem appears as a dynamical self energy and a source term. In the circuit representation, these terms become the Norton admittance and Norton current source seen by the retained quantum port. The same Schur complement construction extends to multiport reductions, composite system environment partitions, density matrix dynamics, and Lindblad evolution in Liouville space.

authors.name: Anthony J. Cressman, Rahul Sarpeshkar

papers.title: Continuous Time Quantum Walk Propagation for Irregular Temporal Graph Forecasting
papers.summary: Continuous time quantum walks built on graph Laplacians produce non monotonic graph propagation features through quantum interference during evolution, which classical diffusion cannot achieve. Such walks deliver a physically motivated propagation scheme for temporal graph signal modeling. We propose Quantum Walk Temporal Architecture (QWTA), which replaces classical graph propagation with a CTQW-type parameterized spectral propagator. QWTA embeds effective observation intervals into the spectral phase modulation of the propagation kernel. QWTA-Base preserves exact CTQW spectral evolution and serves as a physically faithful propagation reference. QWTA-GR further introduces phase soft clipping and gated residual fusion to stabilize propagation. The results show that explicit phase encoding of irregular time intervals, when combined with suitable stabilization, provides a physically motivated and competitive graph propagation design for temporal graph forecasting with missing historical observations.

authors.name: Jiaqi Sun, Tianhao Li, Zhihao Bian

papers.title: Detecting non-Gaussianity and quantum non-Gaussianity via multicopy interference
papers.summary: We develop tests of non-Gaussianity for bosonic systems based on interference between identically prepared copies of the state. The tests use real orthogonal transformations that mix the copies while preserving their collective mode. These transformations commute with identical Gaussian unitaries applied to each copy, allowing us to derive exact Gaussian benchmarks. For single-mode states, purity alone determines the Gaussian reference value, and any discrepancy certifies non-Gaussianity. A two-copy SWAP measurement supplies the purity calibration, while informative tests within this family begin at three copies. We describe a measurement protocol with finite-sample error bounds that use passive interferometry and photon-number-resolving detectors. We also derive purity-dependent inequalities, including joint constraints on higher-power real moments, whose violation excludes convex mixtures of Gaussian states (thus certifying quantum non-Gaussianity). Finally, we extend the reference formulas to multimode systems and prove completeness of the covariance-calibrated hierarchy for states with finite mean photon number.

authors.name: Hao Dai, Matteo G. A. Paris, Yue Zhang

papers.title: Robust Quantum Extremal Numbers
papers.summary: Absolutely maximally entangled (AME) states have attracted extensive attention because of their fundamental role and applications in quantum information. When an AME state does not exist, an extremal maximally entangled (EME) state is a pure multipartite state that maximizes the number of subsystems of size $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ whose reduced states (obtained by tracing out all other parties) are maximally mixed. We study this maximum and extend the problem to a robust setting, in which small deviations from maximal mixing are allowed. We quantify these deviations using the purity of each reduced state and derive bounds by summing the deviations over selected groups of subsystems or over all subsystems of the target size. Local inequalities lead to combinatorial bounds based on forbidden hypergraphs and Tur\\'an-type counting, improving robust bounds for several general families of multipartite systems. Global inequalities, combined with combinatorial arguments and linear programming, determine the fourth and fifth known quantum extremal numbers: the maximal counts are 112 for nine qubits and 200 for ten qubits. We further show that these counts remain unchanged in the robust setting for eight-, nine-, and ten-qubit systems when the allowed deviations from maximal mixing are below $1/5$, $1/143$, and $1/16$, respectively. These results provide a unified framework for determining exact and robust bounds on the number of maximally mixed reduced states.

authors.name: Wanchen Zhang, Zicheng Han, Xiande Zhang

papers.title: Information-Calibrated Quantum Diffusion: Aligning Forward Noise with Reverse Recoverability
papers.summary: Quantum diffusion models typically parameterize forward corruption by raw channel strength, even though this parameter does not directly quantify how much ensemble information is erased or how difficult the corresponding reverse problem is. We introduce the classical--quantum information decrement $\Delta_t=I(X{:}Q_{t-1})-I(X{:}Q_t)$ as an intrinsic diffusion coordinate that links forward noise allocation to reverse recoverability. Along depolarization, equalizing $\Delta_t$ yields the unique minimax discretization of the forward information loss, while universal recoverability gives the same quantity an operational interpretation as a physically attainable local recovery budget. We further show that such local calibration is not sufficient for stochastic generation: models can satisfy the same recovery criterion while producing substantially different state distributions. This motivates a stochastic learner that combines information-calibrated recovery constraints with distribution matching. We establish finite-sample calibration and compositional trace-Wasserstein control for the resulting learner. Controlled quantum experiments validate the predicted information--recovery alignment, show that the recovery constraints improve local inversion, and confirm the complementary role of distribution matching in endpoint generation. The resulting framework also achieves stronger endpoint trace-Wasserstein performance than an official QuDDPM implementation with fewer trainable parameters. Overall, our work provides a unified information-theoretic principle for designing forward schedules, calibrating reverse steps, and separating physical recovery from generative coverage in quantum diffusion.

authors.name: Qipeng Qian, Jialiang Jin, Shihao Wang Yuntao Qian

papers.title: Quantum annealing through a first-order phase transition: Field theory approach
papers.summary: Unlike second-order phase transitions, a first-order transition has a stage, in which a system is trapped in a metastable state. The decay of this state leads to abundant excitations over the ground state. We present a field theory for kinetics of defects emerging during quantum annealing computations. This theory predicts several power laws for the error generation rate during quantum annealing either through or near the first-order phase transition. Sharp changes between the power exponents are predicted for continuous parameter changes. Observation of this behavior would be a signature of first-order critical points and could help identify and avoid them for better computations. The driven Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick model (LMGm) serves as the minimal model of interacting Ising spins that demonstrates this behavior.

authors.name: Diego Andr\'es Rivera Orona, Predrag Puno\v{s}evac, Nikolai A. Sinitsyn

papers.title: Absolutely Maximally Entangled States for Odd Prime Power Local Dimension
papers.summary: An absolutely maximally entangled (AME) state is a pure state of $N$ parties with $d$ levels each whose reduced states on every subset of at most half the parties are maximally mixed. Such states provide perfect tensors and optimal quantum error-correcting codes. Determining the values of $N$ and $d$ for which they exist is one of the central problems in multipartite entanglement. For every odd prime power, $q=p^e\ge3$, we construct a stabilizer $\mathrm{AME}(2q,q)$ state and prove the existence of stabilizer $\mathrm{AME}(N,q)$ states for $N=2,3,\ldots,2q$. The construction uses a closed-form $q\times q$ bordered-circulant matrix $A_q$ over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ to generate a Hermitian self-dual maximum distance separable (MDS) code $[2q,q,q+1]_{q^2}$. These codes lie outside the generalized Reed-Solomon family, including its extended forms. In suitable local bases, the parent states yield Butson Hadamard matrices of order $q^q$ with $p$th-root entries, which become $q$-unitary after normalization. Paired projections on antipodal coordinates give all even lengths from $q+1$ to $2q$; one-party projections and standard short-length constructions complete the range. Weighted submatrices give further explicit realizations.

authors.name: Mykhailo Hontarenko, Karol \.{Z}yczkowski

papers.title: Optimal Joint Lower Bound for Sparse Quantum Linear System Solvers
papers.summary: Quantum linear system solvers form one of the central algorithmic primitives in quantum computing, with applications ranging from differential equations and optimization to machine learning. Their cost is commonly measured through query complexity, which counts the number of oracle calls needed to access the input matrix. In the sparse-access model, this complexity is governed by three parameters: the condition number $\kappa$, the sparsity $s$ of the input matrix, and the target precision $\varepsilon$. The dependence on $\kappa$ and $\varepsilon$ is already well understood through the lower bound $\Omega(\kappa\log(1/\varepsilon))$, which matches the best known scaling in these parameters. Once the sparsity $s$ is included, however, the expected lower bound has long been conjectured to be $\Omega(\kappa\sqrt{s}\log(1/\varepsilon))$. Recent work by Mori et al. [Quantum Sci. Tech. 11 035063 (2026)] made an important step towards this goal by establishing the lower bound $\Omega(\kappa\sqrt{s})$ for constant error $\varepsilon$. In this work, we complete the picture and prove the full joint lower bound $\Omega(\kappa\sqrt{s}\log(1/\varepsilon))$ in the sparse-access model, thereby establishing the anticipated dependence on all three parameters simultaneously.

authors.name: Dhrumil Patel

papers.title: Dynamical, thermal, and ground-state multiparameter quantum metrology: Fundamental limits and their attainability in magnetometry
papers.summary: We study the simultaneous estimation of parameters in Hamiltonians $H_{\vec{\theta}}=H_{\vec{\theta}}^P+H^C$, with $H^C$ a control term, for unitary dynamics, thermal equilibrium, and ground states. In each case, we bound the quantum Fisher information matrix by the covariance matrix of the parameter generators, extending single-parameter bounds and identifying the conditions for saturation. At thermal equilibrium, a complementary lower bound quantifies the cost of non-commutativity. For vector magnetometry, we derive asymptotically tight bounds and identify many-body control Hamiltonians that approach them in all three settings.

authors.name: Riccardo Pedroni, V\'ictor Izquierdo, Advay Burte, Paolo Abiuso, John Calsamiglia, Mart\'i Perarnau-Llobet

papers.title: Causal Query Compression for Lindblad Dynamics: Optimal Queries and Nearly Linear Local Simulation
papers.summary: We construct a causal query compiler for time-dependent Lindblad dynamics and establish query and gate bounds under distinct input models. With coherent block encodings of the Hamiltonian and individual jump operators, a Lipschitz generator can be simulated to diamond-norm error $\varepsilon$ using $O(1+\tau+\log(1/\varepsilon)/\log(e+\log(1/\varepsilon)/\tau))$ controlled queries, where $\tau=T(\alpha_H+\sum_\mu\alpha_\mu^2)$. This bound is independent of the time-grid size and is worst-case optimal for $\tau\ge1$. Weak active entry and clean return yield a factorial history tail; combining two reuse lengths removes the auxiliary input. A three-call polar correction supplies the Lindblad cells. The compiler also characterizes the minimum oracle action of bounded adaptive Markovian protocols by quantum query complexity and the general adversary bound, up to constant factors. For finite-range dynamics on $n$ lattice sites, efficient coherent evaluation of the local matrices and fixed local parameters give $O(n(T+1)\operatorname{polylog}X)$ elementary gates, where $X=\max\{e,n(T+1)(1+K_t+B)/\varepsilon\}$, for piecewise H\"older generators with fixed exponent, local variation bound $K_t$, and at most $B$ breakpoints per term. The jumps need not commute. This gate bound includes evaluation, arithmetic, selection, routing, and environment storage. Its proof combines a spatial decomposition on a common bath, compilation on occupied inputs, and routing on compressed records. Reusing bath storage between short segments gives depth $(T+1)\operatorname{polylog}X$ and space $n\operatorname{polylog}X$.

authors.name: Jacob Kitchen

papers.title: Inverse-Designed Nanobeam Cavities for High-Cooperativity Spin-Photon Interfaces in Silicon
papers.summary: Telecom-band spin defects in silicon offer a compelling platform for integrated quantum networks by combining scalable silicon photonics with spin-based quantum memories and multiqubit registers. The T center and recently demonstrated Al1 center are particularly promising, but their limited coherent zero-phonon emission requires strong cavity enhancement for efficient spin-photon interfaces. Here, we inverse-design silicon nanobeam cavities for both centers using a unified adjoint-optimization framework targeting Purcell enhancement, resonance alignment, and photon extraction. For each emitter, symmetric cavities maximize Purcell enhancement, while asymmetric cavities provide directional coupling to an integrated waveguide. Three-dimensional finite-difference time-domain simulations yield loaded quality factors up to 3.25 x 10^6, Purcell factors up to 7.49 x 10^5, and cooperativities of approximately 1.4 x 10^3 to 2.6 x 10^4, corresponding to cavity-coupled emission fractions exceeding 99.9%. The asymmetric cavities direct approximately 90% of emitted power into a single on-chip waveguide while maintaining cooperativity above 1.4 x 10^3. Under nanometer-scale fabrication perturbations, all four designs remain within the high-cooperativity regime, and high cooperativity persists when the cavity quality factor is constrained to a realistic absorption-limited value of 10^5. This unified, fabrication-compatible framework establishes a scalable cavity-design route for silicon telecom spin-photon interfaces and, to our knowledge, the first cavity designs for the Al1 center.

authors.name: Nail Letty, Md Sakibul Islam, Wayesh Qarony

papers.title: Toward an Optimal Quantum Algorithm for Geometrically Local Hamiltonian Simulation
papers.summary: Understanding the dynamics of interacting quantum systems is a central goal of quantum simulation. For geometrically local Hamiltonians, locality suggests that digital simulation should retain much of the parallelism of the underlying dynamics. For a target accuracy $\epsilon$, we construct a nearest-neighbor quantum circuit that simulates the dynamics of an $n$-qubit, time-independent, finite-range Hamiltonian with normalized local interaction strength on a fixed-dimensional lattice for time $T\ge1$, with circuit depth $O(T\log(nT/\epsilon))$ and gate count $O(nT\log(nT/\epsilon))$. This reduces the polylogarithmic overhead of Haah, Hastings, Kothari, and Low to a single logarithm. On logarithmic-scale blocks from the Lieb--Robinson decomposition, a shallow but highly accurate implementation is essential for reducing the circuit depth. Our key observation is that spatial localization also controls the cost of high precision. In each block, the error of a constant-order product formula is compensated for by a correction, yielding exponential accuracy. The correction can be implemented with depth proportional to the block diameter, introducing no additional asymptotic depth scale beyond that required by spatial localization. Furthermore, we prove an unconditional circuit-depth lower bound for uniform XXZ Hamiltonians: at fixed evolution time $T$ in the stated regime and sufficiently small fixed error $\epsilon$, any nearest-neighbor quantum circuit simulating these dynamics requires depth $\Omega(\log n/\log\log n)$. This matches our $O(\log n)$ upper bound up to a doubly logarithmic factor, establishing near-optimal circuit depth for lattice Hamiltonian simulation in this regime. Together, these results clarify the role of locality and precision in determining the circuit complexity of quantum dynamics and suggest broader principles for spatially constrained quantum computation.

authors.name: Zheyu Shen, Yusen Wu, Penghui Yao, Xiao Yuan, Yukun Zhang

papers.title: Two-center Dirac equation in a Gaussian basis set
papers.summary: A method for solving the two-center Dirac equation using a Gaussian-product basis set tailored to the axial symmetry of diatomic systems is presented. For the ground state of H$_2^+$ at an internuclear distance $R=2.0~a_0$, we obtain a relativistic energy with relative precision at the $10^{-18}$ level. The properties of the basis set allow for an analytic Fourier transform of the wave function. As a first application we evaluate, for the first time, the zero-potential contribution to the one-loop self-energy for H$_2^+$ in Feynman and Coulomb gauges. Although this contribution is not separately gauge invariant, its calculation provides a proof of principle for the use of the present framework in prospective QED calculations.

authors.name: D\'avid Ferenc

papers.title: Shallow Quantum Circuits for Geometrically Local Lindblad Dynamics
papers.summary: Open-system dynamics govern decoherence, transport, and engineered dissipation in quantum many-body systems. We propose a quantum algorithm for simulating time-independent, finite-range Lindblad dynamics with bounded local strength on a constant-dimensional lattice of $n$ sites, allowing noncommuting jump operators. For time $T\ge1$ and diamond-norm error at most $\epsilon$, it has depth $O(T\operatorname{polylog}(nT/\epsilon))$ and gate count $O(nT\operatorname{polylog}(nT/\epsilon))$. These results extend the HHKL spatial decomposition to open systems. The main obstacle is that the reversible overlap corrections used for unitary dynamics have no direct analogue for dissipative channels. We overcome this by retaining the environment in a shared unitary dilation, keeping information lost from the system coherently available and making the spatial corrections reversible. We prove exponential occupation bounds for the environmental states generated by the decomposition, allowing compact representation and coherent simulation of local factors on the inputs that arise. The construction reduces each short-time evolution to a constant number of parallel layers on regions of logarithmic diameter, using nearest-neighbour gates and polylogarithmic auxiliary density. We also prove unconditional worst-case lower bounds using time-independent, purely dissipative processes that transport quantum information. For circuits with local quantum and classical communication, the lower bounds are $\Omega(nT)$ for the expected gate count and $\Omega(T)$ for depth on time scales up to the lattice diameter. They match the upper bounds' leading time and volume dependence up to polylogarithmic factors. At fixed time and sufficiently small fixed error, we further prove a depth lower bound of $\Omega(\log n/\log\log n)$, showing that global accuracy can require increasing depth as the lattice grows.

authors.name: Zheyu Shen, Yusen Wu, Xiao Yuan, Yukun Zhang

papers.title: Rounded Clocks and Finite Precision: A Transfer Principle Between Continuous and Discrete Quantum Dynamics
papers.summary: I present a short approach to discretizing continuous unitary evolution in finite dimensions. For a time-dependent Hamiltonian $H(s)$ with $s\in[0,1]$ and an integer $T\ge1$, let $U(T)$ be the evolution of $H(t/T)$ over time $T$, and let $W_T=e^{-iH((T-1)/T)}\cdots e^{-iH(0)}$ be the product of the unitaries generated by its samples. With a half-step phase at each end, $V(T)=e^{-iH(1)/2}W_Te^{iH(0)/2}$ is the evolution generated by $H(\lfloor t+1/2\rfloor/T)$, where $\lfloor t+1/2\rfloor$ is a rounded clock, time at finite precision. Whereas Duhamel's formula only bounds $\|V(T)-U(T)\|$ by a constant, I show that $\|V(T)-U(T)\|=O(1/T)$ in operator norm, with explicit constants, whenever $H'$ is Lipschitz and every sample has eigenvalue differences at most a fixed width below $2\pi$. The gain comes from cancellation within and between time steps. This general transfer theorem assumes neither adiabaticity nor a spectral gap, and any operator-norm bound for $U(T)$ transfers to $V(T)$ with an added $O(1/T)$. Nonetheless, discrete adiabatic theorems for $W_T$ follow from continuous ones, because the end phases commute with the spectral projectors of $H(0)$ and $H(1)$. For a product of samples of a $C^2$ unitary family, a continuously moving arc of fixed length $\vartheta$ that avoids the spectrum determines a Hermitian logarithm meeting the width condition, and the $O(1/T)$ bound has coefficients $O(\vartheta^{-3})$. In the easier direction, Duhamel's formula shows that rounding the clock to midpoints and truncating the entries of a regulated time-dependent Hamiltonian at a fixed binary place gives a product within $T$ times the error of the rounded, truncated Hamiltonian.

authors.name: Michael Jarret

papers.title: Fault-tolerant resource estimation for ground-state preparation via Lindblad simulation
papers.summary: Recent advances in algorithms for simulating Lindblad dynamics have clarified their theoretical potential for state preparation, but their practicality in the early fault-tolerant regime and beyond remains uncertain. In this work, we address this by investigating the cost of preparing ground states of the fermionic Hubbard model, following the single-ancilla approach of [Phys. Rev. Research 6, 033147 (2024)]. We derive rigorous error bounds including constant prefactors, and compare to empirical error behavior and practical convergence parameters obtained from circuit-level simulations. We find that empirically chosen parameters can reduce the required resources by orders of magnitude, resulting in an estimated $7.7 \times 10^8$ T gates to perform one unit of time evolution targeting the low-energy subspace of a 36-site fermionic Hubbard model. We identify the accurate filtering of energy transitions as the main source of this cost.

authors.name: Marius Bothe, Patrick Schoepf, Nick S. Blunt

papers.title: Finite-time quantum equilibration from local correlations
papers.summary: We study equilibration of a fixed subsystem coupled to an initially maximally mixed bath. We show that the worst-input mean-square error, maximised over observation windows of length $T$, is bounded from above and below by the mean square of a complete local autocorrelation on $[0,T]$. The constants depend only on the subsystem dimension, and no assumption on degeneracies of energies or energy gaps is required. Subtracting the stationary part of the correlation gives equilibration to the temporal state; retaining it gives thermalisation to the maximally mixed state. We then obtain explicit bounds for two static Hamiltonian families. A periodic spin-clock model thermalises on $O(n\log n)$ windows at fixed accuracy despite an exponentially small positive energy. A randomly dressed commuting model, with interaction range $O(\log N)$, has expected error $O(N^{-b}+T^{-1})$ while retaining an extensive family of conserved observables. We explain how the locally weighted spectrum determines these bounds.

authors.name: Piotr \'Cwikli\'nski

papers.title: Bell's go theorem: regaining local causality with a new notion of realism
papers.summary: Bell's theorem is popularly stated as the inconsistency of quantum theory with local realism. Realism is here formalized by the ontological models framework, where elements of reality are points of a measurable space and probabilities obey the Kolmogorov axioms. In the Bell scenario, locally causal ontological models posit a common cause supporting a global valuation, a joint assignment of outcomes to all measurements at once, across incompatible contexts. Within this notion of realism, Bell's theorem makes any realist explanation of the quantum predictions conspiratorial: any mechanism, whether superluminal, superdeterministic, or retrocausal, must be finely tuned so as never to manifest operationally. We redefine realism through a new ontological framework that generalizes the standard one. The elements of reality, which we call records, are no longer points but relational parts of a point-free generalization of a topological space (sublocales of a locale). A record shared by two incompatible contexts establishes the sameness of a measurement across them, without such pairwise identities composing into a global valuation, and the common cause is then a web of such records. Within this framework, Bell's no-go theorem becomes a go theorem: local causality, restated for records, is no longer at odds with the quantum statistics. This is possible because modularity, the inclusion-exclusion law of classical probability, fails across incompatible contexts, so that the probability theory generalizes Kolmogorov's. We exhibit explicit models reproducing several quantum strategies, including the optimal CHSH violation. More broadly, locally causal models of this kind attain every Bell-CHSH value up to the algebraic maximum. A realist explanation of the quantum predictions need not be conspiratorial; every causal influence posited by these models is reflected in the operational predictions.

authors.name: Lorenzo Catani, Nesta van der Schaaf, Rui Soares Barbosa

papers.title: Euler's thirty-six officers need not all be entangled: real AME(4,6), families and classification
papers.summary: Absolutely maximally entangled states of four six-level systems, AME$(4,6)$, are the quantum solutions of Euler's problem of the thirty-six officers. Until recently all reported solutions were complex, and it was conjectured that no real orthogonal 2-unitary matrix of order $36$ exists. We give real AME$(4,6)$ states with $60$ non-zero coefficients in $\{\pm1,\sqrt2\}/\sqrt{72}$. Of their thirty-six officers, $12$ are classical, as some must be whenever fewer than $72$ coefficients are non-zero. They lie in the $-1$ eigenspace of an order-$4$ local symmetry, and on their support the AME conditions become linear. We derive two closed-form families of AME$(4,6)$ states that meet at one of these states: a $10$-parameter family that is supported on $72$ basis states, and an $11$-parameter family on $60$ basis states. At each of its two ends the first family loses $12$ coefficients, and the AME states on the remaining $60$ basis states form an $11$-parameter family: the second family at one end, and an analogous family at the other. These two $60$-term families contain $4096$ real AME states up to diagonal local unitaries, $1024$ of which are limits of the first family. They fall into exactly $20$ classes under local unitaries and permutations of the parties, and we certify their separation with interval arithmetic.

authors.name: Palash Pandya

papers.title: Thermal activation of photon catalysis in difference-intensity Mach-Zehnder interferometry with squeezed thermal light
papers.summary: Realistic non-Gaussian operations, which can be implemented by mixing a nonclassical Gaussian state with a Fock state at a beam splitter and then heralding on a photon-number-resolving detector, are known to improve phase estimation in a Mach-Zehnder interferometer. The existing studies have considered the single-mode squeezed vacuum for difference-intensity and parity detection, and the two-mode squeezed thermal state for parity detection alone as the initial Gaussian resources. However, a real squeezer in the lab actually produces single-mode squeezed thermal light, which has not been studied in a coherent-plus-resource interferometer. We take up this case and using the phase space Wigner picture, we obtain the heralded state produced by photon subtraction, addition and catalysis on a single-mode squeezed thermal resource, and evaluate the corresponding phase sensitivities. Single-photon catalysis, which is useless on squeezed vacuum, becomes a useful operation for any thermal occupation above $\nth\simeq0.2$, and since it heralds with a probability near one-half, it turns out to be the best success-weighted operation over the whole thermal range. In the vacuum limit our results reproduce the known hierarchy, where two-photon catalysis is the best operation. The quantum Fisher information computations confirms that thermal noise enhances the phase information encoded in the catalyzed state, demonstrating that difference-intensity detection closely approaches the ultimate precision bound across most operational regimes, and, together with a loss analysis, verifies the robustness of the effect.

authors.name: Kirtpreet Singh, Arvind

papers.title: Designing Robust Quantum Gates
papers.summary: For given control channels, quantum control theory determines whether quantum gates can be realized, but not their resilience to errors. We address this problem by establishing existence criteria for robust gate implementation in $d$-level systems. Our criteria reveal that implementability of all gates is not enough: a universal family of robust gates exists if and only if, in addition, the driven Hamiltonian operators share no common symmetry. When these criteria hold, we can make every gate resilient to any combination of static perturbations, uniform Hamiltonian rescaling, perturbations at a finite set of selected frequencies, and perturbations with arbitrary selected waveforms. We can impose robustness conditions broadly with limited information about errors, e.g., against any static perturbations; we can also tailor these conditions to the platform, e.g., against environment-induced noise with dominant spectral peaks, requiring no spectral details beyond the peak frequencies. We numerically construct explicit protocols for robust gates, reducing average gate infidelity by approximately two to seven orders of magnitude under Hamiltonian perturbations and environment-induced noise. Together, our existence criteria and numerical constructions provide practical guidance for evaluating the potential of quantum platforms and designing robust quantum gates.

authors.name: Yuanxing Hao, Marin Bukov

papers.title: Optimal robust single-qubit gates in superconducting quantum processors
papers.summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires high-fidelity quantum gates that are resilient to control errors and device imperfections. Here, we develop energy-optimal control pulses for single-qubit gates that are simultaneously robust against frequency detuning and waveform inhomogeneities while also suppressing leakage outside the computational subspace. Combining the optimized pulse envelopes with an adaptive control scheme, we experimentally demonstrate optimal robust gates on a superconducting quantum processor. For a gate duration of 90ns, we achieve fidelities above 99.9% for the X gate and 99.6% for Hadamard-type gates. For the X gate, we maintain fidelities above 99.5% for simultaneous drive-amplitude variations up to 20% and qubit detuning up to 4 MHz. This robustness outperforms that of conventional Gaussian pulses by an order of magnitude, without much difference in peak gate fidelity. These results establish a route towards robust single-qubit control in large-scale quantum processors, advancing the development of fault-tolerant quantum computing.

authors.name: Tangyou Huang, Anuj Aggarwal, Jingjun Zhu, Akshay Gaikwad, David Niepce, Marcus Rommel, Andreas Nylander, Amr Osman, Janka Bizn\'arov\'a, Anita Fadavi Roudsari, St\'ephane Gu\'erin, Gheorghe Sorin Paraoanu, Anton Frisk Kockum, Giovanna Tancredi

papers.title: Low-field dephasing time of an optically polarized NV$^-$ spin bath beyond the P1 limit in diamond: a cluster-correlation-expansion and exact spin-bath study
papers.summary: Dense ensembles of nitrogen-vacancy (NV$^-$) centres in nitrogen-rich diamond dephase on the electron spins of the substitutional nitrogen (P1) centres. If the paramagnetic nitrogen is instead converted into NV$^-$ centres, the laser that initializes the sensor also pumps the bath into $m_s = 0$, a state with no moment along its own axis. Using cluster-correlation-expansion (CCE) calculations with a dynamical mean field, combined with an exact solver for probe-bath exchange and with no adjustable parameter, this paper asks whether such an optically polarized NV$^-$ bath dephases a sensor more slowly than a P1 bath of the same density. The answer is set by the field. In a field along [111], three quarters of the bath centres lie off the field axis, and the moment of their $m_s = 0$ state along the field grows from 0.04 at 25 G to 0.46 at 300 G and 0.81 at 800 G. At 25 G the polarized bath is therefore nearly silent: at 0.57 ppm the dephasing time $T_2^*$ of a separately addressed $^{15}$NV$^-$ probe is 112 $\mu$s, six times the 18.0 $\mu$s of a P1 bath, and still 2.4 times at 90% polarization; an ensemble measurement gains a factor of two. At 300 G the advantage over P1 shrinks to 1.4, and at 800 G the polarized bath dephases faster than P1. The field dependence of every bath, P1 included, follows the mean moment of its centres along the field. For the Hahn echo, bath relaxation ($T_1$ = 6 ms) caps the gain: a $^{15}$NV$^-$ probe in a polarized bath reaches 1.5 times the P1 value at 25 G and 1.14-1.16 times at 300 and 800 G. Driving a single $^{14}$N hyperfine line at 25 G lengthens the ensemble $T_2^*$ to 38 $\mu$s ppm, four times the experimental P1 value, implying a 3.5-12-fold dc sensitivity gain over conventional diamond with 10-30% NV$^-$ conversion. Optical polarization of an NV$^-$ bath at low field therefore offers dephasing times beyond the P1 limit of nitrogen-rich diamond.

authors.name: Chikara Shinei

papers.title: Conditional Reset-Enhanced Dissipative Quantum Metrology
papers.summary: Open quantum sensors work either in a transient regime with finely timed readout or in a steady-state regime with robust but weaker sensitivity. To overcome this trade-off, we ask whether repeatedly resetting a probe to a fixed state, even a suboptimal one, can outperform the optimal single-shot transient protocol. We prove that blind resets, triggered by an external clock, cannot do so even with memory. Conditional resets, triggered by the probe's own state, break this no-go result by capturing parameter-dependent quantum jumps or by recycling heralded losses, for parameters encoded in dissipative rates and Hamiltonians alike. A three-level thermometer capturing thermal excitations outperforms the optimal no-reset protocol in both transient and steady-state regimes, even with a $40\%$ preparation error. Conditional resets can even saturate the ultimate bound of nonequilibrium thermometry with a single readout. Heralded recycling enables steady-state frequency estimation to outperform optimal transient Ramsey interferometry. The advantages extend to interacting probes and to elapsed-time estimation, and both mechanisms can be realized using established experimental techniques.

authors.name: Silan Li, Qingjun Tong, Ruicheng Bao

papers.title: Homodyne versus heterodyne detection near Gaussian states: Fraction of the quantum Fisher information recovered
papers.summary: Homodyne and heterodyne detection are the standard measurements of an optical mode. Which of them yields more information is known only for particular tasks, with opposite answers for displacements and tomography. We compare them for every small change of a Gaussian state by their efficiency, the recovered fraction of the quantum Fisher information. We prove that near any Gaussian state of any number of modes the quantum Fisher information and the Fisher information of any Gaussian measurement are sums over the Hermite orders of the change, each term fixed by the covariance matrix and the measurement. A fixed Gaussian measurement measures no change more efficiently than the best displacement. Near a thermal state of one mode closed-form efficiencies reconcile the known comparisons, and homodyne detection at a uniformly random phase recovers at most one half, a bound raised by squeezing. Near a coherent state both detections recover exactly one half for every change of finite quantum Fisher information (the largest possible average). At the two-mode squeezed vacuum, homodyne detection of both modes at uniformly random phases is as efficient as heterodyne detection for every such change. On simulated records of one set of distant states, a likelihood-ratio observer shows a heterodyne advantage under Gaussian noise and none under loss, as the theory predicts. Under dephasing it shows none. Neural networks on reconstructed Wigner functions can show a heterodyne advantage absent from the records. For random non-Gaussian changes of up to seven photons near a thermal state the median efficiencies of both detections lie between 0.04 and 0.19, 5 to 25 times below the optimal measurement.

authors.name: Franciszek Grzywa, Sebastian Dolata, Karol Bartkiewicz

papers.title: Structural Bottlenecks in QAOA Mixer Design: Transport and Causal Reach
papers.summary: The choice of mixer is central to the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), yet no single structural measure captures every limitation of a shallow circuit. We study two complementary properties: configuration-space transport, which constrains probability concentration, and finite-depth causal reach, which limits the problem information available to local observables. In the transport analysis, first-order bounds in the small-$\beta$ and small-$\gamma$ regimes reduce to the same cost-weighted Dirichlet energy on connected regular mixer graphs. A non-perturbative $\ell_1$-spreading bound also gives a problem-dependent restriction on the expected objective and on the spreading required for a target approximation ratio. For MaxCut, we augment the transverse-field mixer with graph-aligned two-qubit interactions and establish a causal-radius bound of $(k+1)p$ at depth $p$. Numerical experiments at $k=1$ on cycles, circular ladders, and high-girth regular bipartite graphs show higher best-found approximation ratios for $X+XX$ and $X+YY$ than for standard $X$ at equal depth. Although these augmentations have the same causal-radius bound, $X+YY$ performs better in every tested setting, highlighting the role of operator structure alongside causal reach.

authors.name: Jasjyot Singh Gulati, Tharrmashastha SAPV

papers.title: Quantum-Walk Inspired Spectral Metrics for Evaluating QAOA Mixers
papers.summary: QAOA mixers play an important role in enabling exploration of the exponentially large solution space of binary optimization problems. However, the choice of mixer Hamiltonian is typically guided by convention and implementation or circuit constraints, rather than by a graph-topology-aware criterion. In this work, inspired by quantum-walk mixing theory, we propose two complementary spectral heuristics for characterizing QAOA mixer topologies. The first is the normalized minimum eigenvalue separation of the mixer Hamiltonian $H_M$, while the second is the long-time averaged minimum eigenvalue separation of the mixer unitary $U_M(\beta)=e^{-i\beta H_M}$. Both quantities are invariant under any positive rescaling of the mixer Hamiltonian and provide Hamiltonian- and unitary-level characterizations of the mixer's spectral structure. We use them as heuristic indicators of the mixer dynamics relevant to amplitude redistribution during QAOA evolution. We derive exact expressions and asymptotic bounds for the complete graph, hypercube, cycle, and balanced 2-D torus, revealing a broad spectral separation between the studied topology classes. We then compare these separations with empirical QAOA performance. For random permutation-invariant cost Hamiltonians, the observed performance ordering is broadly consistent with the spectral characterization. In contrast, for structured 1-D and 2-D Ising QUBOs, this ordering breaks down, indicating that mixer-cost alignment can become important. These results illustrate both the usefulness and the limitations of topology-level, cost-agnostic spectral heuristics for QAOA mixer selection.

authors.name: Jasjyot Singh Gulati, Tharrmashastha SAPV

papers.title: Universal quantum control in biorthogonal framework
papers.summary: As a paradigm for describing the open-quantum-system dynamics, the non-Hermitian Schr\"odinger equation generally modifies the state norm, impeding the coherent control over the system. With a general instantaneous representation spanned by biorthogonal ancillary bases, we develop a biorthogonal quantum-control theory for finite-dimensional systems under a general time-dependent non-Hermitian Hamiltonian. In particular, we derive a necessary and sufficient condition for extracting the transitionless pathways that transport parallel in both ket and bra states. When this condition is satisfied by a set of projectors constructed with biorthogonal basis states, the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian becomes diagonal in the relevant biorthogonal subspace, enabling arbitrary initial state to evolve as a superposition of several transitionless passages. Our theory is justified by the bidirectional population transfer, a non-Hermitian holomonic quantum gate implemented in a three-level system, and chiral state conversion. For the bidirectional transfer and the holonomic gate, we can further identify the parametric constraints under which a unitary transformation is formed to link the initial and target states. As a result, the final state is automatically normalized even though the transitional dynamics is nonunitary. In population transfer, controlled gain and loss cut the required coherent pulse area, delivering shorter transfer times than the Hermitian benchmark at equal average Rabi frequency. For the chiral state conversion, we find that a closed parametric loop along opposite directions leads to distinct final state, which is irrelevant to encircling the exceptional point or not. Our work integrates the universal quantum control into the biorthogonal framework, displaying full-rank coherent control in non-Hermitian systems.

authors.name: Chen-yi Zhang, Jun Jing

papers.title: Photon-loss tolerance of the surface-GKP code with anti-photon-loss decoding
papers.summary: Photon loss somewhat limits fault-tolerant photonic quantum computing. We investigate its effect on finite-energy Gottesman--Kitaev--Preskill (GKP) states by modeling the pure-loss channel directly. We obtain photon-loss threshold estimates for the surface-GKP code using nearest-lattice-point inner GKP decoding and minimum-weight perfect matching for the outer surface code. For GKP states with $\epsilon=0.01$ and $\epsilon=0.05$, corresponding to GKP squeezing of $20$ and $13\,\mathrm{dB}$, the estimated thresholds are $\gamma^\ast=5.5\%$ ($0.24\,\mathrm{dB}$) and $\gamma^\ast=5.9\%$ ($0.26\,\mathrm{dB}$), respectively. We then introduce an anti-photon-loss inner decoder that compensates for the contraction of the measured quadrature. It increases the corresponding threshold estimates to $\gamma^\ast=9.8\%$ ($0.45\,\mathrm{dB}$) and $\gamma^\ast=6.3\%$ ($0.28\,\mathrm{dB}$). Our results highlight the importance of accounting for loss-induced lattice contraction in inner decoding and demonstrate that quadrature compensation enhances the photon-loss tolerance of surface-GKP codes for both high- and moderate-quality GKP states, providing a route toward more photon-loss-robust optical quantum computing.

authors.name: Guan-Ju Yan, Pei-Lin Du, Ke-Ming Hu, Jun-Jie He, Yu-Ze Zhu, Xing-Yu Chen, Lin Yang, An-Bang Wu, Hao Tang, Xian-Min Jin

papers.title: Autonomous steady-state quantum magic under local noise
papers.summary: We determine the local reset cost of sustaining quantum magic under continuous depolarization. Static spin interactions convert reset-induced polarization into nonstabilizer correlations. For interactions involving at most $k$ spins and local coherent strength $J$, the optimal strong-noise threshold obeys $K_{\rm on}^{(k)}/\gamma=\Theta_k[(\gamma/J)^{1/(k-1)}]$, where $\gamma$ is the noise rate and $K$ the reset cap. The exponent is uniform in device size, and the two-body leading coefficient is $1/(2\sqrt{2})$. The hierarchy follows from a coherent transition competing with simultaneous local defects. In weak noise, population amplification across growing devices lets the normalized onset cost vanish with static two-body interactions. Entropy balance separately constrains the size and total reset rate required for a fixed global resource. Explicit two-, three-, and four-body dynamics generate magic from free inputs and converge to a unique mixed steady state. A physical two-body construction connects this stationary resource to its coherent budget, control precision, and preparation time.

authors.name: Mingdi Xu, Lei Pan

papers.title: Spatial Cost of Recovering a Fusion Qubit in a Critical Spin Chain
papers.summary: Four Kramers--Wannier defects in a critical Ising chain encode a qubit over a common pure bulk ground state in a fixed symmetry sector. We determine the spatial cost of recovering it from arbitrary preselected physical spins, allowing unrestricted joint decoding. In the infinite-chain limit followed by increasing defect separation, vanishing error under linear spin budgets requires filling the central gap and at least one outer gap in density. The shorter three-defect interval attains the sharp leading cost through single-spin measurements and classical feedforward. Near-minimal successful supports approach a shortest such span in density. Below this cost, a benchmark finite-ring budget window separates entanglement-breaking connected access from entanglement-preserving single-gap perforations. For a selected two-component family, single-spin Pauli measurements and a one-way classical message yield a scale-stable Bell recovery advantage. The output channel supports positive transmission rates over independently prepared blocks, with coding performed at fixed geometry before the ordered spatial limits. Collective fusion records in discarded spins bound recovery from above, while conjugate retained records certify coherence. Finite-ring examples show that Bell-optimal one-qubit compression can reduce the full output's capacity. On two uncoupled chains with independent bulk states, a repetition embedding raises the leading cost. A matched interacting Ashkin--Teller ladder retains finite-ring geometric separation at every finite nonnegative coupling. The results distinguish useful quantum access from vanishing-error recovery and connect both to critical many-body statistics.

authors.name: Yi Liang

papers.title: Recovery gates as a resource in repetition-code process tomography: exhaustive gate-optimal designs for three, five and seven qubits
papers.summary: Process tomography on a stabilizer code compares the logical channel of a repetition code against a reference channel, through a decoder almost always fixed to the standard minimum-weight one. We ask how many physical single-qubit Pauli gates that decoder needs when the measurement basis is fixed, the constraint under which the count is a resource rather than a bookkeeping artefact. Exhaustive enumeration of every recovery design at $n=3$, $5$ and $7$ qubits, each rank decided in exact arithmetic, gives minima of $0$, $1$ and $5$ gates, against $6$, $10$ and $14$ for first-order decoding and $6$, $50$ and $308$ for full minimum-weight decoding. The count depends only on how many sites are corrected, never on which, so the design problem splits into a budget and a placement; but the placement decides identifiability, and more sites is not monotonically better: at $n=7$ full decoding has rank $24$ of $27$, and the precision curve at $n=3$ is U-shaped under a calibration-residual floor. At the median of $40$ working points the three-gate design is $9.0$ times more precise than the standard six-gate decoder, and better at every one of them; the factor belongs to the point, the ordering does not. Because that advantage requires choosing the placement at the point, we also certify a floor that needs no such choice: two three-gate placements in parallel lose no direction that either sees, and cost at most $\sqrt{2}$ in worst-parameter deviation at equal total shots, giving recoverability at every point for at most twice the shots. At a unit per-component error the pair reaches a $10\,\mathrm{mrad}$ worst-parameter target in $\sim10^{5}$ shots at a median working point. Finally, the optimal designs are not covariant under chain reversal: on the collision locus of arXiv:2610.19779 they separate the mirror pair by $1.3\times10^{-3}$ while leaving the Jacobian at full rank.

authors.name: Long Huang

papers.title: Sample complexity of learning fermionic and bosonic Gaussian states with single-copy and entangled measurements
papers.summary: With single-copy measurements, every mixed fermionic Gaussian state on $m$ modes, pure modes included, is learned to trace distance $\epsilon$ from $\Theta(m^3/\epsilon^2)$ copies, with no logarithmic factor, against the known $\Theta(m^2/\epsilon^2)$ for collective measurements. We prove the upper bound, resolving Conjecture 10.1 of arXiv:2609.23189 (lower bound for $\epsilon\le1/3600$), and fill most open entries of the sample-complexity table of fermionic and bosonic Gaussian states, for single-copy, $k$-copy and collective measurements. With blocks of $k$ copies, the covariant highest-weight measurement of arXiv:2611.07271, read out through the Weyl-shift estimator, is exactly unbiased for every state; it gives $\Theta(\max\{m^3/k,m^2\}/\epsilon^2)$ in Frobenius norm on all states and in trace distance on every class at a fixed distance from the pure boundary. The gain $1/k$ ($k\le m$) away from the pure boundary, against $1/\sqrt k$ on cold number-conserving states, is therefore attained. Learning a quadratic fermionic Hamiltonian in Frobenius norm from its Gibbs state at bounded $\beta\|h\|$ has the same rate. For bosonic Gaussian states with bounded covariance, any displacement and squeezing, and occupations $n_1\le\dots\le n_m$, $O((m^2+r^3+\sum_{i,j>r}1/(n_i+n_j))/\epsilon^2)$ single-copy measurements suffice, $r$ the largest index with $r\,n_r\le2$; this is the minimax rate on dyadic-interval classes, with no spectral gap or cold-mode count assumed, and holds with no covariance bound for displaced passive states. With no bound on energy or squeezing, non-Gaussian measurements learn centred one-mode states, mixed included, from $O(\epsilon^{-2})$ and centred pure $m$-mode states from $O(m^2/\epsilon^2)$ single copies, free of the $\log\log E$ term of Gaussian measurements, and $m$-mode states from $O(m^3/\epsilon^2)$ copies, entangled only in a first round on blocks of $4m+6$.

authors.name: Ron Rubin

papers.title: Maximal Violation of Mermin Inequality for Commuting von Neumann Algebras and Multipartite Vacuum Entanglement in QFT
papers.summary: Summers and Werner proved that Bell inequalities are violated maximally and generically in the vacuum of a relativistic quantum field theory in [S. J. Summers and R. Werner, Commun. Math. Phys. 110 (1987), 247-259]. Their criterion concerns two-party case, that is, there are two algebras of quantum observables: one algebra and its commutant. In this case, the maximal CHSH value is converged to in every normal state exactly when the algebra is strongly stable. In the paper, we study the corresponding question for three and more mutually commuting von Neumann algebras. We focus on the multipartite Mermin inequalities instead of CHSH ones. For the tripartite Mermin functional we show that maximal violation in every normal state is equivalent to the existence of a common sequence of asymptotic GHZ stabilizers. Strong stability of each local factor is an necessary condition for maximal violation, and a joint embedding of an infinite GHZ tensor product is sufficient. Counterexamples show that strong stability and type III_1 of the individual algebras, even together with tripartite duality, do not suffice to arrive at the maximal violation. The results are also extended to n>=3 parties.

authors.name: Kan He, Jinchuan Hou, Shuyuan Yang, Bingke Zheng

papers.title: Low-energy spectral-window truncation for compact U(1) lattice gauge theory
papers.summary: We establish a nonasymptotic electric-flux truncation bound covering the entire vacuum-relative low-energy spectral window of the original pure compact $U(1)$ lattice Hamiltonian. Formulated on a three-dimensional periodic cubic lattice with $N\geq3$ sites per direction at $\theta=0$ in the gauge-invariant zero-global-flux sector, our factorial-squared tail-norm estimate applies uniformly to every normalized vector in the window without requiring physical eigenvalue isolation, a window-edge gap, or nondegeneracy, and carries no window-dimension factor. This uniform control bounds ordered low-energy eigenvalue and excitation-energy errors while governing finite-time hard-wall evolution initialized from each state's normalized projection. Within this model, an analytic finite-volume strong-coupling construction certifies a nonvacuum band and an order-one coherent plaquette signal change that persists under a specified finite cutoff. The window estimate further provides precision-dependent sufficient cutoffs, a polar-decomposition linear isometric encoding for reference-entangled inputs, and readout bounds for the local electric square. Under lattice refinement at fixed positive bare coupling, physical volume, window width, and evolution duration, cutoffs scaling as $\beta\log N/\log\log N$ with $\beta>2$ drive the state and bounded-readout truncation errors to zero.

authors.name: Yi Liang

papers.title: Sensing frequencies at the discrete Grover-Heisenberg limit using a single qubit
papers.summary: We consider a fundamental quantum sensing task: detecting weak oscillating fields with unknown strength and frequency. Recent work by Allen et al. established a fundamental lower bound on the required sensing time, which they named the "Grover-Heisenberg limit", and gave a protocol attaining this limit. The protocol relies on auxiliary qubits, which are used to run Grover's algorithm as a subroutine, leaving open the question of whether a single sensing qubit can achieve the same scaling. We show that a single qubit suffices for a discrete version of this problem in which the frequency belongs to an arbitrary, but known, finite set of candidate frequencies. Our protocol's sensing time grows only as the square root of the number of candidate frequencies. We prove that this square-root dependence, which we refer to as the "discrete Grover-Heisenberg limit", is optimal in the worst case.

authors.name: Boyang Chen, Andrea Coladangelo, Jerry Li, Haocheng Zhang

papers.title: Communication inequalities: robust quantum advantage, measurement testing and dimension witnessing with minimal setups
papers.summary: Communication scenarios (CS) are arguably the simplest setting in which quantum behaviors can be observed. Yet, in contrast to Bell scenarios or prepare-measure scenarios with shared randomness, no general method is known to separate classical and quantum statistics. Here we close this gap by deriving dimensional inequalities to separate classical and quantum statistics in CS. These depend only on four parameters of the input-output statistics, corresponding to correlated and anticorrelated events. Under dimensional assumptions, saturating one of the inequalities certifies SIC-POVMs with analytical noise robustness. The inequalities also yield a dimension witness for both correlated and anti-correlated statistics, without the need of measurement incompatibility.

authors.name: Albert Rico, Mani Zartab, Javier Fern\'andez, John Calsamiglia, Some Sankar Bhattacharya

papers.title: Fast mixing and thermal phases from strong decay of correlations
papers.summary: We show that a strong form of correlation decay in quantum Gibbs states has far-reaching dynamical consequences. For a smooth path of geometrically local commuting Hamiltonians whose Gibbs states satisfy strong decay of correlations, we construct $\mathrm{O}(1)$-time quasi-local Lindbladian evolutions exactly connecting these states in both directions, together with $\mathrm{O}(1)$-time quasi-local Hamiltonian evolutions exactly connecting their canonical purifications. These quasi-local connections strengthen previously known quantum-channel circuit constructions based on the decay of connected correlation functions [R. Ma, V. Khemani, and S. Sang, PRX Quantum 7, 033052 (2026)], which approximately connect states within the same phase but have depths that grow logarithmically with system size. Furthermore, if the Gibbs-state path contains a product state, we prove that the single-site Glauber dynamics has a $\Omega(1)$ spectral gap independent of the system size throughout the path. This establishes Glauber-dynamics fast mixing for models that may violate the strong spatial mixing condition used in prior proofs, including (1) the $q$-state Potts model throughout the high-temperature phase for any $q$ and any finite dimension; (2) the Ising model with a longitudinal field at low temperature, with frustrating perturbations that destroy monotonicity of the dynamics; and (3) the three-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_2$ lattice gauge theory at low temperatures comparing to a field perturbation, even though the model supports classical memories at intermediate temperatures. Intriguingly, we establish fast mixing of these classical Markov chains using tools from quantum physics like Lieb-Robinson bounds.

authors.name: Chao Yin, Vedika Khemani

papers.title: QuantumInputOutput.jl: A Julia framework for input-output theory with quantum pulses and the SLH formalism
papers.summary: The interaction of traveling photonic pulses with quantum systems is a fundamental process for many quantum technologies such as quantum communication, control, and measurement protocols.
