First-principles calculations for NaF at 17~K reveal that the same streaming-induced mode coupling responsible for the perturbative nonlocal correction in the Guyer--Krumhansl (G--K) reduction drives a nonperturbative transformation of the isolated momentum-organized relaxational channel into a dominant complex-conjugate streaming pair. This transformation breaks down the single-relaxational-channel constitutive structure of G--K, while oscillatory temperature dynamics persist below the short-period boundary of its predicted oscillatory window. At shorter periods, heat-current weight redistributes among multiple collision-coupled streaming channels before approaching independently damped phonon streaming. Increasing temperature provides a distinct route beyond hydrodynamics by eliminating the isolated momentum-organized sector, even as oscillatory temperature dynamics persist. Thus, the breakdown of a hydrodynamic constitutive description can reflect a reorganization of heat-current transport rather than the disappearance of oscillatory temperature dynamics, and agreement with temperature measurements alone does not validate the constitutive structure of a reduced theory.

authors.name: Yi Zeng, Jianjun Dong

papers.title: Charge-Transfer Energy Governed by $f$-$d$ Coulomb Interaction in Rare-Earth Systems
papers.summary: The $f$-$d$ Coulomb interaction ($U_{\rm fd}$) plays a central role in low-energy theories describing valence fluctuations and quantum valence criticality in rare-earth systems. In contrast, core-level spectroscopies have conventionally been analyzed using the phenomenological charge-transfer energy ($\Delta$), and the relationship between these two descriptions has remained unclear. Here, we develop a spectroscopic framework demonstrating that the charge-transfer energy contains an $f$-$d$ Coulomb contribution $U_{\rm fd}n_d$ arising from the $d$-electron occupation ($n_d$), leading to the charge-transfer energy $\Delta'$. We apply this framework to the prototypical valence-transition compound YbInCu$_4$ and demonstrate, from combined analyses of core-level photoemission and $L$-edge x-ray absorption spectroscopy, that the observed spectroscopic evolution across the first-order valence transition is consistently interpreted in terms of the variation of $\Delta'$.

authors.name: Norimasa Sasabe, Shinji Watanabe, Akira Yasui, Naomi Kawamura, Kojiro Mimura, Takayuki Uozumi, Masaichiro Mizumaki, Hitoshi Sato

papers.title: Mixed-Sign Kitaev Exchange in Jahn-Teller-Distorted CrI$_2$
papers.summary: Kitaev couplings with ferromagnetic (FM) or antiferromagnetic (AFM) character shape magnetic frustration and phases differently in real materials, yet their coexistence within a single material remains unexplored. Here, we propose Jahn-Teller distortion as a route to realizing such coexistence on inequivalent bonds. First-principles calculations identify monolayer CrI$_2$ as such a system, with AFM and FM Kitaev couplings on the short and long bonds, respectively. These opposite signs are robust against variations in Hubbard $U$, functionals, and strain. A minimal tight-binding model links this sign contrast to Jahn-Teller-split $t_{2g}$ orbitals and their hopping to $e_g$ orbitals. We further adopt the cluster expansion method and develop a realistic machine-learned spin Hamiltonian, which reproduces the experimentally observed proper-screw geometry and propagation direction and reveals highly nonuniform spin rotation, with turning angles ranging from $48.0^\circ$ to $93.9^\circ$. Both proper-screw anisotropy and strong anharmonic spin rotation arise from the mixed-sign Kitaev interaction. These findings not only establish Jahn-Teller distortion as a microscopic route to mixed-sign Kitaev exchange, but also open a new avenue for exploring novel magnetic phases.

authors.name: Shiyan Gao, Zekuo Yang, Chuanhang Chen, Zefeng Chen, Lianchuang Li, Hongjun Xiang, Changsong Xu

papers.title: Spectroscopic evidence for unconventional surface magnetism in the Kondo insulator FeSb$_2$
papers.summary: Kondo insulators have a non-magnetic bulk due to many-body screening of local moment by conduction electrons. However, the surface of these systems has reduced density of itinerant electrons and may experience a Kondo breakdown, leading to recovery of non-zero local moments and possible magnetic order. Here we use angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy to investigate the (010) surface of a $d$-$p$ electron Kondo insulator FeSb$_2$, which is predicted to host a bulk $d$-wave altermagnetic state in the absence of Kondo screening. We find anisotropic splitting on the surface states with a maximum in the $k_z$ direction and a minimum in the $k_x$ direction. The splitting is apparently suppressed with increasing temperature or with Te doping, suggesting that the splitting arises from a magnetic order rather than Rashba effects. Considering the proximity of the bulk to a $d$-wave altermagnetic state and considering the symmetry of the crystal on the surface, we postulate that our observations may be consistent with an emergent surface altermagnetic order. Such an unconventional 2-dimensional magnetic order naturally hosted on an insulating, non-magnet bulk substrate may offer a promising platform for versatile applications.

authors.name: Ke-Jun Xu, Erin E. Fleck Jonathan A. Sobota, Nhat Huy M. Tran, Shuyi Li, Youzhe Chen, Soonsang Huh, Takeshi Kondo, Makoto Hashimoto, Dong-Hui Lu, Zhi-Xun Shen, Dung-Hai Lee, Chunjing Jia, Robert J. Birgeneau

papers.title: Electrical transport of surface-bound electrons on annealed solid neon
papers.summary: We study the dc transport of electrons bound to the surface of solid neon using the conventional Sommer-Tanner method. First, we find that the capacitive cross-talk for the thickness of solid samples on the order of a millimeter varies substantially with the temperature and is strongly affected by the sample annealing. Second, we find that, even for the annealed samples, the observed response of electrons differs significantly from that of the surface-bound electrons on liquid helium and cannot be satisfactorily described by conventional models. Despite this, we managed to extract the resistance of the electron system from its in-phase response and investigate the temperature dependence in a wide range between 1.4 and 20 K. In a high-temperature range between 16 and 20 K, the resistance behavior is found to agree very well with the vapor-atom scattering mechanism, while at lower temperatures it is consistent with temperature-dependent scattering by surface roughness. Our analysis indicates a high electron mobility of electrons on solid neon but two orders of magnitude lower density than expected. These results suggest surface electrons as a suitable probe for studying the morphology of the neon surface but call for a better understanding of the experimental method applicable to such systems.

authors.name: Ka Wing Yip, Tomoyuki Tani, Jui-Yin Lin, Mikhail Belianchikov, Denis Konstantinov

papers.title: Velocity weakening and stick-slip in mean-field depinning with stress overshoots
papers.summary: We study a fully connected depinning model with transient stress overshoots of strength $M$, driven through a spring of stiffness $k_0$. Combining exact stationary relations, linear stability analysis, direct simulations, and population dynamics, we connect the force--velocity characteristic to stick-slip motion and quasistatic avalanche statistics. For $M>1$, two distinct stiffness scales organize the response. At $k_0=k_{\rm w}\equiv M-1$, the stationary characteristic first develops a velocity-weakening branch, whereas $k_0=k_{\rm q}\equiv(M-1)^2/(4M)$ marks the onset of finite-amplitude stick-slip in the quasistatic limit. Their separation produces an intermediate regime in which the quasistatic force converges to a stationary value, whereas finite-velocity driving produces stick-slip below a critical velocity. Quasistatic avalanches in this regime undergo transient amplification and display an excess of large, asymmetric events---"ghost kings"---that remain finite. By contrast, at and below $k_{\rm q}$ the same amplification produces system-spanning "genuine kings" and a finite quasistatic force cycle. These results show how elastic loading dynamically selects among the branches of a reentrant force--velocity relation and clarify the connection between velocity weakening, stick-slip, and runaway avalanches.

authors.name: Adrien Rezzouk, Alberto Rosso

papers.title: Theory of anisotropic magnetotransport beyond the constant relaxation-time approximation in multi-Weyl semimetals
papers.summary: Multi-Weyl semimetals, characterized by Weyl nodes carrying higher monopole charges, provide a platform for exploring topological magnetotransport beyond the conventional Weyl paradigm. Here, we develop a generalized semiclassical Boltzmann framework for multi-Weyl semimetals with arbitrary monopole charge $N$, incorporating the orbital magnetic moment (OMM) into the quasiparticle dispersion and Berry-curvature-modified dynamics, together with a momentum-dependent collision integral accounting for intra- and intervalley scattering. We investigate the longitudinal magnetoconductivity (LMC) and planar Hall conductivity (PHC) for $N=1$, $2$, and $3$, considering both nonmagnetic and magnetic impurity scattering. In the absence of OMM, the LMC remains positive and quadratic in the magnetic field throughout the investigated scattering regime, consistent with conventional chiral-anomaly-assisted transport. Including OMM, however, leads to a sign reversal of the LMC under sufficiently strong intervalley scattering for the $\sigma_0$ and $\sigma_z$ impurity channels. Remarkably, the critical intervalley scattering strength decreases systematically with increasing monopole charge, indicating an enhanced tendency toward negative LMC in higher-charge Weyl systems. Furthermore, we find that the PHC also undergoes a sign reversal for $N=2$ and $N=3$ in the same impurity channels, while remaining positive for $N=1$ within the investigated parameter range. The angular dependences retain their characteristic $\sin^2\gamma$-like and $\sin2\gamma$ profiles for LMC and PHC, respectively, even across the sign reversal. Our results demonstrate that the interplay of Berry curvature, OMM, monopole charge, and impurity scattering can produce qualitatively distinct weak-field magnetotransport responses beyond the conventional chiral-anomaly picture.

authors.name: Azaz Ahmad, Shantanu Mukherjee, Mohd Hashim Raza, Gautham Varma K., Takami Tohyama

papers.title: Free energy profile computations for force-induced melting of a short B-DNA using Jarzynski equality
papers.summary: We initially equilibrate a system of solvated 12-base pair canonical B-DNA of a specified sequence in a state of no external force acting on it (state $A: f=0$). A switching experiment is then performed by pulling one end of the DNA while restraining its other end. The pulling force is taken up to a maximum of 400 pN (state $B$), at a specified constant rate. The non-equilibrium work done W associated with this finite-time process is determined by integrating the extension of the DNA molecule with respect to the applied force. The distribution of the work values $P(W)$ is obtained by repeating the pulling process several times, wherein each time, the process is started with macroscopic state $A$. The free energy profile $\Phi(f)$ is obtained by a suitably devised method from the Jarzynski equality. The conformational space of the DNA is also sampled in an equilibrium method of umbrella sampling by considering the end-to-end length $\xi$ as the reaction coordinate. The associated potential of mean force (PMF) $\Phi(\xi)$ is then computed by invoking the weighted histogram analysis method (WHAM). From the results, we observe that the equilibrium free energy difference between two states, $A$ and $B$, $\Delta F_{AB} ~(=F_B -F_A)$ obtained through both methods, is in close agreement with each other, despite the differences along the profiles $\Phi(f)$ and $\Phi(\xi)$, attributed to their distinct pathways of unzipping.

authors.name: S. Siva Nasarayya Chari, Prabal K. Maiti

papers.title: Exciton-polarons in monolayer semiconductors with drifting electrons
papers.summary: Recent work has demonstrated that the optical absorption of moderately doped two-dimensional semiconductors can be described in terms of exciton-polarons. In this picture, interactions between a photoexcited exciton and a Fermi sea of excess charge carriers split the exciton spectrum into a lower-energy attractive polaron branch and a higher-energy repulsive polaron branch. Due to the negligible in-plane momentum of photons, however, optical measurements probe only exciton-polarons near zero momentum, leaving their finite-momentum physics largely unexplored. Here we propose accessing this regime by measuring the absorption in the presence of an electric bias current. In effect, this displaces the electronic Fermi sea in momentum space, such that an optically active exciton-polaron at rest acquires finite momentum relative to the charge carriers. Using a diagrammatic formulation of the exciton-polaron problem, we derive exact relations between the spectral and quasiparticle properties of current-biased exciton-polarons and their finite-momentum counterparts in an equilibrium Fermi sea. These relations show that absorption measurements with drifting electrons can reconstruct the momentum dependence of the quasiparticle properties for both branches. We estimate that experimentally accessible currents can probe a broad momentum range while remaining within the linear-response regime.

authors.name: Shadman Iqbal, Jesper Levinsen, Meera M. Parish, Dmitry K. Efimkin

papers.title: Growing length scales while approaching the glass transition
papers.summary: Even after decades of research, the nature of the glass transition is controversially debated: Kinetic freezing phenomena, purely local strain-mediated effects, or collective phenomena including a hidden phase transition are usually discussed. In this work, we check reports on clusters of correlated particles in supercooled liquids which grow upon approaching the glass-transition. We specifically focus on dielectric studies providing approximate access to the four-point correlation function, which allows insight into the evolution of so-called amorphous order. Existing temperature-dependent data derived from the three-point correlation function or higher-order dielectric susceptibilities are modeled using the random first-order transition theory combined with the Vogel-Fulcher-Tammann law. This ansatz enables detailed predictions concerning normalized correlation lengths or the number of correlated particles as function of temperature and fragility. It provides a good fit to the experimental data for all materials investigated, including network and molecular glass formers and polymers. We conclude that length scales and corresponding particle numbers determined by the different methods used are at least similar and closely related to those considered by the theory. Moreover, the model predictions on the fragility dependence of the number of correlated molecules are at least approximately fulfilled. Existing criticism concerning an apparent lack of criticality in the temperature dependence of experimental correlation lengths is discussed in terms of this fragility dependence: All available data are well consistent with a hidden phase transition which is best revealed for the most fragile liquids.

authors.name: Alois Loidl, Peter Lunkenheimer, Konrad Samwer

papers.title: Chirality-polarized superradiance induced by quantized orbital-angular-momentum transfer in a ring cavity
papers.summary: We investigate a spin-$1/2$ Bose-Einstein condensate coupled to two counterpropagating modes of an optical ring cavity and driven by Laguerre-Gaussian Raman beams carrying quantized orbital angular momentum (OAM). We demonstrate that competition between OAM-selective Raman scattering channels controls collective superradiance through self-consistent atom--cavity feedback, linking atomic orbital motion to cavity-chirality selection. For unequal OAM transfer, one cavity mode dominates the superradiant response, with its chirality switchable by the Raman pump strengths. In contrast, equal OAM transfer allows both counterpropagating modes to coexist. The resulting chirality-polarized phases support distinct vortex and vortex--antivortex configurations with reconstructed synthetic gauge-field textures. Remarkably, contact interactions can reshape the vortex topology without changing the dominant cavity chirality, revealing distinct responses of atomic and photonic degrees of freedom. The predicted mode switching and vortex ordering can be probed through cavity output and spin-resolved imaging in a proposed $^{87}$Rb implementation. Our results establish quantized OAM transfer as a mechanism for controlling collective cavity emission beyond conventional atomic SOAMC.

authors.name: Yingqi Liu, Jingjun You, Jing Tang, Yuangang Deng

papers.title: Basic introduction to Freidlin-Wentzell theory
papers.summary: Freidlin-Wentzell theory provides the quantitative foundation for rare, noise-induced transitions in stochastic dynamical systems, predicting optimal transition pathways, the exponential scaling of mean escape times, and the long-term occupancy of competing attractors in metastable systems. Here we present a pedagogical, physics-oriented review built around a unified Hamiltonian framework: starting from the infinitesimal generator of a continuous-time Markov process, we derive the local Hamiltonian, obtain the Lagrangian and action functional via Legendre-Fenchel duality, and construct the quasi-potential landscape. We apply this streamlined formalism across weak-noise diffusions, Markov jump processes, weakly interacting particle ensembles, and nonequilibrium stochastic fields, alongside exact conditions for macroscopic coarse-graining. Along the way, we highlight how broken detailed balance drives forward and reverse transition paths apart, explain where local linear stability and Gaussian approximations break down, and assemble multi-attractor landscapes using combinatorial $W$-graphs. Finally, we bridge the analytical theory to modern numerical solvers, including ordered upwind methods, geometric minimum action algorithms, and neural-network parameterizations, and provide an accompanying GPU-accelerated Python package.

authors.name: Jiawei Yan

papers.title: Spectral Moments of the Projected Hubbard Configuration Graph: Connectivity, Exchange, and Virtual Doublons
papers.summary: At strong on-site repulsion, the lowest band of $n$ lattice fermions is the spectrum of the hopping projected onto configurations without double occupancy, $H_\infty=P_0H_tP_0$. We study its moments, for few fermions in the square-lattice Hubbard model and, where the arguments allow, on any finite graph. (1) For spin-independent Hermitian hopping (no on-site terms) on any $N\geq2$-site graph, $\mu_2=\frac{n(N-n)}{N(N-1)}\sum_{i\neq j}|t_{ij}|^2$, for any spin composition. (2) On any finite graph, $\mu_4$ is exactly linear in the same-spin pair count, as four hops permute particles by at most a transposition or 3-cycle; for uniform hopping on a simple graph with $N\geq4$ the slope is $\alpha(N,n)=-8C_4(N-n)(8N-11n-2)/[N(N-1)(N-2)(N-3)]$, fixed by the number $C_4$ of 4-cycles. (3) At large finite $U$, the second-order Schrieffer-Wolff correction is Hilbert-Schmidt orthogonal to $H_\infty$ on every triangle-free graph, so the band variance has no $1/U$ term; its $U^{-2}$ coefficient, an exact trace checked by exact diagonalization, is negative at the low fillings computed. (4) Under a Peierls flux, the exchange slope $\alpha(N,2,\Phi)=-\frac{64}{N-1}\cos\Phi_\square$ ($L\times L$ tori, $L=3$ or $L\geq5$) carries the ordinary charge-$e$ harmonic, while the doublon (bound-pair) hopping acquires a doubled phase, $t_de^{2iA_{ij}}$: the second-order single-doublon Hamiltonian is exactly $\pi$-periodic ($h/2e$) under a boundary twist, and the exact two-electron U-band follows numerically, up to $O((2\lambda)^L/U^{L-1})$. Result (1), the permutation bound, the orthogonality in (3) and the doubled phase are machine-checked in Lean 4. Repulsive binding and the pair charge $2e$ are known; new are the exact moment structure and the derivation of the doubled phase. We make no claim about many-pair phase stiffness, off-diagonal long-range order or superconductivity.

authors.name: D. Souza

papers.title: On the richness of metamaterials generated by recursive cell division
papers.summary: Scale-rich metamaterials are one member of a family of recursive cell divisions, which differ in which cell is cut, where the cut passes and at what angle. We characterise six members of this family through three network mappings, the cell tree, the dual graph of ligaments and junctions, and the frame graph of spans, and through their elastic-wave properties: the effective refractive index n, its isotropy and the band over which it holds. The dual-graph degree law, the mean degree and the age law of the ligaments hit by new ones are the same for every rule, so they cannot distinguish the materials. The cell tree and the cell shapes do differ, and one consequence of them explains the physics: the tail of long spans in the frame graph. With the longest spans as the length scale, the bending part of the inverse squared index follows a single power law across rules, densities and numbers of ligaments, and the same spans set the lowest local resonance and the band edge. The stretching part, which caps the index, is carried by the straight frame lines of the tiling rather than by the division. Random cut angles produce elongated cells and long spans, hence high index and a narrow band; cuts perpendicular to the long axis of the cell keep the cells compact, giving low index and a wide band. Cutting through the centroid instead of a random point bounds the split fraction between 4/9 and 5/9, which removes the area hierarchy without changing the index. The cut angle interpolates continuously between these limits, and the isotropy peaks where the ligament orientations become isotropic while the cells are still compact. In three dimensions the plate and strut divisions are stretching dominated and the index stays low for every rule.

authors.name: Alexei Vazquez

papers.title: Giant Raman Optical Activity in Chiral and Polar Ni$_3$TeO$_6$
papers.summary: Raman optical activity (ROA) measures the difference in Raman scattering intensity for right- and left-circularly polarized light and reflects the chirality of excitations. In solids, ROA is commonly very weak. For the phonons of chiral and polar Ni$_3$TeO$_6$, we find a giant ROA with magnitude 100 times higher than commonly reported for molecules. The systematic analysis based on phonon selection rules allows the chiral and achiral scattering channels to be separated. First-principles calculations of the Raman tensor at finite phonon momentum relate the effect to the phonon modulation of the band-geometric and band-dispersion contributions to optical gyrotropy. This establishes Raman optical activity as a probe of electron--phonon modulation of the band geometry in an insulator.

authors.name: Philipp Stein, Ravi Kaushik, Evgenia V. Komleva, Thomas C. Koethe, Vladimir Tsurkan, Istv\'an K\'ezsm\'arki, Markus Gr\"uninger, Sergey V. Streltsov, Sergey Artyukhin, Paul H. M. van Loosdrecht

papers.title: Angular dependence of the low-temperature skyrmion state in Cu$_2$OSeO$_3$
papers.summary: In the cubic chiral magnet Cu$_2$OSeO$_3$, a low-temperature skyrmion state (LTS) and a metastable tilted conical state emerge for magnetic field along $\langle 100\rangle$, both stabilized by magnetocrystalline anisotropies. We report how these states evolve when the magnetic field is rotated from $\langle 100\rangle$ via $\langle 111\rangle$ to $\langle 110\rangle$. Measurements of the magnetization and the AC susceptibility are combined with broadband microwave spectroscopy on the same cuboid sample at 5\,K. In the microwave spectra, the characteristic gigahertz excitations, notably the counterclockwise gyration mode of the skyrmions, provide a direct indicator of the character of the magnetic states and a qualitative measure of their volume fractions. Both techniques consistently show that signatures of the LTS decrease in strength under rotation and are observed only for field directions within ${\sim}20^{\circ}$ of $\langle 100\rangle$. In this range, the field values at which the skyrmions unwind remain essentially unchanged. In contrast, signatures of the tilted conical state persist up to ${\sim}40^{\circ}$, beyond which the conventional sequence of helical, conical, and field-polarized states is recovered. Thus, the tilted conical state, while being a prerequisite for the nucleation of the LTS under field sweeps, is not sufficient for its formation.

authors.name: Christian Oberleitner, Andreas Bauer, Lukas Heindl, Lin Chen, Aisha Aqeel, Christian H. Back, Hans Huebl, Christian Pfleiderer

papers.title: The microscopic origin of the hysteretic hydrogen adsorption in Double Wall Carbon Nanotubes bundles
papers.summary: In a recent study we reported large hysteretic hydrogen adsorption in samples made out of Double Wall Carbon Nanotubes (DWCNT) at supercritical temperatures (50 K, 77 K and 150 K), a physical behavior of practical interest. Here, we center our efforts in elucidate its physical origin by means of neutron diffraction (ND) and computer simulations. After a detailed theoretical modeling of the ND signal we were able to quantitatively study how the nanostructure of the material reacts to the hydrogen loads. An expansion of the bundle structure with increasing hydrogen load was found. Taking advantage of the translational symmetry of a DWCNT bundle along the nanotube axis, a two dimensional numerical analogue of the system helped us to clarify the microscopic origin of the hysteresis. Two microscopic mechanisms are identified as responsible for the metastable hydrogen adsorption, one structurally static in character, namely, H$_{2}$-load dependent effective energy barriers between interstitials, the other related to the structural deformation, namely, the opening/closing of the channels between interstitials with increasing/decreasing H$_{2}$ loads owing to the concomitant bundle expansion/contraction.

authors.name: Carlos Cabrillo, Ricardo Fern\'andez-Perea, Felix Fern\'andez-Alonso

papers.title: Two channels of magnetic renormalization in the terahertz lattice response of FePS$_{3}$
papers.summary: Interlayer vibrations probe how magnetic van der Waals layers are stacked and coupled. In the zigzag antiferromagnet FePS$_3$, ultrafast experiments show that the interlayer shear couples strongly to the magnetic order, but not how magnetism renormalizes the shear stiffness and damping. Here, using terahertz time-domain spectroscopy, we measure the anisotropic conductivity of FePS$_3$ from 1.6 to 300 K and in fields up to 7 T normal to the layers. We observe absorption bands at 0.6-0.8 and 1.3-2.4 THz that persist into the paramagnetic phase. The lower one is consistent with an interlayer shear resonance; the magnetic order stiffens one of its in-plane components and softens the other, reversing their splitting at the N\'eel temperature. We identify two channels of magnetic renormalization: frequency shifts are confined to the ordered phase, whereas the linewidths of this resonance and most oscillator strengths follow short-range spin correlations persisting well above the transition. The field acts mainly on the higher resonance in one orientation: near 3.2 T, its softening accelerates and its linewidth has a cusp-like minimum, consistent with critical slowing down of a field-induced order parameter. These results give an equilibrium view of spin-shear coupling, which is anisotropic and persists above the N\'eel temperature through short-range correlations.

authors.name: Eduardo D. Stefanato, Nicolas M. Kawahala, Ana Carolina F. de Brito, Jan Plutnar, Zdenek Sofer, Bernardo R. A. Neves, Ingrid D. Barcelos, Felix G. G. Hernandez

papers.title: Multi-symmetry projected coupled cluster theory with triples corrections
papers.summary: Symmetry projection and coupled cluster theory provide complementary descriptions of static and dynamic correlation. We introduce two approximate perturbative triples corrections to spin- and point-group-projected coupled cluster with single and double excitations (PCCSD). The coherent $(T)$ correction combines triples intermediates over the projection grid, whereas $+(T)$ evaluates the conventional triples expression using PCCSD amplitudes. Both recover conventional $(T)$ in the absence of projection. We assess these corrections for N$_2$ and C$_2$ dissociation, $3d$ transition-metal monoxides, and Cr$_2$. Projection improves the singles-and-doubles description and distinguishes selected low-lying symmetry sectors. For the six-monoxide benchmark subset, coherent $(T)$ reduces the PCCSD mean absolute error from $13.4$ to $3.0~\mEh$, achieving accuracy comparable to conventional CCSD(T). Both triples corrections restore the short-bond minimum missing from the PCCSD curves of Cr$_2$, with coherent $(T)$ giving a well depth closer to extrapolated DMRG. In contrast, $+(T)$ provides more balanced N$_2$ and C$_2$ dissociation curves. These results demonstrate the benefits of perturbative triples in PCC, while their system-dependent performance highlights the need for a more systematic treatment.

authors.name: Ruiheng Song, Thomas M. Henderson, Gustavo E. Scuseria

papers.title: Surface-bulk magnetic dichotomy in intercalated transition metal dichalcogenides
papers.summary: Magnetically intercalated transition metal dichalcogenides are layered materials with highly tunable magnetic orders and unconventional transport properties. Here we report a surface-bulk magnetic dichotomy in $\mathrm{M}_{1/3}\mathrm{T}\mathrm{X}_{2}$, in which the surface and bulk favor distinct magnetic orders. In $\mathrm{Fe}_{1/3}\mathrm{Nb}\mathrm{S}_{2}$, angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) results are reproduced by an A-type antiferromagnetic electronic structure, while neutron scattering and bulk DFT+$U$ calculations identify stripe order as the bulk ground state. DFT+$U$ slab calculations resolve this contradiction by showing that relaxation of an Fe-terminated surface reverses the magnetic preference from stripe to A-type order. The same dichotomy recovers the $K$-centered Fermi-surface pockets that are observed in $\mathrm{Co}_{1/3}\mathrm{Nb}\mathrm{S}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{Co}_{1/3}\mathrm{Ta}\mathrm{S}_{2}$ but absent from previous bulk calculations. Notably, the surface-stabilized magnetic phase of $\mathrm{Fe}_{1/3}\mathrm{Nb}\mathrm{S}_{2}$ carries nonrelativistic spin splitting and can exhibit altermagnetic character. These results caution against the general association of ARPES signals with bulk magnetic states in these systems, and suggest surface-bulk magnetic dichotomy as a promising route to realize magnetic phases, including altermagnetism, that are not energetically favored in the bulk.

authors.name: Ke Liao, Wenxin Li, Kelly Dai, Ariel Mazor, Shan Wu, Yu He, Tianyu Zhu

papers.title: Robust Antiferromagnetic Ordering above 500 K in a Family of Bilayer van der Waals Materials
papers.summary: Stabilizing magnetic order above room temperature in layered materials is highly desirable for low-dimensional spintronics applications. However, realizing room-temperature antiferromagnetism in layered magnets remains challenging. Here, we present a layered semiconducting oxyhalide material family, Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$X$_2$ ($X$ = F, Cl, Br), which exhibits robust high-temperature antiferromagnetic ordering. The two-dimensional nature and scalability of this system are demonstrated by atomically resolving the van der Waals gap of Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$Br$_2$ and synthesizing centimeter-scale single crystals of Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$Cl$_2$. Temperature-dependent neutron scattering and magnetization measurements determine their G-type magnetic structure and transition temperature. Remarkably, the N\'eel temperature of Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$F$_2$ ($\sim$580 K) is the highest among all reported layered antiferromagnets. Density functional theory calculations demonstrate that strong nearest-neighbor superexchange interactions along both out-of-plane and in-plane directions, particularly the magnetic couplings along lattice $c$ direction within the bilayer motif, are primarily responsible for the high N\'eel temperatures in Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$X$_2$. In contrast, inter-bilayer spin couplings are negligibly weak, without much influence on the stabilization of the antiferromagnetic order. Therefore, theoretical calculations predict that this robust antiferromagnetic order could persist or even strengthens at room-temperature even at the monolayer limit. Our results highlight iron-based layered oxyhalides as a promising platform for exploring beyond-room-temperature antiferromagnetism in the two-dimensional limit, holding immense potential in areas like information storage and spin-based devices.

authors.name: Tengda Rong, Linxin Wu, Xingke Fu, Anqi Huang, Feiran Shen, Zixian Dong, Jianwei Huang, Hao Li, Benyuan Cheng, Lunhua He, Long Jiang, Kun Cao, Zhen Chen, Meng Wang, Xiang Chen

papers.title: Stabilization of LaH$_{10}$ with Thorium: Superconductivity in (La,Th)H$_{10}$ up to 232 K near 1 Mbar
papers.summary: Ternary lanthanum-based hydrides are among the best high-temperature superconductors. Here we show that substituting La with thorium stabilizes La(Th)H$_{10}$ clathrate structure at $\sim$1 Mbar while only minimally suppressing superconductivity. The resulting cubic (La,Th)H$_{10}$ phase, synthesized from relatively air-stable La$_2$Th, La$_3$Th and La$_5$Th alloys, reaches an onset $\textit{T$_c$}$ = 232 K at 134 GPa, as confirmed by contact resistance measurements. Superconductivity was verified by two independent methods: electrical resistance and contactless radio-frequency measurements under applied magnetic fields at various pressures. Using a record-high pulsed current of 380 mA, we investigated critical phenomena in P6$_3$/mmc-(La,Th)H$_9$ at 173 GPa, which allowed for the experimental determination of a single superconducting gap within the s-wave model: $\Delta(0) = 37 \pm 4.5$ meV and $2\Delta(0)/kT_c = 4.9 \pm 0.6$. The La-Th-H system is chemically rich: in addition to the decahydride and nonahydride mentioned above, we also identified nanocrystalline I4/mmm-(La,Th)H$_4$ (5-6 nm grain size), (La,Th)H$_6$, as well as $hP13$, $cF80$ and $A15$ phases with compositions of (La,Th)H$_{5.75-6.25}$ and $\textit{T$_c$}$ $\approx$ 83 K at 70-80 GPa, and a possible (La,Th)H$_{16}$ polyhydride.

authors.name: Dmitrii V. Semenok, Mikhail A. Volkov, Andrey V. Sadakov, Alexander T. Daniyarkhodzhaev, Alexey S. Usoltsev, Vladimir M. Pudalov, Mikhail I. Volgin, Iurii M. Nevolin, Toni Helm, Di Zhou, Viktor V. Struzhkin, Ivan A. Troyan

papers.title: Calculating correlation functions in integrable spin chains from local conserved charges and currents
papers.summary: We develop a simple algebraic method for calculating correlation functions in integrable spin chains. We introduce current minors, antisymmetrized products of local conserved charge densities and their currents, and prove that their expectation values are determinants of density and current mean values. Decomposing local operators into current minors, we derive factorized formulas for correlation functions in terms of current mean values, valid in any nondegenerate eigenstate. Applying the method to the spin-$1/2$ XXZ chain and, more generally, to every representation of the Temperley--Lieb algebra, we prove previously conjectured factorized formulas for short-distance correlation functions.

authors.name: Kohei Fukai

papers.title: Interface-Selective Extreme Ultraviolet Second Harmonic Generation Away from Linear Absorption Edges
papers.summary: Extreme ultraviolet (XUV) second harmonic generation (SHG) combines interface selectivity with core-level element specificity but has so far been limited to linear absorption edges. Here, we measure XUVSHG from an indium tin oxide capped MoO$_3$/SiO$_2$/Si photovoltaic heterojunction for fundamental energies of 60--76\,eV, below the Si L$_{2,3}$-edge. Where linear absorption is a featureless valence background, we observe a strong, structured XUVSHG response with maxima near 70 and 76\,eV. Layer-resolved first-principles calculations reproduce both maxima and assign them to the Si/SiO$_2$ interface, the 76\,eV peak to the bridging Si monolayer and the 70\,eV peak to the near-interface substrate. Bethe--Salpeter calculations for bulk Si connect the signal to Si 2$p$ excitons at 140--160\,eV. At the Si L$_{2,3}$-edge, the calculated response is instead governed by MoO$_3$-induced asymmetry at the oxide interface. These findings establish off-edge XUV SHG as a powerful approach for selectively probing distinct buried interfaces within complex material heterostructures.

authors.name: Bailey R. Nebgen, Shane W. Devlin, Franky Bernal, Aga Ridhova, James Bullock, Daniel R. Schacher, Jake D. Koralek, Yuya Kubota, Shigeki Owada, Toshihide Sumi, XingYu Su, Iwao Matsuda, Keith V. Lawler, Walter S. Drisdell, Michael W. Zuerch, Craig P. Schwartz

papers.title: A feedback-driven central limit theorem with $q$-Gaussian limits
papers.summary: We establish a central limit theorem, the feedback-driven central limit theorem, for sums whose summands are independent noise variables multiplied by an amplitude that depends on the preceding normalized sum $y$. The summands are martingale differences whose conditional variance, $c+b\,y^{2}$, depends quadratically on $y$, with feedback strength $b$; unlike in the martingale central limit theorem, this conditional variance does not settle to a constant. The noise has finite variance; for positive feedback we assume, as in Lyapunov's theorem, a finite third moment, and for negative feedback bounded noise, so that the conditional variance stays nonnegative. For positive feedback, the normalized sum converges to a Student law, equivalently a $q$-Gaussian with $1<q<2$, independently of the noise distribution. For negative feedback, it converges to a compactly supported density, which is a $q$-Gaussian with $q<1$ when $-\tfrac12<b<0$. The Gaussian law, $q=1$, is recovered at zero feedback, while the Cauchy law, $q=2$, is obtained only as a limiting case, in a triangular array in which the feedback grows slowly with the number of terms. Thus every $q<2$ is obtained for a fixed feedback strength, and $q=2$ as a limit. We further show that the balance identity behind the theorem singles out quadratic feedback: a $q$-Gaussian with $q<2$ satisfies it only for a quadratic conditional variance, and no $q$-Gaussian with $2\le q<3$ satisfies it for any conditional variance. The proofs use the method of moments for negative feedback and a Wasserstein coupling argument for positive feedback, including cases in which the limiting variance is infinite.

authors.name: G. Baris Bagci, Thomas Oikonomou

papers.title: Optical spin Edelstein response of d-wave altermagnets
papers.summary: The momentum-dependent spin splitting and compensated magnetic order in altermagnets offer opportunities for electrical control of spin polarization. We explore the spin Edelstein effect in the frequency domain of a two-dimensional d-wave altermagnet with Rashba spin-orbit coupling. We calculate the spin-velocity susceptibility response function beyond the intraband response regime and find that the interband longitudinal and transverse Edelstein responses are governed by the Zeeman quantum metric and Zeeman Berry curvature, respectively. The density of states presents a logarithmic van Hove singularity at exactly the negative value of the energy below which four disconnected Fermi contours emerge. This defines three distinctive regions for the position of the Fermi level, through which the Edelstein susceptibility tensor displays characteristic spectral features, reflecting the topological change of the Fermi surface. The resulting spin magnetization shows a strong dependence on the driving frequency and on the orientation of the in-plane external electric field. Our results highlight new possibilities for electrical and optical control of the spin Edelstein effect in altermagnets that could find spintronic applications.

authors.name: M. A. Mojarro, R. Carrillo-Bastos, Jes\'us A. Maytorena

papers.title: Logarithmic thermodynamic cost of prediction from rare observations
papers.summary: A memory predicting changes in its environment from rare observations must spend energy on sampling and recording. We consider autonomous chemical memories driven by a sample-and-hold sensor observing an environment that switches at rate gamma, with sampling frequency f<<gamma. An ideal observer with access to the full observation history can retain predictive information proportional to f. However, retaining a finite fraction of this information in an autonomous physical memory requires work of order kBT ln(gamma/f) per sensor change. This additional thermodynamic cost arises from the competing requirements of suppressing false records during long intervals between observations and responding rapidly to new observations. We establish a universal low-power bound on predictive information, which grows at most as P/ln(P_ref/P) with power budget P, uniformly over any finite number of memory states and independently of network topology and memory relaxation times. We further demonstrate that memory architecture determines the attainable scaling. With bounded transition rates and readout from the memory alone, two-state memories are limited to P^2 scaling, whereas a three-state memory is sufficient to attain the optimal logarithmic scaling. Our results establish a fundamental thermodynamic distinction between acquiring information and maintaining a useful record of a changing environment.

authors.name: Andrey V. Dobrynin, Anastasia Stroujkova

papers.title: Oxygens breathe, electrons jump
papers.summary: Electronic transport in polyanionic battery cathodes proceeds through small-polaron hopping between transition-metal sites and is commonly assumed to be tightly coupled to the motion of charge-compensating mobile ions. Using olivine Li$_x$MnPO$_4$ as a prototypical platform, we use first-principles molecular dynamics with extended Hubbard functionals to follow, in real time and at finite temperature, the adiabatic evolution of Mn oxidation states and atomic sublattices. We find that polaron hopping and cation migration are dynamically decoupled: Mn$^{2+}$/Mn$^{3+}$ valence exchanges occur frequently while the intercalated ions remain confined to their sites, and hopping is gated by the local oxygen framework. Freezing the six oxygen atoms of an individual MnO$_6$ octahedron excludes that site from the hopping network, while increasing the fictitious oxygen mass slows down electronic transport. Each valence exchange coincides with a concerted breathing of the donor and acceptor octahedra ($\Delta V \simeq 2$ $\r{A}^3$), with their volume asymmetry crossing zero at the transition, consistent with the Holstein-Marcus coincidence condition. The hopping rate yields an activation energy of $E_a = 0.20 \pm 0.03$ eV, closely matching the elastic energy scale of the two coordination cages ($\lambda_V/4 \approx 0.20$ eV). These results identify the oxygen coordination cage, not the mobile cation sublattice, as the dynamical gate for small-polaron transport: a site can accept the electron only if its cage can breathe, and the barrier is governed by cage elasticity. Selective constraints and mass scaling applied to first-principles dynamics provide a general route to link electronic and lattice degrees of freedom in redox-active materials, opening the door to framework engineering in intercalation and mixed ionic-electronic conductors.

authors.name: Cristiano Malica, Nicola Marzari

papers.title: Self-doped correlated adatom lattices on cubic boron nitride
papers.summary: We survey triangular adatom lattices on the (111) surfaces of cubic boron nitride (cBN) for strongly correlated two-dimensional electron systems. Using density functional theory combined with the constrained random phase approximation and charge self-consistent dynamical mean-field theory, we identify twelve promising candidates. Group-III (group-V) adatoms on the N- (B-)termination realize clean one-band Hubbard systems, while group-III and transition-metal (V, Cr, Mn) adatoms on the B-termination realize two-band Hubbard systems. Importantly, the polar III-V character of cBN induces self-doping by $\pm 1/4$ electron away from integer filling. With strong Hubbard (and Hund's) interactions and small hoppings, most systems are doped Mott insulators. Heavy quasielectrons with mass renormalizations up to 4 and strong local moments up to 2.5 $\mu_B$ put our systems into a regime where unconventional superconductivity on the triangular lattice has been predicted.

authors.name: Niklas Enderlein, Tim Kullick, Henri Menke, Roland Gillen, Janina Maultzsch, Philipp Hansmann

papers.title: Strain-Engineering Giant Pseudo-Electric Fields in Multilayer Graphene
papers.summary: Electromagnetic scalar and vector potentials can be engineered in solids through lattice distortions, providing a versatile means of tuning electronic band structures. The pseudovector component, which generates pseudo-magnetic fields, has received much attention for its ability to realize a zero-field quantum Hall effect. However, the pseudoscalar component, giving rise to pseudo-electric fields to which many electronic systems are intrinsically susceptible, has not yet been experimentally explored. Here, we demonstrate the emergence and profound consequences of the pseudoscalar potential in a multilayer graphene system. Atomic relaxation reconstructs the system into large Bernalstacked domains separated by one-dimensional rhombohedral channels. Within this inter-dimensional system, we achieve the first direct atomic-scale imaging of distinct lattice deformations in graphene under strain. In rhombohedral channels, we observe that the tensile lattice deformation induces giant pseudo-electric fields, producing ultra-flat dispersion with divergent density of states and a large energy gap. This results in enhanced electronic correlations, leading to flat-band instabilities and striped modulation in the density of states that would otherwise require strong external displacement fields. Moreover, the gap opened by the pseudoscalar potential protects topological boundary states that persist in the absence of applied fields. Our results provide a comprehensive atomic-scale characterization of graphene elasticity and direct spectroscopic evidence for the nontrivial pseudo-electric field arising from lattice distortion. More broadly, it provides an intrinsic and tunable pathway to new quantum states

authors.name: Yiwen Liu, Ambikesh Gupta, Adri\'an Ceferino, Youngjoon Choi, Pierre A. Pantale\'on, Zhen Zhan, Suman Sanki, Hari Stoyanov, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Francisco Guinea, Andrea Young, Haim Beidenkopf, Nurit Avraham

papers.title: Phase diagram and lattice structure of interlayer vortices in multilayer Ising superconductors in parallel magnetic fields
papers.summary: In this work, we investigate layered $s$-wave Ising superconductors under an in-plane magnetic field using self-consistent solutions of the microscopic Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations. Comparing bilayer, four-layer, and infinite-layer systems, we determine how the phase diagram and vortex structure evolve with layer number. Compared to standard Ginzburg-Landau treatments, our approach applies over a broader parameter regime and self-consistently resolves the spatial and layer dependence of the gap amplitude without prescribing its form. We find that the field range supporting the conventional Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) phase (defined as having no interlayer vortices) is reduced with increasing layer number and is essentially absent at nonzero magnetic flux in the infinite-layer system, consistent with recent thickness-dependent experiments on multilayer 2H-NbSe$_2$. In the infinite-layer limit, the Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov (FFLO) phase containing interlayer vortices persists to progressively larger in-plane fields as temperature is lowered below the zero-field critical temperature, consistent with the experimentally observed low-temperature enhancement of the upper critical field. The vortex structure also evolves with interlayer hopping: in four-layer systems, for the fluxes and system sizes considered, increasing hopping reorganizes vortices from outer to inner interlayer junctions. At larger hopping, the gap distortion associated with an interior vortex extends to the surface layers, producing gap suppression comparable to that in the interior layers. Representative six-layer calculations show that interior vortices likewise produce a finite, although weaker, modulation of the surface-layer gap. These results highlight layer number and interlayer tunneling as key parameters governing the phase diagram and vortex arrangement in multilayer Ising superconductors.

authors.name: Subhradeep Mahata, Uddalok Nag, J. K. Jain

papers.title: Rashba Effect and Type-III Broken-Gap Band Alignment in MoTe$_2$/HfS$_2$ van der Waals Heterostructures for Tunnel Field-Effect Transistors
papers.summary: Two-dimensional van der Waals heterostructures (vdWHs) based on transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have emerged as promising platforms for next-generation low-power electronics and spintronics. Here, we investigate the structural, electronic, and spin properties of MoTe$_2$/HfS$_2$ vdWHs using first-principles density functional theory calculations. Our results reveal an intrinsic type-III (broken-gap) band alignment, making this heterostructure highly attractive for tunnel field-effect transistor (TFET) applications. In addition, inversion-symmetry breaking at the interface, combined with strong spin-orbit coupling, induces a pronounced Rashba spin splitting around the $\Gamma$ point, accompanied by characteristic helical spin textures. We further show that external vertical electric fields, twist engineering, and both out-of-plane and in-plane strain provide efficient means to tune the band alignment, charge transfer, and Rashba parameters. In particular, electric fields and mechanical strain can drive reversible transitions between type-II and type-III band alignments while simultaneously modifying the Rashba spin texture and the band-to-band tunneling (BTBT) window. The twisted heterostructure with $\theta = 21.79^\circ$ exhibits similar tunability, including strain-induced transitions between distinct band-alignment regimes. These findings establish MoTe$_2$/HfS$_2$ vdWHs as versatile multifunctional platforms combining electrically tunable Rashba spin splitting with controllable type-II/type-III band alignment, offering promising opportunities for next-generation TFETs and spintronic devices.

authors.name: Daniel S. Lopes, Bruno P. e Silva, Diego R. da Costa, Alexandre C. Dias, Rodrigo G. Amorim, Teldo A. S. Pereira, Jeanlex S. de Sousa

papers.title: Sharp bounds on the Eliashberg critical temperature: a comparison principle, convexity in the spectrum, and the Kiessling-Altshuler-Yuzbashyan conjectures
papers.summary: In Eliashberg theory of phonon-mediated superconductivity with vanishing Coulomb pseudopotential, the critical temperature $T_c$ marks the linear instability of the normal state. Kiessling, Altshuler and Yuzbashyan (KAY) characterized it through the top eigenvalue of a compact operator on Matsubara-frequency sequences. They proved that $T_c$ is unique at strong coupling and conjectured $T_c<C(\lambda\langle\omega^2\rangle)^{1/2}$ for every coupling $\lambda$, with $\langle\omega^2\rangle$ the second moment of the normalized phonon spectrum and $C\approx0.1827$ sharp, a bound Leavens stated in 1977 on partly numerical grounds. A preprint by Kondratev, not yet peer reviewed, gives a proof of this bound and of all-coupling uniqueness. We give an independent proof, for every spectrum with finite second moment, based on a comparison principle that is also Kondratev's central step and was proved to first order by Bergmann and Rainer: strengthening the pairing interaction at every Matsubara transfer, strictly at the smallest one, strictly raises the top eigenvalue. At fixed $\lambda$ and $\langle\omega^2\rangle$ a single Einstein mode maximizes $T_c$. Convexity of the top eigenvalue in the spectrum gives sharp bounds on $T_c$ by the moments $\int\omega^n\alpha^2F d\omega$, $0\le n\le1$, including Leavens's zeroth-moment bound $T_c\le c_0\int\alpha^2F d\omega$, $c_0\approx0.231$ numerically, optimal at moderate coupling. All bounds persist under a Coulomb pseudopotential with symmetric cutoff. A prefix decomposition of non-increasing vectors proves a third KAY conjecture, not treated in the preprint. The finite-dimensional core, including that conjecture, is formalized in Lean 4, and two computer-assisted proofs independent of the comparison principle confirm the Einstein bound.

authors.name: Davis Rens

papers.title: Anomalous temperature dependence of the band gap in TiNCl
papers.summary: We report an unusual nonmonotonic temperature dependence of the optical band gap in the layered nitride halide TiNCl, revealed by temperature-dependent photoluminescence (PL) and diffuse reflectance spectroscopy. The band gap, determined from the PL spectra, decreases with increasing temperature at low temperatures, reaches a minimum near 50 K, and then increases at higher temperatures. This behavior contrasts with the monotonic decrease typically observed in conventional semiconductors. The observed temperature dependence is well reproduced by a Bose-Einstein oscillator model with two characteristic phonon energies of approximately 8.9 meV and 1.2 meV. Based on temperature-dependent X-ray diffraction measurements and first-principles calculations using the experimental lattice parameters, we found that the contribution of thermal expansion is negligibly small compared with the observed band-gap variation. Furthermore, first-principles phonon calculations for the optimized crystal structure revealed peaks in the phonon density of states near these two characteristic energies. These results suggest that electron-phonon interactions play an important role in the anomalous temperature dependence of the optical band gap in TiNCl, with low- and higher-energy phonons contributing to the low-temperature decrease and the higher-temperature increase, respectively.

authors.name: Masaru Oda, Taisei Ukon, Yuma Mori, Kazuma Nakamura, Masashi Tanaka, Hisao Kondo, Aishi Yamamoto

papers.title: Efficient Finite-Temperature Krylov Methods Based on Imaginary-Time Evolution
papers.summary: We develop two finite-temperature Krylov methods that construct Krylov subspaces using imaginary-time evolution rather than direct applications of the Hamiltonian. The finite-temperature imaginary-time Lanczos method (FTiTL) applies the Lanczos method to the imaginary-time evolution operator, whereas the finite-temperature imaginary-time Krylov method (FTiTK) constructs a generalized eigenvalue problem using a nonorthogonal Krylov basis. We evaluate the accuracy and computational efficiency of these methods for the square-lattice transverse-field Ising model, using exact diagonalization for $N=16$ and quantum Monte Carlo results for $N=32$ as references. With appropriately chosen imaginary-time steps, both methods achieve higher accuracy than the conventional finite-temperature Lanczos method (FTLM) with fewer local operator applications in the ferromagnetic regime and near the quantum critical point. For $N=32$, FTiTL requires approximately half as many local operator applications as FTLM to achieve a root-mean-square error of $10^{-2}$ or less in the specific heat $C/N$. Furthermore, FTiTK can be implemented using only one state vector of full Hilbert-space dimension, halving the memory required for storing state vectors relative to FTLM.

authors.name: Hiroto Yamamoto, Katsuhiro Morita

papers.title: Bending Rigidity of Smectic Filaments
papers.summary: Many biological and engineered filaments exhibit internal structure or fluidity that alters their elastic behavior. We study the elasticity of microscale filamentous smectic condensates, grown during liquid-liquid crystal phase separation. We use a Fourier analysis of their thermal bend fluctuations to measure their persistence length, which follows a non-classic linear scaling with their cross-sectional area, in contrast to the classic quadratic scaling for elastic filaments. We rationalize this scaling using the Helfrich energy to compute the free energy of bending a filament with internal smectic fluid ordering. Our analysis then provides a direct method to measure the bend modulus K, which quantifies the rigidity of smectic layers; providing the first method to directly measure K for dispersed smectic phases. We quantify the softening of filaments in the presence of shorter alkyl-tail mesogen dopants, decreasing K by up to ~35%. Out results suggest how nanoscale smectic organization and molecular composition determine filament-scale elasticity, informing the control of filament mechanics and self-assembly in biomimetic and engineered materials.

authors.name: Haotian Long, Shamiah A. Williams, Chinedum O. Osuji, Christopher A. Browne

papers.title: Inversion of magnetization anisotropy in low magnetic fields for textured Bi2223 superconductor due to magnetic responses from superconducting crystallites and intercrystalline boundaries
papers.summary: A detailed study of the magnetic anisotropy of a bulk textured high-temperature superconductor Bi2223 has been carried out. In the range of moderate and high fields (up to 1 kOe), the difference {\Delta}M between the upper and lower branches of the magnetization hysteresis loop is larger when the external magnetic field H is parallel to the normal of the texturing plane (H||NTP) than when H is parallel to the texturing plane (H {\perp} NTP). This magnetic anisotropy is typical for such textured superconductors. However, at small values of the maximum applied field Hmax (up to 15 Oe at a temperature T = 78 K), an anomalous inversion of anisotropy has been found: {\Delta}M(H||NTP) < {\Delta}M(H {\perp} NTP). It has been established that in the field range up to ~30 Oe (the first penetration field into Bi2223 crystallites is about 30 Oe at T = 78 K), the magnetic hysteresis is determined only by the magnetic flux trapped in the intercrystallite boundary subsystem. The pronounced platelet shape of the Bi2223 crystallites leads to partial screening of the external field inside the sample when the field is oriented parallel to the crystallite c-axis. The observed inverse anisotropy {\Delta}M(H||NTP) < {\Delta}M(H {\perp} NTP) has been explained by the fact that the effective magnetic field into the intercrystallite boundaries is smaller for the H||NTP orientation than for H {\perp} NTP. Therefore, when the field is oriented H||NTP, a larger external field is required for magnetic flux to penetrate into the sample inner than for the H {\perp} NTP orientation.

authors.name: D. A. Balaev, S. V. Semenov, D. M. Gokhfeld, M. I. Petrov

papers.title: Scaling a Universal Graph Neural Network Force Field to Billions of Atoms on Desk-Side GPUs
papers.summary: Machine-learning force fields are capable of simulating billions of atoms, but usually require high-performance supercomputing clusters. We show that a universal graph neural network force field, ALIGNN-FF, evaluates energies and forces of more than one billion atoms on desk-side computers such as the NVIDIA GB10, which has 128 GB of unified memory, by using a cube-and-halo decomposition. The halo contains every atom within the model's 20 {\AA} receptive field, which makes the result exact. One GB10 holds 216,000 atoms with forces as a single graph. The cube-and-halo decomposition removes this limit, enabling an evaluation of 2 billion atoms on nine GB10s. We also demonstrate three case studies: a billion-atom polycrystal, a 102-million-atom microelectronic gate stack and a 1.07-million-atom satellite tobacco mosaic virus in water. This brings single-point evaluations at experimentally relevant sizes within reach of one research group. The code is available at: https://github.com/atomgptlab/scalingmat.

authors.name: Jaehyung Lee, Kamal Choudhary

papers.title: Nitrogen Defect Coupling in Epitaxial LaFeO3 From Structural Reconstruction to Water Oxidation
papers.summary: Earth-abundant ABO3-type perovskite oxides provide a versatile platform for understanding how anion chemistry and defects govern electrocatalytic behavior. Here, we use epitaxial LaFeO3-xNy thin films to reveal how dilute N incorporation (<0.8% N/O) couples to defect formation, structural reconstruction, and water oxidation. Nitrogen-plasma-assisted pulsed laser deposition introduces N and is accompanied by reduced oxygen content, localized Fe-metal exsolution, and pronounced lattice expansion, while preserving predominantly Fe3+ in the bulk of the film. Ab initio calculations identify a plausible charge-balanced extended defect configuration involving coupled oxygen and Fe vacancies with substitutional N incorporation, reproducing the experimentally observed lattice expansion while preserving the bulk-average Fe oxidation state. The resulting electronic-state redistribution is accompanied by substantially modified electrical transport and nearly two orders of magnitude higher initial oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity than undoped LaFeO3. Under OER conditions, however, the highly active as-grown state is metastable: near-surface N depletion and Fe0 oxidation/removal accompany rapid initial activity decay toward a quasi-steady state. pH-dependent kinetics and post-OER anion redistribution are consistent with possible lattice-oxygen participation. These results establish relationships among dilute anion incorporation, coupled defect reconstruction, electronic properties, and electrochemical behavior in perovskite oxides.

authors.name: Le Wang, Shan Lin, Min-Ju Choi, Krishna P. Koirala, Mark E. Bowden, Jeffrey A. Dhas, Zihua Zhu, George E. Sterbinsky, Tiffany C. Kaspar, Chongmin Wang, Scott A. Chambers, Ho Nyung Lee, Peter V. Sushko, Yingge Du

papers.title: Molecular-orbital origin of weak orbital ferromagnetism and anomalous Hall effect in a trimerized kagome antiferromagnet
papers.summary: We reveal the molecular-orbital origin of weak orbital ferromagnetism and the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) induced by noncollinear spin order in a trimerized kagome lattice. By transforming to the molecular-orbital basis of an isolated trimer in the double-exchange regime, we derive an effective low-energy model for the states with opposite orbital angular momenta $m= \pm 1$ subject to an effective Zeeman field arising from spin chirality and spin-orbit (SO) coupling. In this representation, the kagome-lattice problem maps onto a triangular lattice of trimers, while the nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor hoppings of the original lattice generate complex hopping amplitudes between neighboring trimers. This formulation provides a transparent picture of how spin chirality and SO coupling can be recast as an effective Zeeman field that lifts the degeneracy of the $m= \pm 1$ states, breaks time-reversal symmetry, and thereby gives rise to weak orbital ferromagnetism and the AHE. The resulting phase diagram includes metallic phases, topologically trivial insulating phases, as well as several topological phases characterized by nonzero Chern numbers and the quantum anomalous Hall effect. We further identify an alternative route to time-reversal-symmetry breaking and orbital magnetization, driven by an emergent gauge field arising solely from complex inter-trimer hoppings and requiring no effective Zeeman field.

authors.name: I. V. Solovyev

papers.title: Role of crystal-field degrees of freedom in square and rectangular skyrmion lattices in noncentrosymmetric tetragonal magnets
papers.summary: We investigate the role of crystal-field degrees of freedom in stabilizing square and rectangular skyrmion lattices in a noncentrosymmetric localized-moment model on a square lattice. The magnetic phases are determined using self-consistent mean-field calculations. We first consider a single crystal-field doublet with exchange and polar-type Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interactions. We find square skyrmion lattices with distinct magnetic periods, as well as a rectangular skyrmion lattice that spontaneously breaks the in-plane fourfold rotational symmetry. Their stability and field-induced phase sequences are strongly controlled by the crystal-field wave function, including reentrant behavior of the rectangular phase. Second-neighbor exchange further modifies the competition among these states. When a second crystal-field doublet is retained, additional rectangular skyrmion lattices with distinct modulation patterns emerge, together with axial single-$Q$ states and various double-$Q$ states. These results demonstrate that crystal-field degrees of freedom provide a microscopic mechanism for tuning the stability, spatial symmetry, and topology of multiple-$Q$ magnetic states.

authors.name: Cong Guan, Yan S. Zha, Satoru Hayami

papers.title: Intertwined Spin Chirality and Weyl Topology Driven Giant Hall Responses in Nd$_{4}$Sb$_3$
papers.summary: Magnetic Weyl materials offer a unique platform for coupling magnetic order with real- and momentum-space topology, yet their simultaneous manifestation in a single material remains uncommon. Here, Nd$_4$Sb$_3$ is established as a highly spin-polarized magnetic Weyl semimetal exhibiting intertwined anomalous and topological Hall responses. Nd$_4$Sb$_3$ orders ferromagnetically below $T_{\mathrm{C}}\sim72$ K and undergoes spin reorientation near 42 K into a non-coplanar magnetic state. A large topological Hall resistivity of $\sim3.9 \mu\Omega$ cm and anomalous Hall conductivity reaching $\sim1170$ S cm$^{-1}$ are observed. First-principles calculations identify an energetically preferred non-coplanar state with finite local scalar spin chirality, providing a microscopic route to the real-space Berry phase underlying the topological Hall effect. Calculated exchange interactions reveal dominant ferromagnetic exchange together with anisotropic exchange and finite Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interactions, while Monte Carlo simulations yield a magnetic transition near 78 K, close to the experimental $T_{\mathrm{C}}$. Concurrently, magnetic reconstruction profoundly reshapes the reciprocal-space topology, increasing the number of Weyl-point pairs from 42 in the collinear ferromagnetic state to 115 in the non-coplanar state. Berry-curvature calculations yield an intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity of $\sim983$ S cm$^{-1}$ at the experimentally determined carrier concentration, closely reproducing the experimental intrinsic contribution of $\sim990$ S cm$^{-1}$. These results establish Nd$_4$Sb$_3$ as a compelling platform where magnetic reconstruction intertwines real-space spin chirality with momentum-space Weyl topology.

authors.name: Anu, Subhasmita Kar, Bhagyashree Pol, Debarghya Dutta, Aftab Alam, P D Babu

papers.title: Excitonic magnetism and competing valence bond solid instabilities in $d^4$ ruthenium compounds
papers.summary: Spin-orbit entangled $d^4$ Mott insulators serve as a rich playground for unconventional magnetism and competing quantum electronic ground states. Intra-ionic spin-orbit coupling $\lambda_{\rm{SOC}}$ generates a non-magnetic $J_{\rm{eff}} = 0$ singlet ground state separated from an excited $J_{\rm{eff}} = 1$ triplet. The effective intra-atomic gap ${\Delta}_{\rm{eff}}$ between the ground state and lowest excited state is determined by $\lambda_{\rm{SOC}}$ and non-cubic crystal field ${\Delta}_{\rm{cf}}$. The intersite magnetic exchange $J_{\rm{ex}}$ induces dispersion of the excited $J_{\rm{eff}} = 1$ triplet. When the triplet bandwidth $W_{\rm{t}}$ overcomes ${\Delta}_{\rm{eff}}$, the system undergoes long-range magnetic ordering which is viewed as a condensation of spin-orbit excitons and called excitonic magnetism. In this review, we systematically survey representative $d^4$ ruthenium compounds across four distinct structural connectivities of Ru-ligand octahedra, from K$_2$RuCl$_6$ with isolated octahedra, corner-sharing perovskite Ca$_2$RuO$_4$, edge-sharing honeycombs, to corner-sharing pyrochlores, and map them onto a conceptual parameter axis of $W_{\rm{t}} / {\Delta}_{\rm{eff}}$. We demonstrate that $d^4$ ruthenium compounds not only represent evolution from a $J_{\rm{eff}} = 0$ Mott state to excitonic magnetism but encompass a broader competition of diverse electronic phases arising from spin-orbit coupling, exchange interactions, electron hopping, crystal field and bond covalency inhabiting similar energy scales. Near excitonic quantum critical point, where $W_{\rm{t}} \sim {\Delta}_{\rm{eff}}$, lattice geometry and chemical bonds of constituent atoms play a decisive role in selecting the electronic ground state, frequently driving valence bond solid formation that pre-empts excitonic quantum criticality.

authors.name: Aleksandra Krajewska, Tomohiro Takayama, Hidenori Takagi

papers.title: Kinetic and Thermodynamic Limits of Sodium Pore Filling in Hard Carbon
papers.summary: The low-voltage plateau-like capacity of hard carbon anodes is widely regarded as a key signature of sodium storage in closed pores, often defining the performance of Na-ion batteries. Here, we combine first-principles calculations with a grand canonical Monte Carlo pore-filling model to show that Na storage in closed pores is not governed by a single equilibrium-plateau mechanism but by a distribution of pore-specific thermodynamic and kinetic activation processes. Thermodynamically, the voltage at which Na pore filling becomes favorable decreases with increasing pore size. Kinetically, pore filling involves Na nucleation, coalescence, growth, and bulk diffusion. While small pores fill rapidly, large pores exhibit both a smaller thermodynamic stimulus and significant kinetic limitations. Nucleation can be accelerated by introducing defects at the pore walls, although an excessively high defect concentration slows bulk diffusion. This work shows that not all closed pores contribute equally to Na storage: some may be thermodynamically favorable but kinetically inactive under realistic charge/discharge rates. Because of this, the inverse design of hard carbon electrodes should target a kinetically accessible pore-size and defect-density window that balances high plateau-like capacity with fast-charging performance.

authors.name: Ihor Radchenko (Centre of Excellence ENSEMBLE3 Sp. z o. o), Andr\'es Felipe Usuga (Centre of Excellence ENSEMBLE3 Sp. z o. o), Yuxin Tang (Fuzhou University), Oleksandr I. Malyi (Qingyuan Innovation Laboratory)

papers.title: Multiple moir\'e polarization textures in twisted trilayers
papers.summary: Twisted van der Waals layers exhibit nontrivial polarization textures from moir\'e-modulated stacking and the inherited sliding ferroelectricity. However, in any twisted bilayer, the topology of polarization texture is essentially fixed due to the inherent twist-stacking landscape for a given material. Here, this constraint is overcome in some twisted trilayers, where the relative moir\'e phase emerges as an additional structural degree of freedom. Using CrI$_3$ and BN as representative sliding ferroelectrics with distinct symmetries, it is clarified how the relative moir\'e phases reshape the trilayer stacking landscapes and tune the net polarization texture by layer sliding. The multiple moir\'e polarization textures can be attributed to the interference of original moir\'e patterns of the two bilayer subsystems.

authors.name: Haoshen Ye, Ying Zhou, Shuai Dong

papers.title: Vortex solitons in spin-orbit-coupled atomic-molecular condensates
papers.summary: In our previous study of a three-dimensional (3D) atomic-molecular Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) with quadratic nonlinearity and spin-orbit coupling (SOC), stable solitons are realized as semi-vortex (SV) or mixed-mode (MM) states, with SOC applied solely to the atomic component. In the SV state, the molecular part forms a pure vortex, while the atomic part remains a hybrid of fundamental and vortex modes. This prevents the overall self-bound state from achieving a fully pure vortex configuration, with the total vortex component always less than $100\%$. Here, we extend the study to two dimensions (2D) and uncover a qualitatively different behavior: purely quadratic 2D systems support not only ground-state (GS) SV solitons, but also higher-order excited-state (ES) solitons that are genuine full vortices (a feature absent in the 3D counterpart). For both GS and ES solitons, stable vortex states exist only when the SOC strength $\lambda$ exceeds a minimum threshold $\lambda_{\min}$, which increases monotonically with $S_1$. Conversely, the critical detuning $\alpha_c$ decreases monotonically with $S_1$, indicating that higher-order vortices are more susceptible to destabilization. For $\lambda < \lambda_{\min}$, the system forms MM states instead of vortex solitons. Our results demonstrate that dimensional reduction to 2D enables the emergence of pure-vortex excited states, establishing a new pathway for stabilizing high-charge topological excitations in ultracold molecular gases.

authors.name: Chao Kong, Jinqing Li, Chunfeng Huang, Yijia Zhu, Zhonghua Li, Jingwen Li, Huiwen Xiang, Yuzhen Tang, Zhenwang Li, Yue Liang, Haiming Deng, Gui-hua Chen, Zhiwei Fan

papers.title: Optical writing of Dzyaloshinskii N\'eel-type skyrmions
papers.summary: Ultrashort laser pulses offer a route to write nanoscale topological magnetic textures for information processing. Magnetic skyrmions are prototypical examples, yet optically generating them with controlled position, type, and, in particular, chirality remains challenging. This challenge arises because magnetic dipolar interactions, which often drive skyrmion formation, preserve the degeneracy between opposite chiralities, leaving no uniquely selected spin configuration. Here, we show that in an ultrathin Co/Pt film, sequences of picosecond circularly polarized laser pulses can write N\'eel-type, fixed-chirality skyrmions stabilized solely by the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction. Combining Lorentz transmission electron microscopy and magneto-optical microscopy, we comprehensively reconstruct their internal spin structure across multiple length scales, ranging from nanometres to micrometers. Using asymmetric skyrmion-expansion measurements, we determined the sign and magnitude of the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and identified the written chirality. Our findings connect deterministic optical writing with the controlled spin structure of skyrmions, advancing optical control of topological textures for opto-spintronic applications.

authors.name: Dinar Khusyainov, Lukas K\"orber, Sheng Li, Rein Liefferink, Thibaud Denneulin, Andr\'as Kov\'acs, Fabian Kammerbauer, Robert Fr\"omter, Mathias Kl\"aui, Dmytro Afanasiev, Alexey Kimel, Johan H. Mentink, Rafal E. Dunin-Borkowski, Theo Rasing

papers.title: Noise-induced manifolds: reduction of slow--fast SDEs to switching processes
papers.summary: When constituents copy one another, as in reaction networks, collective behaviour and opinion dynamics, the noise of copying vanishes at consensus and can make a system bistable. More generally this noise vanishes on whole manifolds, along which slower variables keep moving and set the switching rates, yet no general method derives these switching dynamics. Here we reduce slow--fast stochastic differential equations whose fast noise acts in a single direction to a switching diffusion or piecewise-deterministic Markov process (PDMP), using the absorption probabilities of the fast noise in place of an invariant measure, and derive a first-order correction for the finite duration of switches. For the two-species Togashi--Kaneko model the reduction recovers our earlier PDMP, and the correction captures how the stationary composition depends on the timescale separation. In a model of foraging ants with a depleting food source, the hazard of leaving a source rises through every stay, which makes the colony unlikely to leave a source soon after arriving there.

authors.name: Jeremy R. Worsfold, Patrick Ryan, Richard G. Morris

papers.title: Model-free stiffness measurement of microscale soft contacts by far-field traction force microscopy
papers.summary: The microscale stiffness of soft materials governs their contact mechanics, adhesion and friction, yet it is surprisingly difficult to measure. Micro or nanoindentation is typically used, but extracting stiffness from these measurements requires using contact mechanics models (e.g. JKR), whose assumptions often break down for soft adhesive contacts. Here, we introduce far-field traction force microscopy (FF-TFM) to extract stiffness without using any contact model. We drag a colloidal probe mounted on an atomic-force microscope across a soft surface, measuring the friction force while imaging the displacements of fluorescent tracers on the substrate. Far from the contact, in the elastic limit, these lateral displacements depend solely on the friction force and the substrate stiffness, and fitting them with the point-force solution thus gives the substrate's Young's modulus directly. We successfully match bulk rheology moduli with FF-TFM for six different silicone elastomers, where JKR fits to indentation data underestimate moduli by as much as 40\% of their bulk values. Our approach also enables tracking how the probe slips across the surface. We find that soft contacts can "pre-slip" with no detectable signature in the force signal, unlike stiffer contacts. FF-TFM thus offers a contact-model-free route to measuring microscale stiffness and slip behavior in soft materials.

authors.name: Keumkyung Kuk, Shivaprakash N. Ramakrishna, Nancy A. Burnham, Robert W. Style, Lucio Isa

papers.title: Delay-induced anomalous density-polarization relation in chiral active matter
papers.summary: Aligning active matter can spontaneously exhibit diverse forms of ordered collective motion, and higher local density is generally expected to enhance local polarization. Meanwhile, delays in agents' responses are widespread in real active systems, raising the question of how delayed alignment affects collective motion and, in particular, whether higher local density still strengthens polar order. Here, using a chiral active particle (CAP) model with delayed alignment, we uncover a counterintuitive anomalous density-polarization relation (DPR) within droplets: the local polarization first increases and then decreases with increasing local density. Analysis of the deviation-angle dynamics reveals a delay-induced supercritical discrete Hopf bifurcation. Noise-sustained oscillations before the bifurcation and self-sustained oscillations afterward broaden the deviation-angle distribution and reduce polarization.
