Increasing the delay shifts the bifurcation to lower densities, enhancing the anomalous DPR in agreement with simulations. Using the nonequilibrium landscape-flux theory, we further identify the nonequilibrium flux as the dynamical origin of the anomalous DPR. Our findings not only establish time delay as a control knob for collective behavior in chiral active matter, but also offer a useful analytical perspective on anomalous density-order relations in other nonequilibrium systems exhibiting collective order.

authors.name: Dongrun Jian, Jie Su, Jun Wang, Jin Wang

papers.title: Polymorphism and crystal suppression in symmetric mixtures with entropic interactions
papers.summary: We investigate the phases of a binary mixture of hard spheres with equal diameter and negative non-additivity, favoring hetero-coordination in dense samples. By performing extensive swap Monte Carlo simulations, we show that in an interval of small non-additivities, close to the eutectic point, the mixture fails to crystallize and the compressed fluid gets stuck in an amorphous state. The onset of glass at intermediate compositions is associated with the competition between FCC and B2 (CsCl-type) crystal structures. As the propensity of particles to hetero-coordinate grows further, however, the B2 crystal gives way to a B1 (NaCl-type) crystal at equimolarity, and again the mixture orders for all compositions. We argue that this happens because of the underlying FCC symmetry of the B1 crystal. These results, pertaining to a model with excluded-volume interactions only, point to the key role of entropy in generating amorphous structures in multi-component metallic, inorganic, and soft-matter glass formers.

authors.name: Santi Prestipino, Giuseppe Pellicane, Enrique Lomba, Franz Saija

papers.title: Dynamical theory of the East model. I. A review on the Zwanzig-Mori projection-operator formalism
papers.summary: The East model is a paradigmatic kinetically constrained spin model in one dimension that exhibits glassy dynamics. This review surveys the progress on the theoretical description of the dynamics of the East model, focusing on the spin time correlation function and the relaxation time. We summarize rigorous results on the super-Arrhenius scaling of the relaxation time in the low-temperature limit. We then present a unified derivation of the Zwanzig-Mori projection-operator formalism for both the fluctuation and domain bases. Within this formalism, an infinite hierarchy of coupled equations for the time correlation function and memory kernels emerges---a structure reminiscent of generalized mode-coupling theory developed for supercooled liquids. We review the analytical approximations obtained by truncating or closing the hierarchy at first or second orders and compare them against Monte Carlo simulations. Although these approaches perform reasonably at moderate temperatures, they universally fail in the low-temperature regime: mode-coupling closure schemes in the fluctuation basis introduce spurious ergodicity-breaking transitions, while truncations in the domain basis discard slower modes and fail to capture the asymptotic divergence of the relaxation time. The loss of analytical tractability beyond second order remains the central obstacle, underscoring the fundamental difficulty of describing hierarchical relaxation even in this ``simplest'' model of glassy dynamics.

authors.name: Chong Zha, Yuliang Jin

papers.title: Altermagnetism in moir\'e quasicrystals
papers.summary: Altermagnetism is a collinear compensated magnetic phase with zero net magnetization and momentum-dependent spin polarization. Quasicrystalline altermagnetism extends altermagnetism beyond periodic crystals, with noncrystallographic symmetries allowing high-order spin polarization patterns. Here, we propose a symmetry-based approach to realizing quasicrystalline altermagnetism by twisting collinear magnetic layers. Specifically, we demonstrate that the $30^{\circ}$-twisted honeycomb lattice bilayers form the dodecagonal quasicrystals supporting an $i$-wave altermagnetic phase. We further find that $45^{\circ}$-twisted bilayers preserving fourfold rotational symmetry support a mirror-driven $l$-wave phase with eight nodal lines. We characterize these altermagnetic patterns through plane-wave-projected spin-resolved spectral functions and spin-resolved conductances. Our work provides a systematic route to high-angular-order quasicrystalline altermagnetism through twist engineering.

authors.name: Zi-Ming Wang, Rui Chen, Dong-Hui Xu

papers.title: A tunable multi-gated platform for superlattice engineering in bilayer graphene
papers.summary: Periodic potentials with length scales much larger than crystal lattice constants can generate low-energy electronic minibands. While small-angle twisted van der Waals heterostructures have been widely used to realize such physics, correlated phases are often limited by twist-angle inhomogeneity, strain, and disorder. Here, we investigate high-quality Bernal bilayer graphene placed on a patterned graphite gate, featuring a triangular array of holes, forming a new class of "gate-engineered" superlattices tunable through three independent electrostatic gates. Near the charge neutrality point, we observe insulating states characteristic of miniband formation. Temperature-dependent transport reveals activated gaps consistent with theory, and Hall measurements indicate charge-carrier inversion. Notably, the superlattice can be reconfigured electrostatically using various gate combinations, enabling flexible band-structure design without mechanical twisting. The results highlight a new route to band engineering, potentially extendable to complex periodic structures that are untenable in natural materials.

authors.name: Saisab Bhowmik, Satyarth Srivastav, Aditya Mehta, Robin Bajaj, Suvronil Datta, Rohit S Bhandari, Nikhlesh S. Mehta, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Manish Jain, Hridis K. Pal, U. Chandni

papers.title: Hund physics in the quarter-filled two-band Hubbard-Kanamori model: Crystal-field splitting and non-local Correlations
papers.summary: We address the effect of crystal-field splitting and non-local correlations in the quarter-filled two-orbital Hubbard-Kanamori model. The role of the Hund's coupling in this configuration is not obvious since the atomic ground state has only one electron per site. Yet, previous works identified fingerprints of the Hund's coupling defining a weak Hund's metal at least at finite temperature. Using single-site dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) and two-site cellular DMFT based on a selected configuration-interaction solver we investigate the zero-temperature properties of the weak Hund's metal. Within DMFT we draw the boundary for the weak Hund's metal, which is consistent with previous finite-temperature results. Interestingly, we find that the fingerprints of the Hund's coupling are quite robust to the lifting of the orbital degeneracy and they survive up to splittings of a quarter of the bandwidth, well beyond those at which a two-stage Kondo screening disappears. Including non-local correlations in cluster DMFT demonstrates the robustness of the single-site DMFT picture, even if Mott localization occurs at smaller interactions. In the metal the intersite correlations are weak and insensitive to $J$, while in the localized state we find nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic, antiferro-orbital correlations that are manifest also in the mutual information between sites.

authors.name: Diego Florez-Ablan, Carlos Mejuto-Zaera, Massimo Capone

papers.title: Large pseudo-orbital magnetic moment of magnons in CrI$_3$ nanotubes
papers.summary: Recently discovered CrI$_3$ nanotubes are expected to host unusual radial magnetic order states, on account of the strong out-of-plane magnetic anisotropy of the two-dimensional parent material. The detection of these peculiar magnetic states is challenging, and motivates the quest for unique features that can be probed experimentally. Using linear spin-wave theory, we show that an axial magnetic field tilts the radial phase into a conical one that threads the tube with an Aharonov-Bohm flux for magnons. This flux endows magnons with a pseudo-orbital magnetic moment, reaching approximately six Bohr magnetons, three times conventional magnon spin moment, and therefore detectable through magnon spectroscopy, providing a smoking gun for the radial and conical magnetic order in CrI$_3$ nanotubes.

authors.name: David Sanz (Universidad de Alicante, San Vicente del Raspeig, Spain), J. Fern\'andez-Rossier (Universidad de Alicante, San Vicente del Raspeig, Spain, International Iberian Nanotechnology Laboratory, Braga, Portugal)

papers.title: Orbital-dependent electronic correlations and single-band character in layered palladates
papers.summary: Layered palladates provide a $4d$ platform for examining electronic correlations in materials with cuprate-like structural and orbital characteristics. Using fully charge-self-consistent density functional theory plus dynamical mean-field theory, we investigate the orbital- and layer-resolved electronic structures of LaPdO$_2$, RbSr$_2$PdO$_3$, BaLaPdO$_2$Cl$_2$, La$_4$Pd$_3$O$_8$, and La$_5$Pd$_4$O$_{10}$. Under the conditions studied, all compounds remain metallic, with low-energy states dominated by the Pd-$d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbital. This orbital exhibits stronger mass renormalization than the Pd-$d_{z^2}$ orbital. LaPdO$_2$ and BaLaPdO$_2$Cl$_2$ show moderate correlations, whereas RbSr$_2$PdO$_3$ is more weakly correlated. Both the trilayer La$_4$Pd$_3$O$_8$ and quadlayer La$_5$Pd$_4$O$_{10}$ remain weakly correlated, with similar Pd-$d_{x^2-y^2}$ mass enhancements and little difference between inner- and outer-layer Pd sites. Among the structures studied, BaLaPdO$_2$Cl$_2$ is closest to a cuprate-like single-band description, whereas RbSr$_2$PdO$_3$ retains an additional electron pocket with Pd-$d_{z^2}$ character. These results establish a comparative picture of weak to moderate, orbital-dependent electronic correlations in layered palladates.

authors.name: Jing-Xuan Wang, Jia-Ming Wang, Rong-Qiang He, Zhong-Yi Lu

papers.title: Moir\'e Excitons in a Chern Ferromagnet
papers.summary: Recent experiments have established excitonic optical resonances as powerful probes and control knobs of moir\'e Chern ferromagnets. However, the microscopic nature of excitons formed on such interaction-driven, time-reversal-symmetry-broken ground states remains largely unexplored. In this paper, using a Gutzwiller plus Bethe-Salpeter equation framework, we investigate twisted bilayer MoTe2 at hole filling {\nu}_h=1 and identify two near-infrared Chern-ferromagnet excitons (CFEs) selectively coupled to opposite circular polarizations. Strong electron-hole interactions markedly enhance their energy separation and drive a pronounced momentum-space reconstruction of the emergent X- state, beyond the quasiparticle-transition picture. We further find that this reconstruction enhances the interlayer electron-hole character of X-, giving rise to a giant quadratic Stark response. These findings reveal the nontrivial interplay between electron-electron correlations and electron-hole interactions underlying CFE formation, providing optical fingerprints of moir\'e Chern-ferromagnetic order and a microscopic basis for its optical control.

authors.name: Shiyu Peng, Yifan Wang, Peiyao Qin, Yixuan Liu, Xi Dai, Chen Hu

papers.title: Low-energy states of a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain connected perpendicularly to a metallic lead
papers.summary: Recently, Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chains (SSHCs) coupled to metallic leads have attracted attention. In particular Mart\'{\i}nez {\it et al.} [Phys. Rev. Res. {\bf 8}, 043118 (2026)] studied a topological SSHC connected at one of its ends perpendicularly to a metallic lead modeled by a tight-binding chain. Here, we extend their results by incorporating the finite-size splitting of the end modes of the isolated SSHC, which are determined analytically with high accuracy. We also derive simple analytical expressions, valid in the low-energy regime, for the zero-temperature conductance through the lead and the relevant spectral densities. We find that, when the chemical potential coincides with that of the half-filled SSHC, the conductance reaches its maximum value, equal to that of the lead in the absence of the SSHC. By contrast, the conductance vanishes when the chemical potential is shifted by an amount equal to half the end-mode splitting.

authors.name: A. A. Aligia

papers.title: A Density Functional Tight Binding Model for Rapid Screening of Spin-Orbit-Coupling-Driven Topological Properties in Bismuth
papers.summary: We present a transferable Density Functional Tight Binding (DFTB) model for bismuth with explicit spin-orbit coupling that enables exploration of the structural degrees of freedom governing topological properties with minimal computational resources. We have used our DFTB model to run high-throughput calculations at a scale that would be significantly more expensive with standard Kohn-Sham Density Functional Theory (DFT) to determine a strain-buckling map of electronic and topological properties for bismuthene, where we identify regions of band gap closure and band inversion as a function of structural parameters. We show that our approach yields an accurate band structure for the rhombohedral phase, where small band gaps exist at or near time-reversal-invariant momentum (TRIM) points. We then demonstrate the transferability of our model to bismuth properties not included in our training data through determination of the rhombohedral phase phonon density of states and energetic ordering of additional bismuth solid phases. Finally, we have validated our topological predictions through comparison to DFT results for the optimized bilayer geometries, a band inversion order parameter, and the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant as a function of monolayer unit cell length. Our efforts establish DFTB as a rigorous approach for topological characterization while yielding approximately three orders of magnitude increase in computational efficiency relative to DFT. Our model can thus serve as a computational tool for topological materials discovery by enabling large-scale computational screening to address the potentially complex relationship between physical-chemical properties and the resulting topological classification.

authors.name: Nir Goldman, Ben Hourahine

papers.title: A Free Energy Approach to Modelling Disordered Hyperuniform Patterns
papers.summary: We present a free-energy-based approach for modelling disordered hyperuniform patterns. Specifically, we devise a phase-field crystal model with a correlation kernel that simultaneously selects for a continuous range of degenerate wave modes. At small wave vectors, we construct the correlation function by inverting the Ornstein-Zernike relation to approximate the structure factor of a hyperuniform pattern. Our model demonstrates a crossover between liquid, crystalline, quasicrystalline, and long-lived disordered states depending on the specified free energy parameter and driving force. We show that, for a fixed driving force, the specific structures and wave vectors selected by the density field can be controlled by modulating the width of the correlation kernel. Furthermore, we show that the scaling of the low-wave-vector region of the correlation function can accurately reproduce a specified hyperuniform exponent, independently of the structural properties at larger wave numbers. Our results establish a free-energy-based framework for describing disordered hyperuniform states, demonstrating and enabling independent control over structural selection and long-wavelength density correlations.

authors.name: Alex Mamaev, Enno Igel, Axel Voigt, Marco Salvalaglio

papers.title: Vortex states in submicron titanomagnetite particles
papers.summary: Numerical simulation is used to study the magnetic properties of spheroidal titanomagnetite particles Fe(3-x)TixO4 (0.4 < x < 0.6) with semi-axes ratio ranging from 0.5 to 1.5 and transverse diameters D = 100 - 480 nm. It is shown that various vortex micromagnetic states can emerge in the titanomagnetite particles depending on the titanium concentration, aspect ratio and particle diameter. The single-domain particle diameters are determined using the energy diagrams for stationary uniform and vortex states. The remanent magnetization of dilute assemblies of titanomagnetite particles with varying titanium content are calculated as a function of the transverse particle diameter D. It is demonstrated that for submicron-sized titanomagnetite particles, D ~ 500 nm, the normalized remanent magnetization of the assembly reaches very low values, M/Ms < 0.01, where Ms is the saturation magnetization of the particles.

authors.name: Olga N. Serebryakova, Nikolai A. Usov

papers.title: Accessing Electrode Edges: Upright Mounting for Site-Specific Cryogenic Atom Probe Tomography of Lithium-Ion Batteries
papers.summary: Cryogenic atom probe tomography (cryo-APT) is increasingly being used to map the three-dimensional distribution of highly reactive species in heterogeneous materials, including those found in battery systems. However, site-specific preparation of localised features and liquid-solid interfaces remains challenging, particularly when regions of interest (ROIs) are concentrated along electrode edges that are difficult to access using conventional mounting geometries. Here, we present a cryo-APT workflow incorporating an upright-mounting procedure that enables targeted specimen preparation of localised regions using plasma focused ion beam (PFIB) microscopy and milling under cryogenic conditions. We first demonstrate the approach using an electrolyte-wetted graphite electrode, successfully preparing and analysing a specimen containing both an edge-localised electrolyte deposit and the underlying graphite and Cu current collector. We then apply the workflow to a cycled graphite electrode, targeting Li dendrites concentrated around the electrode perimeter and successfully preparing and analysing the targeted Li-rich region. Beyond battery systems, this approach offers potential for site-specific cryo-APT of edge-localised features across a broader range of material systems, where conventional specimen preparation geometries may limit access to ROIs.

authors.name: Syeda Ramin Jannat, James O. Douglas, Neil Mulcahy, Lukas Worch, Aigerim Omirkhan, Zhenyu Guo, Yuanzhu Zhao, Maria-Magdalena Titirici, Ifan E. L. Stephens, Mary P. Ryan, Baptiste Gault, Michele Shelly Conroy

papers.title: Atomistic Insights into the All-Optical Switching of GdCo Alloys with Minimal Gd Concentration
papers.summary: Single-pulse all-optical helicity-independent switching (AO-HIS) is most commonly observed in Gd-based ferrimagnets near magnetization compensation. Recent experiments, however, demonstrated switching in Pt/Co/Pt-based heterostructures containing only a small amount of Gd at a Co/Pt interface. Here, we use atomistic spin-dynamics simulations to test an effective interfacial GdCo-alloy picture and to determine how species-dependent spin-bath coupling controls the minimum Gd concentration required for reversal. We compare a three-monolayer Co film with Gd confined to the surface layer and a three-dimensional uniformly alloyed GdCo model. Within the present uniform-heating model, robust transient toggle-like reversal is obtained far from compensation when the Gd coupling to the thermal bath is substantially weaker than that of Co; for {\lambda}Co = 0.02 and {\lambda}Co = 0.001, reversal occurs down to 1.5 at. % total Gd for selected pulse parameters. Increasing the Gd content accelerates reversal, consistent with the interpretation of Gd as an angular-momentum reservoir, whereas dilute interfacial Gd produces slower and more stochastic dynamics. These results show that compensation is not a fundamental requirement for ultrafast AO-HIS and identify the effective Gd spin-bath coupling as a key control parameter. Quantitative comparison with experiment will require explicit optical absorption, stack-dependent heat flow, dipolar fields, and a stable-final-state switching criterion.

authors.name: Paul-Iulian Gavriloaea, Jackson L. Ross, Richard F. L. Evans, Roy Chantrell, St\'ephane Mangin, Oksana Chubykalo-Fesenko

papers.title: Energy spectrum of trions in semiconductors
papers.summary: Energy levels of trions in a bulk semiconductor crystal are calculated by two different numerical methods. On the one hand, we construct the finite-element solution of the Schr\"{o}dinger equation in the total angular momentum representation. On the other hand, we use the Gaussian expansion method (GEM), applied to each of the three Faddeev components of the wave function. The results for the total angular momenta $J=0$ and $J=1$ of the trion were obtained for a wide range of the hole-to-electron mass ratios covering most existing semiconductor compounds. The dependencies of the energies on the mass ratio for trions in a bulk crystal qualitatively agree with the results for a simplified model of a trion in a 1D quantum wire, for which the three-body energies can be calculated with arbitrary precision as well as easily approximated using Born-Oppenheimer potential-energy curves. A comparison of our results with data from other publicly available three-body codes as well as with the energies of well-known atomic counterparts, in particular, with vibrational energy levels of the molecular hydrogen ion, shows a good agreement and confirms the accuracy of the numerical data. We found that GEM significantly improves the precision of the obtained trion energies compared to previous calculations. Our calculations demonstrate that, for most semiconductor compounds, only one trion state with zero total angular momentum exists.

authors.name: Pavel A. Belov, Lucas Happ, Stefan Scheel, Evgeny A. Yarevsky

papers.title: Renormalization group study of critical behavior of $O(m)$ model with cubic anisotropy and extended defects: two-loop approximation
papers.summary: We study the impact of quenched extended defects correlated in $\epsilon_d$ dimensions and randomly distributed in the remaining $d - \epsilon_d$ dimensions on the critical properties of a $d$-dimensional $O(m)$-symmetric system with cubic anisotropy. Exploiting the field-theoretic renormalization-group approach within the minimal subtraction scheme, we compute the two-loop renormalization-group functions. Applying resummation techniques to analyze the asymptotic series, we estimate the marginal values of $\epsilon_d$ above which disorder becomes relevant for the physically important cases $m = 2$ and $m = 3$ in $d = 3$. We report numerical values of the critical exponents for the disorder-induced universality classes.

authors.name: D. Shapoval, M. Dudka

papers.title: Failure of Mean-Field Critical Scaling and Two Distinct Dissipation Regimes in La$_2$SmNi$_2$O$_{7-\delta}$
papers.summary: Recently, superconductivity with an onset transition temperature ($T_{\mathrm{c}}^{\mathrm{onset}}$) up to 96 K has been observed in the $\mathrm{La}_{2-x}\mathrm{Sm}_{1+x}\mathrm{Ni}_2\mathrm{O}_{7-\delta}$ system under pressure, providing an attractive platform for investigating superconducting mechanisms in nickelates. Here, we systematically analyzed the critical scaling and vortex dynamics for the $\mathrm{La}_2\mathrm{Sm}\mathrm{Ni}_2\mathrm{O}_{7-\delta}$ single crystal with $T_{\mathrm{c}}^{\mathrm{onset}}=92.5$ K under pressure. Within the Ullah--Dorsey framework, neither the two-dimensional nor three-dimensional scaling provides a good collapse near $T_{\mathrm{c}}^{\mathrm{MF}}$. This failure may be associated with the multiband composite order parameter of bilayer nickelates, in which pairing is mainly driven by antiferromagnetic exchange in the $d_{z^2}$ orbital, whereas the superfluid stiffness is mainly governed by the $d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbital. The two-step decrease in the logarithmic resistivity reveals two distinct dissipative regimes. The low-temperature regime is well described by the thermally assisted flux flow (TAFF) model, whereas the high-temperature regime cannot be explained by the vortex dynamics involved with the superconducting fluctuation. The crossover between the two regimes may be associated with the orbital-dependent evolution of vortex cores. These results suggest the significant role of the composite order parameter in critical fluctuations and vortex-motion dissipation in nickelates.

authors.name: Yongze Ye, Feiyu Li, Di Peng, Junjie Zhang, Hai-Hu Wen

papers.title: Emptiness formation in quantum fluids: a hydrodynamic solution
papers.summary: We develop an auxiliary-kernel method for constructing the hydrodynamic instantons that govern macroscopic emptiness formation in one-dimensional Galilean quantum fluids. The key step is to represent the equation of state by an auxiliary integral kernel inspired by the Bethe ansatz. For equations of state admitting such a representation, we reduce the imaginary-time hydrodynamic problem to a single integral equation. Its solution determines the full density and current profiles, the vacuum boundary, and the leading emptiness rate. Notably, the construction does not require microscopic integrability. For the Lieb--Liniger gas, we derive the previously conjectured integral equation for the leading rate and use a known elliptic solution to obtain explicit expressions for the rate and vacuum boundary. Direct hydrodynamic numerics support the predicted boundary. We also recover known instanton solutions for a family of polytropic fluids.

authors.name: Alexander G. Abanov, Boris A. Khanikati

papers.title: Electrostatic and magnetic control of the anomalous Josephson phase in ferromagnetic hybrid junctions
papers.summary: We report phase-sensitive measurements of Josephson junctions formed in InAs nanowires with epitaxial ferromagnetic EuS and superconducting Al shells. Using a superconducting interferometer, we observe a continuous, hysteretic anomalous phase shift under axial magnetic-field sweeps. A remanent phase bias persists at zero applied field and depends on magnetic history. Electrostatic gating strongly modifies the magnitude of the phase response, revealing its sensitivity to the transverse electronic structure of the nanowire. Self-consistent electrostatic simulations show that the effective Rashba spin-orbit coupling follows the measured gate-dependent phase response, suggesting its central role in the electrostatic control of the anomalous Josephson phase.

authors.name: D. Rana, O. S. Kurapati, N. Vanjarapu, J. Zhao, J. B. F. Wolters, Y. Liu, P. Krogstrup, A. L. R. Manesco, S. D. Escribano, E. Prada, S. Vaitiek\.{e}nas

papers.title: Hyperkagome antiferromagnetism in the iron garnet Almandine Fe$_3$Al$_2$Si$_3$O$_{12}$
papers.summary: Antiferromagnets on the hyperkagome lattice provide a three-dimensional route to strong magnetic frustration, but experimentally accessible realizations with well-established microscopic Hamiltonians remain scarce. Garnets are a broad family of materials in which magnetic ions can form two interpenetrating hyperkagome lattices, giving rise to spin glass, spin-liquid and hidden-order physics. Here we identify the iron aluminosilicate garnet almandine, Fe$_3$Al$_2$Si$_3$O$_{12}$, as a spin-$2$ hyperkagome antiferromagnet. Using density functional theory energy mapping, we determine a Heisenberg Hamiltonian for the high-spin Fe$^{2+}$ moments and find dominant nearest-neighbor antiferromagnetic exchange, as well as significant longer-range interactions. Classical Monte Carlo simulations of this Hamiltonian, combined with quantum-to-classical rescaling of the spin length, show a transition to antiferromagnetic order at $T_{\rm N}\approx9.8$\~K, in excellent agreement with specific heat experiments. The resulting non-collinear magnetic state is naturally described by magnetic toroidal octupolar order, which we connect to known results for the highly frustrated hyperkagome antiferromagnet gadolinium gallium garnet, Gd$_3$Ga$_5$O$_{12}$. We also calculate magnetic neutron diffraction amplitudes as well as static and dynamic structure factors using semiclassical dynamics, providing quantitative predictions for future neutron scattering experiments. Our results establish almandine as a chemically accessible realization of frustrated hyperkagome magnetism in the garnet family.

authors.name: Minnong Zhang, Harald O. Jeschke, Daniel Guterding

papers.title: Computing rare events in L\'evy-driven systems via optimal control
papers.summary: We extend the optimal control formulation of sample path large deviation theory, which has proven effective for numerical computation of instantons and sharp probability estimates in stochastic differential equations with Gaussian noise, to systems with light-tailed L\'evy noise. In the scaling limit of small jumps and high intensity, such systems satisfy a large deviation principle of Freidlin-Wentzell type, with a running cost given by the Legendre transform of the noise cumulant generating function. We propose to numerically minimize this cost over noise realizations subject to the system dynamics, which yields the instanton without having to solve Hamilton's equations, and naturally handles degenerate and multiplicative noise. When the cumulant generating function has a bounded domain, the cost grows only linearly for large noise, and instantons can contain jumps. We analyze when jumps are not only admissible but optimal, depending on the subleading behavior of the cost and on the drift, and show how jumps can be resolved numerically through a time reparameterization that freezes physical time. For continuous instantons, we derive Riccati and Fredholm determinant expressions for the leading-order prefactor, and we discuss the modifications needed when the instanton jumps. We illustrate and validate our methods against Monte Carlo simulations in several examples: a two-dimensional nonlinear model, an active run-and-tumble particle with non-Gaussian tumbling noise, and the Ghil-Sellers energy balance climate model with L\'evy-perturbed solar forcing.

authors.name: Jinan Pan, Timo Schorlepp

papers.title: Galerkin methods for unconventional superconductors with long-range interactions on 3D lattices
papers.summary: We develop an analysis and a B-spline Galerkin method for the matrix-valued Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) gap equation of unconventional superconductors with general long-range interaction kernels on arbitrary Bravais lattices. We define the BCS free energy functional on lattices, show that it is bounded from below, and characterise solutions of the gap equation as its stationary points. For non-repulsive kernels, we prove that fixed-point iteration never increases the free energy and drives the residual to zero. The algebraically decaying tails of the interaction are described by Epstein zeta functions, so the method applies to any power-law exponent $\nu>0$, including exponents at or below the lattice dimension such as dipolar interactions in three-dimensional lattices. In the B-spline Galerkin basis, the singular convolutions correspond to block-circulant matrices whose eigenvalues are lattice sums, applied without quadrature at FFT cost. Each iteration takes log-linear work and linear memory, and Broyden updates accelerate convergence. By engineering a suitable dispersion for a prescribed gap, we obtain non-trivial analytic singlet and triplet solutions of the gap equation with power-law interactions on the integer lattice at zero temperature, to our knowledge the first ones. Benchmarks against these solutions and against highly resolved numerical data show convergence rates determined by the B-spline degree and the regularity of the solution. Finally, we compute a nodal superconductor with long-range interactions on the three-dimensional fcc lattice: a chiral state with a line node and two topologically non-trivial Weyl point nodes. On 16 cores, the method reaches a residual of $1.5\times10^{-13}$ for 6.3 million complex unknowns in less than two minutes.

authors.name: Andreas A. Buchheit, Torsten Ke{\ss}ler, Sergej Rjasanow

papers.title: Matching two-dimensional statistics does not certify three-dimensional transport in battery electrodes
papers.summary: Three-dimensional battery electrode structures reconstructed from two-dimensional micrographs are routinely used to predict transport, assuming that matching the measured 2D statistics reproduces the relevant 3D properties. We test this premise on X-ray tomograms of three all-solid-state cathodes. With a differentiable conductivity solver, we optimise voxel structures that match the real electrode in phase fractions, boundary density, two- and three-point correlations and lineal-path functions, on all section planes, slab by slab and layer by layer, within measurement noise. Every sample has statistical twins conducting 10-88-fold less than the real electrode, robust to 5^3 majority filtering, whereas the most conductive are at most 3.3-fold above it. The twins rearrange rather than remove material, severing or funnelling through-plane paths. A classifier on 2D sections detects them, as it does current 2D-to-3D generators: the information is in the images but not in the statistics. Matching standard 2D statistics therefore does not certify 3D transport.

authors.name: Maziar Raissi, Devesh Upadhyay

papers.title: Higher-dimensional homogenization of quasiperiodic elastic materials
papers.summary: Quasiperiodic geometrical arrangements, which exhibit long-range order in the absence of periodicity, have attracted interest in the design of composites and mechanical metamaterials. In this context, direct numerical simulations explicitly resolving the quasiperiodic microstructure become prohibitively expensive for macroscopic problems, motivating the development of homogenized continuum models. However, the absence of a periodic unit cell in physical space hinders the use of conventional homogenization methods. In the present work, we exploit higher-dimensional periodic representations to perform computational homogenization of quasiperiodic elastic composites. Thereby, effective properties are obtained from unit-cell problems solved using the fast Fourier transform in higher-dimensional spaces. Using two-dimensional Penrose tilings and three-dimensional Ammann--Kramer--Neri tilings as paradigmatic examples, we describe the distribution of heterogeneous material properties in the corresponding higher-dimensional unit cells, compute effective elasticity tensors, and assess convergence of fully resolved finite patches to the homogenized limits. We provide open-source implementations of all numerical models.

authors.name: Weiyuan Fan, Jacinto Ulloa

papers.title: On Hamilton-Jacobi equations and perceptron models
papers.summary: The solution to a finite-dimensional Hamilton-Jacobi equation is classically known to admit a variational representation in two situations: when the nonlinearity is convex or concave, by the Hopf-Lax formula; and when the initial condition is convex or concave, by the Hopf formula. We identify a third situation: the space variable is split into two groups of coordinates, the nonlinearity is the scalar product of the two corresponding partial gradients, and the initial condition is the sum of a convex function of the first group of coordinates and of an arbitrary Lipschitz function of the second group. This structure is precisely that of the Hamilton-Jacobi equations describing the limit free energy of perceptron models. We illustrate this point by identifying the limit free energy of a class of perceptron models that can be rewritten as bipartite spin glasses, with Ising spins in one layer and bounded soft spins in the other. We also discuss how to extend the approach to several other classes of models, including general Ising and spherical perceptrons, possibly with labelled patterns.

authors.name: Hong-Bin Chen, Jean-Christophe Mourrat

papers.title: The $N$-channel white-noise Schr\"odinger operator in all three Dyson classes. I. Explicit stationary admittance distribution, density of states and outgoing Kontsevich matrix Airy integrals
papers.summary: We obtain an explicit stationary distribution of the matrix Riccati variable---the boundary admittance---for an $N$-channel Schr\"odinger operator with Gaussian white-noise disorder, in all three Dyson symmetry classes $\beta=1,2,4$. Uniform absorption regularizes the Riccati dynamics, and the distribution's normalization factorizes into outgoing Kontsevich matrix Airy integrals. This gives a common route to the density of states and the sum of Lyapunov exponents, extending Halperin's scalar solution to coupled channels. Exact finite-$N$ formulas connect two spectral regimes: the Lifshitz tail, including its symmetry-dependent prefactor, and the collective large-$N$ edge. We reduce the $\beta=4$ and even-$N$ $\beta=1$ problems to unitary orthogonal polynomials and an auxiliary recursion. Their critical double-scaling limit yields edge profiles on the $N^{-4/5}$ energy scale, governed by a complex Painlev\'e-I tritronqu\'ee solution and a linear auxiliary equation. We conjecture that these profiles describe a universal edge regime of random band matrices.

authors.name: Yan V. Fyodorov

papers.title: Emergent kagome-like electronic texture in epitaxial $\beta$-Sb on Al(111)
papers.summary: We report the epitaxial growth of $\beta$-Sb on Al(111) and the emergence of a kagome-like electronic texture with increasing Sb coverage. The surface evolves from disordered clusters through honeycomb and dice patterns before kagome-like regions appear. Diffraction, scanning tunneling microscopy, spectroscopy, and density functional calculations identify the ordered phase as $\beta$-Sb formed by AB stacking of two dice layers, with the honeycomb phase serving as a precursor. The kagome-like maxima occupy bridge positions within the same lateral lattice and differ in apparent height from dice regions by only about 25 pm. Together with the absence of an additional chemical component or distinct band manifold in photoemission, these observations support an electronic origin of the kagome-like contrast. Comparison of local tunneling spectra with calculated orbital projections suggests an energy selective change in the relative spectral contributions of Sb p states. Interface separation tests reveal sensitivity to Al-Sb coupling, while vacuum local density of states calculations identify states with enhanced bridge density. These results suggest that local interface changes could alter the balance between atomic and bridge contributions to tunneling within $\beta$-Sb. For a reference $\beta$-Sb model retaining the epitaxial geometry after Al removal, spin-orbit coupling modifies local band dispersions while the structure remains metallic. The model exhibits a finite intrinsic spin Hall response that varies with chemical potential.

authors.name: Yang Wang, Pujing Zhang

papers.title: Orbital antiferromagnetic currents in a frustrated fermionic ladder
papers.summary: We consider a spinless $t$-$t'$ ionic Hubbard chain at 1/2 filling and large hopping ratio $t'/t$. In this limit the model adequately maps onto a weakly coupled triangular ladder with a potential interchain bias. The low-energy properties of the system are formed due to the interplay of geometrical frustration, correlations and charge imbalance. We derive the effective field-theoretical model to study universal properties of the model in the scaling limit. We show that at full dynamical frustration the ground state of the ladder represents a repulsive version of the Luther-Emery liquid with dominant orbital antiferromagnetic correlations exhibiting the slowest power-law decay in the ground state. Pairing correlations also display algebraic order but are subdominant. At an incomplete dynamical frustration a finite commensurability gap is dynamically generated, and the fluctuating OAF transforms to a long-range ordered state with a spontaneously broken time reversal symmetry. The mass gap in the spectrum of relative density fluctuations gets suppressed upon increasing the potential bias.

authors.name: Shota Garuchava, G. I. Japaridze, A. A. Nersesyan

papers.title: The large $|U|$ expansion for a half-filled asymmetric Hubbard model on a triangular ladder in the presence of spin-dependent magnetic flux
papers.summary: We consider a half-filled system of spin-1/2 fermions on a triangular ladder with spin-dependent hopping in the presence of spin-dependent flux. Using the Schrieffer-Wolff transformation, we derive an effective spin Hamiltonian describing the infrared properties of the system in the limit of strong on-site repulsion. The expansion is performed up to the third order in the hopping amplitude over on-site interaction energy. It is shown that the low-energy spin excitations are described by an anisotropic $XXZ$ Heisenberg model with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and an unconventional three-spin (correlated exchange) term in the presence of an extended magnetic field. The latter couples not only to $z$-projection of the total spin on a triangular plaquette but also to the product of $z$-components of three spins located on vertices of the triangle. In the case of strong attractive interaction, the corresponding effective model is derived from the repulsive one using the one-spin-component particle-hole transformation. The effective Hamiltonian is given by the same $XXZ$ Heisenberg model, as in the repulsive case, but in terms of pseudospin (charge) operators.

authors.name: Shota Garuchava, Bachana Beradze, Tatia Sharia, George I. Japaridze

papers.title: Easy-plane ferromagnetism in single-crystal ErB$_{2}$ at low temperatures
papers.summary: We report a study of high-quality single crystals of the hexagonal rare-earth diboride ErB$_{2}$ prepared by means of the self-adjusted flux travelling-solvent floating-zone technique. Comprehensive measurements of the ac susceptibility, magnetization, specific heat, and electrical resistivity consistently establish a paramagnetic state at room temperature which develops strong easy-plane magnetic anisotropy of the hexagonal basal plane below a temperature $T_{\rm x} \approx 50$~K. Below a pronounced second-order phase transition at $T_{c} = 14$~K long-range magnetic order stabilizes. Excellent agreement with both the qualitative phenomenology and the quantitative characteristics of the thermodynamic and transport properties under applied magnetic fields up to 30\,T identifies the magnetic order in ErB$_2$ as a showcase par excellence of pronounced easy-plane ferromagnetism of Er$^{3+}$ local moments, in the presence of crystal electric fields and Van Vleck contributions.

authors.name: Christoph Resch, Georg Benka, Andreas Bauer, Elvina Dilmieva, Ulrich Zeitler, Christian Pfleiderer

papers.title: Nonreciprocal Shapiro steps in Josephson diodes
papers.summary: Various microscopic mechanisms have been proposed for the Josephson diode effect, which are unified phenomenologically within a nonreciprocal resistively and capacitively shunted junction model. We further systematically investigate the dynamical response of these Josephson diodes to radio-frequency AC driving current, focusing in particular on the nonreciprocity of Shapiro steps. We show that the Shapiro step structures encode the information about the underlying diode mechanisms in both overdamped and noised underdamped junctions. In particular, we propose the zero-voltate step center as a fingerprint of different Josephson diode mechanisms in the overdamped regime, which is captured analytically within a harmonic approximation for small AC amplitudes. Our results provides a route to experimentally distinguish different Josephson diode mechanisms, including those with and without time-reversal symmetry breaking.

authors.name: Da Wang, Qiang-Hua Wang, Congjun Wu

papers.title: Microscopic and collective signatures of feature learning in neural networks
papers.summary: Feature extraction - the ability to identify relevant properties of data - is a key factor underlying the success of deep learning. Yet, it has proved difficult to elucidate its nature within existing predictive theories, to the extent that there is no consensus on the very definition of feature learning. A promising hint in this direction comes from previous phenomenological observations of quasi-universal aspects in the training dynamics of neural networks, displayed by simple properties of feature geometry. We address this problem within a statistical-mechanics framework for Bayesian learning in one hidden layer neural networks with standard parameterization. Analytical computations in the proportional limit (when both the network width and the size of the training set are large) can quantify fingerprints of feature learning, both collective ones (related to manifold geometry) and microscopic ones (related to the weights). In particular, (i) the distance between different class manifolds in feature space is a nonmonotonic function of the temperature, which we interpret as the equilibrium counterpart of a phenomenon observed under gradient descent (GD) dynamics, and (ii) the microscopic learnable parameters in the network undergo a finite data-dependent displacement with respect to the infinite-width limit, and develop correlations. These results indicate that nontrivial feature learning is at play in a regime where the posterior predictive distribution is that of Gaussian process regression with a trivially rescaled prior.

authors.name: Andrea Corti, Rosalba Pacelli, Pietro Rotondo, Marco Gherardi

papers.title: Quantum Theory of Exciton Magnetic Moment: Interaction and Quantum Geometric Effects
papers.summary: Combining magnetometry with optical spectroscopy has uncovered novel quantum phenomena and is emerging as a powerful probe of quantum materials. However, the theory of the magnetic response of excitons, correlated electron-hole pairs in insulators, remains incomplete due to insufficient treatment of electron-hole interactions and quantum geometric effects. In biased bilayer graphene, for instance, theoretical predictions of valley g-factors for p-excitons deviate from experiment by nearly an order of magnitude. Here, we develop a quantum theory of the exciton orbital magnetic moment, based on first-order perturbation theory within the GW plus Bethe-Salpeter Equation approach and a rigorous treatment of the position operator in the response of exciton states to a magnetic field. Our formalism reveals three distinct contributions that go beyond the heuristic approaches used in the literature: a Berry-phase-corrected single-particle electron and hole moment difference, a term from envelope-function winding linked to electron-hole relative motion, and a center-of-mass correction from exciton band quantum geometry, with the latter two being completely new effects not considered in previous studies. Our ab initio calculations yield results in excellent agreement with experiment, establishing the importance of interaction and quantum geometric effects in the magnetic response of excitons.

authors.name: Gurjyot Sethi, Jiawei Ruan, Fang Zhang, Weichen Tang, Chen Hu, Mit Naik, Steven G. Louie

papers.title: Effect of Mangosteen Peel (Garcinia mangostana L.) and Grass Jelly Leaf (Cyclea barbata L. Miers) Natural Dye Mixing Ratio on the Optical, Morphological, and Photovoltaic Properties of Dye-Sensitized Solar Cells (DSSC)
papers.summary: Dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) are promising low-cost and environmentally friendly photovoltaic devices. This study explores the effect of the mixing ratio of natural dyes extracted from mangosteen peel (MP) and grass jelly leaves (GJL) on the optical, chemical, morphological, and photovoltaic properties of DSSCs. Dye solutions were prepared from crude extracts at a fixed concentration of 0.6 g/mL, with MP:GJL volume ratios varied from 3:1 to 1:3. UV-Vis absorption spectra showed that MP contributes to the UV-blue region (350-450 nm) and GJL to the red region (600-700 nm), giving the mixtures a broader, more panchromatic absorption. Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectra confirmed that both extracts share hydroxyl (-OH) and carbonyl/carboxyl (C=O, C-O) groups capable of anchoring the pigments onto TiO$_2$, with a stronger glycosidic C-O-C band for MP. Optical and FESEM imaging revealed that balanced and GJL-rich mixtures form more uniform, crack-free films than single dyes. Current-voltage (J-V) measurements of three independently fabricated cells per composition (n=3) under identical white-light illumination showed that the 1:3 (MP:GJL) ratio gave the highest apparent power conversion efficiency, about 1.3 and 1.7 times that of the single MP and GJL dyes, respectively. Because the input power was estimated photometrically (lux) rather than with a calibrated AM1.5G source, these efficiencies are apparent (relative) indicators for comparing samples, not absolute values. The improvement is attributed to the complementary absorption of the two pigments, while direct electrochemical confirmation of the charge-transfer mechanism remains for future work.

authors.name: Eka Nurfani, Haifa Salsabila, Dwiky I. Bakhtiar, Wahyu S. Sipahutar, M Alvien Ghifari, Rishal Asri, Meqorry Yusfi, Tarmizi Taher, Aditya Rianjanu, Robi Kurniawan

papers.title: A General-Purpose and Efficient Machine-Learned Potential for SiC from Ambient to Extreme Environments
papers.summary: Silicon carbide (SiC) polymorphs are widely employed as nuclear materials, mechanical components, and wide-bandgap semiconductors. The rapid advancement of SiC-based applications has been complemented by computational modeling studies, including both ab initio and classical atomistic approaches. In this work, we develop a computationally efficient, general-purpose machine-learned interatomic potential (ML-IAP) capable of multimillion-atom molecular dynamics simulations. Building on the tabulated Gaussian approximation potential (tabGAP) framework, we introduce an additional embedding term that captures local atomic coordination, improving accuracy and generality, while retaining high computational efficiency. Using this ML-tabGAP model, we map a broad pressure-temperature phase diagram, simulate the threshold displacement energy distributions for the 2H and 3C polymorphs, and simulate primary irradiation damage in 3C. Across a benchmark covering conditions from ambient to extreme, including high-pressure/high-temperature states and high-energy cascade damage, tabGAP provides a favorable balance of accuracy, robustness, transferability, and computational cost among the tested empirical and ML-IAPs.

authors.name: Jintong Wu, Zhuang Shao, Junlei Zhao, Flyura Djurabekova, Kai Nordlund, Fredric Granberg, Qingmin Zhang, and Jesper Byggm\"astar

papers.title: Experimental methods to measure thermal hysteresis of martensite-austenite transition in bulk \b{eta}-Cu-Zn-Al composition gradient single crystals
papers.summary: Improvement of functional and structural fatigue endurance for applications of ferroelastic materials requires an optimization of their composition. We propose an experimental methodology to explore the model \b{eta}-Cu-Zn-Al system. It is based on an original route to process bulk gradient composition single crystals to investigate fine variation of composition range coupled with local measurements of the austenite-martensite microstructure by light microscopy during the transformation. The latter method is compared with differential scanning calorimetry measurements. The methodology is applied to different narrow ranges (up to 4 at%) of composition of standard CuZnAl shape memory alloys where local fluctuations of hysteresis of 3 K are observed.

authors.name: O. Goisot, L. Porcar, R. Haettel, H. vanLandeghem, F. Robaut, O. Robach, M. Verdier

papers.title: Monte Carlo Sampling for Wave Functions Requiring (Anti)Symmetrization
papers.summary: Many strongly correlated states, such as those arising in the fractional quantum Hall effect and spin liquids, are described by wave functions obtained by dividing particles into multiple clusters, constructing a readily evaluable wave function in each cluster, and (anti)symmetrizing across these clusters. We introduce a method to compute quantities such as energies and correlators, using Monte Carlo simulations for these states. Our framework overcomes the factorial scaling of explicit (anti)symmetrization, allowing for studies of systems beyond the reach of exact diagonalization.

authors.name: Koyena Bose, Steven H. Simon, Ajit C. Balram

papers.title: Giant enhancement of attosecond tunnel ionization competes with disorder-driven decoherence in amorphized silicon
papers.summary: High-harmonic generation (HHG) and tunnel ionization in solids are strong-field phenomena sensitive to the attosecond dynamics of laser-driven electron-hole pairs. While HHG has been used extensively as a spectroscopic probe in crystalline systems, its potential as a probe of disorder on the length scale of electron-hole trajectories remains relatively unexplored. Furthermore, with the advent of petahertz electronics, there is a growing need for controlling ionization on the nanoscale. Here, we show how focused-ion beam driven amorphization of silicon leads to a giant enhancement ($>$250 times) of yield for lower-order harmonics and quenching of higher-order harmonics, consistent with a dramatically enhanced tunnel ionization yield and disorder-induced decoherence, respectively. Modelling the real-space quantum dynamics, we show how electron-hole coherence in the amorphous phase is lost over a characteristic length of approximately five lattice sites. HHG spectroscopy also reveals remnant order inherited from the original cubic structure. Our results establish HHG spectroscopy as a probe of medium-range order and pave the way for new opportunities in lightwave nanoelectronics.

authors.name: D. N. Purschke, D. Vick, A. C\'ardenas, N. Haram, P. Bastani, S. Gholam-Mirzaei, S. Mokhtari, V. Jelic, J. Chen, J. Canlas, J. Tordiff, Md. W. Rahman, A. Yu. Naumov, D. M. Villeneuve, A. Staudte, M. Salomons, R. E. F. Silva, \'A. Jim\'enez-Gal\'an, G. Vampa

papers.title: jahn-teller-dynamics: Python package to determine vibronic interaction demonstrated on molecules and trigonal defect qubits
papers.summary: Trigonal solid-state defects are often subjects of spontaneous symmetry breaking driven by the $E\otimes e$ Jahn-Teller effect, reflecting strong electron-phonon coupling. These systems, particularly paramagnetic defect qubits in solids are central for quantum technology applications, where accurate knowledge of their fine-structure parameters - shaped by the complex interplay of spin-orbit and electron-phonon interactions - is essential. We introduce the $\mathtt{jahn {\text -} teller {\text -} dynamics}$ package, a Python code that implements the first-principles approach of [Phys. Rev. X 8, 021063 (2018)] to accurately compute the spin-orbit-phonon entanglement in trigonal defects utilizing the output from density functional theory calculations (DFT) to predict fine-structure parameters of zero-phonon lines (ZPLs), including Zeeman shifts under external magnetic fields. We demonstrate its capabilities on negatively charged Group-IV-vacancy (G4V) defects in diamond: SiV$^-$, GeV$^-$, SnV$^-$, PbV$^-$ and the neutral N$_3$V$^0$ defect in diamond, and the CH$_3$O$^0$ methoxy radical. Additionally, we implement a generic electron-phonon code that is capable entangling an arbitrary amount of (i) vibration modes and (ii) electronic levels by (iii) arbitrarily high order of vibronic interaction terms. Exemplarily, we demonstrate the Jahn-Teller multimode problem on the CH$_3$O$^0$ methoxy radical and the Pseudo Jahn-Teller case on the $C_4H_4^+$ butatrien cation.

authors.name: Balazs Toth, Adam Gali, Gergo Thiering

papers.title: Approximate Surface Tension of Phase Separating Interfaces using Residual Forces
papers.summary: Extending methods that have been successful in determining the surface tension of equilibrium interfaces to active Brownian particle systems have resulted in negative and/or unusually large values of the interfacial tension, raising questions about the applicability of these frameworks to nonequilibrium interfaces. The absence of a general framework for understanding interfacial tension independently of equilibrium thermodynamics makes this problem particularly challenging. Here, I develop a new framework that provides an order-of-magnitude estimate of the interfacial tension using average force densities that are accessible even when the system is not in thermodynamic equilibrium. Applying this framework to active interfaces yields estimates that differ substantially in both sign and magnitude from previously reported results, highlighting the need to reassess existing approaches to interfacial tension in active matter.

authors.name: Bal Krishan

papers.title: Electric-field-controlled altermagnetic spin-momentum locking and ultrahigh tunneling magnetoresistance in Bilayer Cr$_{2}$SeO
papers.summary: Altermagnets offer a promising platform for spintronics by combining zero net magnetization with nonrelativistic spin splitting, yet efficient electrical manipulation of their spin-dependent transport remains challenging. Here, using first-principles calculations, we show that an out-of-plane electric field induces spin-momentum locking in bilayer Cr$_{2}$SeO, gives rise to a magneto-optical Kerr effect, and drives a semiconductor-to-metal transition at sufficiently high field magnitudes. Reversing the field direction switches the spin-momentum-locking pattern, which reverses the sign of the Kerr rotation angle as well as that of the longitudinal and transverse spin conductivities. Leveraging this electric-field-controlled spin-momentum locking, we propose a dual-gate altermagnetic tunnel junction in which high- and low-resistance states are realized without reversing the N\'eel vector. The resistance switching originates from the matching and mismatching of spin-polarized conducting channels in momentum space, yielding a tunneling magnetoresistance ratio on the order of $10^{8}$. Our findings provide a theoretical basis for realizing electric-field-controlled spin-momentum locking in bilayer Cr$_{2}$SeO and developing all-electrically controlled altermagnetic spintronic devices.

authors.name: Yunfei Gao, Aolin Li, Zesen Fu, Bei Zhang, Haiming Duan, Fangping Ouyang

papers.title: Stochastic Thermodynamics of Associative Memory
papers.summary: Dense Associative Memory networks (DenseAMs) unify several popular paradigms in Artificial Intelligence (AI), such as Hopfield Networks, transformers, and diffusion models, while casting their computational properties into the language of dynamical systems and energy landscapes. This formulation provides a natural setting for studying thermodynamics and computation in neural systems, because DenseAMs are simultaneously simple enough to admit analytic treatment and rich enough to implement nontrivial computational function. Aspects of these networks have been studied at equilibrium and at zero temperature, but the thermodynamic costs associated with their operation out of equilibrium are largely unexplored. Here, we define the thermodynamic entropy production associated with the operation of such networks, and study polynomial DenseAMs at intermediate memory load. At large system sizes and intermediate and low load, we use dynamical mean field theory to characterize out-of-equilibrium properties, work requirements, and memory transition times when driving the system with corrupted memories. We characterize a failure mode of higher order networks not observed at zero temperature. Further, we develop a method for calculating work and power costs in the mean field limit. Finally, we find tradeoffs between entropy production, memory retrieval accuracy, and operation speed.

authors.name: Spencer Rooke, Dmitry Krotov, Vijay Balasubramanian, David Wolpert

papers.title: Evidence of the de Almeida-Thouless transition in three-dimensional spin glasses
papers.summary: The nature of spin-glass states in a magnetic field remains a major open problem in statistical physics. The existence of the de Almeida-Thouless (dAT) transition for three-dimensional (3D) spin glasses in a field is still debated. We introduce a new computational method to define the spin-glass susceptibility, which is robust against the broad tail in the overlap distribution that undermines conventional analyses. Applying this approach to the Edwards-Anderson spin-glass model in 2D and 3D, and contrasting with the 3D Ising (without disorder) and mean-field spin-glass models, we find a stark difference: the locus of susceptibility maxima bends to the right in the field-temperature plane for the Ising and 2D spin-glass cases, indicating a supercritical crossover line, but bends to the left for the mean-field and 3D spin glasses - a signature of the dAT line. Finite-size scaling further suggests that the peak susceptibility diverges with system size in 3D spin glasses under a field, while saturating in 2D. These results provide direct numerical evidence for the dAT transition in 3D, supporting the replica symmetry breaking scenario.

authors.name: L. H. Miranda-Filho, Yuliang Jin

papers.title: Band splitting in the altermagnet CrSb
papers.summary: Altermagnets are a class of metallic magnets characterized by spin-split electron bands. Like an- tiferromagnets they lack spontaneous bulk magnetisation. The initial description of the momentum dependent spin splitting of electron bands in altermagnets was based on the spin groups approach, which is valid when relativistic interactions are neglected. Then the spin-orbit coupling has been taken into account according with time-reversal-odd, even-parity irreducible representations of cen- trosymmetric point groups formally considered by R.M.Fernandes et al, Phys.Rev.B 109, 024404 (2024). The problem of electron band splitting should be discussed based on crystal symmetry of concrete altermagnet material. Here, the band spin-splitting in hexagonal altermagnet CrSb is established using magnetic groups formalism that allows to find the additional spin splitting missed in frame of exchange approximation. Another type of spin splitting takes place in so called hidden altermagnets. This type materials do not possess symmetry in respect of space and time inversion but are symmetric in respect of the product of these operations known as toroid symmetry. There is demonstrated the real space spin splitting in materials with toroid symmetry.

authors.name: Vladimir P. Mineev

papers.title: Linear response of the Chern insulator MnBi$_2$Te$_4$: A Wannier function approach
papers.summary: Recent work demonstrated that in the long wavelength limit the linear response of a Chern insulator to finite-frequency electric fields is the sum of two terms: A general frequency-dependent Kubo contribution that is present irrespective of band topology, and a topological Hall term that vanishes for topologically trivial insulators. Motivated by recent experiments and theoretical predictions, we use these expressions to calculate the optical conductivity and susceptibility of intrinsically magnetic MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ thin films with one, four, five, and eleven septuple layers by combining density functional theory with "single-shot" Wannier functions. To characterize the underlying topology of these systems, we compute the two-dimensional Chern number of these films using recently derived global expressions formulated in terms of Bloch energies and velocity matrix elements; the use of these expressions allows us to circumvent numerical issues at band crossings. Films with eleven septuple layers are of particular interest. We find that they have the same Chern number as five septuple layer films, in contrast to the reported "higher Chern-number phase" of these systems in other studies; we discuss a few possible reasons for the discrepancy. A layer-resolved decomposition of the static reactive susceptibility reveals a non-uniform spatial distribution, with interlayer contributions dominating over intralayer contributions and the bulk layers accounting for nearly 70% of the total response. We also identify spin-orbit coupling-driven band inversions as a possible indicator of these topological phases.

authors.name: Matthew Albert, Javier Sivianes, Jason G. Kattan, Julen Iba\~nez-Azpiroz, J. E. Sipe

papers.title: Dynamics of O(2) excitations in a non-reciprocal medium
papers.summary: We investigate emergent dynamics due to non-reciprocity in the O(2) model. The lattice XY model, where non-reciprocity stems from vision cone like couplings, can be described by a continuum description in which non-reciprocity translates into a new term depending on the rotational of the orientation field. We argue that non-reciprocity is akin to activity and we highlight the connection between our hydrodynamic equation and the constant density Toner-Tu framework. The active force advects and reshapes patterns, a generic feature found in many non-reciprocal systems. We show how 1d excitations in the non-reciprocal O(2) model can be described by a generalized Burgers equation, derived from our continuum model. We then extend the results to 2d perturbations. As such, we establish the first principles of excitation trajectory control in a non-reciprocal O(2) medium. Concretely, we explain how tuning the degree of non-reciprocity and the orientation of the background medium impacts the time evolution of excitations. We also showcase how initially different excitations lead to very different dynamical behavior. Non-reciprocity also affects the stability of defect-free excitations with non-zero winding numbers and, unlike in its equilibrium O(2) counterpart, enables the system, above a certain threshold, to relax to its ground state.

authors.name: Ylann Rouzaire, Daniel JG Pearce, Ignacio Pagonabarraga, Demian Levis

papers.title: Spectral Softening and the Structural Breakdown of Thermodynamic Equilibrium
papers.summary: Reversible quasistatic thermodynamics requires normalizable instantaneous equilibrium states and dynamics allowing their attainment or tracking. We examine these requirements in a driven two-dimensional quadratic Hamiltonian with an angular-momentum coupling and a spatially uniform momentum shift $p_c(t)$, representable by a time-dependent vector potential. Its undriven part has normal-mode frequencies $\omega_\pm=\omega_1\pm\omega_2$ and the Fock--Darwin structure of a charged oscillator in a perpendicular magnetic field. At the exact soft-mode endpoint $\omega_-=0$, confinement is lost in one normal-mode sector. For every strictly positive $\omega_-$, the canonical Gibbs state remains normalizable; only at the endpoint does the canonical trace cease to be finite. In the quasi-soft regime, where $\omega_-\to0^+$, exact adjacent-level couplings yield a dimensionless adiabatic parameter proportional to $|\dot p_c|/\omega_-^2$. The standard adiabatic criterion requires this parameter to remain much smaller than unity. At a fixed occupation and a fixed nonzero driving rate, however small, this parameter grows without bound as $\omega_-\to0^+$, eventually violating this criterion. In an open system, thermal tracking additionally depends on relaxation relative to the driving timescale. An explicit linear system--bath coupling illustrates why the relaxation rate cannot be inferred from the soft-mode spacing alone. Finally, the thermal Wigner function and its classical limit show that phase-space confinement is lost in both descriptions at the soft-mode endpoint. Taken together, our results show that canonical equilibrium is lost at $\omega_-=0$. For $\omega_->0$, the Gibbs state exists, while the ability to track it dynamically depends on the driving and dissipation.

authors.name: Ilki Kim

papers.title: Quantum-Geometric Spin Magnetization and Spin Currents Across Altermagnetic Symmetry Classes
papers.summary: Altermagnets host spin-split band structures despite vanishing equilibrium spin magnetization, making field-induced responses a direct probe of their quantum geometry. Based on symmetry, altermagnets can be classified into M-, S-, A-, and S/A-type according to the presence or absence of inversion and time-reversal symmetries. We develop a unified framework using a generalized quantum geometric tensor that captures both momentum translations and spin rotations of Bloch states. In particular, we introduce the Zeeman counterpart of the conventional spin quantum geometric tensor, whose real and imaginary parts define the Zeeman spin quantum metric and Zeeman spin Berry curvature, respectively. Using this framework, we study linear spin magnetization and spin currents induced by electric and magnetic fields. We show that M- and S-type altermagnets support intrinsic electric-field-induced spin currents and magnetic-field-induced spin magnetization, while A-type altermagnets exhibit both electric and magnetic field induced spin current and spin magnetization. For S/A-type altermagnets, neither inversion nor time-reversal symmetry alone determines the allowed responses. Applying our theory to the S-type $d$-wave altermagnet $\mathrm{FeSb}_2$ and a Rashba-coupled S/A-type $d$-wave altermagnet, we find complete agreement with the symmetry constraints. The predicted responses are sizable and within reach of magnetometry and spin-transport experiments. Our results establish a symmetry based quantum geometric framework for spin responses in altermagnets and highlight their potential for experimental detection and spintronic applications.

authors.name: Neelanjan Chakraborti, Snehasish Nandy, Sudeep Kumar Ghosh

papers.title: Conductivity of a Non-Galilean--Invariant Fermi Liquid: Exact Solution of the Kinetic Equation
papers.summary: We obtain an exact expression for the conductivity of a non-Galilean-invariant Fermi liquid with impurities by solving the kinetic equation with both screened Coulomb and $z=3$ Pomeranchuk critical interactions. While consistent with previous asymptotic results, our solution shows that electron-electron interactions enter the conductivity solely via the quasiparticle scattering time, $\tau_{\mathrm{ee}}$. Accordingly, the crossovers between the collisionless and hydrodynamic regimes occur when $1/\tau_{\mathrm{ee}}$ becomes comparable to the larger of the impurity scattering rate and the probe frequency, $\Omega$. Importantly, this crossover is governed by the quasiparticle scattering rate, rather than by a suppressed effective current-relaxation rate. The exact solution also shows that the electron-electron correction to the dc conductivity remains parametrically smaller than the residual conductivity throughout the Fermi-liquid regime. For the optical conductivity, our solution also provides access to the hydrodynamic regime, $\Omega\ll 1/\tau_{\mathrm{ee}}$, which is inaccessible within perturbation theory. Near a $z=3$ Pomeranchuk quantum critical point, consistency between the kinetic-equation and Kubo approaches requires proper inclusion of mass renormalization within the Eliashberg approximation, which also ensures that the crossover between the collisionless and hydrodynamic regimes in the optical conductivity occurs at the Planckian scale $\Omega\sim T$.

authors.name: Tatia Kiliptari, Vladimir I. Yudson, Dmitrii L. Maslov

papers.title: Rare events of small-noise Doob conditioned processes
papers.summary: Doob fixed-time conditioning enables the sampling of rare trajectories of Markov processes by modifying the drift so that reaching a prescribed target at a given time is guaranteed. We study the statistics of this conditioned path ensemble through the moment generating function in the weak-noise large deviation regime. Since the Doob drift is rarely available in closed form, we reinterpret the conditioned ensemble as the original process post-selected on the terminal constraint, thereby avoiding explicit construction of the Doob transform. This viewpoint then yields an optimal-control representation for the leading exponential contribution to the generating function, expressed as a variational principle with terminal boundary conditions set by the Doob end-point constraint. We illustrate the framework with two analytical examples and with an application to heat dissipation under Doob-controlled dynamics in a minimal model of biomolecular folding.

authors.name: Iago N. Mamede, Francesco Coghi

papers.title: Quantum Interference Corrections in Electron Hydrodynamics
papers.summary: We show that quantum-interference corrections in an electron fluid are tightly constrained by hydrodynamic Ward identities: charge and momentum conservation protect the $m=0,\pm1$ sectors, so the leading correction first appears in the spin-two $m=\pm2$ stress sector. The resulting hydrodynamic Cooperon has a robust infrared structure that renormalizes stress relaxation, and hence the viscosity. In channel flow this lowers the viscous resistivity, producing a hydrodynamic interference signature with the opposite sign to ordinary weak localization.

authors.name: Alberto Cortijo

papers.title: Roughness-robust surface altermagnetism in $PT$ antiferromagnets
papers.summary: Surface altermagnetism extends spin splitting beyond bulk altermagnets through symmetry reduction at surfaces and interfaces. An existing classification applies to the local symmetry of atomically flat surface terraces. Here we address the symmetry of macroscopic spin-momentum correlations that survive averaging over compensated rough surfaces. These correlations are governed by the surface antisymmetry Laue class. Because rough-surface altermagnetism is forbidden at any surface of a magnet with antitranslations, the classification reduces to $PT$-symmetric antiferromagnets. By restoring all symmetries leaving the surface normal invariant, roughness can generate compensated surface altermagnets from uncompensated flat terminations or suppress spin splitting. Roughness-robust surface altermagnetism in $PT$-symmetric antiferromagnets offers a route to combine bulk electrical switchability with altermagnetic surface transport.

authors.name: K. D. Belashchenko

papers.title: Time-local nonequilibrium Green's function method for real-time dynamics in quantum systems coupled to superconducting leads
papers.summary: We develop a time-local nonequilibrium Green's function formulation for real-time dynamics in quantum systems coupled to superconducting leads. The superconducting lead self-energy is a strongly frequency-dependent matrix in Nambu space, giving rise to nonlocal memory kernels in the time domain. This makes direct propagation of the Kadanoff-Baym (KB) equations computationally demanding. To overcome this difficulty, we extend the auxiliary-mode expansion, originally developed for normal-metal leads, to Nambu-space self-energies. This allows us to decompose the superconducting lead self-energy into a finite number of exponential modes and to transform the KB equations with memory integrals into a closed set of ordinary differential equations. The resulting time-local equations enable efficient real-time simulations under general time-dependent bias voltages, superconducting phases, and one-body Hamiltonians of the central system, while retaining the memory effects induced by superconducting leads. As an application, we analyze voltage-quench dynamics in a superconductor-quantum-dot-superconductor junction and show that, after a dc bias is suddenly applied, the system evolves through a transient regime and relaxes to an ac Josephson periodic steady state. The resulting periodic steady-state current agrees with the Floquet Green's function solution, validating the present real-time formulation.

authors.name: Taira Kawamura

papers.title: Quantum sensing of weak ferromagnetism in a phase-separated Mn-doped CaFe$_3$O$_5$
papers.summary: Doping of transition metal oxides such as CaFe$_3$O$_5$ offers a controlled way to tune the interplay of charge, spin, and lattice degrees of freedom, yet local-probe studies remain difficult because strong correlations and dynamic charge-spin fluctuations obscure fine spectroscopic features in powder samples. Here, we employ quantum magnetometry based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in nanodiamonds impressed into an Mn-doped CaFe$_3$O$_5$ powder pellet to probe static and dynamic magnetic fields across the weak ferromagnetic transition. The splitting and broadening of the optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) spectra exhibit an order-parameter-like increase by $\sim 15 ~{\rm MHz}$ upon cooling below the critical temperature, $T_{\rm c}$. Concomitantly, the spin-lattice relaxation rate, $1/T_1$, exhibits a pronounced enhancement at $T_\mathrm{c}$, increasing approximately fivefold from its high-temperature value. Moreover, detailed lineshape fits of ODMR spectra together with the stretched-exponential NV magnetization recovery curves corroborate the proposed electronic phase segregation in charge-ordered and charge-averaged phases at the microscale. The presented study demonstrates the viability of using nanodiamonds as a platform for local magnetic probing of strongly correlated matter, including phenomena such as electronic phase separation.

authors.name: Izidor Benedi\v{c}i\v{c}, J. Paul Attfield, Denis Ar\v{c}on

papers.title: Bifurcation reorganization governs snap-through pathways in folded elastic ribbons
papers.summary: Snap-through in slender elastic structures is often viewed as a sudden transition between stable configurations, yet both the pathway and direction of this transition can vary fundamentally. A structure may snap while preserving symmetry or first undergo symmetry breaking, and the transition may occur between either of two competing stable states. Here, we show that localized folds provide a geometric means of programming these transition characteristics in elastic ribbons. We study a ribbon with two folds placed symmetrically about its midpoint and demonstrate that varying the fold position reorganizes the underlying bifurcation landscape. Three distinct instability-mediated pathways are identified: a supercritical pitchfork followed by stable asymmetric deformation and subsequent saddle-node-induced snap-through, a subcritical pitchfork directly triggering asymmetric snap-through, and a saddle-node inducing symmetry-preserving snap-through. Moreover, changing the fold position reverses which metastable branch loses stability, leading to both top-to-bottom and bottom-to-top transitions. We show that these transitions are governed by three aspects of bifurcation reorganization: changes in pitchfork criticality, reversal of the relative ordering of pitchfork and saddle-node bifurcations, and switching of the destabilized metastable state. Combining experiments, discrete differential geometry simulations, and numerical continuation, we identify six snap-through regimes arising from two transition directions and three instability-mediated pathways, and construct a global bifurcation map characterizing their dependence on fold position.

authors.name: Weicheng Huang, Qun Zhang, Bohan Zhang, Mingchao Liu

papers.title: Quantitative Theory for the Amplitude of Fluorescence Quantum Beats from Geminate Triplet-Pair Fusion
