papers.summary: We derive the amplitude of fluorescence quantum beats caused by geminate triplet-exciton fusion from the full set of parameters that characterize singlet fission and triplet exciton dynamics. We apply the theory to tetracene and rubrene single crystals. We find that the amplitude depends on the fission time in tetracene, but does not do so in rubrene, where it is determined by the dimensionality of triplet transport. Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations reproduce the experimental data in both materials, for a fission time of the order of 200 ps and isotropic triplet transport in tetracene, and for a triplet hopping time along the herringbone axis of 200-300 ps and anisotropic transport in rubrene.

authors.name: Zachary Rex, B\'ach Pham Xu\^an, Gerald Curran III, Ivan Biaggio

papers.title: Interface-Confined Superconductivity with Thickness-Independent Superfluid Stiffness in (Pb,Sn)Te/FeTe Bilayers
papers.summary: Interface-induced superconductivity in FeTe-based heterostructures provides a promising route toward topological superconductivity, yet the roles of the neighboring layers topology, symmetry, and electronic structure remain unresolved. In this work, we employ molecular beam epitaxy to grow Pb1-xSnxTe/FeTe bilayers and use angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy to track the evolution of the Pb1-xSnxTe layer from a trivial insulator to a topological crystalline insulator hosting multiple Dirac surface states. Electrical transport measurements reveal robust superconductivity throughout the entire composition range, with a nearly constant superconducting transition temperature of ~12 K despite substantial changes in the electronic structure and topology of Pb1-xSnxTe. Double-coil mutual-inductance measurements further reveal comparable superfluid stiffness across the topological phase transition and nearly thickness-independent superfluid stiffness despite large variations in the constituent-layer thicknesses, demonstrating that superconductivity is confined near the interface. These results establish that superconductivity in FeTe-based heterostructures is largely insensitive to the topology, crystal symmetry, and detailed electronic structure of the neighboring layer, supporting a primary origin in modifications to the FeTe layer. The coexistence of interface-confined superconductivity and tunable multiple Dirac surface states in Pb1-xSnxTe/FeTe bilayers provides a versatile platform for exploring topological superconductivity and interactions among multiple Majorana zero modes.

authors.name: Zi-Jie Yan, Hongtao Rong, Yiyuan Luo, Yufei Zhao, Pu Xiao, Cequn Li, Zihao Wang, Lok-Kan Lai, Annie G. Wang, Zhiyuan Xi, Yanxing Li, Xiaoyu Wei, Ke Wang, Katja C. Nowack, Binghai Yan, Chih-Kang Shih, Cui-Zu Chang

papers.title: Model inference from fluid flow in continuum theories of active matter
papers.summary: Active matter systems are driven out of thermodynamic equilibrium by localized, microscale energy dissipation. While active field theories are highly successful at simulating these non-equilibrium phenomena (the forward problem), characterizing real-world active materials is fundamentally bottle-necked by the difficulty of measuring active stresses directly. This paper addresses the inverse problem using deep learning: model inference and model selection from observable flow field data of active fluids. We formulate an inversion framework applied to two cornerstone paradigms of active continuum physics: Active Model H (representing scalar active matter) and Active Nematics (representing active systems with orientational order). We demonstrate that the kinetic energy spectrum obtained from the fluid flow field preserves a high-fidelity signature of activity to infer parameters of active model H and active nematics. The classification of the models requires comparison using conventional numerical work against predicted parameters. Our deep learning method presents a principled way to bear upon questions of model inference and selection given the flow field data in continuum models of active matter.

authors.name: Aditya Mohapatra, Sagarika Adhikary, Rajesh Singh

papers.title: First-principles calculation of electron-phonon spectral functions for defects using phonon interpolation
papers.summary: Accurate optical lineshapes of point defects require dense sampling of lattice vibrations, which is challenging for direct first-principles supercell calculations. We introduce a phonon-interpolation method for calculating Huang-Rhys spectral densities and optical lineshapes within the harmonic Franck-Condon framework. By exploiting the spatial localization of transition-induced forces, the method obtains electron-phonon coupling from a tractable defect supercell and samples its vibrational response on dense reciprocal-space grids, avoiding explicit construction and diagonalization of large hypercell dynamical matrices. Applied to the negatively charged nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond, the method resolves low-energy acoustic contributions, the dominant phonon sideband structure, and finer optical-phonon features. The resulting temperature-dependent photoluminescence lineshapes reproduce the main features of experimental spectra after accounting for additional broadening. The approach offers an efficient route to high-resolution defect spectra and can, in principle, complement embedding and machine-learning methods.

authors.name: Zoltan Santha, Gergo Thiering

papers.title: Electronic and magnetic properties of small one-dimensional Wigner crystals from an ab initio approach
papers.summary: We present an ab initio method to study the electronic properties of small one-dimensional Wigner crystals. In particular, we focus on the calculation of the electronic charge distribution. Our theoretical studies are motivated by the experimental observation of few-electron Wigner crystals in a carbon nanotube [Science 364, 870 (2019)]. We model the experimental setup by confining electrons in a one-dimensional potential well with hard-wall boundary conditions. We represent the Hamiltonian of the system in a basis of Slater determinants and perform full configuration interaction to ensure we capture all the electron correlation for a given basis set. As the one-particle basis set we use particle-in-a-box wave functions which by construction satisfy the boundary conditions. With our approach, we obtain accurate electronic density profiles of small one-dimensional Wigner crystals. These profiles clearly show the localisation of the electrons. Moreover, we calculate the exchange coupling constant of the Wigner dimer by mapping our ab initio method on a Heisenberg Hamiltonian. We obtain a reasonable agreement with a result in the literature.

authors.name: Daniele Lagasco, Jan Arjan Berger

papers.title: Structure-Property Correlation of Cr/Cu-MnFeCoNi High-Entropy Alloys for Alkaline Water Electrolysis
papers.summary: High-entropy alloys (HEAs), with their unique compositional-complexity and tunable surface chemistry, have emerged as promising electrocatalysts for energy conversion. The catalytic activity of HEA often arises from the interplay between the intrinsic activity of the individual elements and the synergistic effects generated at the interfaces. Even a single-element substitution in a multicomponent HEA can substantially alter the surface-chemistry and electrochemical kinetics of the active surface. Here we investigated the structure-property relationship of CrMnFeCoNi (HEA-Cr) and MnFeCoNiCu (HEA-Cu) HEAs by comparing the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity. Under the same experimental condition, HEA-Cu outperforms HEA-Cr towards both HER and OER. Substituting Cr with Cu significantly enhances the bifunctional activity, where HEA-Cu achieved a lower overpotential (538 mV) and Tafel slope (165 mVdec-1) when compared with HEA-Cr. Computational analysis corroborates these findings, showing that Cu substitution modulates the electronic-structure to provide favorable binding energies for reaction intermediates (H*, O*, OH*, and OOH*). Interestingly, unlike HER, recovered HEA-Cu after OER showed migration of Cu forming a Cu-rich outer layer shell with a multimetallic core. These findings demonstrate the potential of single-element substitution in HEAs as a strategy for designing high-performance, cost-effective catalysts for efficient water electrolysis.

authors.name: Shreyasi Chattopadhyaya, Raphael B. de Oliveira, Deepti Gangwar, Tymofii S Pieshkov, Marcelo L. Pereira Junior, Dhiman Banik, Astrid Campos-Mata, Atin Pramanik, Soumyabrata Roy, Douglas S. Galv\~ao, Chandra Sekhar Tiwary, Krishanu Biswas, Pulickel M Ajayana

papers.title: Proximity effects of chiral magnetization on transition metal dichalcogenides monolayers
papers.summary: We consider the proximity effects of a commensurate chiral $120^{\circ}$ N\'eel magnetic structure on the transport and optical properties of a transition metal dichalcogenide monolayer (TMD ML). The enlarged magnetic unit cell leads to the folding of the Brillouin zone and enables efficient intervalley spin-flip scattering. Starting from a six band tight binding model, we develop an effective $k\cdot p$ model, which describes the coupling between charge carriers in the TMD ML and the chiral magnetization. We predict the anomalous antiferromagnetic Hall effect (AHE) for conduction electrons and describe it accounting for the interplay between anomalous velocity, side jump, and skew scattering contributions. The proximity of the chiral magnetization also leads to the mixing and splitting of the exciton resonances in the two valleys which are related by the time reversal symmetry despite zero net magnetization. Finally, we demonstrate the possibility to measure the distribution of in-plane orientation of the chiral magnetization through Faraday rotation and the ellipticity of incident linearly polarized light.

authors.name: Vladimir N. Mantsevich, Igor S. Krivenko, Dmitry S. Smirnov

papers.title: Valley-controlled chiral magnetism in transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers
papers.summary: We put forward the Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) interaction in transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers as a tool to create and control a chiral magnetic texture. We show that in the spin-valley locking regime, the RKKY interaction acts as a Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya coupling with an effective spin rotation period exactly equal to the tripled lattice constant. Using mean field theory and classical Monte Carlo simulations, we demonstrate that this interaction qualitatively reshapes the phase diagram of atomically thin antiferromagnets. It destroys the chirality-related phase transition by selecting a single chirality value even when the RKKY interaction is small. At the same time, it shifts the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition associated with spins orientation to higher temperatures. We argue that the valley degree of freedom of electrons mediating the RKKY interaction provides a powerful control knob for exploring non-universal phase transitions and quantum spin liquid states in two-dimensional van der Waals heterostructures.

authors.name: Igor S. Krivenko, Vladimir N. Mantsevich, Dmitry S. Smirnov

papers.title: Thermal Stability of Two-Dimensional Crystals with Extended OH Hydrogen-Bonded Chains
papers.summary: Numerical simulations of the dynamics of monolayer structures of molecules deposited on a sheet of hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) have been performed. It is shown that molecules containing benzene rings and hydroxyl groups can form stable two-dimensional crystals with linear hydrogen-bonded chains OH$\cdots$OH$\cdots$OH$\cdots$. Such structures are formed by the following molecules: phenol (C$_6$H$_5$OH), hydroquinone (C$_6$H$_4$(OH)$_2$), 4-phenylphenol (C$_6$H$_5$-C$_6$H$_4$OH), 4-(4-phenylphenyl)phenol (C$_6$H$_5$-C$_6$H$_4$-C$_6$H$_4$OH), paracetamol (CH$_3$C(O)NHC$_6$H$_4$OH), 4-hydroxybenzanilide (C$_6$H$_5$C(O)NHC$_6$H$_4$OH) and 4,4$^\prime$-dihydroxybenzanilide (C$_6$H$_4$OHC(O)NHC$_6$H$_4$OH). On the one hand, the benzene rings in these molecules ensure their strong interaction with the flat substrate; on the other hand, they do not hinder the formation of long hydrogen-bonded chains. The monolayer structures of these molecules exhibit high thermal stability: the onset melting temperatures of their 2D crystals are 112, 257, 237, 337, 277, 407, and 483$^\circ$C, respectively. The simulations suggest that structures composed of h-BN sheets and molecules of hydroquinone, paracetamol, 4-hydroxybenzanilide and 4,4$^\prime$-dihydroxybenzanilide can be used for the development of novel proton-exchange membranes capable of operating at elevated temperatures.

authors.name: Alexander V. Savin

papers.title: Nonlocality relates cuprate photoemission $\omega/T$ scaling to a broad dielectric loss peak
papers.summary: Photoemission spectroscopy on high $T_c$ cuprates reveals a puzzling nodal self-energy with $\omega/T$ scaling and an exponent varying continuously with doping. Meanwhile, electron energy loss spectroscopy finds a broad $\sim 1$eV peak whose physical origin remains debated. We propose they share a common origin by introducing a phenomenological model of nonlocal screening in a many-body charged fluid. The model's key feature is spatially nonlocal effective repulsions between carriers $V_{\alpha}(r) \sim 1/r^\alpha$, with doping-dependent $\alpha$. The model predicts a falsifiable relationship between independently measured self-energy exponent $\gamma$ and loss function peak dispersion exponent $\alpha$, as $\gamma = 2-\frac{1}{\alpha}$. This can be tested using modern ARPES and EELS. Nonlocality provides an alternative route to $\omega/T$ scaling in observables, although it is conventionally regarded as a signature of quantum criticality.

authors.name: Jian Xian Sim

papers.title: Kinetic Lifshitz invariants and dynamics of nonreciprocal fluctuations in superconductors
papers.summary: We derive the generalized time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau theory of a disordered noncentrosymmetric superconductor from the Keldysh nonlinear sigma model, using a two-dimensional electron gas with Rashba spin-orbit coupling and an in-plane Zeeman field as a minimal model. On the thermodynamic side we construct the Lifshitz invariants of the free energy, the linear and cubic gradient terms and the momentum-odd part of the quartic vertex, and trace their dependence on disorder. The couplings of the quadratic sector are governed by a single closed-form kernel controlled by the ratio of the Dyakonov-Perel spin-relaxation rate to temperature. It interpolates between the weak-relaxation regime, where the invariants are suppressed, and the relaxation-dominated regime, where the helical modulation of the order parameter saturates at a universal, disorder-independent value. This crossover reconciles known results for the magnetoelectric couplings of disordered Rashba superconductors. Because the theory is formulated on the Keldysh contour, it also determines the dissipative dynamics: the relaxation rate of a fluctuation with pair momentum $q$, and hence the Langevin noise power, acquires a term odd in $q$ and odd in the magnetic field. The structure of this kinetic Lifshitz invariant is dictated by Onsager reciprocity: friction and noise change together, so that equal-time fluctuations remain Gibbsian while the relaxation dynamics becomes nonreciprocal. As applications we compute the superconducting diode efficiency near $T_c$, where the cubic invariant competes with the quartic vertex and with higher-gradient terms, reversing the sign of the diode coefficient. We also consider fluctuation-induced magnetochiral anisotropy above $T_c$, which grows as the inverse square of the distance to $T_c$ and is suppressed in the relaxation-dominated regime.

authors.name: Tony Liu, Joaquim Telles de Miranda, Daniel Shaffer, Alex Levchenko

papers.title: Dynamic Pseudogap Model
papers.summary: We formulate a theory of pseudogap formation generated by dynamic finite nesting vector ${\bf Q}$ fluctuations with characteristic oscillation frequency $\omega_0$, and damping $\gamma$. Starting from a Hamiltonian describing electrons coupled to a classical Gaussian random field, we introduce the double - series representations of the single - particle Green's function within an Abelian (commuting) approximation to the exact SU(2) time evolution of the pseudogap problem. The resulting propagator naturally acquires a generalized Bogoliubov structure in which every stochastic scattering history is characterized by an effective dynamic gap, leading to a coherent superposition of dynamically broadened sidebands with complex Poisson weights. A central result of the theory is the emergence of a dynamically generated decoherence scale $\Gamma_{\rm eff}$ governing the crossover between two qualitatively different pseudogap regimes. For $\omega_0>\Gamma_{\rm eff}$ the fluctuating field is resolved coherently and the double-series representation provides a controlled description of dynamic sideband formation. Conversely, when $\Gamma_{\rm eff}\gtrsim\omega_0$, coherence is progressively lost and the theory crosses over to the quasistatic fluctuating - gap regime described by the exact continued-fraction solution. The coherent and quasistatic descriptions are therefore interpreted as two complementary asymptotic limits of the same microscopic dynamic pseudogap model. The detailed results of numerical calculations for electron spectral density and density of states supporting our approach are presented for different sets of model parameters confirming the general picture of this crossover.

authors.name: E. Z. Kuchinskii, M. V. Sadovskii

papers.title: Flexo-Strain Engineering of Phonons and Ferrons in Thin Films of Van der Waals Ferrielectrics
papers.summary: The influence of the flexoelectric coupling on the fluctuations of electric polarization and elastic strains can lead to the principal changes of the dispersion law of soft optical and acoustic phonons and ferrons in a bulk van der Waals ferrielectric. Since the size, gradient and strain effects determine phase diagrams and polarization behavior in thin films, it is reasonable to assume that the flexocoupling and mismatch strains should have a strong influence on the dispersion of phonons and ferrons in thin ferroelectric films. Using the Landau-Ginzburg-Devonshire approach, in this work we reveal that the dispersion of soft optical and acoustic phonons and ferrons is strongly dependent on the sign and magnitude of elastic strains, which originate from the lattice constants mismatch in thin strained films of van der Waals ferrielectric CuInP2S6. In particular, the frequency of acoustic phonons and ferrons approaches zero at nonzero wavevectors k>k_cr, where the critical value of the wavevector k_cr is determined by the mismatch strain, flexoelectric coupling strength and temperature. Zeroing of the acoustic phonon frequency, that appears with increase of tensile strains, indicates a dynamic instability induced by the flexo-strain effects, that may evolve into a spatially modulated incommensurate polar phase with increase in the flexocoupling strength. Analytical results, derived in this work, open the way for flexo-strain engineering of soft phonon and ferron dispersion in thin films of van der Waals ferrielectrics.

authors.name: Anna N. Morozovska, Eugene A. Eliseev, Yujie Zhu, Mykola Yelisieiev, Hanna V. Shevliakova, Yulian M. Vysochanskii, Venkatraman Gopalan, Long-Qing Chen, Jia-Mian Hu

papers.title: Exact autoregressive sampling of planar Ising spin glasses via the Kac--Ward theory
papers.summary: Independent samples from the Boltzmann distribution are valuable for estimating spin-glass observables and evaluating approximate sampling methods. Local Markov chain Monte Carlo methods typically generate temporally correlated samples and can encounter critical slowing down or metastable trapping, while neural autoregressive samplers such as variational autoregressive networks generate independent but approximate samples. Here we present an exact autoregressive sampling algorithm for planar Ising spin glasses based on the Kac--Ward theory. Under the chain-rule factorization, sequentially fixing spins induces boundary-localized external fields, which destroy the zero-field structure required for exact evaluation. By encoding these fields with a planarity-preserving auxiliary spin construction, the conditional partition functions are mapped to an extended zero-field Ising model and exactly evaluated using the Kac--Ward determinant formula. The method generates strictly independent and identically distributed samples with exact normalized likelihoods at a computational cost of $\mathcal{O}(N^{5/2})$ for $N$ spins, thereby providing an exact baseline for benchmarking neural autoregressive samplers.

authors.name: Jing Liu, Tao Chen, Tianrui Che, Lei Wang, Youjin Deng, Pan Zhang

papers.title: Nucleation and propagation of brittle fracture as a constrained energy minimization problem
papers.summary: This paper presents a macroscopic, or continuum, theory aimed at describing when, where, and why cracks nucleate and propagate in nominally elastic brittle materials under monotonic, quasi-static, but otherwise arbitrary mechanical loads. Motivated by recent insights, the proposed sharp theory posits that: \emph{cracks nucleate and propagate exclusively in regions where the strength surface of the material is exceeded, with their evolution dictated by the minimization of the sum of the potential --- the elastic energy minus the work done by the externally applied forces --- and surface energies.} While the theory applies to materials with any elasticity (linear or nonlinear) and any material symmetry (isotropic or anisotropic), attention is restricted here to the most basic case of isotropic elastic brittle materials. For demonstration purposes, the theory is confronted with a set of nine tests that span the entire range of well-settled experimental knowledge on fracture nucleation and propagation --- the so-called ``Nine Circles of Elastic Brittle Fracture'' --- on both a hard material (a silicate glass) and a soft material (a synthetic rubber).

authors.name: Oscar Lopez-Pamies, Farhad Kamarei, Gilles A. Francfort, Alessandro Giacomini

papers.title: Spin-current rectifier and linear magnon Edelstein effect in $p$-wave antialtermagnets
papers.summary: We show that $p$-wave magnetic insulators efficiently generate magnetization via a linear thermal magnon Edelstein effect. Furthermore, they can generate perfectly nonreciprocal spin currents through a purely even-order nonlinear response. This makes them promising candidates for spin-current rectification. More generally, we find that odd-parity-wave magnets with coplanar ground states host magnons with zero magnetic moment in the plane. Instead the magnons carry a colinear, out-of-plane magnetic moment, placing coplanar odd-parity-wave magnets within the class of antialtermagnets. We establish these general results using symmetry arguments and demonstrate them explicitly for a two-dimensional model with a coplanar ground state containing the minimal number of sublattices, inspired by the ground state of CeNiAsO. Our conclusions hold both in the absence and in the presence of spin-orbit coupling.

authors.name: Kristian M{\ae}land, Bj\"orn Trauzettel

papers.title: Dephasing-Induced Universal Spin Fluctuations in a Localized Hubbard Chain
papers.summary: Decoherence usually washes out quantum effects. We show that in a disordered chain it can instead switch on universal fluctuations. In the infinite-$U$ Hubbard chain, particles cannot pass one another, so the spin crossing a cut is fixed by the number of particles that cross. Without an environment, disorder localizes the charge and the spin fluctuations stop growing. Dephasing restores diffusion: the spin width grows again as $t^{1/8}$, fastest at an intermediate dephasing rate, and the spin distribution takes the same non-Gaussian M-Wright form as in the clean chain.

authors.name: C\u{a}t\u{a}lin Pa\c{s}cu Moca, Ovidiu I. P\^{a}\c{t}u, Bal\'{a}zs D\'{o}ra

papers.title: Spin-Exchange Induced Confinement of Correlated Bound States in the Continuum
papers.summary: Repulsively bound doublons are two-particle composites formed by strong interactions and are usually separated from the scattering continuum. Introducing spin-exchange coupling (SEC) fundamentally alters the underlying band structure, providing a powerful tuning knob to shift these isolated pairs toward this continuum. However, because entering such a regime typically dictates immediate dissociation, whether this coupling can drive these pairs inside while preserving their bound nature constitutes a fundamental unresolved challenge. Here we show that spin-exchange coupling in the one-dimensional extended Fermi-Hubbard model can drive doublons into the two-particle scattering continuum. Most of these states hybridize with extended channels and decay, whereas a subset remains decoupled and spatially bound, forming many-body bound states in the continuum (BICs). We map the interacting two-particle problem onto a two-dimensional lattice of coupled acoustic cavities, and experimentally observe both the radiating doublon continuum and the confined BIC states. These results demonstrate that spin-exchange coupling can turn selected doublons into interaction-induced BICs, deepening the understanding of continuum physics for interaction-bound pairs.

authors.name: Kai Chen, Junyan Guan, Zhongming Gu, Jie Zhu

papers.title: Memory-induced optimal switching in a dynamic Ising-Kuramoto model
papers.summary: We study how internal spin switching competes with phase decorrelation in a globally coupled dynamic Ising--Kuramoto model. Linear response about the nonmagnetic incoherent state gives $K_c=[(\mu+\beta_s\gamma)\chi_\gamma]^{-1}$, where $\chi_\gamma$ is a switching-weighted Laplace transform of the free phase correlation. Under explicit assumptions on that correlation, we establish sufficient conditions for the mean-field linear instability threshold to attain a global minimum at a finite positive switching rate, strictly below both endpoint thresholds. The criterion separates low-rate integrated phase memory from high-rate short-time correlation structure. Finite-correlation-time Ornstein--Uhlenbeck forcing satisfies the high-rate condition; applying the sufficient criterion still requires checking the low-rate moment condition. The white-noise threshold is monotone or exactly flat. Finite-system simulations exhibit appreciable spin-weighted coherence, weak ordinary coherence and a strong antiphase sector bias. On a magnetized background, amplitude ratios are quantitatively consistent with the predicted linear-mode composition locally near onset. Direct finite-size tests of the nonmagnetic threshold minimum remain unresolved under the prespecified support rule, despite the predicted conditional contrast signs at two tested OU times.

authors.name: Reon Hayashi

papers.title: CTMRG as a tensor-network message-passing algorithm
papers.summary: We formulate the corner transfer matrix equations, and the corner transfer matrix renormalization group built on them, as a set of local equations on general planar graphs. These equations depend only on the local subgraphs of the planar graph and are glued together consistently to describe the whole graph. Solving them yields message tensors and corner matrices, which can be used to construct an MPS environment for any connected subgraph. We test the proposed equations on the ferromagnetic Ising model, on a variety of infinite lattices (including hyperbolic ones) and on finite graphs, and find systematic improvement over belief propagation.

authors.name: Illia Lukin, Andrii Sotnikov

papers.title: Ultra-small-angle graphene twistronics with monolayer spacers: From interlayer hybridisation and moir\'e effects to high-temperature magnetotransport oscillations
papers.summary: Based on the analysis of moir\'e superlattice characteristics and interlayer hybridisation in small-angle twisted graphene multilayers with a monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) spacer, we predict spectral features and quantum transport effects in these systems. Here, we consider both a twisted bilayer and double bilayers with a spacer, discuss double bilayers in two stacking orders - with and without inversion symmetry - and also compare the results obtained with self-consistent Hartree calculations with and without in-plane periodic charge distribution, offering computationally efficient models for these graphene/hBN/graphene moir\'e systems. We note parametric intervals where the appearance of minibands can be enhanced by tuning with an out-of-plane displacement field, and identify the miniband edges and van Hove singularities across a broad range of densities and displacement fields. These system host Lifshitz transitions at which the Fermi lines form a network across moir\'e Brillouin zones, and to which Brown-Zak oscillations converge at low magnetic field and elevated temperatures. We analyse interlayer hybridisation across the same parameter space, discuss how hybridisation affects in-plane magneto-transport in ultra-high-mobility structures, and predict that semiclassical magneto-oscillations of interlayer hybridisation can lead to 1/B-periodic quantum oscillations of resistivity persistent to high temperature.

authors.name: Benjamin Fuller, Haowei Fan, Agustin Montemurro, Yuyuan Pan, Alexey I. Berdyugin, Vladimir I. Falko, Xiao Li

papers.title: Large-Tiny Spin-Stripe SDW Order in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ via $^{139}$La-NQR Spectroscopy: Reconsideration Based on the $Am2m$ Structure
papers.summary: The lower-symmetry $Am2m$ structure was recently proposed as the intrinsic ambient-pressure phase of La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ based on synchrotron x-ray diffraction, whereas earlier studies investigated its properties assuming the commonly accepted $Amam$ structure. Here, we reexamine the crystal structure in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ and the spin configuration of spin-density-wave (SDW) state via $^{139}$La nuclear quadrupole resonance (NQR). The observation of two distinct La(2) sites in the NQR spectra is naturally accounted for by the $Am2m$ structure without any special assumptions, whereas it cannot be reconciled within the $Amam$ framework. Within the $Am2m$ framework, we reanalyze the spin configuration of the SDW phase and identify it as a large-tiny spin-stripe structure, arising naturally from two inequivalent Ni sites with large and tiny magnetic moments. These results establish the itinerant nature of the SDW order at ambient pressure in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$, providing a basis for understanding its relationship to the emergence of high-$T_c$ superconductivity under high pressure.

authors.name: Mitsuharu Yashima, Hongnam Lee, Takumi Ino, Nina Seto, Masataka Kakoi, Hiroya Sakurai, Yoshihiko Takano, Hidekazu Mukuda

papers.title: Topological Splitting of Sondheimer Oscillations in Thin-Film Weyl Semimetals
papers.summary: We discuss topological effects on Sondheimer oscillations in the magnetoresistance of thin-film Weyl semimetals. The Sondheimer oscillations are periodic in magnetic field and originate from the commensurability between the film thickness and the cyclotron-orbit pitch. Using Boltzmann transport theory, we investigate the effects of Berry curvature and orbital magnetic moment on the oscillations. We find that the Sondheimer oscillations split into two branches with different frequencies and that each branch becomes chirped because its frequency depends on magnetic field. These features originate from the orbital-Zeeman-induced deformation of the Fermi surface. The same mechanism also applies to Dirac semimetals.

authors.name: Toshihito Osada

papers.title: Generalised Fluctuating Dynamic Density-Functional Theory: Derivation and Applications
papers.summary: Classical density-functional theory (DFT) determines the equilibrium density distributions of complex many-body systems by bridging microscopic and macroscopic fluid descriptions via a free-energy variational principle. For time-dependent settings, dynamic DFT (DDFT) extends this formalism to govern the evolution of relevant order parameters, typically the number density. However, deterministic DDFT fails for mesoscopic systems far from equilibrium, where non-negligible thermal fluctuations require a stochastic extension: fluctuating DDFT (FDDFT). Here, we derive a generalised FDDFT from first principles, starting from microscopic Hamiltonian dynamics via systematic coarse-graining and Zwanzig's projection operator formalism. The resulting equations govern arbitrary observable fields driven by thermodynamic forces from a general entropy functional. These dynamics decompose into reversible, dissipative, and stochastic contributions, explicitly linked to microscopic mechanics via the Liouville operator, Green-Kubo relations, and the fluctuation-dissipation theorem, respectively. To delineate these coarse-grained descriptions, we show that ensemble averaging over fluctuations reduces our framework to a generalised macroscopic DDFT. Finally, we demonstrate the breadth of our formalism by applying it to two prototypical fluid classes. In the colloidal regime, it recovers the recently established colloidal FDDFT. For simple atomic and molecular fluids, we derive the non-isothermal Landau--Lifshitz fluctuating Navier-Stokes equations, providing a first-principles foundation for this classical phenomenological model and clarifying its statistical-mechanical assumptions.

authors.name: Toby Kay, Serafim Kalliadasis

papers.title: Motility-Induced Phase Separation of Run-and-Tumble Particles under Local Stochastic Resetting
papers.summary: We investigate the non-equilibrium stationary states of a one-dimensional active gas composed of run-and-tumble particles (RTPs) undergoing motility-induced phase separation (MIPS) and subjected to local stochastic resetting at the origin. Unlike global resetting, local resetting maintains a mass-injection flux at the origin while preserving large-scale spatial self-organization. We demonstrate that above a critical resetting rate $r_c$, the active system undergoes a transition toward a stationary two-phase state featuring a dense liquid droplet centered at the origin coexisting with a surrounding gas phase. Using kinetic evolution equations, we derive the exact steady-state density profile expressed in terms of the Lambert function. The size of the droplet has a non-monotonic dependence on the resetting rate $r$, and attains its maximum. Furthermore, we analyze the dynamical stability of the supersaturated gas phase and show that a nucleated droplet relaxes exponentially toward its steady-state size with a relaxation timescale of $1/r$. We extend our framework to model a finite resetting velocity, proving that the stationary droplet size is invariant with respect to the resetting velocity.

authors.name: Pascal Grange

papers.title: Resonant-pair energy return beyond the early Green-Kubo plateau in a quartic chain
papers.summary: The Green-Kubo formula gives the thermal conductivity as the long-time limit of the running Green-Kubo integral, the time integral of the equilibrium heat-current autocorrelation function. In simulations, this integral often approaches a plateau at finite time. We study how it evolves after such an early plateau in a weakly coupled chain of quartic oscillators, where the plateau value is close to the rate at which independent neighboring cells exchange energy. Two neighboring cells with nearly equal frequencies form a resonant pair: their relative phase oscillates like a pendulum, and energy that has crossed the bond between them flows back. We show that, at weak coupling, the running integral of such a pair follows the pendulum trapping response of nonlinear Landau damping. For the quartic potential, the small-oscillation period of this pendulum, $T_{\rm lib}\propto\varepsilon^{-1/2}$ with intercell coupling $\varepsilon$, does not depend on energy, so all resonant pairs share one time scale. Without fitted parameters, the theory predicts that the running integral of an isolated pair falls to a negative first minimum of $-0.74$ times the plateau value at $0.952\,T_{\rm lib}$. Simulations of isolated pairs approach this prediction as the coupling decreases. In chains, the first minimum occurs on the same time scale but is shallower, and a small positive value can remain much later. Chains of strongly chaotic cells show no comparable decrease, and energy-conserving noise much faster than $1/T_{\rm lib}$ largely removes the decrease. The pair response provides a quantitative finite-time reference for interpreting early Green-Kubo plateaus in such chains.

authors.name: Julian Olszewski, Zijian Liu, Jie Xu

papers.title: Topology of Wannierizable Insulators
papers.summary: We study the freedom in choosing Wannier centers and the associated symmetry representations in noninteracting Wannierizable insulators. We compare Wyckoff deformations of atomic configurations with symmetry-preserving adiabatic deformations of occupied states, both with and without adding common occupied atomic orbitals. Explicit examples show that stable Wyckoff equivalence and adiabatic equivalence at fixed filling do not imply each other. In spinless $Fm'm'm'$, an Euler class distinguishes stably Wyckoff-equivalent configurations. In spinless $P\overline1'$, adiabatically equivalent configurations remain distinct under stable Wyckoff deformations. We also classify when stable Wyckoff and stable adiabatic equivalence coincide. They agree in two or fewer dimensions and in three-dimensional spinful systems. For three-dimensional spinless systems, Chern insulator pumps give additional equivalences in 134 magnetic space groups. These groups preserve spacetime orientation and have a point whose site-symmetry group contains $222$, $\overline1'$, or $\overline4'$.

authors.name: Ken Shiozaki

papers.title: Quantum 3xplorer: AI-Native Engine for Next-Generation Quantum Materials Modeling
papers.summary: Quantum-mechanical approaches, such as density functional theory (DFT), underpin much of modern computational materials science and are the primary source of data for AI-driven discovery. Yet the established electronic-structure codes today represent decades-old software architectures, making new physical models slow and costly to implement, validate, and deploy on emerging hardware. We present Quantum 3xplorer (Q3, pronounced "Quantum Explorer"), an AI-native quantum simulation engine written from scratch by AI coding agents under the direction and supervision of domain scientists. As a first and demanding validation case, we implement plane-wave pseudopotential DFT end to end: norm-conserving, ultrasoft, and projector-augmented-wave formalisms, spin polarization, DFT+U, and dispersion corrections, together with forces, stresses, structural relaxation, and electronic-structure analysis. Q3 reproduces established reference implementations, runs faster on a single core in representative benchmarks, and scales across GPU-accelerated supercomputers. It was developed in weeks rather than years. Its layered, physics-first architecture separates abstract quantum-mechanical concepts from their numerical representations, making its framework extendable beyond plane waves to other basis sets and levels of theory. Its inputs and outputs follow structured, schema-validated data standards, making every result AI-ready. Q3 is open source under Apache 2.0 and built to be reused, extended, and improved by the research community. Q3 points to a paradigm shift in how computational quantum science is done. Scientists define the physics, formulate the models, and set the criteria for validation; AI agents write, test, and optimize the code. The decades-long path from a new theory to a trusted, high-performance implementation can thus collapse to days, significantly accelerating scientific discovery.

authors.name: Vsevolod Biryukov, Sergey V. Barabash, Pranab Kumar Das, Jack Deslippe, Mauro Del Ben, Felipe H. da Jornada, Yuming Shi, Johannes Voss, Zhenglu Li, Kamal Choudhary, Ruth Pachter, Steven G. Louie, Marvin L. Cohen, Timur Bazhirov

papers.title: Ab Initio strain-dependent vibrational analysis of different silicene structures for 2D devices
papers.summary: We report first-principles phonon dynamics studies in isotropically strained mono-layer silicene films of various topologies by density functional theory and density functional perturbation theory methods. The strain introduced in the sheets are of both tensile and compressive nature and its effect on the thermal transport properties are analysed using the Boltzmann Transport Equation (BTE) reported. We performed electronic and vibrational analysis of each silicene topology and concluded that hhk-silicene is a potential candidate for next generation electro-thermal devices due its molecular stability, bulk-Si like bandgap and tolerable thermal performance that can be engineered by strain. The novel hhk-silicene topology offers excellent thermal and electronic capabilities that are sensitive to strain along with the band gap following a near-linear monotonically decreasing trend making it suitable for strain-tronics applications.

authors.name: Archishman Gupta, Ankit Arora

papers.title: Three New Phases in the Two-Dimensional Potts Model at Complex Temperature
papers.summary: The complex-temperature phase structure of the two-dimensional Potts model has remained largely unresolved despite decades of study. Here we determine the complex-temperature phase diagram of the 3-state Potts model, and uncover three gapless phases beyond the familiar ferromagnetic and paramagnetic phases. This is done by combining tensor-network free energies with the Poisson equation to compute the Fisher zero density in the thermodynamic limit. The resulting zero distribution unifies and revises long-standing conjectures on the zero loci, and outlines each phase. One is a non-conformal gapless phase, with an exponentially growing number of low-lying transfer-matrix levels distributed across all momentum sectors. The other two are Luttinger-liquid phases with complex-valued Luttinger parameters related by the Kramers-Wannier duality. At the antiferromagnetic critical point, the Luttinger parameter equals 3, while its limit from the adjacent Luttinger-liquid phase is 6. These findings reveal rich phase structures and unconventional critical behavior in a classical textbook model.

authors.name: Fang-Cheng Wang, Qi-Jun Ye, Xin-Zheng Li

papers.title: AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics
papers.summary: AgBiS2 has rapidly risen in efficiency as single-junction photovoltaics (PVs), but its potential for tandem PVs is unexplored. Herein, we perform optical modeling based on the experimental absorption spectrum of AgBiS2, revealing that, as the NIR sub-cell, efficiencies exceeding 47.5% are achievable in triple-junction tandems, superseding tandems using Pb/Sn perovskite NIR cells (44.2%). However, fulfilling this potential requires overcoming the limited transport properties of AgBiS2 nanocrystal films, which constrains film thicknesses to only 30-50 nm, severely restricting NIR response. A solution-phase ligand exchange process is herein developed, allowing one-step deposition of passivated AgBiS2 nanocrystals that maintain efficient charge-carrier extraction despite an order of magnitude increase in film thickness. These films enable 24.0%-efficient four-terminal tandems with visible-light-absorbing lead-halide perovskite sub-cells, and monolithic tandems successfully demonstrating voltage addition. AgBiS2 PVs have high stability, retaining >90% of the original efficiency after 3 months of storage in dry air without encapsulation. This work establishes the significant potential of AgBiS2 as a stable and scalable NIR absorber for tandem PVs.

authors.name: Shiling Dong, Yongjie Wang, Hae-Jun Seok, Mengyuan Huang, Edward Newton, Der Ying Chen, Yixin Wang, Xiaoyu Guo, Keisuke Takemoto, Dusan Ivanovic, Avari Roy, Yongge Yang, Grey Christoforo, Rebekah Fraser, Seongrok Seo, John O'Sullivan, Ha Kyung Park, Jack M. Woolley, Ji-Seon Kim, Ruy S. Bonilla, Henry J. Snaith, Qing Shen, Aditya Sadhanala, Lydia H. Wong, Robert L. Z. Hoye

papers.title: Multi-Fidelity Machine Learning for Predicting Startup Stress Growth and Strain Hardening in Wormlike Micellar Solutions
papers.summary: Wormlike micellar solutions exhibit formulation-dependent nonlinear startup responses, including stress overshoot, undershoot, and strain hardening, making prediction across compositions and shear rates challenging. We developed a multi-fidelity machine-learning framework to predict stress-growth curves in cetylpyridinium chloride (CPyCl)-based wormlike micelles from sparse experimental measurements. The framework combines a low-fidelity analytical model describing the overall startup response with high-fidelity experimental data capturing formulation-specific nonlinear features. This approach addresses the limited and uneven coverage of salt chemistry, concentration, and shear rate without relying solely on data-intensive neural-network training. The trained model predicts complete stress-growth responses at untested shear rates and enables extraction of strain-hardening characteristics from interpolated curves. By augmenting sparse rheological measurements, the framework provides a basis for exploring relationships among formulation variables, linear viscoelastic properties, and nonlinear startup behavior, while supporting more efficient characterization of wormlike micellar solutions.

authors.name: Saghar Zolfaghari, Nunzia Lauriello, Ilaria Cusano, Marcello Ferranti, Rossana Pasquino, Safa Jamali

papers.title: Strain-Glass Dynamics in the Superionic Conductor Na3PS4
papers.summary: Ionic conduction in solid-state electrolytes is conventionally described as cations migrating through a static host lattice. Yet the fastest conductors are often the most disordered, and how disorder shapes mesoscale transport remains unresolved. Using Bragg X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy on a micrometer-sized ball-milled Na3PS4 particle, we find that the host is not static. The cubic phase behaves as a strain glass of three degenerate tetragonal variants whose domain walls move under residual milling stress, crossing over irreversibly to thermally activated dynamics on annealing. Rearrangements occur as scale-free avalanches, as in ferroelastic martensites but without external driving, while the tetragonal polymorph shows none of these features and relaxes fifty times more slowly. These dynamics evolve on timescales comparable to ionic diffusion across the particle. This work introduces a probe of dynamics in locally frustrated solid electrolytes, revealing that mechanochemical synthesis yields not merely a metastable polymorph, but a stress-driven strain glass.

authors.name: Erik S. Lamb, Nicol\`o D'Anna, Phillip Ridley, Nelson Hua, Ivan Zaluzhnyy, James Burrow, Emilio Escauriza, Robin Glefke, Boyan K. Stoychev, Mingze Wan, Zhe Ren, Fabian Westermeier, Michael Sprung, Alex Fra\~n\'o, Ying Shirley Meng, Oleg G. Shpyrko

papers.title: Statistical approach of random packing of polydisperse hyperspheres: with application to binomial and lognormal size distributions
papers.summary: This paper addresses the packing fraction of polydisperse similar hyperspheres with a discrete binomial and continuous lognormal particle size distribution. First, a closed form expression is derived of a mix consisting of multiple discrete particles in D-dimensional Euclidean space R^D with small size differences. A recently developed analytical model for binary packings with small size ratio u is used, here applying it to the statistically probable particle pairs in the multi-sized mix. The new model is subsequently applied to discretely sized particles with a binomial number distribution and a constant size ratio u between each subsequent particle size. By taking the limit of u -> 1 and an infinite number of particles sizes, the binomial particle distribution is transformed into a continuous lognormal distribution. The resulting expression for the packing fraction can be solved in closed form, resulting in an original expression for the packing fraction of mixtures of hyperparticles with a lognormal distribution. This explicit expression is governed by the standard deviation, the Euclidean dimension D, and the monosized packing fraction of the considered particle shape. For a number of particle shapes and their packing modes (from looser to denser) the scaled expression is thoroughly compared with data reported in the literature. They concern packed particles with small standard deviations and in Euclidean dimensions D = 2 and 3, and good agreement is found. For large standard deviations the scaled packing fraction approaches a limiting value, which appears not to depend on the Euclidean dimension. Based on the insight, a closed form expression is put forward for the packing fraction that matches the small standard deviation solution, and the large standard deviation asymptote, so covering arbitrary standard deviations, Euclidean dimensions, particle types, and their mode of packing.

authors.name: H. J. H. Brouwers

papers.title: Symmetry-protected isolation of the quantum metric in chiral type-II semi-Dirac semimetals
papers.summary: Quantum geometry, comprising the Berry curvature (BC) and the quantum metric (QM), underpins a wide array of topological and transport phenomena. However, in most solid-state platforms, BC and QM signals are inherently entangled, making their experimental separation highly challenging. Here, we demonstrate that the chiral limit of type-II semi-Dirac semimetals provides a symmetry-protected mechanism to cleanly isolate the QM. At the chiral limit where the spin-orbit gap $m_z=0$, chiral and $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetries strictly suppress the BC, its dipole (BCD), and the shift current, leaving the QM and its dipole (QMD) as the sole sources of the optical and nonlinear Hall responses. This pure-QM regime exhibits distinct experimental fingerprints, including a divergent longitudinal optical conductivity and a QMD-induced nonlinear Hall conductivity that exhibits a pronounced singularity as the chemical potential approaches the nodal point. Turning on a finite $m_z$ reactivates the BC channels, transitioning the system from a pure-QM phase into a mixed geometric phase. By deriving a scaling law for the nonlinear Hall conductivity, we establish a direct experimental strategy to separate the mixed Drude, BCD, and QMD contributions based on their distinct relaxation-time dependencies. Our findings identify chiral type-II semi-Dirac semimetals as highly tunable platforms for isolating and probing intrinsic quantum geometric effects.

authors.name: Wen-Hao Bian, Jing Wang

papers.title: Frank Elastic Constants of Associating Rigid-Rodlike Systems
papers.summary: Frank elastic constants of associating rigid rodlike systems are investigated using a mean field theory combined with the Straley elastic free energy formalism. Incorporating the aggregation equilibrium and size-dependent orientational ordering, we analyze the concentration and temperature dependences of the elastic constants for both a monomer--dimer model and a fully polydisperse rodlike aggregate model. We find that aggregation selectively enhances the bend elastic constant through the long-tailed volume fraction distribution, resulting in pronounced elastic anisotropy, $K_{33}\gg K_{11}>K_{22}$. Decreasing temperature or increasing concentration promotes the formation of long rodlike aggregates and induces a rapid increase in the bend elasticity, while the relation $K_{11}=3K_{22}$ remains unchanged.

authors.name: Akihiko Matsuyama

papers.title: The Outer Eshelby Problem in Amorphous Solids with Odd Dipole Screening
papers.summary: The so-called "2-dimensional Eshelby problem" was defined by JD Eshelby, where a circle is cut out of an elastic sheet, deformed into an ellipse, and forced back into the material. This creates a quadrupolar response which turned out to be very relevant for describing plastic deformations in amorphous solids. Moreover, the resulting strain field has been used to describe how elasto-plastic models respond to external strains. It is thus important to examine carefully the Eshelby problem in amorphous solids, especially when anomalous elasticity is at play. Here we solve the Eshelby problem in amorphous solids with both even and odd dipole screening and a complete analytical result is obtained for the displacement and strain fields. The analytical results are crucial for understanding the anomalous responses in displacement fields measured directly from experiments and numerical simulations. The computation of strain fields clearly demonstrates the deviations from their classical counterparts for perfectly elastic solids. The decomposition of the displacement field shows the excitation of higher-order Fourier modes. The presence of higher excitations other than the imposed Eshelby geometry therefore suggests the possible nonlinear mode coupling that can influence and modify the anomalous responses.

authors.name: Avanish Kumar, Jin Shang, Itamar Procaccia

papers.title: Harmonic origin of local symmetry breaking in PbTe revealed using machine-learned potentials
papers.summary: We use machine-learned interatomic potentials combined with higher-order interatomic force constant models to show that finite-range polar correlations in PbTe are driven by long-range harmonic interactions rather than lattice anharmonicity. Our molecular dynamics simulations reveal a spatial polar correlation range exceeding 50 {\AA} at low temperatures and decreasing with increasing temperature. Selective interatomic force constant mapping demonstrates that crystal anharmonicity usually associated with the formation of polar nanoregions suppresses polar correlations. Instead, long-range harmonic interactions extending to 13 {\AA} are necessary to reproduce the spatial coherence of local dipoles. In reciprocal space, these extended harmonic interactions correspond to high curvature of the transverse optical (TO) phonon branch at the $\Gamma$ point. Comparison with isostructural NaCl connects these extended interactions to local underscreening of predominantly Coulombic forces. Our results provide a key microscopic description of finite-range polar correlations and a framework for understanding local symmetry breaking in centrosymmetric materials.

authors.name: Seongjoo Jung, Nicola A. Spaldin

papers.title: Three-dimensional dopant depth determination from momentum-resolved core-loss 4D-STEM data
papers.summary: Moving beyond specimen-projected micrographs in scanning transmission electron microscopy to determine a three-dimensional distribution of dopants is of vital importance for materials characterization and development. Within the Born approximation, Fourier transformation over probe position of a momentum-resolved core-loss 4D-STEM dataset reveals fringes whose frequency encodes the dopant's distance from the focal plane. We address two principal challenges which arise under experimental circumstances. First, fringe contrast is degraded by dynamical scattering, but can be partially recovered by acquiring off major zone axes. Second, the excessive doses typical of core-loss scattering can be alleviated using a Bayesian framework which, on a simulated Fe-doped strontium titanate, achieves nanometre to sub-nanometre depth precision from 100 to 1000 core-loss counts, depending on the signal-to-background.

authors.name: Michael Deimetry

papers.title: Why "quantum spin liquids" are quantum singlet liquids
papers.summary: The last couple of decades have seen enormous theoretical and experimental research efforts aimed at finding quantum spin liquids (QSLs) in geometrically frustrated (GF) magnetic materials. Experimental demonstrations of QSLs are challenging due to the indirect character of possible QSL signatures and the presence of impurities in materials, which may destroy or obscure a QSL. At the same time, the theoretical literature often lacks consensus about the ground states of quantum spins on even the simplest GF magnetic lattices. We summarize experimental evidence that in the impurity-free limit, available GF magnetic materials that do not develop magnetic order at low temperatures would form {\it a quantum singlet liquid}, i.e. a disordered state of non-magnetic excitations. We further confirm with theoretical arguments the existence of such a singlet liquid and its gapless character in materials with half-integer spins per primitive magnetic cell. Such a liquid manifests itself in the thermodynamics of GF magnets while having no magnetic features at low temperatures.

authors.name: Sergey Syzranov, Arthur P. Ramirez

papers.title: Quantum inverse scattering for the 20-vertex model up to Dynkin automorphism: 3D Poisson structure, triangular height functions, weak integrability
papers.summary: We initiate a novel application of the quantum inverse scattering method for the 20-vertex model, building upon seminal work from Faddeev and Takhtajan on the study of Hamiltonian systems. In comparison to a previous work of the author in late 2023 which characterized integrability of a Hamiltonian flow for the 6-vertex model from integrability of inhomogeneous limit shapes, formalized in a work of Keating, Reshetikhin and Sridhar, notions similar to those of integrability can be realized for the 20-vertex model by studying new classes of higher-dimensional L-operators. Such L-operators provided by Boos and colleagues have algebraic, combinatorial, and geometric, qualities, all of which impact leading order approximations of correlations, products of L-operators, the transfer matrix, and the quantum monodromy matrix.

authors.name: Pete Rigas

papers.title: Phase transition in compressed sensing using log-sum penalty and adaptive smoothing
papers.summary: In many real-world problems, recovering sparse signals from underdetermined linear systems remains a fundamental challenge. Although $\ell_1$ norm minimization is widely used, it suffers from estimation bias that prevents it from reaching the Bayes-optimal reconstruction limit. Nonconvex alternatives, such as the log-sum penalty, have been proposed to promote stronger sparsity. However, maintaining their algorithmic stability is challenging. To address this challenge, we introduce an adaptive smoothing strategy within an approximate message passing framework to mitigate algorithmic instability. Furthermore, we evaluate the typical exact-recovery threshold for Gaussian measurement matrices using the replica method and state evolution. The results indicate that the adaptive method achieves exact recovery over a broader region than $\ell_1$-norm minimization, although metastable states hinder the attainment of the information-theoretic limit.

authors.name: Keisuke Morita, Federico Ricci-Tersenghi, Masayuki Ohzeki

papers.title: Limit theorems for random walks with spatio-temporal drift
papers.summary: We study a class of discrete-time random walks in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose conditional drift decays polynomially in time and grows polynomially with the distance from the origin to the current position. This class is related to several models of self-interacting random processes. We determine the asymptotic behavior of the walk under the assumption that its increments have moments of order $p$ for some $p>2$. In the linear case, where the drift depends linearly on the current position, we establish a phase transition in the convergence in distribution of the normalized process to Gaussian limits. In the nonlinear case, we identify three distinct regimes separated by a critical line and show that the normalized process exhibits qualitatively different behaviors in each regime, including convergence in distribution to a Gaussian law, convergence to a non-Gaussian limit given by the stationary distribution of a stochastic differential equation, and almost sure localization on a hypersphere.

authors.name: Ngo P. N. Ngoc, Tuan-Minh Nguyen

papers.title: ST-Dist: Distilling Spatial Transcriptomics Predictions into Interpretable Gene Axes for Distant Metastasis Prediction
papers.summary: Distant metastasis at diagnosis determines the treatment of prostate cancer, but predicting it from routine biopsy slides is challenging as the signs of metastasis are not clearly localized and are more subtle than in standard tumor detection and subtyping tasks. Multiple instance learning (MIL) on pathology foundation-model features has become the standard approach when labeled data are abundant, but such models remain hard to interpret. Distant metastasis is further challenging, because confirming the label requires clinical follow-up beyond the routine H&E slides. To this end, we propose ST-Dist, which distills the gene expression predicted by a spatial transcriptomics (ST) model into a linear head mapping each tile's foundation-model features onto named gene axes. The slide's projections along these interpretable gene axes are then used for distant metastasis prediction with a simple logistic regression. On 497 prostate needle biopsies (205 patients), ST-Dist reaches an AUROC of 91.37%, above nine MIL baselines. It remains competitive on the public TCGA-COAD and TCGA-KIRC cohorts, and it has the highest mean AUROC over the three cohorts. The ablations on the prostate biopsies show that the gene axes outperform a linear probe on encoder features, dimension-matched principal components, random gene panels and the ST model's own predicted expression, and the gain over the probe holds on all 13 pathology encoder settings that we tested. ST-Dist thus offers a simple, accurate and interpretable route from H&E to distant metastasis prediction.

authors.name: Sandesh Pokhrel, Hamid Manoochehri, Beatrice S. Knudsen, Tolga Tasdizen

papers.title: Information about Optic Nerve Head Biomechanics is Already Coded in Your Clinical Charts and Can be Used to Predict Glaucoma Progression
papers.summary: Glaucoma patients routinely undergo optical coherence tomography (OCT) imaging and intraocular pressure (IOP) assessment as part of standard care. Because IOP typically differs across visits, it is possible to map visit-to-visit ONH strains by registering OCT volumes acquired under different IOPs. These strains reflect ONH elasticity and, over longer intervals, also capture growth and remodeling of the ONH. In this study, we evaluated whether such visit-to-visit ONH strain signatures could serve as predictors of glaucoma progression. We retrospectively analyzed 525 eyes from 430 glaucoma patients (238 fast and 287 slow progressors), defining fast progression by a visual field index slope of -1.5% per year or worse. 3D strain maps were derived from baseline and follow-up OCT scans using AI. Predictions using T=1 to T=4 follow-up visits were evaluated by five-fold cross-validation in a long-term cohort (T=1: 1.30 years; T=4: 5.26 years) and short-term testing (T=1: 0.46 years; T=4: 1.25 years). Overall, IOP differed between paired visits in 92% of cases. Long-term T=1 prediction achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.74 and accuracy of 0.72. A single short-term follow-up (T=1) yielded an AUC of 0.75 and accuracy of 0.71; four follow-ups yielded an AUC of 0.87 and accuracy of 0.82. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) identified neuroretinal rim compression and prelaminar elongation associated with fast progression, with substantial inter-eye variability. Overall, visit-to-visit ONH strains derived from routine OCT predicted glaucoma progression after a single follow-up visit at a mean interval of 0.46 years. These findings suggest that short-term OCT/IOP assessments could provide valuable insights into ONH biomechanics, identify eyes at risk of rapid progression, and reveal distinct strain signatures associated with disease progression.

authors.name: Yibo Chen, Patipol Tiyajamorn, Charis Y. N. Chiang, Deepta Ghate, Thanadet Chuangsuwanich, Micha\"el J. A. Girard

papers.title: Mutual Colormap Dependence: How Recoloring Biomedical Images Changes Vision-Language Model Answers
papers.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) are being built to answer questions about biomedical images, yet they never see the measured intensities, only the colors that a colormap has assigned to them. For questions about image content, the colormap should not change the answer. We call the extent to which it does Mutual Colormap Dependence (MCD), the mutual information between the colormap and a model's answer, which is zero exactly when every colormap yields the same answer distribution. Because VLMs sample their answers, we compare recoloring with a control that uses the same number of calls to ask again about the unchanged gray image, so that ordinary resampling is not mistaken for an effect of the colormap. We test GPT-5.4, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Qwen3-VL-235B under six luminance-monotonic colormaps (gray, viridis, plasma, inferno, magma, and cividis) on 50 medical visual-question-answering items from 16 SLAKE images, 64 ChestX-ray14 chest radiographs, and 200 BBBC039 fluorescence-microscopy images for exact nucleus counting. Every prompt tells the model to ignore the colormap. Even so, with three answers per colormap on the chest radiographs, the answers of all four models depend on the colormap (all Holm-adjusted $p \leq 0.002$). For Claude, some colored map overturns the majority answer on 29 of the 64 radiographs, where resampling gray alone overturns about 4, and Qwen's accuracy falls from 0.54 under gray to between 0.32 and 0.41 under the colored maps, mostly because it abstains. With one answer per colormap, recoloring adds disagreement beyond repeated sampling in 5 of 12 model-panel cells under per-cell 95% intervals, and repeating the instruction to ignore color does not reliably reduce it. The colormap is therefore part of what a VLM sees, and it can change the answer.

authors.name: Siddharth Vohra, Runmin Jiang, Min Xu

papers.title: Angel: Anchor-Structured Neural Gaussians for Explicit Fetal Diffusion MRI Slice-to-Volume Reconstruction with Cross-Subject Learning
papers.summary: Diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (dMRI) provides a noninvasive view of developing tissue microstructure and white matter tracts in the fetal brain. During acquisition, however, fetal motion disrupts spatial correspondence between slices, diffusion encoding directions and signal intensities. We introduce ANGEL, an anchor-structured neural Gaussian framework for accurate slice-to-volume reconstruction (SVR) of fetal dMRI, that simultaneously estimates diffusion signal, fetal motion and intensity artefacts. Unlike standard explicit Gaussian representation, ANGEL is designed to prevent absorption of noise and artefacts into the reconstructed dMRI by learning a compact representation of spatio-angular signal via a shared decoder that predicts 3D Gaussians across anchors and subjects. The individual anatomical variability is compactly represented through subject-specific anchors. Experiments on simulated neonatal and in vivo fetal data show significant improvement of dMRI reconstruction in both spatial and angular domains, in comparison to explicit Gaussian representation, implicit neural representation as well as classical methods.

authors.name: Wenxuan Wu, Lucy Hall, Jonathan O'Muircheartaigh, Joseph V. Hajnal, J-Donald Tournier, Maria Deprez

papers.title: Learn Locally, Extend Globally: Koopman Eigenfunctions and the Basin of Attraction
papers.summary: Koopman eigenfunctions associated with the Jacobian eigenvalues of a stable equilibrium are Lyapunov functions defined exactly on its basin of attraction. We turn this into a computational procedure for power systems. Eigenfunctions estimated by extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD) are written as functions of the state, made to vanish at the equilibrium by centering the lifted variable $\cos\delta$, and verified on a grid with the model: two Lyapunov candidates from the EDMD spectrum certify up to 66\% of the basin of a single-machine infinite-bus system from data in the linear region. The Koopman semigroup property then extends the EDMD-Lie eigenfunction to the whole basin, recovered at the grid resolution with its isostables and isochrons.

authors.name: Marcos Netto, Bukunmi Gabriel Odunlami, Aditya Kale, Andrey Bernstein

papers.title: Bayesian Learning of Uncertain Linear System Behaviours
papers.summary: We present a Bayesian approach to learning uncertain behavioural representations of linear dynamical systems from noisy input-output data. In behavioural systems theory, the finite-horizon behaviour of a linear system is represented by a subspace. We quantify uncertainty in this subspace through probability distributions on the Grassmann manifold. This leads to a geometric formulation of Bayesian inference over the Grassmannian. We derive the posterior distribution under Gaussian measurement noise and discuss how uncertainty in the inferred behaviour can be propagated to trajectory predictions, with a view towards data-driven control.

authors.name: Noreen Abdelwahab, Alberto Padoan, Dominic Liao-McPherson

papers.title: AGI: Agility Index for Power Systems Dynamic Performance, Inspired by Reynolds Number
papers.summary: Multiple established metrics and indices exist to quantify the dynamic performance of power systems. With the growth of inverter based resources, these mostly conventional metrics and indices may not encompass all important elements and variables that hold information about the grid performance, especially the damping properties. This paper proposes the Agility Index (AGI), which is a Reynolds number-inspired metric for power system dynamics relating the ratio of inertia to damping. With the current trends towards high-power inverter assets and reduced-inertia grids, explicit attention is necessary in monitoring inertia and damping together. This paper shares insights the AGI presents about the dynamic performance of power systems.

authors.name: Maria Vabson, Amir Sajadi, Bri-Mathias Hodge

papers.title: Lie Group Structure of Six Degree-of-Freedom Rigid-Body Uncertainty Representation and Propagation
papers.summary: For six-degree-of-freedom rigid-body motion, the choice of Lie-group structure affects both how well the group-theoretic mean and covariance represent the state distribution and how accurately these moments are propagated. A quaternion-based, left-trivialized semidirect-product formulation of the velocity phase space is developed for the actuated body-frame dynamics, with closed-form group operations and Jacobians that avoid matrix-group embeddings. We derive the controlled stochastic dynamics and establish that the direct- and semidirect-product formulations describe the same physical process under the specified noise model. Since the semidirect exponential coordinates account for frame changes between body twists at different poses, they capture pose--twist coupling more naturally. A lunar powered-descent experiment assesses low-order moment representations of uncertainty and propagation performance under the proposed group structure using two distinct algorithms. Compared with direct-product formulations and a linearized baseline, the proposed structure improves the representation of the banana-shaped body-velocity distribution using group-theoretic moments, yields more consistent propagated moments, and produces distribution approximations that agree more closely with the Monte Carlo reference. In this experiment, changing the group structure accounts for most of the observed improvement, highlighting the practical value of the proposed semidirect-product formulation.

authors.name: Zhuochen Wang, Panagiotis Tsiotras

papers.title: Distance-Certified Safe Control in Unknown Environments via Spatio-Temporal Composition of Gaussian Processes
papers.summary: In this paper, we propose a distance-certified safety control framework for unknown and dynamic environments. The proposed strategy relies on a spatio-temporal composition of Gaussian Process (GP) barriers from environment point clouds. A point-cloud-dependent covariance kernel is constructed to smoothly combine individual GP representations, yielding a continuously differentiable posterior mean and a diagonal observation Gram matrix that avoids dense covariance inversions. We then derive a closed-form calibration of the GP length scale accounting for spatial approximation errors and finite point-cloud coverage, guaranteeing a prescribed minimum distance from the true obstacle boundary. To handle moving obstacles and updated observations, the scan-based barriers are certified over finite validity horizons and smoothly combined into a time-varying Control Barrier Function (CBF). Under problem feasibility conditions, the associated CBF-based safety control guarantees forward invariance of the certified safe set, thereby ensuring the prescribed distance from the obstacles. Unicycle simulations with static and moving obstacles illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

authors.name: Davide Zarabini, Stefano Di Gregorio, Giuseppe Notarstefano

papers.title: Model-Free UPS Control Tuning for Improved Low-Voltage Ride-Through in AI Data Centers
papers.summary: Voltage sags can trigger protection trips in uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems, abruptly reducing the power that AI data centers draw from the grid. This paper improves the low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) capability of AI data centers equipped with double-conversion UPS systems by tuning their existing converter controls. We formulate a bound-constrained optimization problem to maximize the ride-through area, defined as the integral of ride-through time over a range of retained grid voltages. To solve this problem, we develop a batched projected zeroth-order optimization algorithm with adaptive moment estimation (BPZO-Adam). The algorithm evaluates candidate control settings using only simulated ride-through times, making it suitable for vendor-supplied black-box models. Simulations using the TAMU-ERCOT electromagnetic transient (EMT) AI data center model show that tuning converter control parameters increases the ride-through area by 10.6\%. In a separate study, tuning the controls yields a larger ride-through area than increasing the DC-link capacitance tenfold.

authors.name: Haowen Xu, Xin Chen

papers.title: Non-Uniform Array Configuration and Antenna Deactivation for Energy-Efficient Sensing
papers.summary: This paper proposes a non-uniform array design framework for energy-efficient multi-target sensing by jointly optimizing the antenna configuration and the transmit covariance matrix (TCM). To begin with, a limited number of antennas are selected from a set of antenna locations to maximize the minimum mainlobe-to-peak-sidelobe-level ratio (MMPSR) over a sensing region. Next, the antenna configuration is optimized using a simulated annealing (SA)-based search, while a TCM optimization problem is formulated using Charnes-Cooper transformation and solved as a convex semidefinite program for each fixed configuration. Subsequently, an adaptive antenna deactivation strategy is developed to determine the maximum number of antennas that can be switched off while satisfying an MMPSR requirement. Finally, simulation results demonstrate that the proposed non-uniform array design outperforms fixed uniform and non-uniform array benchmarks and requires fewer active antennas to achieve a required sensing performance, thereby supporting energy-efficient sensing.

authors.name: Parisa Ramezani, Meesam Jafri, Marina Petrova, Emil Bj{\"o}rnson

papers.title: Job-Level Workload Allocation for Data Centers Under Flexible Interconnections
papers.summary: Flexible interconnections allow data centers to connect to the grid sooner without upgrading the grid infrastructure, if they accept limits on their grid power during periods of grid stress. When a limit is reached, the data center must slow some of its computing jobs. This choice sets the cost of flexibility, because the work done by a job is worth far more than the energy it uses. This paper models how jobs respond when their power is reduced, and proposes a real-time method that shares the available power among jobs according to their value. It also gives grid planners a simple measure of how much power a data center can reduce, and for how long. A one-year case study of a 100-MW data center shows that the proposed method lowers the cost of meeting grid limits, and that on-site generation and storage lower it further.

authors.name: Tanmay Mishra, Arash Omidi, Mads R. Almassalkhi

papers.title: Reliable Conditioned Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability via Subsolution Learning on Exact Local Windows
papers.summary: Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability computes the maximal safe set and a safety filter for a given obstacle configuration, but it must be re-solved whenever the obstacles change, which a deployed robot cannot afford. Learning a single value function conditioned on the obstacle set removes the re-solve, yet it sharpens the central weakness of learned reachability: one network must now cover a whole family of safety problems, and its approximation error carries no preferred sign, so rare obstacle configurations silently produce false-safe states. To address these challenges, we present a conditioned reachability model designed so that the remaining error falls on the conservative side. Specifically, our method caps the obstacle margin, which makes the value function provably local, in the sense that obstacles farther than a known threshold cannot affect it, so the model reads only a body-frame window, trains on small scenes, and transfers to scenes of any size with millisecond per-scene preparation. Moreover, the output structure builds the value bound into the model. By training with counterexample mining over the finite-dimensional window configuration space, we maximize the claimed safe volume subject to the HJ inequality, so the learned set grows toward the true safe set from the conservative side. Across all tested obstacle settings, ours is the only method that combines recovery comparable to per-scene DeepReach training with near-zero rollout collisions. We also extend the method to a 10D quadrotor, again with markedly lower collision rates than the baselines.

authors.name: Seunghwan Jang, Wei Xiao

papers.title: Joint RF-VLP Position and Velocity Tracking: Bayesian Estimation and Performance Analysis
papers.summary: Visible light positioning (VLP) provides accurate indoor positioning through optical received signal strength (RSS) measurements, while radio-frequency (RF) delay and Doppler measurements offer complementary range and velocity information. Motivated by this complementarity, we investigate joint RF--VLP position and velocity tracking, addressing both recursive state estimation and its fundamental performance characteristics. We formulate a Bayesian maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation problem that combines optical RSS, RF delay and Doppler measurements, and motion prediction, and develop a Gauss--Newton-based algorithm for recursive tracking.
