papers.summary: We present COSMIC (Constrained Optimization via Sliding Mode for Inequality Constraints), a continuous-time solver for inequality-constrained optimization. COSMIC couples primal gradient-flow dynamics with multiplier dynamics derived from sliding mode control laws on a manifold defined by the smoothed Fischer-Burmeister function. We prove that COSMIC's trajectories reach this manifold in finite time from any primal initial point, after which the dynamics reduces to the gradient flow of a logarithmic barrier function. This yields a control-theoretic interpretation of barrier methods while allowing infeasible initialization. For strongly convex problems, we further establish exponential convergence to the minimizer. To address the numerical stiffness that arises in discretization, we develop a modified discrete-time algorithm. We validate COSMIC across various machine learning applications, demonstrating its ability to solve optimization problems accurately while scaling effectively to high-dimensional settings.

authors.name: Rawan Hoteit, Veronica Centorrino, Efe C. Balta, John Lygeros

papers.title: Physics-Grounded STL Monitoring from Image Observations
papers.summary: Robotic manipulation missions must satisfy timed and conditional requirements that can be expressed in signal temporal logic (STL). While a practical means of monitoring these requirements is from camera images, this is challenging because STL robustness depends on physical margins, such as distances and clearances, that are not directly observed. Rather than learning a separate visual monitor for each formula, we learn a shared latent representation from multi-view images and decode physically meaningful margins for individual predicates. Co-training the encoder with predicate decoders increases the certification rate from 58.7% to 96.3% compared with a frozen encoder, despite nearly unchanged predicate sign accuracy. STL semantics then compose these margins into robustness estimates for any bounded formula over the trained predicates, without retraining. We further calibrate the decoding errors of selected STL clauses using conformal prediction, yielding two-sided intervals that certify both satisfaction and violation and propagate through interval STL to any formula composed from the clauses. In simulated kitchen missions (LIBERO), our monitor correctly predicts satisfaction or violation in 98.9% of 4662 evaluations across 18 unseen formulas. For missions lasting up to 17 min, calibrated bounds establish satisfaction or violation for 96.9% of missions without incorrect conclusions. A single calibration also provides simultaneous 91.0% coverage across all 255 conjunctions of eight clauses, allowing new formulas without recalibration.

authors.name: Xinpei Ni, Glen Chou, Samuel Coogan

papers.title: Real-Time Air Pollution Monitoring and Tracking via Adaptive Density-Driven Multi-UAV Coordination
papers.summary: Accurate and timely air pollution monitoring and tracking are critical for protecting public health and supporting effective environmental management. This paper presents an adaptive Density-Driven Control (D$^2$C) framework for coordinating multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to track and map dynamically evolving pollutant distributions. The proposed framework extends the D$^2$C strategy to guide UAV trajectories based on predictive pollutant propagation and dynamically updated reference densities. A sensor-driven surrogate plume update mechanism is employed, in which reference samples are propagated using locally sensed concentration gradients and wind estimates through gradient attraction, wind advection, inter-sample repulsion, and stochastic diffusion, enabling UAVs to maintain an accurate spatio-temporal representation of the pollution field. The framework utilizes a coordinated structure where individual UAVs share their local measurements with a central coordinator to maintain a unified set of reference samples, facilitating systematic target allocation and trajectory planning. Simulation results under both mild and strong wind conditions demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in terms of Sinkhorn distance. Specifically, in scenarios where the plume drifts beyond a fixed monitoring domain under high-velocity, time-varying wind fields, the tested baseline methods fail to maintain tracking, whereas the proposed D$^2$C framework successfully adapts to the evolving distribution. These findings highlight D$^2$C as an efficient and resilient solution for atmospheric monitoring in dynamic environments.

authors.name: Julian Martinez, Ruchika Singh, Mohammad Afrazi, Kooktae Lee

papers.title: Distance-Certified Polyak-type Stepsizes for Subgradient Methods under H\"older Growth
papers.summary: In this paper, we consider nonsmooth convex optimization under a H{\"o}lder growth condition, with quadratic growth and weak sharp minima as two important special cases. Existing subgradient methods often employ predetermined decaying stepsize schedules, whereas the classical Polyak stepsize selects its stepsize adaptively but requires knowledge of the optimal value. We introduce a new distance-certified subgradient method (\DCSG) that follows a one-step optimization principle analogous to that underlying the Polyak stepsize, without requiring the optimal value. Specifically, \DCSG{} maintains a valid upper certificate for the current squared distance to the solution set. The method selects each stepsize by minimizing the worst-case upper bound on the next squared distance over all distances consistent with this certificate. We show that the resulting minimax problem admits a closed-form solution, yielding an explicit adaptive stepsize update. Under uniformly bounded subgradients, \DCSG{} improves upon the convergence rate of the classical subgradient method and matches the state-of-the-art rates for Lipschitz convex optimization under H{\"o}lder growth. In particular, it achieves linear convergence under sharp growth. Numerical experiments illustrate the performance of \DCSG.

authors.name: Kornpholkrit Weraarchakul, Yang Zheng

papers.title: Radar Waveform Design via Convex Semidefinite Relaxation
papers.summary: The ambiguity function (AF) of a radar waveform describes its ability to resolve targets in range and Doppler. Designing a waveform that attains a prescribed AF magnitude is a phase retrieval problem with four trivial ambiguities, and a time- or band-limited pulse is determined up to these ambiguities by at most three times as many AF samples as it has time samples or frequencies. Existing solvers for the narrowband AF, however, are non-convex: they cannot guarantee that they reach the global minimizer, which is unique only up to the trivial ambiguities, so the recovered pulse depends on the starting point. This letter addresses this gap by lifting the problem to positive semidefinite matrices supported on the pulse band, where each AF sample becomes the magnitude of a linear functional. In the lifted space, recovery is formulated as a convex program, and a dual certificate provides a sufficient condition for exactness. The proposed algorithm, wavex, combines an initialization by relaxed reflections, convex semidefinite surrogate steps, and a local polish. Numerical experiments show that wavex accurately recovers band-limited pulses from complete AFs and from AFs with most of their samples removed, provided the remaining samples determine the pulse, and that its accuracy degrades gracefully as the noise increases. wavex is built on the open-source library invexapi, and the code that reproduces every result is available at https://github.com/samuelpinilla/waveX.

authors.name: Samuel Pinilla

papers.title: Feasibility certificates for DeePC: A set invariance approach
papers.summary: DeePC is posed on a window of past inputs and outputs, so its feasible set is a set of histories and is not available in closed form. We write the DeePC solution as an implicit ReLU network whose weights are built from Hankel matrices and whose activation patterns are the critical regions of the underlying quadratic program. This gives, directly from the Hankel matrices, the feasible set of DeePC as a polyhedral projection, its explicit piecewise-affine control law, and an exact linear model of the history window. We compute three invariant sets of histories: the maximal positively invariant set of the unsaturated linear branch, the region of recursive feasibility of DeePC without terminal ingredients, and the maximal control invariant set of admissible histories. We show these sets are nested and provide numerical examples.

authors.name: Daniel O'Neill, Ross Drummond, Pablo R. Baldivieso-Monasterios

papers.title: Achievable Information Rate for FTN under a Reduced Complexity BCJR Receiver
papers.summary: The capacity of faster-than-Nyquist (FTN) signaling in additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channels has been established and is achieved by Gaussian inputs. However, the capacity of FTN signaling with finite-constellations is not yet fully characterized. The achievable information rate (AIR) provides a lower bound on this constrained capacity by quantifying the rate supported by a specified input distribution and receiver. This paper investigates the AIR of FTN signaling with finite constellations using full-state and reduced-state Bahl-Cocke-Jelinek-Raviv (BCJR) receivers, with bidirectional decision feedback incorporated into the reduced-state receiver. Especially, the detection problem is formulated in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS), where a geometric foundation is established to understand FTN under severe time packing. The formulation establishes that the Ungerboeck metric remains valid even when the noise covariance is singular. We further characterize detection errors geometrically using RKHS distances between competing sequences. We also study outage probability for reduced-state detection, which occurs when AIR is zero, in addition to deriving the zero-AIR outage criterion for reduced-state detection. Unlike ISI-free Nyquist signaling, reduced-state FTN detection can retain residual ISI that causes the receiver to assign excessive confidence to incorrect symbols, leading to outage even at high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Our results confirm both the spectral efficiency gains and the feasibility of FTN systems employing finite constellations and realistic receiver architectures.

authors.name: Zichao Zhang, Gokhan M. Guvensen, Melda Yuksel, Halim Yanikomeroglu

papers.title: Contraction Analysis and Control of Polynomial Dynamical Systems
papers.summary: Contraction analysis has found broad applications in synchronization, tracking, observer design, and nonlinear feedback control. However, establishing contraction conditions for polynomial dynamical systems remains challenging due to their state-dependent Jacobians. In this article, we develop a tensor-based framework for contraction analysis of polynomial dynamical systems by exploiting the structure of orthogonally decomposable (odeco) coefficient tensors. By transforming the dynamics into modal coordinates, we derive necessary and sufficient semicontraction conditions and characterize state-dependent semimetrics. We establish fundamental limitations on exponential contraction and prove polynomial decay of differential displacements on forward-invariant regions. To accommodate more general polynomial dynamical systems, we extend the framework to include linear dynamics and non-odeco tensor perturbations, deriving computationally tractable contraction certificates with explicit robustness guarantees. We further develop convex feedback synthesis conditions based on linear matrix inequalities for general input matrices. We demonstrate the effectiveness and computational scalability of the proposed framework through numerical experiments on both synthetic systems and nonlinear elastic relaxation models.

authors.name: Xin Mao, Anqi Dong, Can Chen

papers.title: High-Speed Forward and Reverse Tractor-Trailer Driving with Learned Vehicle Dynamics
papers.summary: Tractor-trailer systems are difficult to control, especially unstable during reverse motion, and their dynamics depend on difficult-to-measure factors, including road friction and suspension coefficients. We introduce a learned dynamics model for tractor-trailer control and compare it with a reduced-order dynamics model with Fiala tire forces as an analytic baseline. Specifically, we compare a model predictive path integral (MPPI) controller that uses the learned dynamics model to an MPPI controller that uses the analytic model, as well as to three additional baseline controllers. In the main closed-loop tracking experiments across four simulated environments, MPPI with learned dynamics achieves mean speeds closer to the target magnitudes and lower root-mean-square (RMS) hitch angles than MPPI with the analytic model at every tested setpoint, with higher completion rates in seven of eight reverse configurations.

authors.name: Aaron Chen, David Shen, Taekyung Kim, Kaleb Ben Naveed, Dimitra Panagou

papers.title: Physics-informed neural network for model-based global computation of the asymptotic phase of limit-cycle oscillators
papers.summary: The asymptotic phase is the central object of phase reduction theory for limit-cycle oscillators. It is a scalar coordinate defined throughout the basin of attraction of a limit cycle that advances at a constant natural frequency along every trajectory. Computing the phase from a given mathematical model requires solving a first-order partial differential equation (PDE) over the entire basin, which is challenging due to high computation costs and complex boundary conditions. In this study, we propose a physics-informed neural network to efficiently calculate the asymptotic phase of limit-cycle oscillators. By incorporating three types of loss functions, we train a physics-informed neural network (PINN) to satisfy the governing PDE for the asymptotic phase and the adjoint equation for the phase gradient. The trained network delivers the phase function accurately and, via automatic differentiation, allows the calculation of the phase gradient governing the oscillator's response to perturbations, which enables rapid entrainment closed-loop control using strong inputs. We validate the approach using three types of limit-cycle oscillators and demonstrate that the PINN can facilitate fast and global phase-locking control.

authors.name: Petar Mircheski, Hiroya Nakao

papers.title: Inverse Problem for Super-linearization with Single Observable and Diagonalizable Principal Submatrix
papers.summary: Super-linearization is, roughly speaking, embedding an $n$-dimensional nonlinear dynamical system into an $(n + m)$-dimensional linear system. We introduce and address, in this paper, the inverse problem: given a linear system $\dot x= M x$, what type of dynamical systems can be super-linearized to it? We focus on the special case where the dimension reduction is one (i.e., $m = 1$) and the leading $n$-by-$n$ principal submatrix of $M$ is diagonalizable, and provide a solution to the problem.

authors.name: Haoyu Yin, Xudong Chen

papers.title: Optimal Dynamic Quantizers for Periodically Time-Varying Systems via Cyclic Reformulation
papers.summary: This paper addresses the design of optimal dynamic quantizers for discrete-time linear periodically time-varying (LPTV) plants with discrete-valued inputs. Optimal dynamic quantizers, which minimize the worst-case output error caused by quantization, are well established for linear time-invariant (LTI) plants, whereas the corresponding design for plants with periodically time-varying dynamics has not been addressed. For square LPTV plants having relative degree one at every time phase, this paper derives an optimal periodic dynamic quantizer in closed form. The quantizer is constructed by applying the LTI theory to the cycled plant obtained by cyclic reformulation and reading off its periodic coefficient matrices block by block; its optimality is then verified directly, showing that it attains a performance lower bound determined by the largest instantaneous input-to-output gain over the time phases. The worst-case output error of general periodic dynamic quantizers is also characterized. The optimal quantizer is shown to be stable if and only if all invariant zeros of the cycled plant lie in the open unit disk, which is the condition that governs stable causal inversion of LPTV plants. A numerical example with comparisons to conventional quantizers illustrates the results.

authors.name: Hiroshi Okajima

papers.title: ExtremeDrive: A Real-World Dataset and Benchmark for Critical Driving
papers.summary: Existing autonomous driving datasets and benchmarks provide extensive resources for routine driving, yet real-world data covering safety-critical scenarios and extreme environmental conditions remain limited. To address this gap, we present ExtremeDrive, a real-world dataset and benchmark covering emergency maneuvers, complex traffic interactions, and adverse conditions such as slippery or snow-covered roads, alongside routine driving. The dataset comprises 589 driving scenes curated from a larger pool of real-world driving recordings, with calibrated and aligned multisensor data and reviewed annotations of road structure and traffic participants. We further establish a benchmark to evaluate planned trajectories through simulated vehicle execution, measuring safety-related metrics and driving performance. Experiments at equal training set sizes show that incorporating critical driving data reduces trajectory prediction errors and improves mean critical-success rates in critical scenarios. ExtremeDrive provides a unified resource for learning and evaluating autonomous driving in safety-critical scenarios and extreme environmental conditions.

authors.name: Xinhan Li, Yuhong Jiang, Shiyue Zhao, Junzhi Zhang, Chengkun He, Ruihai Ma, Shijie Zhao, Wenxuan Cheng, Jinbo Lv, Tao Liu

papers.title: A Lifted Hessian-Riemannian Gradient Flow for LQR Synthesis under Passivity Constraints
papers.summary: The static state-feedback gain that renders a linear system passive at an external port and minimizes a linear quadratic regulator (LQR) cost cannot be computed by convex optimization, since the passivity certificate and the LQR cost are coupled bilinearly through the common gain. A previous indirect approach restricts the gain to a convex inner approximation of the passivity region, which is conservative and whose construction scales exponentially with the number of gain entries. This paper proposes a direct approach. The set of strictly passivating gains is the image of a convex lifted set of inverse storage matrices and transformed gains. We describe this set by a strict linear matrix inequality and an affine equality for every feedthrough matrix with positive semidefinite symmetric part, including feedthrough matrices with a singular symmetric part, and minimize the LQR cost over it by a gradient flow whose metric is the Hessian of a logarithmic barrier. For multi-input systems, this Hessian is singular along gain changes that preserve the storage function, and we complete the metric along these directions by the metric of the gain space. We prove that the flow exists for all times, that every gain along the flow is strictly passivating with an explicit storage function, and that the cost decreases monotonically while the gains remain in a compact set of stabilizing gains. Numerical examples show that the flow attains a lower cost than the indirect approach, that the completion is required for multi-input systems, and that the flow can converge to a local minimizer on nonconvex passivity regions.

authors.name: Armin Gie{\ss}ler, S\"oren Hohmann

papers.title: Verification-Guided Safety-Repair of Learned Controllers
papers.summary: Formal verification can certify that a learned controller is safe. But what should be done when verification fails? Simply suppressing actions that lead to unsafe next states is insufficient because the dangerous action that ultimately caused the safety violation might have occurred many steps earlier. Retraining modifies the policy globally, thereby potentially introducing new failures. Instead, we introduce ReachECO, a verification-guided repair procedure that exploits the information of failed multi-step reachability analysis for synthesizing explicit constraints on controller behavior. For Differentiable Weightless Controllers, the repairs compile into exact circuit patches that leave the controller unchanged everywhere outside the targeted policy cells. We prove soundness and termination of the repair procedure for ReachECO, as well as, assuming exhaustive continuation search, completeness relative to the reachability abstraction. Empirically, we demonstrate \method's ability to successfully repair otherwise unsafe controllers in three continuous-control benchmarks: ACC, Docking2D and Car2D.

authors.name: Fabian Kresse, Sobhan Gharanfoli, Nikolaus Vertovec, Alessandro Abate, Thomas A. Henzinger, Christoph H. Lampert

papers.title: Sign Primal-Dual Gradient Dynamics for Supply-Demand Coordination under Binary Human Feedback
papers.summary: This paper addresses supply-demand coordination, in which a supplier sets prices to balance the demands of multiple buyers against limited resources. Existing studies typically solve the supply-demand coordination problem with a distributed algorithm called primal-dual gradient dynamics (PDGD), assuming that each buyer discloses the value of its own utility or marginal utility function. In contrast, we assume that each buyer discloses only binary information, namely whether it wants more or less of the current amount, and propose Sign PDGD. Sign PDGD is a PDGD algorithm in which the buyers' update depends only on the sign information. We analyze the convergence of Sign PDGD by interpreting it as a sliding mode control (SMC). For a quadratic cost and linear constraints, we show that under a gain condition, the primal and dual variables converge to the optimal solution. Numerical simulations on a toy resource-sharing problem confirm the two-phase behavior of SMC and show that the primal and dual variables approach the optimal solution.

authors.name: Yuya Miyaoka, Kengo Urata, Masaki Inoue

papers.title: Early UAV Detection Using 5G NR LEO Downlinks for Passive ISAC
papers.summary: 5G New Radio (NR) low-Earth-orbit (LEO) downlinks enable passive integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) detection. Weak echoes require motion-compensated accumulation, but exhaustive searches postpone alerts. We propose a receiver that combines selective Doppler-rate search, early UAV alerts and continued delay-Doppler estimation. Classical, statistical and neural configurations select rates of Doppler change to search, while a shared correlation score determines detection. Simulated echo delay, Doppler and power follow the moving satellite-UAV-receiver geometry, propagation loss, assumed scattering and antenna response. In a line-of-sight scene with acquired beams and UAVs at 5-8 km horizontal distance, all three configurations match exhaustive search at 92.9% correct final detections, with 0.10-0.13% observed false alerts on no-UAV recordings. The neural configuration reduces mean time to the first correct alert by 36.5% versus exhaustive search and 21.9% versus the closest literature baseline, averaging over successfully detected UAVs. These results demonstrate earlier UAV alerts while preserving exhaustive search's final detection accuracy, supporting passive sensing over cellular satellites.

authors.name: Mohamed Hamad, Nizar Zorba, Tamer Khattab, Hamid Saeedi, Halim Yanikomeroglu

papers.title: Transferable Neural CBFs via Generalized Closure
papers.summary: Classical control barrier functions (CBFs) provide safety constraints for controllers, but designing them by hand is difficult for underactuated vehicles and the resulting safe sets can be overly conservative. Neural CBFs can learn more informative barriers from data, yet a learned barrier is usually verified only for one fixed obstacle configuration. We study whether one neural barrier can be reused across environments by expressing the state relative to each obstacle. The key gap is that these relative coordinates may discard information needed to predict their own evolution. We give a generalized closure condition that represents this missing information as a residual and a lifting theorem that transfers a verified relative-coordinate barrier to every obstacle in a family. A rank test also identifies when symmetry alone cannot justify the transfer. We validate the conditions on a double integrator, a planar aircraft, and a 12-state quadrotor. Coordinates that fail the test lead to obstacle penetration or to a barrier condition that fails near hover, whereas body-frame coordinates close exactly for the quadrotor. The resulting barrier transfers to new maps without retraining and is effective in the reported deployment and fast-start experiments.

authors.name: Nishant Jayesh Bhave, Parthib Khound

papers.title: Learning Morse Lyapunov functions through invertible neural networks
papers.summary: Towards data-driven stability certificates of dynamical systems, we are witnessing renewed interest in studying and exploiting the structure of Lyapunov functions. Especially Lyapunov functions that are locally quadratic (i.e., Morse) gained popularity ever since it was understood that they can be written as the norm squared of a diffeomorphism. This topological representation alludes to parametrizations using invertible neural networks. In this note we discuss when and how such functions can be learned. In particular, using neural ODEs (NODEs), we characterize Sobolev approximation of these diffeomorphisms on compact sets and show how this naturally relates to stability. We also connect our results to PLNets and supply numerical experiments for illustration.

authors.name: Wouter Jongeneel

papers.title: Recursive Spectral Graph Partitioning Coding for Index Assignment in Semantic Communications
papers.summary: Transmitting quantized semantic embeddings over a bit-flip channel requires a binary mapping that minimizes expected reconstruction distortion. The classical Binary Switching Algorithm (BSA) ($\mathcal{O}(K^3 \log K)$ for $K$ centroids) yields locally optimal assignments but ignores hierarchical bit significance, making it incompatible with Unequal Error Protection (UEP). We propose Recursive Spectral Graph Partitioning (RSGP), which recursively bisects the centroid affinity graph along the Fiedler eigenvector so that early bits separate semantically distant groups while later bits refine local structure. RSGP runs in $\mathcal{O}(K^3)$ with no iterative outer loop, and is the only method studied to show a systematic positive UEP gain: protecting early bits over later ones improves accuracy for RSGP, while being neutral or harmful for unstructured assignments. Experiments on the Banking77 dataset and the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) confirm that RSGP consistently matches or exceeds BSA accuracy across codebook sizes and error profiles.

authors.name: Leonardo Roque, Louis-Adrien Dufr\`ene, Quentin Lampin, Gr\'egoire Lefebvre, Mohamad Assaad

papers.title: Hybrid Optimization-Generative Motion Planning for Multiagent Affine Formations
papers.summary: Formation maneuver control enables a multiagent system to cooperatively navigate through constrained environments in collective motion. While various formation controllers exist, they rely heavily on high-quality and dynamically feasible reference trajectories provided a priori, making formation motion planning (FMP) essential. To address the computational challenges for high-dimensional joint trajectories faced by conventional constrained optimization-based solutions, this paper introduces a hybrid optimization-generative framework with a focus on affine formations, which provide the necessary spatial flexibility. By formulating the planning task as a constrained Maximum-a-Posteriori estimation, we decouple multiagent objectives to leverage pre-trained single-agent diffusion priors for dynamic feasibility, obstacle avoidance, and smoothness. We then interleave the generative process with projected gradient descent (PGD) to strictly enforce affine geometric constraints with safety guarantees. Simulations demonstrate that our framework generates highly smooth, collision-free plans that are readily trackable by common distributed controllers and outperforms state-of-the-art planners in various metrics.

authors.name: Zhonggang Li, Hongyu Zhou, Raj Thilak Rajan

papers.title: Reference Replay for Excitation Injection and Subsequent Exponential Convergence under Concurrent Learning Adaptive Control
papers.summary: Concurrent learning (CL) guarantees precise identification of unknown parameters---if data with finite excitation (FE) happens to be collected online. To improve the reliability of CL, this work establishes a mechanism allowing FE-occurrence to be verified a priori: We propose replaying a given training segment in the reference until data with finite excitation is collected online. Provided the training segment fulfills a certain off-line excitation test, FE then occurs in unknown, but finite time. Moreover, we provide an upper bound on the time-to-FE. Even though this bound involves a dependency on the unknown initial Lyapunov-function value, its structure shows that FE occurs in arbitrarily early replay cycles when increasing the control gain; which may motivate employing a high-gain strategy. The theoretical findings are verified on an academic simulation example.

authors.name: Tom Kaufmann, Johann Reger

papers.title: Fundamental Tradeoffs in Sampling, Transmission and Information Freshness: Instantaneous Feedback
papers.summary: We study a time-slotted generate-at-will status-update system over an erasure channel with transmission success probability $q$, subject to average sampling- and transmission-rate constraints $f_s$ and $f_r$, respectively. The sampler-transmitter pair jointly decides whether to idle, retransmit a stale packet, or replace it with a fresh sample. We derive a universal lower bound on the optimal average age of information, analyze a class of stationary randomized policies, and obtain an optimal policy within this class that provides a $4$-approximation guarantee. The joint problem reduces to the sampling-constrained problem when $f_s\leq qf_r$ and the transmission-constrained problem when $f_s\geq f_r$. For $qf_r0$ we construct a finite subset $\bar{\Pi}_{\epsilon}\subset\bar{\Pi}$ and show that the LP restricted to this set yields an $\epsilon$-optimal policy. Finally, we derive a stronger pair of lower bounds by considering systems with only the sampling-rate or transmission-rate constraint. Using these bounds, we construct a policy randomizing among four $(W,R)$ policies with a $2$-approximation guarantee for $qf_r<f_s<f_r$.

authors.name: Subhankar Banerjee, Sennur Ulukus

papers.title: Online Neural Network Training via Closed-Loop Model-Free Tracking Control: An Empirical Study
papers.summary: Training artificial neural networks predominantly relies on offline, gradient-based backpropagation algorithms. In contrast, biological circuits process and retain information through decentralized, continuous-time adaptation. In this work, we explore an online, gradient-free learning methodology by formulating the tuning of synaptic weights as a closed-loop trajectory tracking problem driven by model-free control principles. Rather than performing global optimization across static parameters, decentralized controllers adjust synaptic interactions in real-time using solely local input-output tracking errors. We present an exploratory benchmark neural architecture, whose purpose is to assess the dynamic resilience of the proposed approach, particularly in tracking target outputs and adapting to abrupt non-stationarities and structural perturbations (such as topological changes or dynamic dropout) without requiring offline retraining. This empirical preliminary study provides a proof-of-concept for control-theoretic learning paradigms and outlines the foundation for scalable, dynamically evolving connectome frameworks.

authors.name: Lo\"ic Michel, Jean-Pierre Barbot

papers.title: Parallel Branch Model Predictive Control on GPUs
papers.summary: We present a GPU-based solver for trajectory planning problems using branch model predictive control. Building on iterative LQR methods, we adopt a multiple-shooting formulation for the system dynamics and use an augmented Lagrangian method to handle general stage-wise constraints. This design enables straightforward warm-starting. The constraint-handling capability of our solver is validated on two challenging trajectory planning problems. In addition, we develop two tailored inner LQR solvers that exploit the tree-sparse structure. The solvers offer different levels of parallelism, making them appropriate for different tree sizes. The numerical results demonstrate that, compared to a high-performance CPU-based solver, our approach achieves superior performance on large-scale problems.

authors.name: Luyao Zhang, Chenghuai Lin, Sergio Grammatico

papers.title: A Connectively Stable and Robust DAPI Control Scheme for Islanded Networks of Microgrids
papers.summary: The transition towards clean energy and the introduction of Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) are giving rise to the emergence of Microgrids (MGs) and Networks of MGs (NMGs). MGs and NMGs can operate autonomously in islanded mode. However, they face challenges in terms of secondary level frequency and voltage regulation, due to the variable nature of Renewable Energy Sources (RES) and loads. Distributed-Averaging Proportional-Integral (DAPI) control has been proposed in the literature for distributed frequency and voltage control of droop-controlled DERs, but it might not guarantee robustness to cyber-physical disturbances. To address this, we propose a robust DAPI frequency and voltage control scheme that ensures robustness using the concept of connective stability, along with the invariant ellipsoid technique for disturbance rejection. The proposed scheme adds additional degrees of freedom to determine the strength of distributed control, providing an option for more robust action. Simulation of an NMG model in MATLAB/Simulink consisting of 3 MGs and 5 DERs shows that the proposed scheme minimizes frequency and voltage deviations during cyber-physical disturbance events compared to the baseline, dissipativity-based and H-infinity-based techniques.

authors.name: Ahmed Saad Al-Karsani, Maryam Khanbaghi, Aleksandar Ze\v{c}evi\'c

papers.title: Autonomous and Distributed Synchronization and Restoration of an Islanded Network of Microgrids
papers.summary: The transition towards clean energy and the introduction of Inverter-Based Resources (IBRs) are leading to the formation of Microgrids (MGs) and Networks of MGs (NMGs). MGs and NMGs can operate autonomously in islanded mode, which requires Grid-Forming (GFM) IBRs that can perform black start, synchronization, restoration and regulation. However, such IBRs can face synchronization instability issues, which might be worsened by inadequate secondary level frequency and voltage regulation. Accordingly, we propose an autonomous and distributed synchronization and restoration scheme using Distributed-Averaging Proportional-Integral (DAPI) control. To validate the proposed method, we model and simulate a high-fidelity islanded and modified IEEE 123 bus system, modeled as an NMG consisting of 7 MGs. The MATLAB/Simulink simulation results demonstrate an effective autonomous soft- start, synchronization, connection and regulation procedure using DAPI control and distributed breaker operation logic.

authors.name: Ahmed Saad Al-Karsani, Maryam Khanbaghi

papers.title: An Online Multiobjective Policy Gradient for Long-run Average-reward Markov Decision Process
papers.summary: We propose a policy gradient algorithm for multiobjective decision-making on continuous state spaces, in which the long-run average of a reward vector must be steered into a target set despite an adversarial disturbance, by scalarizing the reward along the direction prescribed by Blackwell's Approachability Theorem instead of tuning weights by trial and error. Existing approachability-based learning is confined to countable state spaces, because the scalarization is updated at the visits to a recurrent state, which on a continuous state space has probability zero. We update it instead at the returns to a set after a minimum number of steps, show that a geometric drift condition, uniform over the policy class, controls the cycle lengths while the policy is being learned, and replace the parallel learners of the existing algorithm by a single two-timescale actor-critic. We show that the distance to the target set is asymptotically bounded by the per-cycle remainder from Blackwell's condition, and decompose this remainder into the errors of the actor, the policy class, the direction tracking and the return set. We illustrate the algorithm on a heating, ventilation, and humidity control problem with adversarial weather and occupancy.

authors.name: Rahul Misra, Rafa{\l} Wisniewski, Manuela L. Bujorianu

papers.title: Model-free practical PI-Lead control design by ultimate sensitivity principle
papers.summary: Practical design and tuning of feedback controllers has often to get by without a model of the dynamic process at hand. Only some general assumptions about the system dynamics, in this work type-one stable, can be available for engineers, for instance in motion control applications and many others. This paper proposes a practical and simple in realization procedure for designing a robust PI-Lead control without modeling. The developed method derives from the ultimate sensitivity principles, known in empirical Ziegler-Nichols tuning of PID controllers, and makes use of some general characteristics of the loop shaping. A three-steps procedure is proposed to determine the integration time constant, control gain, and Lead-element in a way to guarantee a sufficient phase margin, while all steps are served by only experimental monitoring of the output value. Proposed method is demonstrated and discussed with experiments accomplished on a noise-perturbed electro-mechanical actuator system.

authors.name: Michael Ruderman

papers.title: Strong nonlinear detectability and moving horizon estimation for nonlinear systems with unknown inputs
papers.summary: This paper investigates state estimation for general nonlinear discrete-time systems subject to measurement noise and possibly unbounded unknown inputs. To approach this problem, we first propose the concept of strong nonlinear detectability, which proves to be a nonlinear counterpart to strong* detectability. Based on the proposed detectability notion, an unknown input state estimator (UISE), which yields bounded estimation error even for unbounded unknown inputs, is designed via a moving horizon estimation strategy using past and current measurements. Next, we tighten this detectability notion to develop a two-stage MHE-based UISE that is computationally more efficient. In a simulation example, both variants of MHE-based UISEs are compared with a conventional MHE to illustrate the merits of the proposed methods.

authors.name: Yang Guo, Jaime A. Moreno, Stefan Streif

papers.title: A Simulation Framework with Guaranteed Error Bounds for Safety and Fuel-Efficiency Analysis of Vehicle Platoons
papers.summary: Vehicle platooning is an important technology in modern transportation systems, offering significant improvements in highway traffic efficiency and fuel economy. Achieving coordinated behavior among vehicles in a platoon depends on wireless communication. However, packet losses in wireless communication can create critical safety issues when they occur together with sudden braking. In this paper, we propose a rigorous simulation-based method for studying such safety issues by analyzing the minimum inter-vehicle distance over time across control parameters that guarantee string stability. In particular, our method computes the exact distance at simulation time instants and guarantees that the change in distance between consecutive simulation time instants remains bounded. Therefore, the distances obtained at simulation times are representative of the continuous-time behavior, and the distances between those times can be accurately approximated. Our derivation relies on a lifted state representation and differential inequalities. For the proposed simulation method, we provide two approaches for selecting simulation times to ensure that the error in distance approximation remains within a given bound. We then extend our method to fuel-efficiency analysis, with guaranteed error bounds for calculating the average fuel savings of vehicles. Through an example involving a highway scenario with a merging lane, we demonstrate that among string-stable control parameter settings for a vehicle platoon, some perform better in terms of safety under simultaneous packet losses and sudden braking. We also identify control parameters that result in tradeoffs between safety and average fuel savings in a vehicle platoon.

authors.name: Yuhao Chen, Ahmet Cetinkaya

papers.title: Full-Time-Scale Power Management for Hybrid AC/DC/DS Microgrid with Dynamic Concatenation and Global Equivalent Circuit Modeling
papers.summary: Hybrid AC/DC/distributed energy storage (DS) microgrids (MGs) provide an effective solution for improving power accessibility and supply reliability in remote and isolated areas.Conventional static power management aims to proportionally allocate power based on unit ratings by scheduling the operation of interlinking converters (ILCs). Recent studies on transient power management emphasize inertia coupling among subgrids by dynamically regulating ILC power flows, thereby enhancing the system resilience against disturbances. In existing literature, these two objectives are normally addressed in a separate fashion and a unified scheme to simultaneously achieve them is rarely found. Furthermore, conventional static management neglects droop-induced frequency and voltage deviations which may seriously compromise the safe operation of sensitive loads. To address these limitations, in this paper, we proposes a full-timescale (FTS) power management for the hybrid MG is proposed.Autonomous frequency/voltage restoration controls are deployed in each subgrid to eliminate droop-induced frequency and voltage deviations, based on which a novel FTS dynamic concatenator is proposed to chain up the static power sharing and transient inertia sharing across different timescales. Moreover, a novel global equivalent circuit model (GECM) is presented to interpret the holistic hybrid system from electrical circuit perspective. Then the static and transient performance of the complex hybrid AC/DC/DS MG can be quantitatively characterized to facilitate easier engineering practices. In-house experiments validate that the proposed FTS dynamic concatenator ensures static power sharing and transient inertia sharing through the ILC in full timescales.

authors.name: Pengfeng Lin, Qingzuo Meng, Yujie Wang, Miao Zhu, Amer M. Ghias, Syed M. Islam, Frede Blaabjerg

papers.title: Contingency Planning for Safety-Critical Autonomous Vehicles: A Review and Perspectives
papers.summary: Contingency planning is an architectural capability that enables autonomous vehicles (AVs) to anticipate and mitigate safety risks arising from safety-relevant logical-mode transitions, such as sensor outages and uncertain interactions. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of the field, synthesizing fragmented literature into a unified logic-conditioned hybrid control framework. Within this formalism, we categorize approaches into two distinct paradigms: Reactive Safety enforces safety constraints or activates fallback actions after a contingency mode has been observed or reliably inferred, whereas Proactive Safety preserves recourse across unresolved mode alternatives through non-anticipative branching. In addition, we propose a fine-grained taxonomy that partitions the landscape into external contingencies (environmental and interactive hazards) and internal contingencies (system faults). Our analysis reveals a fundamental structural divergence: internal faults are predominantly addressed via reactive fail-safe mechanisms, whereas external interaction uncertainties increasingly require proactive branching strategies. Furthermore, we identify a critical methodological divergence: whereas physical hazards are typically managed with formal guarantees, semantic and out-of-distribution anomalies currently rely heavily on empirical validation. We conclude by identifying the open challenges in bridging the gap between theoretical guarantees and practical validation, advocating for hybrid architectures and standardized benchmarking to transition contingency planning from formulation to certifiable real-world deployment.

authors.name: Lei Zheng, Luyao Zhang, Peiqi Yu, Yifan Sun, Sergio Grammatico, Jun Ma, Changliu Liu

papers.title: Robust Hybrid-Gain Control with Prescribed Transient Performance
papers.summary: This paper develops a hybrid-gain robust control framework for first- and second-order nonlinear systems subject to bounded matched disturbances and prescribed transient performance constraints. A common error-function transformation incorporates time-varying tracking-error bounds, while a hybrid-gain-based feedback control law regulates convergence and disturbance rejection. Finite-time convergence and forward invariance of the prescribed-performance funnel are established for first-order systems. For second-order systems, an auxiliary velocity error enables exponential convergence and funnel invariance without assuming a priori boundedness of the transformed state. An initial-condition-dependent bound further provides a sufficient condition for realising the ideal control under actuator limits. Numerical comparisons under common actuator limits and peak-control input demonstrate the trade-off between transient constraint satisfaction and control effort. At equal peak control, tuned first-order baselines track better at the cost of large transient energy. In contrast, the proposed design enforces the funnel guarantee without retuning. In the second-order study, the proposed controller achieves lower integral error and control energy at equal peak control, while under actuator saturation it can leave the funnel slightly. Initial-condition tests further demonstrate the effect of actuator saturation, showcasing ideal funnel-invariance guarantees from physically constrained performance.

authors.name: Amit Shivam, Kiran Kumari, Fernando A. C. C. Fontes

papers.title: Quantale-Enriched Co-Design: Toward a Framework for Quantitative Heterogeneous System Design
papers.summary: Monotone co-design enables compositional engineering design by modeling components as feasibility relations between required resources and provided functionalities. However, its boolean formulation cannot natively represent quantitative criteria such as cost, confidence, or implementation choice. In practice, these considerations are introduced through ad-hoc scalarization or by augmenting the resource space, which obscures system structure and increases computational complexity. Therefore, we develop a quantale-enriched theory of co-design in which resources and functionalities are quantale-enriched categories and design problems are quantale-enriched profunctors, which lifts co-design from boolean feasibility to quantitative evaluation. Series, parallel, and feedback composition remain valid over any commutative quantale, and change-of-base maps between quantales yield heterogeneous composition, so that subsystems evaluated in different local semantics can be composed in a common framework. Numerical examples on a target-tracking system and a UAV delivery problem demonstrate this framework and show how it avoids the drawbacks of boolean-only formulations.

authors.name: Hans Riess, Yujun Huang, Matthew Klawonn, Gioele Zardini, Matthew Hale

papers.title: The Gaussian data assumption does not always lead to the largest Cram\'er-Rao bound
papers.summary: This lecture note addresses the common misconception that the Gaussian distribution always yields the largest Cram\'er-Rao Bound (CRB). We show that this property only holds under restrictive conditions: specifically, when the mean and covariance parameters are decoupled in the Fisher Information Matrix (FIM), when the parameter of interest lies in the mean vector and when there are no additive nuisance parameters. Beyond this framework, we provide counterexamples demonstrating that non-Gaussian distributions can produce larger CRB.

authors.name: Jean-Pierre Delmas, Habti Abeida

papers.title: Switched Control of Complex-Valued Kuramoto Networks
papers.summary: Synchronization in networks of coupled oscillators is classically studied via the Kuramoto model, whose intrinsic nonlinearity limits analytical tractability and complicates control design. Complex-valued extensions circumvent this by embedding phase dynamics into a higher-dimensional linear state space, where regulating complex-state moduli to a common value reproduces the nominal Kuramoto phase dynamics on an invariant manifold. Existing approaches to address this problem correspond, within a control framework, to state-feedback and hybrid reset-based strategies, each with performance constraints. We propose two switched control designs that overcome these limitations: a switched feedforward law ensuring exact phase correspondence at all times, and a feedforward plus sliding-mode law achieving finite-time mapping onto the original Kuramoto dynamics without spectral gain tuning. Additionally, we present a non-autonomous complex-valued MIMO sliding-mode controller that enforces phase locking at a prescribed frequency in finite time, regardless of natural frequencies and coupling strengths, under appropriate control gain selection. Simulations confirm improved transient response, steady-state accuracy, and robustness, including synchronization of heterogeneous networks where the classical real-valued Kuramoto model fails.

authors.name: Lorenzo Giordano, Josep M. Olm, Mario di Bernardo

papers.title: Second-Order Physics-Informed Learning of Road Traffic State using Probe Vehicles
papers.summary: We propose a Physics-Informed Learning framework for reconstructing traffic density and velocity state from sparse trajectory data. The proposed framework relies on the simple idea that a second-order model captures non-steady-state behaviors as minor modifications to first-order solutions. Therefore, the approach implements a tailored second-order correction to the density and the speed of a first-order estimate. This framework is evaluated in a ring-road scenario with real and simulated data. Results show that the implemented framework improves state estimation by achieving lower error and variance than previously investigated frameworks. These results hold for scenarios with heterogeneous driver behaviors (real data) and with different driver behavior models (simulated data), consistent across different penetration rates.

authors.name: S. Betancur Giraldo, H. Nouvel, M. Barreau

papers.title: Dynamic Multi-Robot Task Allocation under Uncertainty and Communication Constraints: A Game-Theoretic Approach
papers.summary: We study dynamic multi-robot task allocation under uncertain task completion, time-window constraints, and incomplete information. Tasks arrive online over a finite horizon and must be completed within specified deadlines, while agents operate from distributed hubs with limited sensing and communication. We model incomplete information through hub-based sensing regions that determine task visibility and a communication graph that governs inter-hub information exchange. Using this framework, we propose Iterative Best Response (IBR), a decentralized policy in which each agent selects the task that maximizes its marginal contribution to the locally observed welfare. We compare IBR against three baselines: Earliest Due Date first (EDD), Hungarian algorithm, and Stochastic Conflict-Based Allocation (SCoBA), on a city-scale package-delivery domain with up to 100 drones and varying task arrival scenarios. Under full and sparse communication, IBR achieves competitive task-completion performance with lower computation time.

authors.name: Maria G. Mendoza, Pan-Yang Su, Bryce L. Ferguson, S. Shankar Sastry

papers.title: Quantification and Regulation of Energy Reserves for Distributed Frequency and Voltage Control of Cyber-Physical Microgrids
papers.summary: The introduction of Renewable Energy Sources (RES) and Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) has led to the formation of cyber-physical Microgrids (MGs) and Networks of MGs (NMGs). MGs and NMGs can operate in islanded mode, transforming the grid into a more distributed system. This has led to extensive studies in the literature on distributed hierarchical control strategies. Previous works have proposed distributed secondary level frequency and voltage regulation control schemes for Battery Energy Storage System (BESS)- based Grid-Forming (GFM) inverters with State of Charge (SoC) balancing. However, control applications in terms of service-based reserves and local resource adequacy in MGs are largely unexplored. Therefore, this paper proposes a BESS-based GFM inverter energy reserves framework, to quantify reserves for hierarchical control operation. Additionally, to partially regulate the proposed energy reserves, we propose the formulation of a modified Distributed-Averaging Proportional-Integral (DAPI) controller with regulation energy reserve consensus. Modal analysis is performed to demonstrate the stability guarantees of energy consensus under simplified assumptions. Cyber-physical Controller Hardware-In-the-Loop (CHIL) simulation is performed on an MG topologically based on the IEEE 13 bus test feeder system in MATLAB/Simulink. The proposed scheme results illustrate effective frequency and voltage regulation along with improved power and energy sharing across droop-controlled and Virtual Synchronous Machine (VSM) controlled inverters

authors.name: Ahmed Saad Al-Karsani, Maryam Khanbaghi

papers.title: Kill-Probability-Maximization Guidance: Breaking from the Miss-Distance-Minimization Paradigm
papers.summary: Classical guidance laws aim at minimizing the miss distance, thus implicitly determining the minimum warhead lethality radius required against nominal targets. However, nonnominal targets or scenarios might render the designed warhead insufficient, causing a significant degradation in the single-shot kill probability (SSKP). We propose a guidance methodology that shifts the interceptor's objective from minimizing the miss distance to directly maximizing the SSKP, while taking into account the warhead's probabilistic lethality model. Complying with the generalized separation theorem, the paradigm presented here modifies deterministic differential-game-based guidance laws using Bayesian decision theory. For this purpose, we obtain the saddle-point solution of the deterministic differential game whose objective is the SSKP. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations demonstrate substantial SSKP improvement over the standard and recently introduced estimation-aware guidance laws, when tested against nominal and nonnominal evasively maneuvering targets.

authors.name: Liraz Mudrik, Yaakov Oshman

papers.title: A Novel Reinforcement Learning Based Framework for Scalable MIMO Interference Alignment
papers.summary: Interference alignment (IA) is a widely recognized approach for mitigating inter-cell interference in multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) networks. Despite its effectiveness, practical deployment remains constrained by two major challenges, i.e., the need for global channel state information (CSI) at each transmitter and the complexity of deriving closed-form solutions for intricate MIMO systems. This work aims to maximize network throughput by effectively mitigating interference using an IA-inspired learning algorithm that addresses its aforementioned challenges. First, we propose a predictive, transformer-based IA framework that estimates CSI to reduce signaling overhead in small-scale MIMO systems. Next, we formulate the IA problem as a multi-objective optimization problem based on subspace coordination and develop two reinforcement learning-based algorithms to enhance the scalability of IA in large-scale MIMO systems. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed methods significantly outperform conventional baselines with up to 30% average user throughput gains over the best performing baseline.

authors.name: Samitha Gunarathne, Eslam Eldeeb, Nurul Huda Mahmood, Italo Atzeni

papers.title: Toward Fair Speech Technologies: A Comprehensive Survey of Bias and Fairness in Speech AI
papers.summary: Speech technologies are deployed in high-stakes settings, yet fairness concerns remain fragmented across tasks and disciplines. Existing surveys either adopt a general machine-learning perspective that overlooks speech-specific properties or focus on a single task, missing failure patterns shared across the speech domain. Synthesizing over 400 studies spanning generation and perception tasks and emerging speech-language models, this survey presents a unified framework that links formal fairness definitions to evaluation, diagnosis, and mitigation. We formalize seven fairness definitions adapted to the speech modality and organize the field's conceptual expansion through three paradigms: Robustness, Representation, and Governance. We then ground evaluation metrics in the mathematical cores of these definitions, organizing them into six families and mapping each family back to the definitions it operationalizes. We diagnose bias sources along the speech processing pipeline, surfacing speech-specific mechanisms such as channel bias as a demographic proxy and annotation subjectivity in emotion labels. We systematize mitigation strategies across four intervention stages, mapping each to the diagnosed sources. Finally, we identify open challenges and propose directions for future research.

authors.name: Yi-Cheng Lin, Yun-Shao Tsai, Kuan-Yu Chen, Hsiao-Ying Huang, Huang-Cheng Chou, Shrikanth Narayanan, Yu Tsao, Jian-Jiun Ding, Hung-yi Lee

papers.title: Dante: An Open Source Model Pre-Training and Fine-Tuning Tool for the Dafne Federated Framework for Medical Image Segmentation
papers.summary: Adapting pre-trained deep learning segmentation models to new clinical domains is a persistent challenge in medical image analysis, particularly when annotated data at the target site are scarce. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning strategies offer a principled solution by selectively updating a controlled subset of model parameters, preserving previously acquired representations while reducing the risk of overfitting on small datasets. This paper introduces DAfNe TrainEr (Dante), an open-source module integrating with the Dafne federated segmentation ecosystem as a dedicated training and fine-tuning backend. Dante supports training from scratch with automatic architecture configuration, configurable layer freezing schedules, and Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) extended to N-dimensional convolutional layers through channel-wise factorization. To validate the module, Gradual Unfreezing (GU) and LoRA are assessed across realistic cross-domain MRI transfer scenarios covering abdominal organ segmentation and brain white matter lesion segmentation, under full-data and few-shot conditions. GU reduced the epochs required to reach 85% of peak performance by up to 63.6% compared to training from scratch, while LoRA achieved Dice Similarity Coefficients up to 0.957 in data-rich scenarios. Both strategies outperformed the baseline across all tested domains, with gains amplified by richer pre-training datasets. These results suggest that Dante can support the adaptation of medical image segmentation models across the evaluated anatomical and imaging domains when annotated target data are limited. Dante code is available at https://github.com/dafne-imaging/dafne-torch-trainer while Dafne ecosystem project is available at https://github.com/dafne-imaging.

authors.name: Giuseppe Timpano, Dibya Kumari, Maria Eugenia Caligiuri, Francesco Santini

papers.title: Revisiting TAS/GSC: A New Perspective and Application to DF Multihop Networks over Nakagami-m Fading Channels
papers.summary: In this work, transmit antenna selection (TAS) and generalized selection combining (GSC), i.e., TAS/GSC, are investigated over independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) Nakagami-$m$ flat fading channels. An alternative analytical approach based on polynomial-power expansions and partial-fraction decomposition is developed to obtain finite-sum representations of the GSC and TAS/GSC output signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) distributions. These representations lead to closed-form expressions for outage probability (OP), symbol error rate (SER), and ergodic capacity. Compared with existing multinomial theorem-based formulations, the derived expressions provide a more structured representation of the coefficients and summation terms. As an example, the proposed approach is applied to decode-and-forward (DF) multihop networks with TAS/GSC at each hop over independent and non-identically distributed (i.n.i.d.) Nakagami-$m$ fading channels. Exact closed-form expressions for the end-to-end OP and ergodic capacity, together with an analytical lower bound on the average SER, are derived. The high-SNR outage behavior is also investigated to determine the diversity order. Finally, the accuracy of the derived analytical expressions is verified by Monte Carlo simulations. Numerical results show that significant performance improvements are obtained with TAS/GSC. Furthermore, the proposed analytical representation provides a basis for investigating related TAS/GSC-assisted multi-antenna relay configurations in emerging wireless networks.

authors.name: Efendi Fidan, B\"u\c{s}ra Demirkol, O\u{g}uz Kucur

papers.title: Jamming-Resilient OTFS-NOMA
papers.summary: In this paper we propose a jamming-resilient sparse delay-Doppler NOMA scheme for OTFS and derive closed-form BER expressions from a Marchenko--Pastur conditioning argument on random unitary submatrices, in contrast to the well-known partial-band error floor of conventional OTFS-NOMA. The resulting bound is Hadamard-DFT-Haar invariant and remains valid under compromise of the shared randomization seed. A superincreasing power allocation brings low-complexity per-bin SIC up to the maximum-likelihood detector on the composite constellation, and a pairwise cluster rule scales the design beyond four users. Compared against a fair-baseline, the proposed scheme is the only configuration without a jammer-induced error floor and gives a ~6dB horizontal SNR gain at BER~=10^{-2}.

authors.name: Michel Kulhandjian, Hovannes Kulhandjian, Theodoros A. Tsiftsis

papers.title: RemoteRF: A Global, Open-Source Sandbox for Wireless Research and Education
papers.summary: Software-defined radios (SDRs) are powerful tools for research and education in wireless communications, but their cost and complexity put them out of reach for many researchers and institutions worldwide. To address this, we introduce RemoteRF, an open-source platform for creating large-scale testbeds of distributed SDRs and multi-modal peripherals that can be managed by a single server and shared across many users. Through a reservation-based framework, users can control devices over the internet via Python scripting, with only device-related commands routed to the server. In research, RemoteRF can be used to evaluate and reproducibly benchmark new physical-layer and full-stack 5G/6G techniques, collect real-world data for machine learning, and give AI agents controlled access to hardware for autonomous experimentation. In education, RemoteRF allows students in virtually any sized class to share a handful of SDRs to learn communication fundamentals through hands-on implementation with actual radios. The software powering RemoteRF is open-source and extensively documented online, allowing anyone to deploy their own instance in a matter of minutes. Beyond local use, instances can also connect to the RemoteRF Global network to share hardware across partner institutions or make devices publicly accessible worldwide. Since being deployed at UCLA, RemoteRF has logged over 4,000 hours of use across more than 250 researchers and students.

authors.name: Ethan Y. Ge, Ian P. Roberts

papers.title: Robust Transmission Design for RIS-Assisted RSMA-SWIPT Systems With Movable Antennas Under Hardware Distortions
papers.summary: To support joint information and energy delivery to energy-constrained users, this paper investigates robust transmission design for a multi-user rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA)-based simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) system empowered by movable antennas (MAs) and a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) under channel state information (CSI) uncertainty and residual hardware impairments (HIs). Unlike fixed-position antenna systems, MAs-enabled systems exhibit position-dependent channels, making CSI uncertainty relevant to both active and passive beamforming and antenna position adaptation. Residual HIs alter the effective signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratios and further couple transmit beamforming, RIS reflection control, common-rate allocation, power-splitting ratios, and antenna positions. These effects jointly yield a highly coupled resource allocation problem. To address this challenge, we propose a robust framework that maximizes the achievable sum-rate by jointly optimizing these variables subject to practical system constraints. A non-linear energy harvesting model is incorporated to capture practical SWIPT operation. The resulting non-convex problem is addressed through successive decomposition into active beamforming, RIS reflection design, power-splitting ratio optimization, and MAs position optimization subproblems, with tractable convex surrogate functions constructed to facilitate computationally efficient solutions. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, showing significant achievable sum-rate gains over benchmark schemes and favorable robustness and convergence behavior.

authors.name: Muhammad Asif, Asim Ihsan, Irfan Muhammad, Mohd Hamza Naim Shaikh, Syed Tariq Shah, Zhu Shoujin, Symeon Chatzinotas

papers.title: WTMOS: A Robust WavLM-Transformer Framework and ViViT Benchmarking for Cross-Corpus Audio MOS Prediction
papers.summary: Automatic Mean Opinion Score (MOS) prediction is essential for evaluating large-scale synthetic speech and audio enhancement systems, yet models frequently struggle with domain shift. This study presents WTMOS, a robust WavLM-Transformer framework and Video Vision Transformer (ViViT) benchmarking suite across three architectural configurations: Frozen Self-Supervised Learning (SSL-FRZ), Fine-Tuned SSL (SSL-FT), and ViViT. Evaluation is conducted in two phases: Part I utilizes a consolidated corpus of 130,652 samples across 19 diverse datasets, while Part II focuses on a purified 17-dataset English-only corpus. To assess robustness, a systematic Leave-One-Dataset-Out (LODO) protocol is employed to quantify the generalization gap between seen and unseen distributions. Finally, the top-performing model is benchmarked against 18 state-of-the-art (SOTA) metrics using the ARECHO framework. Results demonstrate that an English-only purified corpus consistently yields higher predictive precision across all architectures. While SSL-FT achieves the highest performance on seen validation data, the SSL-FRZ model provides superior robustness on unseen distributions, achieving a competitive Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.36 on the URGENT 2024 benchmark - closely matching domain-optimized SOTA metrics (MSE 0.30). Although the ViViT architecture remains below SSL-based models in total capacity, it delivers stable results in English-only trials. LODO results confirm that while models perform significantly better on seen samples, frozen SSL embeddings combined with deep Transformer encoders offer the most stable and scalable solution for universal speech quality assessment. To support further research, the top-performing English-only SSL-Transformer model and weights are made publicly available via Hugging Face.

authors.name: Mustafa Ozan Duman, Ahmet Emir Dirik

papers.title: What does the model actually see? Evaluation protocols and input availability in data-driven prediction of room acoustic parameters
papers.summary: Machine-learnt models are increasingly used to predict ISO 3382-1 room acoustic parameters at unmeasured seats from sparse measurements, with reported coefficients of determination frequently above 0.85. This paper shows that such figures are often determined by the evaluation protocol rather than by the model. Using a multi-condition measurement campaign in a 264-seat conference hall and a 180-seat concert hall, three model families were evaluated under a factorial protocol ablation: validation splits either row-based or grouped by receiver position, and inputs either including measured-at-test quantities (the target position's impulse response, co-located parameter measurements, position identifiers) or restricted to source-receiver geometry and environmental state. Row-based splits with measured-at-test inputs reproduce the high reported accuracies (mean R^2 of 0.81 for the core parameters); grouped splits with deployment-consistent inputs reduce these to 0.09-0.60 and reorder the apparent difficulty of parameter classes. Access to the target's own impulse response at test time reproduces the high accuracy of the row-based folds but provides no benefit under grouped folds. The row-based figure reflects condition interpolation at the measured positions rather than transferable acoustic information. Under the deployment-consistent protocol the spread between Random Forest, the hybrid network, and inverse-distance weighting is several times smaller than the spread between protocols for a fixed model; the learnt models retain a measurable advantage for sound strength and reverberation time, and the high accuracy of the original pipelines re-emerges as condition interpolation at measured positions, a distinct and operationally useful task. A reporting checklist operationalises the findings.

authors.name: Ak{\i}n Oktav

papers.title: Scalable Attention for 5G NR Channel Estimation
papers.summary: Attention-based neural estimators achieve strong channel-estimation accuracy, but the computational cost of global attention over the time-frequency resource grid grows quadratically with the number of subcarriers, and these estimators are typically tied to a single resource allocation. This paper proposes Channel Estimation Attention (CHEA), a low-complexity channel estimator for 5G New Radio (5G NR) multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO). CHEA replaces global attention with a multi-resolution windowed design: a high-resolution encoder preserves local pilot detail, a low-resolution encoder captures wider frequency-domain context, and a local cross-attention decoder transfers this coarse context back to the high-resolution pilot tokens. A per-Physical Resource Block (PRB) upsampling module then reconstructs the channel over the full slot. Because every attention operation is confined to a fixed-size window and reconstruction is performed per PRB, the cost of CHEA scales linearly with the number of subcarriers, and a single trained model supports different PRB allocations without retraining. On a standard-compliant Physical Uplink Shared Channel (PUSCH), CHEA achieves the lowest Mean Squared Error (MSE) among conventional and state-of-the-art neural estimators, while requiring 2.8x to 22.0x lower operations than existing attention-based estimators.

authors.name: Mahdi Abdollahpour, Marco Bertuletti, Yichao Zhang, Yawei Li, Luca Benini, Alessandro Vanelli-Coralli

papers.title: Observer-Assisted Relative-Velocity Compensation with LPV-$H_\infty$ Robust Correction for 3D Trajectory Tracking of Underactuated Non-Minimum-Phase AUVs under Ocean Currents
papers.summary: This paper develops an observer-assisted control architecture for 3D trajectory tracking of torpedo-type underactuated AUVs with non-minimum-phase sway/heave dynamics under unknown ocean currents. A three-stage state-current observer provides relative-velocity estimates to a nonlinear feedforward term for dominant current rejection and to an LMI-certified LPV-$\mathcal{H}_\infty$ correction layer. Feedback-linearising cancellation yields a constant input matrix, enabling convex synthesis without pairwise cross terms. A residual-level break-even law shows that the effective surge disturbance depends on current-estimation error, while a singular-perturbation analysis proves local practical uniform ultimate boundedness on the embedded LPV model. REMUS simulations over three trajectories and four current scenarios show 89-96% current-estimation reduction, about 99% translational residual reduction, and RMS tracking-error reduction from 4.04 m to 0.24 m.

authors.name: Mohammad Sabouri

papers.title: Multilayer Dual-polarized Microstrip Antenna Design by Topology Optimization with Enhanced Bandwidth
papers.summary: Dual-polarized (DP) microstrip antennas are utilized in wireless systems for efficient data transmission. However, their bandwidth is typically very limited. In this contribution, we propose to design DP microstrip antennas with enhanced bandwidth using a density-based topology optimization approach. We formulate an optimization problem that simultaneously accounts for feeding port matching, the ports' isolation, and far-field dual-polarized performance. To enhance the bandwidth, we employ an FR4 stack-up, in which the copper on two layers is optimized simultaneously. We present two antenna designs operating around 5.7 GHz, which show a compromise in performance between a high isolation (more than 40 dB) and enhanced impedance bandwidth (around 10%). The optimized designs are experimentally validated, showing an excellent agreement between the simulated and measured performance.

authors.name: Pan Lu, Eddie Wadbro, Viktor Lundstr\"om, Jonas Starck, Martin Berggren, Emadeldeen Hassan

papers.title: Parameter-Dependent LMI Synthesis for Semi-Global Differential ISS Trajectory Tracking of Nonholonomic Mobile Robots Under Multiplicative Wheel Slip
papers.summary: This paper presents a parameter-dependent linear matrix inequality (LMI) synthesis framework for trajectory tracking of nonholonomic mobile robots subject to multiplicative wheel slip. A sampled polytopic convex formulation jointly targets four design objectives on the variational dynamics in Kanayama coordinates: a prescribed exponential decay rate, an H-infinity disturbance-to-error gain, regional pole placement, and a weighted gain bound acting as a design-time actuator budget. The inverse metric and the auxiliary gain are parameterized affinely in the reference linear and angular velocities. A Slip-to-Disturbance Lemma provides an explicit closed-form upper bound on the additive disturbance equivalent to bounded multiplicative wheel slip in Kanayama coordinates, connecting the physical slip mechanism to the convex synthesis. The dissipation inequality is established at the sixteen vertices of the parameter-rate polytope, and a Lipschitz-based residual condition is given as a sufficient criterion for extending feasibility to interior points; the regions where the criterion succeeds for the synthesized controller, and where it does not, are both reported. An integral representation of the Kanayama residual lifts the variational certificate to a pointwise exponential-plus-ISS bound on the trajectory error directly from the LMI. The certified envelope is the semi-global ball at sigma_bar = 0.10; variable-terrain tests at slip ratios up to plus-minus 50% are reported as empirical observations outside that envelope. In the certified regime, the LPV controller and a fixed-gain LMI baseline produce quantitatively similar tracking records; on the severe-slip probes, the parameter-dependent design retains modest reproducible margins over both the fixed-gain and the classical Kanayama baselines.

authors.name: Mohammad Sabouri

papers.title: GML-Based Optimization for Movable Antenna Wireless Networks: Challenges and Opportunities
papers.summary: Movable antenna (MA) is proposed as an emerging technology for future wireless networks. By leveraging the additional spatial degrees of freedom, MA can proactively reshape the wireless propagation environment, thereby enhancing network performance.However, fully unlocking the potential of MA networks necessitates the joint optimization of MA antenna positioning and beamforming. For this non-convex and highly coupled problem, existing solutions exhibit significant limitations. Therefore, this paper proposes a gradient-based meta learning (GML) optimization framework. Specifically, we first elaborate on the hardware architecture and channel characteristics of MA, based on which we analyze the primary challenges in optimizing MA wireless networks. Subsequently, we introduce the fundamental logic of the GML framework and compare it with existing methods. Furthermore, we discuss the constraint handling strategies for applying the proposed optimization framework to MA networks. A specific case is studied to show the performance of proposed framework based on numerical simulation. Finally, this paper outlines future research directions for both the GML framework and MA wireless networks.

authors.name: Zhendong Li, Yujie Zhao, Zhou Su, Tom H. Luan, Zhiqing Wei, Ying Wang, Wen Chen

papers.title: Separate First, Then Associate: A Two-Stage Approach for Real-World Audio-Visual Speech Enhancement
papers.summary: Audio-visual speech enhancement (AVSE) aims at extracting target speech from multi-speaker mixtures by exploiting visual cues. Although recent studies have reported strong performance on simulated datasets, the performance, however, often drops dramatically when they are applied to real-world audio-visual recordings. To bridge this gap, the Real-World AVSE Challenge held in the ISCSLP 2026 conference calls for participants to design a practical solution for AVSE under real-world conditions, where speaker overlap, acoustic interferences, room reverberation and visual degradations naturally co-exist. In our submission to the challenge, we propose a decoupled \textit{separation-then-association} approach. It consists of two stages: a separation stage in which a trained, audio-only model (i.e., not using visual cues) is used to separate input multi-speaker mixture to individual speaker signals, followed by an association stage, where an audio-visual CLIP model is used to identify the separated speech signal with the highest similarity with the target speaker's facial video via cross-modal similarity matching.
